# Implementation plan

The **action-oriented companion** to the design docs. Design docs say *what* Brainstorm is and *why*; this doc says *how we build it*, *in what order*, and *what "done" means*. When a design doc and this doc disagree about ordering, this doc is updated.

> **Structure (re-implemented 2026-05-18):** the plan is now organised by **three top-level domains** — **Infrastructure**, **Shell**, **Apps** — instead of by stage. Infrastructure and Shell break into **sections → task lists**; each App is its own **task list**. The legacy `Stage N` ids are kept in parentheses + every iteration id is unchanged, so commit / review / OQ references stay valid. Per-iteration narrative, test counts, and build/test signals live in [implementation-log.md](implementation-log.md); the at-a-glance grid is [implementation-plan-table.md](implementation-plan-table.md). All three move together every turn an iteration lands.

Assumes you have read [00-index.md](00-index.md), [foundations/02-architecture.md](foundations/02-architecture.md), [shell/12-shell-architecture.md](shell/12-shell-architecture.md), [foundations/28-vault-and-onboarding.md](foundations/28-vault-and-onboarding.md), [foundations/35-code-conventions.md](foundations/35-code-conventions.md).

## Legend

`✅` done (detail → [log](implementation-log.md)) · `🟡` in flight · `◑` preview-drop only (throwaway renderer shipped; real-wiring half pending) · `⚪` pending · `❌` rejected. **These five are the ONLY status icons.** A bullet leading with anything else (`⛔`, `🟢`, `🟠`, …) is skipped SILENTLY by the parser, so the iteration vanishes from every projection — the vault's Tasks app, the at-a-glance table, the stage rollups — with no error anywhere. Seven bullets had drifted that way and were invisible for weeks; `plan-unknown-status-icons.test.ts` now fails the suite instead. Priority is NOT encoded here — put it in the task text. A task line is `<icon> <id> — <task> — <gate/dep>`. Trailing notes are kept to a clause; nothing in this file is a multi-paragraph block — that is what the log is for.

**`◑` is debt with an expiry, not a state.** Every `◑` must convert to `✅` (real half landed) or be removed by the boundary of the stage that gates its real half. **No `◑` ships in a v1 release build** (v1-exit checklist). A `◑` whose gate has passed and is still `◑` is a release blocker, not an accepted state.

**Iteration ids are immutable.** The id scheme is deliberately mixed (`9.3.5.N4`, `OpenRes-1c`, `B9.1`, `SH-29`, `Mailbox-1`) because ids are never renumbered — commit messages, OQ entries, reviews, and the log all reference them. Scannability is traded for stable traceability on purpose; do not "tidy" ids.

## What "v1" means

Per the phasing tables in [16](security/16-identity-orgs-encryption.md), [27](shell/27-layouts.md), [28](foundations/28-vault-and-onboarding.md), [18](data/18-storage-and-search.md), [22](platform/22-ai-foundations.md), **v1 ships:** sovereign single-user multi-device identity; one vault per window + multi-vault registry; per-entity DEK encryption (single-user proven); SQLite + Yjs + FTS5 + vector hybrid search; App SDK v1 + capability ledger + sandboxed per-app renderers + intents; **all 19 bundled apps** — Notes, code-editor, files, form-designer, theme-editor, database, graph, tasks, calendar, journal, whiteboard, bookmarks, preview, books, automations, **mailbox, web-browser, agent, connector-framework** (Bin is a shell surface); `stacked`+`grid` layouts; composed menu + shortcuts + unified settings; AI broker with BYO keys + on-device embeddings; local install of third-party apps. **The four agentic apps (mailbox / web-browser / agent / connector) are launch-blocking v1, not a later tier** — this resolves the prior scope-limbo and the doc-22 "chat post-v1" reversal (the Agent app is v1, reconciled in [55](apps/55-agent-app.md)). v1 scope is unchanged, but the **public beta shipped EARLY — `v0.1.5` on 2026-06-29** (a usable encrypted multi-device core, not GA; the original `2026-09-01` target is superseded), and the product has since iterated to **`v0.5.0`** (see the release queue in [Release plan & roadmap](#release-plan--roadmap)). The GA definition of done is unchanged.

**v1 explicitly excludes:** accounts, hosted relay, orgs, server-readable spaces, multi-user sharing, `freeform` layouts, app-store distribution, paid features, any commercial surface, **and the post-v1 social surface ([Community-board](#community-board-v2--) + [Chats](#chats-v2--))** — that surface is multi-user by definition and is gated on the v2 org/consumer-account work. These are **v2** (Stage 14, kept under Infrastructure → Commercial backend).

## Workflow standards (every iteration, every domain)

Non-negotiable, unchanged by this restructure — full text in [foundations/35-code-conventions.md](foundations/35-code-conventions.md):

1. **New features ship with tests.** Per-package floors: 85% shell core · 80% SDK · 70% first-party apps. CRDT → property tests; IPC envelopes round-trip through property tests; UI ships a Playwright assertion. Total coverage cannot decrease.
2. **Design, UX, performance are first-class.** No abstraction without three uses. Every user-facing change ships screenshot + keyboard path + screen-reader path + discoverability. Keyboard via the shortcut registry (no raw `e.key`); every string via `t()` from day one. Budget-touching iterations ship before/after numbers; `size-limit` enforced.
3. **Stability + security continuously audited.** Per-PR security review (new capability / IPC / credential / dependency). Stage/section-boundary triggers stability + performance + security audits recorded under `docs/_review/`. Findings → [reference/11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md) or the tracker; no quiet-fix.
4. **Dogfood-surfaced *features* land as a plan rung the same turn they ship.** The friction log ([dogfood/friction-log.md](dogfood/friction-log.md)) is the channel for bugs / design nits / gaps — those triage and fix in place. But when a dogfood session ships a genuinely **new feature** (a new affordance, a cross-app capability, a shared primitive — e.g. the read-only lock fleet, the shared `<EmptyState>`), it gets a tracked iteration id in this plan **in the same turn**, ✅ with its commit(s), not left to live only in the friction log. The plan is the source of truth for *what exists*; a feature the plan can't see is a divergence (the lock fleet + EmptyState + inline-toolbar polish were retro-filed 2026-06-28 exactly because this rule was missing). A bug fix is not a feature — don't over-file; the test is "would a user call this a new thing the product can now do?"

**The bar is uniform by deliberate decision, not oversight.** It does **not** tier by blast radius — a leaf-app polish iteration carries the same tests / security review / four-path UX evidence / three-file sync as a shell-core one. The coordination cost across ~250 iterations is real and **accepted**: the alternative (a tiered bar) leaks regressions exactly through the "low-risk" tier the `apps/*` typecheck-gate hole already proved dangerous (Graph icons regressed 6×). Reviewed 2026-05-19; revisit only with evidence the cost outweighs the leak it prevents.

## North star: the OS for an AI-native company (long-horizon)

**This section changes nothing in the plan below — it is a directional note, not a stage.** The long-horizon product is an **operating system for an AI-native company**: humans + AI agents sharing one knowledge base, one identity system, one capability ledger; agents doing real work with scoped, audited, revocable permissions on owned data. Full thesis in [foundations/67-ai-native-company.md](foundations/67-ai-native-company.md). Three load-bearing facts for *this* doc:

1. **It reorders no stage and adds nothing to v1.** The governed-agent surfaces (agent-as-roster-member type, capability grant/revoke + audit UI for agents) land in their natural slot **after the AI broker (`11.x`)** and the post-Collab identity work — tracked there when scheduled, never pulled forward. Stages 5→11 are unchanged.
2. **It sharpens the *why* of work already on the plan.** Foundation polish and the dogfood-and-fix loop are the present-tense expression of the vision — an AI-native company OS lives on trust, so every "small problem here and there" is a trust leak. The bug burn-down *is* north-star work.
3. **One new design constraint, due when Stage 11 begins:** model selection is a **governed, per-task local↔cloud choice** (not a binary) — the `11.x` AI-broker routing must make "local-first, cloud-when-chosen" a configuration, not a rewrite. Tracked as OQ-AINC-3.

OQ-AINC-1..4 in [reference/11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md) gate the eventual surfaces; none gate any current stage.

**The orchestration spine is now designed.** [platform/69-agent-teams-and-orchestration.md](platform/69-agent-teams-and-orchestration.md) takes the dogfood-team model (identity + specialty + a voice in a shared channel + a coordination discipline) and productizes it: a `brainstorm/Agent/v1` persona-shell-over-a-capability-ceiling, each agent a real Ed25519 principal, a **Team** surface (directory + create/configure + grant/revoke + audit), and orchestration as *assembly* — delegation (`delegate` tool, safe by recursive `intersectAgentTools`), assignment (task `assignee` = agent + a `Trigger`, no lease ledger), and Chat as the agent channel. It **resolves OQ-AINC-1**, **takes a position on OQ-AINC-2** (grant/revoke + audit ships *with* the Team surface), and opens OQ-AT-1..4. Lands **post-beta** as the **Agent-Teams** rungs (`Agent/v1` + identity · Team surface + grants · `delegate` · assignment triggers · seeds); design-only today, no stage reorder.

## Release plan & roadmap

**✅ PUBLIC BETA SHIPPED 2026-06-29 as `v0.1.5`** — ~9 weeks ahead of the original `2026-09-01` target: a usable, encrypted, multi-device core, signed + notarized on macOS (Apple silicon + Intel) and built for Windows + Linux, published on GitHub Releases with in-app auto-update. v1 scope is unchanged — all 19 apps + sync + AI + hardening — and the beta was a milestone *within* v1, not GA. **GA continues on the same single-v1 track with no committed date.**

Forward planning is now organized as **release trains** ([§ Release trains](#release-trains--the-forward-queue-2-heroes-each)) — each carrying two hero features + a mandatory product-polish batch — up to GA (`1.0.0`) and then the v2 commercial stack. The one hard sequencing constraint is the **infra + collaborative-sync line**: single-user trains (`0.8.0`→`0.11.0`) ship on today's infrastructure; multi-user sharing, [peer-to-peer sync](#peer-to-peer-sync-design-only-spike-p2p-0-first-not-started), and v2 sit below the line and need the durable sync node hardened + the collaborative-sync layer finished. *(The pre-beta gate machinery — G0→G4, beta-freeze, decision queue, beta-exit checklist, cut levers — is retired and archived in [implementation-log.md § Beta program (retired)](implementation-log.md#beta-program-retired--shipped-v015-2026-06-29).)*

### Release planning — semver tracks (adopted 2026-07-07)

Releases are the sequencing layer; stages + iteration ids stay the work units and the backlog. Every release is user-facing the moment it publishes (in-app auto-update), so the version number is a promise about blast radius:

- **PATCH `0.x.Y+1`** — fixes, reliability completions, polish, dep/security bumps. No new user-facing surface a user must learn.
- **MINOR `0.X+1.0`** — a feature release with a headline: a new capability the product can now do. Gets a hero What's-New entry, a site refresh, and (when public-worthy) an announce post. Pre-1.0, minor releases may also carry breaking-ish churn, flagged in notes.

- **MAJOR `1.0.0`** — GA, defined by §GA definition of done below (single v1, no committed date). Post-1.0, major = compatibility breaks only.

**Release train — a ~1–2 week milestone that batches many features + fixes, then ships (adopted 2026-07-08).** Every release costs a full multi-arch signed+notarized build, three synced note surfaces, and an auto-update push to every install — overhead that only pays off with a *substantial* delta. So a release is **not** one feature or one fix; it's a **time-boxed milestone** that gathers *several* features and a batch of bug fixes developed over roughly one to two weeks, then cuts as one coherent set. How it runs:

- **The next release is an open milestone bucket**, not a single anchor. Each version row below lists a **theme** + a **bucket** of candidate items (features, fixes, polish). Work lands on `main` continuously; the bucket accumulates.
- **Cut when the window closes and the bucket is a coherent, meaningful set** — a headline feature or two + the fixes that rode along. Not per-item; a single merged PR never triggers a release.
- **A release must still carry a change a user would actually notice.** Internal-only work (tests, tooling, housekeeping, refactors) lands on `main` and rides the train — it never justifies a release alone. (0.2.2 was *held* on exactly this: its whole cycle was a regression test + housekeeping — the F-245 *fix* had already shipped in 0.2.1 — so there was no user-facing delta to release.)
- **Minor vs patch** is decided at cut time by what the bucket ended up containing: a new capability → minor; only fixes/polish → patch.
- Before cutting, **diff `v<lasttag>..origin/main`** and confirm the accumulated delta is genuinely user-facing and worth a build.

**Rules.** (1) The queue below is the source of the next version number — `bun run release prepare <version>` takes it from here, never ad hoc. (2) An iteration landing appends itself to the current train's bucket the same turn (the plan-update rule, applied per release). (3) The train's bucket is re-scoped freely while open; the version type (minor/patch) is decided at cut time by what actually shipped. (4) Scope candidates are validated against friction-log **status** lines, not triage lines. (5) Cut only when the accumulated `v<lasttag>..main` delta is user-facing and coherent — never on a single merged PR.

The owner-side FS held; the survivor path did not. ✅ **`ROT-3a-i` — versioned/monotonic DEK install landed** (2026-07-09, same PR #128): member-wrap format v2 carries an **AAD-authenticated** DEK ordinal, the store ranks by `version DESC`, and `installEntityDek` accepts strictly-newer / rejects ≤ — closing F-ROT-1 (survivor now upgrades to DEK′, proven end-to-end via guest B's real install path), F-ROT-2, F-ROT-3 (replay can't roll back), and OQ-REV-6's stale-wrap. Full shell suite green (527 files / 5787 tests). ✅ **ROT-4 `/security-review` re-run done** (2026-07-09, three independent lenses, [_review/2026-07-09-rot-3a-i-security-review.md](_review/2026-07-09-rot-3a-i-security-review.md)): the online path is **crypto/auth/injection clean**, but found **F-ROT-4** (HIGH) — an offline (or mid-publish-failed) rotation never resumes and `revoke()` returns success anyway, so the DEK is never rotated and the removed member keeps reading new content. ✅ **`ROT-3a-ii` — durable deferred-rotation resume landed** (2026-07-09, same PR #128): `#rotateAfterRevoke` always does its durable half (mint DEK′ + re-wrap + append-to-doc) online or off; a new durable `pending_rotations` table (entities.db v8) + `drainPendingRotations()` (fires on relay-connect + boot) finish the deferred wire delivery — closing F-ROT-4. **All findings (F-ROT-1/2/3/4) closed; ✅ shell PR #128 MERGED to main 2026-07-09** — rotate-on-revoke content forward secrecy is on `main` (`ROT-3a` + `ROT-3a-i` + `ROT-3a-ii`), F-286 → ✅ (content). ### Release trains — the forward queue (2 heroes each)

Beta is **shipped** (`v0.1.5`, 2026-06-29; now `v0.7.0`, 2026-07-21). The forward roadmap is no longer gate-driven — it's a sequence of **release trains**, each carrying **two hero features** (the headline capabilities that name the release) plus the riders and fixes that land in the window — then GA (`1.0.0`), then the v2 commercial stack. Ordering is by dependency, not date; a train cuts when its bucket is coherent (per the release-train rule above). The historical queue (`0.1.9`→`0.7.0`) is above; the shipped-work narrative is in [implementation-log.md](implementation-log.md). *(The pre-beta gate machinery — G0→G4, beta-freeze, beta-exit checklist, decision queue, cut levers, three-clocks — is retired and archived in [implementation-log.md § Beta program (retired)](implementation-log.md#beta-program-retired--shipped-v015-2026-06-29).)*

**Every train also carries a product-polish batch — non-negotiable.** The owner bar is a *polished* product, and right now it isn't there: editor blocks, entity-property rendering, visual-design quality, and element positioning / layout are below the bar. The **`POLISH-*` dogfood-hardening track** (see [Product polish & dogfood hardening](#product-polish--dogfood-hardening-standing-quality-track-polish--owner-driven)) feeds every train — each owner dogfood session that surfaces a functional or visual defect files a `POLISH-*` rung, and no train ships without draining its polish batch. Polish is a co-hero here, not background cleanup.

**⚠️ Release-notes rule (learned at the 0.10.0 cut, 2026-07-25): a What's-New entry may only claim what is *already merged to `main` at tag time*.** The shipped `0.9.0` entry announced **Notion import** — but `IE-7` (shell #282) landed *after* both `v0.9.0` and the `v0.9.1` hotfix, so every 0.9.x user was told a feature was there that wasn't. (`Browser-6` downloads, announced in the same entry, *was* in `v0.9.0` — the entry was written mid-train and only one claim outran the code.) The feature is genuinely present in `0.10.0` and is announced there. **How to not repeat it:** write the entry from the actual `v<last>..main` commit delta at prepare time, never from the train's *planned* bucket — `bun run release prepare` deliberately validates the entry *after* branching off `origin/main`, so the delta is knowable at that exact moment.

**0.8.0 landed rider — analytics observability + vault-in-Downloads fix (✅ shell PR #243, 2026-07-22):** continues the shipped analytics lineage (`0.4.3`/`0.4.5`). (1) **Bug** — vault creation refused any non-empty target folder, so Windows Downloads / OneDrive folders (which carry a `desktop.ini`; also `Thumbs.db` / macOS `.DS_Store`) failed with "Directory is not empty"; `ensureDirectoryUsable` now ignores OS-metadata entries. (2) **Analytics normalized** — an `AnalyticsEvent` enum + `AnalyticsProp` keys replace loose event-name string literals; `App Launched` carries a normalized `app_name`; normalized context (`platform` / `os_version` / `arch` / `locale` / `language` / `region` / `shell_version` / `app_id` / `app_name` / `app_version`) is merged into **every** event. Region is locale-derived — **IP geolocation stays off** (privacy posture preserved). (3) **Error telemetry** — `trackError()` → `Error Encountered` (stable scope + code only, never raw messages/paths that embed the OS username), wired into vault create / open / template-import via `classifyVaultError`; this is what now surfaces the F-456 failure class. Tests: `vault-directory-usable`, `events` (`parseLocale` + taxonomy), `analytics` (context-merge + `trackError`, PII-free).

> **⎯⎯ Infra + collaborative-sync line ⎯⎯**  Everything **below** this line needs the durable sync node hardened for multi-user scale **and** the collaborative-sync layer (`Collab-C5`/`C6` + presence, already partly shipped) finished; the **`P2P-0` spike** ([Peer-to-peer sync](#peer-to-peer-sync-design-only-spike-p2p-0-first-not-started)) reports here and gates the P2P transport. Everything **above** the line is single-user / own-device and ships on the infrastructure we already have. Do **not** pull a below-the-line hero forward across this line — that's the one hard sequencing constraint left in the roadmap.

*(Hero assignments are a sequencing intent, re-scoped freely at cut time by what actually landed — same rule as the historical queue. What's fixed is the **infra + collaborative-sync line** and that **every train drains a polish batch**.)*

### Execution model — multiple agent teams

The plan is now the coordination substrate the multi-agent orchestration protocol (CLAUDE.md §Multi-agent orchestration — dev-MCP lease ledger: `orchestration.claim`/`renew`/`handoff`/`release`) runs against. **As of 2026-05-23 the parallel-app fan-out branch is OFF; remaining work is serialized** ([[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]]):

- **Spine = one serialized owner.** G0→G1→G2-spine is a single claim chain (`orchestration.claim` per rung, `handoff` between). Parallelizing a sequential unknown just produces confident-wrong forks.
- **Phase 1 — shell + infra, no app work.** ✅ **Effectively complete (2026-06-19).** Drained the G2 sync spine (`10.3`→`10.9` ✅) → finished every remaining Shell-section row (OpenRes-1c ✅, Feedback-1/2/3 ✅, Welcome-1 ✅, Net-1/Net-2 ✅, App-lock `13.8` ✅) → Stage 12 (`12.1`/`12.3`/`12.4`/`12.8` ✅, `12.5`/`12.7` ✅; `12.15` infra+edges ✅ 15a/b/c/e/f, only the 15d content fan-out deferred) → Stage 13 hardening (`13.4a` ✅). **Two rows originally filed here are re-scoped *out* of the Phase-1 gate — they're gated on Phase-2 work and can't close before apps start: `Welcome-2` (vault template gallery; gated on the `9.3.5` single-object-space remodel) and `Net-3` (live-DOM feeder; gated on `Browser-1`, a Phase-2 app).** No app iteration is claimed until this phase clears (now satisfied). The G3 quality fan-out (`12.1`/`12.4`/`12.7`) was *part of this phase* — finished before any app slot opened. (**Post-v1, not in Phase 1**: the entire Layouts render pipeline `8.3`/`8.4`/`8.8`/`8.9` — v1 apps ship with their existing hardcoded views; the `Layout/v1` contract `8.1`/`8.2`/`8.5`/`8.6`/`8.7` stays frozen-but-unused until the layout-editor app `8.10` arrives post-release.)
- **Phase 2 — apps serially, one at a time.** Each app gets a single dedicated slot; the slot finishes the app's full remaining ladder **including its previously-fanned-out G2 BP-block adoption** (Tasks `9.14.3`, Calendar `9.15.3`, Whiteboard `9.17.4`/`.7`, Bookmarks `9.18.4`, Database `9.12.16-UI`, Graph `9.13.13b`) inside that app's slot. No claiming a second app while the first is in flight. The G2 table row still names which BP-block adoptions exist — but they're now scheduled inside each app's serial slot, not run in parallel.
- **Concurrency is capped by review/integration throughput, not team count.** The bottleneck is the gates (tests/security/perf review + single-integrator merge to `main`), per the binding-clock point. Authoring is cheap; review is the floor. Going serial concentrates one workstream's review/verify loop in one window — same total verification cost, but lower context-switching overhead and lower confident-wrong-fork risk than 8 apps in flight ahead of an integrator.
- **One integrator to `main`.** The single active builder never writes `main`; the integrator merges cleared branches, runs the §6 dev-MCP re-validate on any structural edit, and keeps plan/log/table in sync.
- **Ledger is the source of truth for who-owns-what.** `orchestration.status` before picking up work; fail-closed on contended claims. Under the serial policy a second active app claim is a protocol violation, not an inefficiency. (dev-MCP offline → the ledger degrades to the hand-edited plan icons until 0.12; treat a `🟡` with no active claim as reapable.)
- **Exception**: a hotfix in app B to unblock the active app A (e.g. a shared SDK extraction touching both) is the integrator's call — not a new app claim.

### GA definition of done (post-beta, **no date** — single v1)

- [ ] All 19 app ladders ✅ — no `◑` anywhere in a release build.
- [ ] `11.4` hybrid search + on-device embeddings; `11.9` AI panel.
- [ ] Official OAuth clients registered + verified for shipped connectors (`Mailbox-9`: Google restricted-scope verification + CASA for Gmail; Microsoft for M365) — end users never open a cloud console.
- [ ] Full Stage 12 (`12.3`/`12.5`/`12.8`) + full Stage 13 (`13.2`/`13.4` stress/`13.5` portability/`13.7` doc review).
- [ ] Every v1-gating OQ resolved (non-struck rows in [Open questions that gate work](#open-questions-that-gate-work)).
- [ ] No open Sev-1 / Sev-2. *(Signing + in-app auto-update already shipped in `v0.1.5`; Windows EV signing `DQ-13.1-B` is the last hardening tail.)*
- [ ] The product-polish bar is met — no open owner-flagged quality-bar defects in the [`POLISH-*` track](#product-polish--dogfood-hardening-standing-quality-track-polish--owner-driven) (editor blocks, properties, visual design, layout all at the polished-product bar).

**Critical path — the spine that reached beta (shipped):** `9.3.5.B/.N1–N5` → `9.3.3` → `9.4/9.5/9.11` → `9.10` → `10.0`→`10.1–10.9` → **[beta ✅ `v0.1.5`]** → `11.0`→`11.1–11.9` → full `12`/`13`. That spine is done; the **forward** critical path is the [infra + collaborative-sync line](#release-trains--the-forward-queue-2-heroes-each) — the durable sync node hardened for multi-user scale + the collaborative-sync layer finished + the `P2P-0` spike reported — which gates every `0.12.0`+ multi-user hero and the whole v2 stack. Effort on late leaf apps does not move that line; the infra + collab-sync work does.

# Infrastructure

The non-visual substrate: build, identity, storage, the capability/IPC spine, the SDK, host services, sync, AI, and the commercial back-of-house. Sections are ordered roughly by dependency.

## Monorepo & worker scaffolding *(Stage 1)*

Goal: package layout per [35](foundations/35-code-conventions.md); `utilityProcess` worker spawn-and-IPC scaffold per [12](shell/12-shell-architecture.md). **OQ-151 → Bun workspaces; OQ-20 deferred to hardening.**

- ✅ 1.1–1.6 — Bun workspaces, build, lint/test/typecheck, storage-worker spawn+dispose, envelope property tests, `size-limit` budgets.

## Identity, credentials & at-rest encryption *(Stage 2 + 3b)*

Goal: vault master key + Ed25519 identity in the OS keystore; credential store; encryption at rest. **OQ-113 keyring · OQ-25 XChaCha20-Poly1305 · OQ-114 Argon2id · OQ-123 no per-item ACL.**

- ✅ 2.1–2.8 — keystore backends (keyring/passphrase/insecure), crypto, identity, credential store, vault session, Security panel.
- ✅ 3b — SQLCipher driver swap **+ on-disk flip landed (2026-05-22)**. `better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers@12.9.0` now declared in `packages/shell/package.json`; `@electron/rebuild@4.0.4` added as devDep and the native addon rebuilt against Electron 41 (`NODE_MODULE_VERSION 145`, matching Electron 41's V8). The full at-rest path (per-DB HKDF key + `PRAGMA key` + atomic plaintext→encrypted migration + fail-closed verify) is unchanged from the code-complete landing; the new half is the **explicit boot-time probe + vault.json mode flag**, per OQ-34 §Stage 3b ("wires the unencrypted-vs-encrypted bit into vault.json so the open path knows which mode to use"). New `main/storage/at-rest-mode.ts` exposes the `AtRestMode` enum (Encrypted / Plaintext), pure `probeAtRestMode()` (drives the live SQLCipher contract probe against `:memory:`, cached for the process, returns `{mode, driverName, reason}`), `describeAtRestMode()` (canonical boot-log wording — `[shell] storage: encrypted at rest` vs `UNENCRYPTED at rest (3b inactive — OQ-34)`), and pure `reconcileAtRestMode(recorded, probed, vaultLabel)` returning one of four outcomes — `Matches`, `UpgradeReady` (recorded-plaintext + probed-encrypted), `FirstStamp` (legacy vault, no field), `DowngradeRefused` (recorded-encrypted + probed-plaintext → throws fail-closed; refusing to open prevents the silent data-loss scenario where a plaintext open against the encrypted DB either fails to read or creates a parallel plaintext copy). Both `createVault` (stamps the live mode) and `openVault` / `activateVault` (probe + reconcile + rewrite-on-stamp-or-upgrade) wire it in, preserving unknown forward-compat fields on the JSON rewrite (`activateVault` uses a parse-mutate-stringify path that retains every other key verbatim). **Tests**: +16 (10 at-rest-mode unit + 6 vault integration: createVault plaintext/encrypted stamp; openVault legacy first-stamp; recorded-encrypted-into-plaintext fail-closed refusal; recorded-plaintext + active-encrypted upgrade; forward-compat field preservation). 5311/5311 workspace green; `bun run verify` 192/192; workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files. **OQ-34 fully resolved** — the env-block (Python 3.14 / libexpat ABI) was on the from-source build path; prebuild-install picked the Electron-ABI binary cleanly. Builder commit forthcoming.

## Local data substrate — SQLite + Yjs *(Stage 3)*

Goal: four domain DBs + Yjs snapshot+tail format on disk; storage + ydoc workers functional. **OQ-18 dedicated ydoc worker · OQ-34 partial (encryption → 3b) · OQ-35 deferred.**

- ✅ 3.1–3.10 — `sqlite.ts` runtime-agnostic driver, four schemas + atomic migrations, repo pattern, `YDocStore` (CRC32 tail + compaction + truncation-tolerant), ydoc worker end-to-end over IPC.

## Capability ledger & IPC broker *(Stage 4)*

Goal: every IPC call capability-checked + identity-stamped; fail-closed; per-app backpressure. **OQ-115 → in-memory cached key for session lifetime.**

- ✅ 4.1–4.8 — default-minimum grants, per-vault ledger, envelope validation, renderer-identity verification, fail-closed `Unavailable`, per-app pending-queue shedding, `onDenied`→audit-log.

## App SDK, manifest & install *(Stage 5)*

Goal: a third-party app installs from disk, launches sandboxed, calls the SDK through the broker. **OQ-2 hybrid manifest schema · OQ-3 orphaned-resolvable types · OQ-4 per-app shared renderer.**

- ✅ 5.1–5.10 — manifest validator, `AppInstaller` (bundle SHA + registry rows + ledger grants), `AppLauncher` (identity-stamped sandboxed window), SDK runtime/bridge/errors, `@brainstorm/sdk-types`, fallback renderer, Stage-4 startup wiring closed.

Four new methods on the storage worker — `uploadBegin({name, mime?, totalBytes?}) → {uploadToken, chunkBytes}`, `uploadChunk({uploadToken, seq, bytesBase64}) → {ok, receivedBytes}` (idempotent per last-seq), `uploadCommit({uploadToken, expectedHash?}) → UploadedFile`, `uploadAbort({uploadToken})` — wired into `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `StorageService` + `runtime.storageProxy` + a `uploadStreamed(args)` convenience wrapper that drives Begin→Chunk-loop→Commit/Abort with progress callback + `AbortSignal` support. Same `storage.kv` cap as the single-envelope path (no new capability surface); same content-addressed destination (`<vault>/data/apps/<appId>/files/<sha256>.<ext>`) so chunked uploads dedupe against single-envelope uploads of the same bytes. **Pure state machine** in `packages/shell/src/workers/storage/upload-session.ts` (~440 lines): per-token write-stream to `<files>/.uploads/<token>` + incremental SHA-256, monotonic seq with idempotent retry of the last seq (identical bytes → no-op; different bytes → Invalid), atomic-rename into the canonical path on commit. **Ceilings**: 2 GiB per token (`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`), 4 concurrent open sessions per app (`MAX_OUTSTANDING_PER_APP`), 5 min idle reaper (`IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) resets on every chunk + tears down the .tmp on fire. **Crash recovery**: `gcOrphans` wipes `<files>/.uploads/` on first `uploadBegin` per app per worker session, so a previous crash can't leak .tmp forever. **Vault rebind / worker reset**: `disposeAll` runs on `setVault` + `_resetStorageWorker` so an in-flight upload across a vault switch can't write into the new vault. **Cross-app token theft**: fail-closed (`uploadToken` resolved against `appId`; the other app sees `Invalid`, never path/state). **expectedHash mismatch**: tmp unlinked, session torn down, `Invalid` returned. The `.uploads/` subdir is unreachable from any renderer since `brainstorm://app-file/...`'s protocol regex requires `<64-hex>.<ext>` (main/index.ts). Rust native addon for the hot path deferred — JS-on-worker for v1; swap if the upload-throughput budget misses. **Tests**: +24 (`upload-session.test.ts` 21 — happy path multi-MB streaming round-trip, expectedHash honoured, dedupe against existing canonical file, unsupported extension, unsafe-appId, no-vault, cross-app token, out-of-order seq, idempotent retry, retry-with-different-bytes, totalBytes overflow + undershoot, zero-bytes commit, expectedHash mismatch deletes tmp, concurrent ceiling per app + isolation across apps, abort deletes tmp, abort silent on unknown / cross-app, gcOrphans on first begin, idle reaper, disposeAllForApp, disposeAll; `upload-chunked.test.ts` 4 integration through the real Broker + ledger — Begin→Chunk→Commit round-trip, cross-app fails closed at worker, chunked + uploadFile dedupe to same URL, CapabilityDenied when storage.kv revoked; `runtime.test.ts` +3 SDK proxy — uploadStreamed drives the protocol with correct caps + seq sequence, calls uploadAbort on chunk rejection, honours AbortSignal). Total 49/49 green on the new + existing storage worker surface; SDK 881/881; integration 160/160. Workspace `tsc` clean, biome clean on touched files. **Unblocks** every consumer of `storage.uploadFile` above the 25 MiB envelope (large video / PDF / image embeds in Notes, Files, etc.) — apps adopt by replacing `storage.uploadFile(name, bytes)` with `storage.uploadStreamed({name, bytes, onProgress?})`. — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).

- ✅ 9.5.2 — BP postMessage transport **landed (2026-05-20)**: the ONE legitimate cross-frame channel; only Block Protocol messages cross the frame, bound to `entityId`, capability-scoped (block runs with zero ambient authority). Standalone primitive in `packages/sdk/src/block-frame/transport.ts` (~325 lines + 697-line test). **Three security gates** on every inbound (honouring 9.5.1's pinned `BLOCK_FRAME_TRANSPORT_REQUIREMENTS_FOR_9_5_2`): identity (`event.source === handle.iframe.contentWindow` — reference compare, rejects sibling-iframe spoofing whose `event.origin` would also be `"null"`), channel-id (per-handle CSPRNG-minted id, rejects replay/guess), phase (`handle.getPhase() === Mounted` — Paused frames don't receive deliveries). **Drop silently** on any gate failure — no per-rejection logging (DoS amplification vector). **Envelope shape**: `{channelId, entityId, direction: BlockFrameMessageDirection (HostToBlock|BlockToHost), kind: BlockFrameMessageKind (Startup|Message), payload}` — direction sender-stamped so receiver rejects opposite-direction (defense vs. block impersonating host's Startup envelope); both discriminators TS string enums per project convention. **Capability passing**: startup envelope (kind=Startup, direction=HostToBlock, payload={capabilities}) flushed once on first Mounted edge — capabilities deep-frozen on entry so caller mutation can't leak. Transport carries the contract; **does NOT enforce** — broker is the gate at 9.4.4. `flushStartup()` exposed so 9.4.4 can wire it from the handle's `onPhase` callback when IO flips to Mounted. **Out-of-phase send: drop, do not queue** — queueing couples lifetime to the host (memory + DoS surface) and contradicts the BP "delivery to a visible block" contract. **Multi-transport-same-handle**: explicitly allowed with channel-id isolation (an inbound from one transport's iframe carrying the OTHER transport's channel id is dropped); rare today (most callers will create exactly one per handle) but forward-compat for entity-multiplexing inside a single iframe. **Close**: removes the window listener, marks transport dead, subsequent `send()` no-op, post-close inbound silent (race-safe via `closed` flag checked before any work). **Integrator fix on top** of builder commit `fb738ae`: parallel reviews (code/security/perf/leak + adversarial pentest pass against a 13-threat transport-specific checklist) cleared 13/13 threats CLOSED + surfaced two should-fixes. **LOW (pentester):** channel-id fallback used `Math.random` when `crypto.randomUUID` was missing — a non-CSPRNG fallback silently weakens the load-bearing inbound-gate defense. Replaced with a two-tier CSPRNG-only chain (`crypto.randomUUID` → `crypto.getRandomValues` with RFC 4122 §4.4 manual UUIDv4 formatting → throw with a fail-loud diagnostic naming the broken invariant). Regression-fenced by two tests (getRandomValues-only path produces well-formed UUIDv4; no-crypto path throws). **CODE-REVIEW should-fix:** multi-transport contract was allowed but undocumented ("today: one per iframe" was misleading); rewrote the `entityId` doc-comment to spell out the channel-id-isolation guarantee. **13-threat pentest checklist** all CLOSED at transport level: sibling-iframe spoof (identity gate), cross-handle replay (per-transport channel-id), startup hijack (direction + kind gate), channel-id guessing (122-bit CSPRNG), DoS flood (silent drop, no rejection state retained), capability mutation (deep-freeze on entry), cross-transport collision (per-transport mint), `event.source` forgery (browser-set WindowProxy, unforgeable from script), targetOrigin="*" leakage (postMessage delivers only to bound contentWindow, NOT broadcast — sandbox prevents top-nav-to-non-opaque), close/inbound race (`closed` flag checked first), phase-flap (per-event synchronous getPhase read, no cache window), re-mount channel-id reuse (channel id bound to transport instance, not handle), capability TOCTOU (transport disclaims enforcement; broker re-checks at request time — design intent, file-doc-pinned). Two open for 9.5.3: real-Chromium spoofing proof (jsdom doesn't enforce sandbox/opaque-origin), payload-size cap at broker boundary. **Tests**: 81/81 block-frame tests pass (45 from 9.5.1 + 36 from 9.5.2 — 34 builder + 2 integrator-fence). Full workspace 4783/4783 green (no flakes this run — confirms the earlier 9.5.1-time reds were parallel-resource contention). Workspace `tsc` clean, biome clean on touched files. Commits `fb738ae` builder + `f4e03ce` integrator. — detail in [log](implementation-log.md). **Hand-off to 9.5.3**: real-Chromium adversarial sweep against the full transport surface (Playwright-level opaque-origin proof, real sibling-iframe spoofing, payload-size cap recommendation, rate-limit consideration); inner-frame helper landing at 9.4.4 consumes the same envelope spec exported here.
- ✅ 9.5.3 — isolation enforcement + adversarial in-jsdom sweep **landed (2026-05-20)**, closes the 9.5 trio. **Six pieces.** **(1) Payload-size cap** in `transport.ts`: configurable `maxPayloadBytes` (default `BLOCK_FRAME_DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 256 KiB`); outbound over-cap drops + counted; inbound over-cap drops + counted; `JSON.stringify(env).length * 2` UTF-16 byte proxy; cyclic / non-serialisable values cap as +Infinity → drop without throwing. **(2) Inbound rate-limit**: `maxInboundPerSecond` (default `BLOCK_FRAME_DEFAULT_MAX_INBOUND_PER_SECOND = 1000`); sliding-window over accepted inbound; charged **only after** security gates pass so a spoofed-identity flood never consumes the budget. **(3) Inner-frame transport helper** in `packages/sdk/src/block-frame/inner-transport.ts` — the block-side mirror, exposed via new subpath `@brainstorm/sdk/block-frame/inner`. `createBlockFrameInnerTransport({expectedChannelId, expectedEntityId, onMessage?, onStartup?, self?, parent?, maxPayloadBytes?})` → `{send, isClosed, hasReceivedStartup, dropCounts, close}`. Same 3-gate INVERTED threat-model mirror: identity (`event.source === window.parent`), channel-id, entity-id, direction (block accepts only HostToBlock), Startup-once-or-discard, kind. No phase gate (block has no visibility signal); no inbound rate-limit (host is trusted in the inner threat model). **(4) `iframe.src`-never-set static CI guard** in `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/iframe-src-check.ts` (TS-AST walker, mirrors 12.2 / 12.9 / 12.11 / 12.12 / 12.13 / 12.14 / SH-30 / SH-31 / SH-32 / 0.11-keyboard pattern — **the structural CI gate inventory now stands at twelve**). Moved kind branch first; Startup envelopes (bounded-by-construction) exempt from the size check; symmetry test with 50-byte cap proves the exemption. **CODE-REVIEW #3** — `dropCounts()` return type was `Readonly<>` but runtime was a mutable shallow spread; wrapped in `Object.freeze({ ... })` in both host and inner; existing leak-prevention test updated to expect TypeError on mutation. **Nit** — `makeEmptyDropCounts` enumerated 12 enum variants by hand in TWO files; replaced with `Object.values(BlockFrameDropReason)` enumeration → exhaustive-by-construction. - ✅ 9.4.5 — SDK `services.bp.dispatch` proxy + host round-trip wiring **landed (2026-05-29)**: closes the last data-path gap in the 9.4 mount-seam arc — the seam mounted the sandboxed frame and flushed Startup, but nothing forwarded a block's BP *request* to the host router, so the block→host→block loop was unwired (Notes mounted `<BpBlockMount>` with no `onMessage`). **(1) Type surface** — `BpMessage` (the app-facing BP 0.3 `Message` wire shape, mirrored in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` so the SDK + apps never pull `@blockprotocol/core`; the shell's `bp/envelope.ts` `BpEnvelope` stays the authoritative parser) + `BpService` (`dispatch(entityId, message) → Promise<BpMessage | null>`) + `bp` added to `AppRuntime.services`. **(2) Runtime proxy** — `bpProxy(bridge)` calls `bp.dispatch` with `args: [{entityId, payload}]` and **`caps: []`**: `bp.dispatch` is structural routing with no ambient authority — the broker allows no-cap methods (`broker-context.ts` checkCapability) and each Graph op is enforced per-type on the entities service downstream, so a block inherits exactly the embedding app's data authority (v1 model, OQ-BP-2). **(3) `<BpBlockMount>` auto-forward** — optional `bp` prop: when set, each inbound block message auto-forwards via `bp.dispatch(entityId, msg)` and the non-null response posts back over the transport (the consumer's `onMessage` still fires first, for observability). The shell re-validates; a malformed/non-dispatchable payload resolves to `null` → nothing sent; bridge errors are swallowed (block degrades to its own rendering, matching the transport's silent-drop contract). `bp` rides a ref like `onMessage` so swapping it never churns the iframe. Every embedding app gets the full round-trip by passing `bp={services.bp}` — no per-app `onMessage` re-wiring. **(4) Notes adoption** — `BlockEmbedView` passes `bp` into its mount; `NotesBrainstorm` gains optional `bp?: BpService` (absent on older shells / preview drop = send-only, which the stub srcdoc already is since it emits no requests yet). **Tests**: +2 runtime proxy (forwards `{entityId, payload}` as a no-cap `bp.dispatch` envelope + unwraps reply; `null` reply passthrough) + 2 mount auto-forward (inbound message → `dispatch` called with `(entityId, request)` + response posted back as a `host-to-block` message envelope; `null` dispatch → nothing posted). 108/108 across SDK runtime + block-mount + shell `bp/` + `bp-graph-pipeline`; `bun run typecheck` clean on packages + apps/notes (pre-existing apps/tasks 9.14.6 WIP errors are unrelated, untouched), biome clean on touched files, apps/notes bundle builds. Design ✅ landed ([data/21-objects-and-collections.md](data/21-objects-and-collections.md), **OQ-DM-1** resolved): no schema/BP/Yjs change; one `type` per object; multi-typing = Collection (=`List/v1`) membership; per-app `kv.json` silos collapse into the shared entities service. **Core data-wiring objective COMPLETE (2026-05-16)** — every first-party app reads/writes real `entities.db`.

Body editor surfacing per app stays in N1–N5 + the per-app workflow rungs.

New `<EditorYjs>` mirrors `<Editor>`'s prop signature and mounts `<BrainstormEditor>` from `@brainstorm/editor` over `useYDoc(noteId)`; `<YDocProvider>` installed at `apps/notes/src/main.tsx` (no-op on shells lacking `runtime.ydoc`). `<BrainstormEditor>` extended (additive only) to accept `additionalNodes` + child plugins so Notes' full plugin tree composes inside the Yjs binding. **Design ambiguity surfaced (load-bearing for N2)**: `@lexical/yjs` 0.21 `createBinding` hardcodes its root as `doc.get('root', XmlText)` — a `Y.XmlText` named `"root"` — while the 9.3.5.B universal-body keystone defines body as `doc.getXmlFragment("body")` — a `Y.XmlFragment` named `"body"`. These coexist in the same doc on the new path (`useUniversalBody(doc)` materialises the body fragment as a change-signal but the editor doesn't write to it; lazy-zero-bytes survives). N1 ships the transport plumbing; reconciling the two names+types (fork `@lexical/yjs` for a custom name, or amend the universal-body contract to `XmlText` named `"root"`) is the architectural call gating N2. **Plugins confirmed parity**: Title / Slash / TurnInto / Tables / Toggle / Embed / Columns / Mention / BlockEmbedPicker / LinkMarkup / Find / Autosave (dual-write — silo persists alongside Yjs in N1; N2 drops it) / BlockGutter / BlockSelection / InlineToolbar / Marquee / Media (drop+inspector) / context-menu / hint / Backlinks / AddPropertyMenu / CheckList / HorizontalRule / MarkdownShortcut / TabIndentation. **Plugins N3-deferred**: `HistoryPlugin` (Yjs UndoManager owns undo/redo under collab); `ListPlugin`/`LinkPlugin` (already mounted by `<BrainstormEditor>` — would double-register); `makeInitialState` / title seeding from `storedTitle` (collab owns bootstrap; a `shouldBootstrap`-compatible initializer command lands at N3). **Flag-off**: byte-identical to today's path — legacy `<Editor>` mount path unchanged. **Tests**: +5 `transport-flag.test.ts` (enum wire-values pinned, both branches, override/reset) + 4 `editor-yjs.test.tsx` (contenteditable mount, two-mount doc-sharing, design-ambiguity pin, bootstrap smoke) — 412/412 notes tests green; 4611/4611 workspace tests green; typecheck workspace + `bunx tsc -p apps/notes` clean. **Build delta**: `apps/notes/package.json` adds `@brainstorm/editor` + `@brainstorm/react-yjs` + `yjs` deps; `apps/notes/src/store/runtime.ts` adds optional `ydoc.resolve` field; `<BrainstormEditor>` additive `additionalNodes` + `children` (existing callers unchanged — `config.nodes` identity preserved when no additional nodes).

Three sub-pieces in one iteration: (1) **Legacy body migration** — every `StoredNote` whose `bodyLegacy` carries a pre-N2 `SerializedEditorState` blob is planted into the universal-body Y.Doc root via a headless `@lexical/yjs` `createBinding` + `syncLexicalUpdateToYjs` inside a single `doc.transact` (one undo step, one update message). (2) **Snippet precompute** — cold-cache rows (`!docEmpty && body === ""`) get `bodyToSnippet(getUniversalBody(doc))` written onto `StoredNote.body`. (3) **Idempotency + reversibility-by-snapshot** — vault-level `notes:migrationVersion = "9.3.5.N4-2026-05-20"` stamp; fast-path is one `storage.get` (the steady-state hot path); `bodyLegacy` retained as the rollback escape-hatch until the v1.0 vault-format freeze in 10.8. Per-note failures isolated (one bad note never takes down the vault). Five outcome classes (`Planted`/`SnippetOnly`/`ClobberAvoided`/`Skipped`/`Failed`) — enum, not string-literal union. **Field narrowing**: `StoredNote.body` narrowed from `string | SerializedEditorState | null` to `string`; pre-N4 `normalize-body.ts` rebuilder retired; codec routes object-shaped on-disk `body` into `bodyLegacy`. New deps: `@lexical/yjs` + `@lexical/headless` (both already pinned `^0.21.0` elsewhere in the workspace; `@lexical/headless` was a devDep, now runtime). **Integrator fix on top**: parallel review pass surfaced a real BLOCKER + three should-fixes. The BLOCKER (perf-review R2, confirmed by leak review item 4) — the renderer-side resolver's `load()` is async, so `resolve()` returns an empty Y.Doc that hydrates via `Y.applyUpdate(REMOTE_ORIGIN)` asynchronously. The migration's `docEmpty` check read `body.length` immediately after `resolve()`, so on a real vault with canonical content in flight it would have classified the doc as empty and PLANTED legacy content on top — silently mixing legacy + canonical inside one Y.Doc. Fix: thread `whenLoaded(id): Promise<void>` through the migration options + await before reading; preload's `runtime.ydoc` shape extended with the field (optional — older shells / preview drops still work). Regression-fenced by a test that models the production race: a fake resolver whose `whenLoaded` applies a snapshot only when awaited. Should-fixes (1) codec silent data-loss when both `body` (legacy-shaped) and `bodyLegacy` are present (rollback target wins; now `console.warn`s the conflict for observability), (2) test pinning that `repo.save` is NOT called on the throw path through `plantSerializedStateIntoDoc`, (3) `MIGRATION_VERSION_KEY` doc comment clarified (per-app KV + advisory perf, not a security gate). **Tests**: 449/449 notes tests green (428 → +21: 16 builder + 3 BLOCKER-fence/throw-path-fence/no-`whenLoaded`-fallback + 2 codec conflict tests). 4689/4689 workspace tests green (the one Errors=1 from full-suite is the same pre-existing apps/preview teardown flake — passes 178/178 in isolation). ## Sync, multi-device & E2E encryption *(Stage 10)*

Goal: realise [16](security/16-identity-orgs-encryption.md) + [06 §Sync](editing/06-collaboration-yjs.md) for the single-user/multi-device subset. **Blocking OQs: OQ-10/26/27/28/29; OQ-18 confirm before 10.1.**

- ✅ 10.0 — **de-risk spike (pulled early, landed 2026-05-20)**: throwaway two-instance prototype in `experiments/sync-spike-10.0/` proved per-entity-DEK + Ed25519-signed XChaCha20-Poly1305 Yjs update envelopes over a blind in-process relay that sees **ciphertext only** (the relay module imports nothing from `@noble/*` and holds no key — structural, asserted at the end of every run). Two Node clients pair via signed `add-device` records, exchange a `kind=wrap` envelope (X25519 ECDH + HKDF + AEAD), then converge concurrent edits to a CRDT-merged title; the relay's view is `(routing header, signature, opaque ciphertext)` only. **OQ-10/26/27/28/29 positioned in [11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md)** (QR-primary + SAS-code fallback; rotation envelope decoupled from access change; org relay enforces only org spaces; access record append-only in `root.meta.access`). Forces 10.2 to swap static-static ECDH wrap for **HPKE (RFC 9180)** — same envelope shape, audited algorithm; 10.4 adds a CI rule "production relay module must not import `@noble/*`" to lock the blind-relay invariant forward. Proposes two non-blocking 10.x followups: wrap+snapshot bundling on fresh-device bootstrap (10.10), routing-token rotation (10.11). — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).
- ✅ 10.1 — per-entity DEK on create **landed (2026-05-22)**: every entity created through the `entities` IPC service mints a fresh 32-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 DEK and seals it under the vault master key in a new `entity_deks` table (v2 migration on `entities.db`; `entities.dek_id` FK forward-allocated since Stage 3). AAD is **domain-separated**: `brainstorm/entity-dek/v1: || entityId` (so a future block/attachment DEK can't cross-confuse; the prefix is load-bearing — bare entity-id AAD fails by test). Lifecycle: forward-allocate `dekId` → `repo.create(... dekId)` + `dekStore.persist(entityId, dekId)` **in one SQLite transaction** (a throw from persist rolls back the entity row, no orphans) → `compose(row)` returns → `dekStore.close(dek)` zeros the plaintext in `finally`. **Plaintext DEK never crosses IPC** — `compose()` doesn't surface `dek_id`; test pins the IPC response contains neither the DEK bytes nor the dekId. The DEK store also zeros the freshly-minted DEK if `sealSecret` or the wrap-INSERT throws mid-call (defense). `hardDelete()` adds an explicit `DELETE FROM entity_deks` alongside its links/change_log cleanup (pragma-independent). `VaultSession.entityDekStore()` uses the same in-flight-promise idiom as `propertiesStore`/`dashboardStore` so concurrent first-callers don't double-construct repos. Shell-internal singletons (root folder, kv-backfill, shortcut bindings, dev seeder) pass `dekId: null` at create; the **10.x retro-wrap pass ✅ landed 2026-05-22** drains those rows on vault open so the Stage 10.3 sync wire path can't silently skip unencrypted rows. Forward contract for 10.3 pinned by test: the wire path MUST recompute AAD from the resolved row's `entity_id` (never the caller-supplied id) so an `entities.dek_id` repoint can't re-introduce the DEK-swap vector. **Tests:** +51 (5278→5284 workspace green; 11 EntityDekStore covering shape / round-trip / AAD-binding / master-key-swap / domain-separator pin / forward-pin / empty-id rejection / zero-on-throw / 2 property tests with N=64 + N=32; 7 EntityDeksRepository covering CRUD + FK cascade + tie-break + delete-by-entity-id; 4 schema v1→v2 migration; service tests covering atomicity rollback + hardDelete cascade + IPC-leak fence). Workspace `tsc:packages` + `tsc:apps` clean. **Spike-forced clauses honoured**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 256-bit DEK (`@noble/ciphers/chacha.js`); persisted at-rest under the vault master key (2.x machinery); never crosses IPC; lifetime = open-entity-session; zeroed on close. Builder commit `4038029` + integrator pass `115a6b0` (atomicity, AAD prefix, defense-in-depth zeroize, in-flight-promise, hardDelete cascade, dropped dead `create()` method, ES-private master-key fields). — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).
- ✅ 10.x — retro-wrap pass for legacy null-DEK rows **landed (2026-05-22)**: new `main/entities/retro-wrap-deks.ts` drains every live entity with `dek_id IS NULL` on vault open, in one SQLite transaction per row — `repo.stampDekId(id, dekId)` (UPDATE guarded by `dek_id IS NULL` so a concurrent writer can't be clobbered, returns false on race) → `dekStore.persist(entityId, dekId)` (mints DEK, seals under master key with the same `brainstorm/entity-dek/v1:` AAD prefix as 10.1, writes `entity_deks` row) → zero the live DEK immediately (the wire path re-`open()`s from the wrap row on demand). **Idempotent by construction** — the next pass sees zero null-dek rows, no marker / generation counter needed; the schema is the marker. **Per-row isolation** — any throw inside one row's transaction unwinds the entity stamp + the wrap-row INSERT together, logs `[retro-wrap] entity <id> failed: <reason>` and counts the row as `skipped`; a corrupt row never blocks the rest of the pass. **Concurrent-stamp race** counted as neither wrapped nor skipped via an internal `RetroWrapStampSkipped` sentinel (the entities.create IPC path winning between `listMissingDekIds()` and the per-row UPDATE). Wired into `onVaultOpened` AFTER `ensureRootFolder` / `runKvBackfill` / `loadShortcutBindings` (each currently creates `dekId: null` singletons) so each open's catch is total. Two new `EntitiesRepository` methods: `listMissingDekIds(): string[]` (read-only, `WHERE dek_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at, id`) + `stampDekId(id, dekId): boolean` (UPDATE guarded by `dek_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL`). Boot log surfaces the one-time line `[brainstorm] retro-wrap null-DEK pass: wrapped N entities (M skipped due to errors)` when non-zero; silent on a steady-state vault. **Precondition for Stage 10.3 sync wire path** — a null-dek row at the wire path is ambiguous (silent skip vs. plaintext leak); the de-risk review picked the only safe answer (every live entity must carry a DEK before 10.3). **Tests:** +17 (5311→5328 workspace green; 8 EntitiesRepository covering listMissingDekIds empty/some/excludes-soft-deleted/deterministic-order + stampDekId set/idempotent/missing-row/refuses-soft-deleted; 9 retroWrapNullDeks covering empty/wraps-only-null/idempotent-second-pass/excludes-soft-deleted/joint-integrity/real-encryption-round-trip/per-row-failure-isolation/concurrent-stamp-race/non-fatal-list-failure). Workspace `tsc:packages` + `tsc:apps` clean; `bun run verify` 209/209; biome clean on touched files (1 formatting fix in `entities-repo.ts` applied alongside the new methods). — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).
- ✅ 10.2 — member-wraps schema in the entity Yjs doc **landed (2026-05-23)**: ships the wrap *schema* + crypto primitives the wire path (10.3) consumes. Three new modules in `packages/shell/src/main/credentials/`: (1) `device-x25519.ts` — separate X25519 keypair for HPKE wraps (orthogonal to the Ed25519 identity; signing vs encryption stays separated), persisted at vault create + lazy-minted on open for pre-10.2 vaults (idempotent — persisted under `device-x25519` keystore account); (2) `hpke.ts` — RFC 9180 base mode (single-shot `sealBase`/`openBase`) on noble primitives, suite **DHKEM(X25519,HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305** (kem_id=0x0020, kdf_id=0x0001, aead_id=0x0003) — the HPKE swap the 10.0 spike forced from static-static ECDH, pinned by the RFC 9180 A.2.1 sequence-0 test vector (full key-schedule output enc + ct matches byte-for-byte); (3) `member-wraps.ts` — the on-doc schema: `MemberWrapPayload = {v, alg, recipientPubB64, encB64, ctB64}` stored as plain JSON inside `doc.getMap("brainstorm.meta").get("wraps")` Y.Array (idempotent get-or-create, namespaced top-level key avoids collision with app types like Lexical's `root`), domain-separated AAD `brainstorm/entity-wrap/v1:` || entityId mirroring the 10.1 entity-dek pattern (a wrap minted for entity X can't be replayed against entity Y), HPKE `info=brainstorm/entity-wrap/v1` pins the binding name + version (future block/attachment DEK wraps under the same suite can't cross-confuse). VaultSession exposes `deviceX25519.{publicKey,publicKeyBase64}` for the wrap-creation path and the secret-encapsulating `unwrapMemberWrap(wrap, entityId)` for the read path; X25519 secret zeroed on dispose alongside masterKey + identitySecret. **Forward-compat:** `listWraps` skips entries that fail `isMemberWrapPayload` so a future schema bump can land on an older client without crashing the codec; the schema version is bumped only on a wire-incompatible change. **Ladder boundary:** like 10.1, this iteration ships the primitive (mints the secret, defines the codec) but **does not yet wire entity-create or the retro-wrap pass to write wraps into Y.Docs** — that pairs with 10.3's encrypted-envelope wire path since both touch the Y.Doc lifecycle (loading the entity doc, applying one update, persisting the snapshot).
