## Peer-to-peer sync *(`P2P-*` design spike; the concrete LAN slice shipped early as `LAN-*` — see below)*

Relay-optional **direct device-to-device sync**: two devices on the same LAN (or reachable over a direct / NAT-traversed channel) exchange the same DEK-sealed Yjs updates the relay carries today, with **no plaintext ever leaving the device** — the relay stays a fallback / bootstrap path, not a requirement. The transport is already treated as "relay **or** P2P" in [data/20-database-growth-and-sync.md](data/20-database-growth-and-sync.md) (incl. the fresh-device bootstrap rule: a peer *or* a relay must be online); this track makes that real. Sits **at the infra + collaborative-sync line** in the [release roadmap](#release-trains--the-forward-queue-2-heroes-each) — the `P2P-0` spike must report before any `0.12.0`+ multi-user hero is committed. Owner call 2026-07-21: add the track, **scope design-only first** (the `10.0` analogue for sync).

> **✅ `P2P-0` REPORTED 2026-07-31** ([platform/79-p2p-sync.md](platform/79-p2p-sync.md)). Headline: **`P2P-1` is startable and nothing gates it**, and most of it is already built, because the `LAN-*` ladder shipped the transport, the listener, the channel-bound admission handshake and the backfill path while `P2P-0` was still unstarted. What remains is the dial flow (nothing writes `syncRelay.lan = true` today), discovery, and two liveness gaps the prototype measured rather than assumed (a 75 s dial to a sleeping peer, and a frozen peer the transport never notices). `LAN-2b(d)` is **not** a prerequisite; the reasoning is in [79 §10](platform/79-p2p-sync.md). `P2P-3` is re-scoped and full ICE/STUN/TURN is explicitly not planned.

- ✅ `P2P-0`: portability / design spike *(2026-07-31, harness `docs/p2p-0-spike`; design [platform/79-p2p-sync.md](platform/79-p2p-sync.md); no product code, by design)*: answered on paper plus a throwaway prototype (`scratch/p2p-0-prototype/`, five Node scripts, measurements in §2 of the doc). **Verdict: `P2P-1` is startable, nothing gates it**; `LAN-2b(d)` is open but is **not** a prerequisite (LAN admission already rebuilds the roster from `listActive()` per access, so a revoked device is refused in both directions before any routing metadata moves; the open half is rotate-on-revoke on the *relay* path, which `P2P-1` neither creates nor closes). **Decisions:** *discovery* = pairing address → mDNS `_brainstorm-sync._tcp` (`bonjour-service`, pure JS) → manual, signaling server rejected for LAN; *transport* = reuse `WebSocketRelayPort` verbatim (already settled by shipped code: `ActiveRelayKind.Lan` and `.WebSocket` are the same class), QUIC/WebRTC rejected; *NAT traversal* = not needed for `P2P-1`/`P2P-2`, `P2P-3` re-scoped (see below); *trust* = the shipped channel-bound HPKE handshake verbatim, only the transport changes; *relay* = supplement not replace, exclusive selection with LAN preferred, relay blindness unchanged. **Three findings the prototype produced, all now `P2P-1` work items:** (i) automatic dialing of a *discovered* address discloses the device Ed25519 pubkey in cleartext to whatever advertises, because `hello` is the client's first message: needs a rotating identity tag in the mDNS TXT *before* the dial; (ii) a dial to a sleeping peer costs **75,010 ms** on the OS default and 3,003 ms with an app deadline, and `WebSocketRelayPort` has no connect deadline; (iii) a frozen peer is **never** noticed by the transport (no keepalive anywhere in the sync tree), while a 5 s heartbeat deadline notices in 5,047 ms. Also found by reading the code: `LAN-3`'s *producing* half was never wired (the listener URL never reaches the pairing payload) and **nothing writes `syncRelay.lan = true`**, so the LAN dial flow does not exist. **OQs:** OQ-P2P-1 ✅ / OQ-P2P-2 ✅ positions taken; OQ-P2P-3/4/5/6 filed open.
- ⚪ `P2P-1`: **LAN peer discovery + the dial flow**; **own-device-only** (single identity, multi-device) *(0.12.0 hero)*. gate: `P2P-0` ✅. Executable brief ([79 §9](platform/79-p2p-sync.md)), six items in dependency order: **(1)** finish `LAN-3`'s producing half (route `LanHostController.onUrlChanged` into the pairing payload; the accepting half already shipped); **(2)** build the LAN dial flow that writes `syncRelay.lan = true` + the Settings affordance for `LanHostMode` (`DEFAULT_LAN_HOST_MODE` is `Off`): this is the item that turns the shipped machinery into a feature; **(3)** add a **3 s connect deadline** and a **heartbeat with a degraded state** (~5 s answer deadline, degrade rather than close: a frozen socket was still usable after wake), prerequisites for (4) being usable; **(4)** mDNS advertise + browse via `bonjour-service`, records treated as **address hints with no liveness meaning** (measured: no `down` event in 20 s after an abrupt kill; rediscovery on a new port in 970 ms under a *new* instance name, so stale records accumulate) and multiple addresses per instance handled; **(5)** the rotating discovery tag gating the dial (security requirement of automatic discovery, same change as (4)); **(6)** fix interface selection (`addresses()[0]` is arbitrary with Docker/VPN/multi-adapter and fails silently) and take a written IPv6 position. **Must NOT** build a host-side durable tail (that is `LAN-9`, gated behind `LAN-2b`) or weaken admission for discovery's convenience. `<gates: packaging, security-review, pentest>`: the `bonjour-service` dep triggers an `electron-builder --dir` dry-run, and (4)+(5) are new attack surface on the first inbound socket (pentest the discover→dial path).
>
> 🟡 **In review — shell [#377](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/377) (`feat/p2p-1-lan-dial`), harness [#174](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/harness/pull/174).** All six brief items are built. **Two of the three declared gates have a latest passing run** (2026-07-31, `docs/_review/evaluations.jsonl`): `security-review` and `pentest` each ran once **red** and then green after the findings were fixed on the branch (shell `158accc1`). Five findings, all fixed: the advert **instance name was outside the MAC** (replayable verbatim under any attacker-chosen name, which is the candidate table's de-dup key, the freshness key for selection, and text rendered in Settings); the **candidate + cooldown tables were unbounded** with expiry only ever evaluated lazily at read; the advert **leaked `os.hostname()` and every interface address including global-scope IPv6** via `bonjour-service` defaults, defeating the rotation the per-boot instance name and 5-minute epoch exist to provide; the browse callback **fell back to a captured secret after vault close**; and discovery **accepted loopback** in an advert address list. 39 adversarial probes kept as `packages/shell/src/main/sync/lan-discovery-attacks.test.ts`.
>
> **NOT ✅ yet, and deliberately.** Three things are still owed: **(a)** the `packaging` gate has **no run** — the `bonjour-service` dependency still needs its `electron-builder --dir` dry-run; **(b)** the two-device dogfood spec `tests/dogfood/collab/012-lan-two-devices.spec.ts` is **RED** for a harness reason, not a product one (`startCollabTeam` gives each persona its own vault, so `meta.devices` never converges and LAN admission correctly refuses — closing it needs a two-**device** primitive in `collab-team.ts`); **(c)** the pentest's real-network half is **unrun** (on-wire rogue advertiser, real-socket half-open / slow-loris against the listener) and is recorded as unrun rather than claimed. Two accepted risks recorded rather than fixed, both belonging to `P2P-2`'s transport-selection scope: an on-path LAN attacker can always deny the link and so force the relay fallback (the surface is honest about it, but there is no LAN-only-never-relay mode), and the relay is still contacted in the boot window before discovery converges.
- ⚪ `P2P-2`: live update exchange on the peer channel with relay fallback + reconciliation on reconnect. gate: `P2P-1`. Mostly **already shipped** as `LAN-6`/`LAN-7`/`LAN-8` (live co-edit converge, the blind `resync{key,sinceSv}` nudge, state-vector diff backfill); what remains is the **transport-selection** half: prefer LAN when a peer is discovered and admitted, fall back to the relay on the (3) deadline, and never run both at once: dual transport is rejected because it silently falsifies the `LAN-5` "no server" status claim. There is **no snapshot-authority conflict** to resolve (OQ-P2P-2): the durable node is a store, not an arbiter, and reconnecting to the relay is the same state-vector operation as reconnecting to a peer. The residue is a *staleness gap* (two devices co-editing on LAN, neither reaching the relay, leaves a cold third device restoring an old state) which is already the documented fresh-device bootstrap position and should be **surfaced** rather than hidden. **Boundary:** reconciliation stays relay-side; a host-side sealed tail is `LAN-9` and inherits its gate.
- ⚪ `P2P-3`: **re-scoped by `P2P-0`** from "NAT traversal" to **direct connectivity wherever the network already allows it**: two machines behind the same NAT reaching each other by private address, an opportunistic UPnP-IGD / NAT-PMP mapping, and a manual port forward. All three reuse the shipped transport unchanged. **Full ICE/STUN/TURN is explicitly not planned** (OQ-P2P-4): NAT traversal needs a rendezvous server anyway, so it does not deliver "no server", and the relay is *already blind*, so it does not deliver privacy either: the payoff is latency and relay-independence, not confidentiality, and that does not justify a permanently-maintained subsystem. If it is ever built, **the blind relay is the signaling channel** (authenticated, always reachable, content-blind: no new server, no new trust relationship) and WebRTC arrives as a second `RelayPort` behind the existing `active-relay.ts` seam. gate: `P2P-2`
- ⚪ `P2P-4`: multi-user P2P (shared entities across identities): only after `Collab-C5`/`C6` land. gate: `P2P-2` + collaborative-sync layer. **`P2P-0` deliberately designed this OUT rather than half-in:** every `P2P-1` mechanism depends on one identity across several devices (the roster is that identity's device list; the discovery tag is derived from that identity's own key), and two different users share neither. So cross-identity admission and cross-identity discovery privacy are **net-new** here, not extensions: any proposal that requires a peer to admit a *different* identity is out of `P2P-1`/`P2P-2` scope by construction. See OQ-P2P-5 for the discovery half.

### LAN P2P sync *(the track-C wedge — `LAN-*`, design [data/lan-p2p-sync.md](data/lan-p2p-sync.md))*

**Filed 2026-07-24 as a plan divergence:** this shipped in shell #264 with its own rung ids and the plan couldn't see it. It is the CONCRETE first slice of `P2P-1`/`P2P-2` (two paired devices on one LAN sync live with **no cloud relay**), taken early as the wedge rather than waiting on the `P2P-0` spike — so `P2P-1`/`P2P-2` now mean "the general transport beyond this LAN slice". Additive by construction: the sealed CRDT + awareness + pairing pipeline is unchanged; only a transport is added, behind the existing `RelayPort`.

- ✅ LAN-1 — **embedded blind relay host** *(shell #264, 2026-07-24 — localhost / in-process proof)*: `main/sync/lan-relay-host.ts` wraps `@brainstorm-os/relay-server`'s `createRelayCore` (the same blind `FrameRouter` fan-out that backs the cloud relay, reused verbatim — RELAY-BLIND CI-fence verified, 0 violations) and adds a per-connection admission gate. Exposes only an in-process `webSocketCtor()`, so the **unchanged** `WebSocketRelayPort` connects to it. **OQ-LAN-1 → Option A.**
- ✅ LAN-2 — **admission gate** *(shell #264)*: SYNC-4b inverted into mutual peer auth — the client signs the host's nonce with its device key (`makeLanChallengeResponder`), the host verifies against the **signed device roster** (`makeLanAdmissionVerifier`). `electLanRole` locks **OQ-LAN-2** (the lower device id hosts — symmetric, negotiation-free, no round-trip). No new crypto primitive.
- ✅ LAN-6 — **tests, green with no cloud relay** *(shell #264)*: election · open-host fan-out (cloud parity) · admit a roster member · reject a non-member · reject a forged signature; plus two `LiveSyncEngine`s over the localhost host proving **live co-edit converge AND backfill** of a peer's offline edits on reconnect (**OQ-LAN-5 → live + backfill in scope**).
- ✅ LAN-3 — discovery bootstrap *(shell #313 accepting half; #377 producing half, `P2P-1`)*: the pairing payload's `relayUrl` slot carries the host's `ws://<lan-ip>:<port>`, behind a scheme **allow-list** (`ws`/`wss` + a host) — the URL is dialed unattended after a QR scan, so it must never be steerable elsewhere (gate pentest #6). ⚠️ **Corrected 2026-07-31:** #313 shipped only the **accepting** half. `LanRelayListener` had always minted exactly the URL the payload wants and `pairing-payload.ts` had always validated it, but nothing connected the two — `LanHostController.onUrlChanged`'s single production consumer was a `console.info`, and the payload took its address from `vault.json`. #377 wired it, and made the target adopt the address as a dial candidate after a successful join. mDNS landed in `P2P-1`; **OQ-LAN-4** closed by [79 §3](platform/79-p2p-sync.md).
- ✅ LAN-4a — **transport selection + status plumbing** *(shell #316, 2026-07-26)*: `ActiveRelayKind.Lan` + `isLanRelayUrl` (loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / IPv6 ULA are LAN, everything else is a relay — deliberately conservative, since claiming "no server" falsely is a privacy lie, not a cosmetic bug). LAN reuses `WebSocketRelayPort` verbatim; only the address and the admission handshake differ. ⚠️ **Corrected 2026-07-31:** `ActiveRelayKind.Lan` was **unreachable in a shipped build** until `P2P-1` (shell #377). Its sole selector is the explicit `syncRelay.lan` flag, and `setSyncRelayConfig`'s only non-test caller never set it — so the whole LAN client half existed and nothing could ever engage it. Fixed three call sites gated on `kind === WebSocket` that would have misread LAN as "no transport" — including `isGatedRelay`, where reporting the *strictest* transport as ungated was the worst of the three.
- ✅ LAN-4b — **the real external bind** *(shell #317 + #323, 2026-07-26/27)* `<gates: packaging, pentest>`: `lan-relay-listener.ts` (G12-named, so the relay-blind fence covers it) binds a real socket via a new `ws` runtime dep — `@brainstorm-os/relay-server` serves through `Bun.serve`, which does not exist in Electron's Node main process. Both gates the dep triggered were run and are in the [ledger](_review/evaluations.jsonl): an electron-builder `--dir` dry-run confirming `ws` is collected *inside* `app.asar` (a directory search reports a false negative), and a `/pentester` pass against the **bound** socket. The pentest **failed first** with three blocking findings — an unauthenticated remote uncaught exception in the main process, a bind failure escaping as uncaught, and a wildcard guard that was a string blocklist bypassable by `0`/`::0`/`0x0` — then passed on re-run. #323 closed the six GA-blocking residue items (accept-layer per-source accounting, refuse-before-101, outbound backpressure, concurrent-start orphan, Origin rejection, 426 fingerprint).
- ✅ LAN-5 — **status UX** *(shell #316; completed #377, `P2P-1`)*: the sync snapshot carries `transportKind`, so the surface can say "syncing on your local network (no server)" instead of showing a peer link as a relay. Real, not cosmetic: on LAN no third party — not even a blind one — sees the traffic. ⚠️ **Corrected 2026-07-31:** main put the field on the wire but the renderer's protocol type never declared it, so it had **zero consumers** and the surface it exists for did not exist. #377 declared it and built the surface. The same correction applies to the LAN host toggle, which #316-era code rendered only inside `SyncSection`'s "status unavailable" early return — on the normal path it was invisible.
- ✅ LAN-7 — **backfill trigger** *(shell #314)*: LAN-6 proved a reconnecting peer *can* backfill, but only when a test drove it by hand. The host now nudges the **existing** subscribers of a routing key when a new peer joins it (`resync{key}`, routing metadata only — the host stays blind); the joiner is excluded, since it has nothing to offer. The port surfaces it as `onResync`, which the wiring turns into the engine's snapshot emit.
- ✅ LAN-8 — **backfill efficiency: send the gap, not the document** *(shell #324, 2026-07-27)*: `subscribe` carries the subscriber's Yjs **state vector**, so the host's resync notification hands `sinceSv` to the peer and the reply is `encodeStateAsUpdate(doc, sv)` — the missing delta rather than the whole document. The ydoc worker's `snapshot` verb takes `sinceStateVectorB64` and a new `stateVector` verb exposes the vector itself. The host stays blind: a state vector is opaque routing metadata, never document content.
- ⚪ LAN-9 — host-side durable tail for the both-peers-absent gap — **also behind the security gate** (`OQ-LAN-5`'s remaining sub-question: present-peer reconciliation for v1, host tail as a fast-follow).
- ⚪ **LAN-2b — close the security gate (NEW 2026-07-26, gates LAN-4/LAN-9).** The gate found the load-bearing mitigations were *specified and not built*, and that the admission principal is the wrong key. Eight blocking items, in dependency order: **(a)** bind admission to an X25519 key agreement and **(b)** implement the client-side host verification — without them a relay attack admits an attacker *as the victim* with no key material. ⚠️ **Revised 2026-07-26:** the design's prescribed "mutual challenge" does NOT work (a signature proves key possession, not that the key is on the other end of *this* connection, so a relay defeats it); the fix is a channel-bound HPKE handshake against the roster's `deviceX25519Pub` — spec: [`data/lan-channel-binding.md`](data/lan-channel-binding.md); **(c)** make the principal the per-device key (decision note: [`data/lan-admission-principal.md`](data/lan-admission-principal.md) — Option A for LAN) (today `account` is the sovereign user key, identical on every device, while the roster keys on `deviceEd25519Pub` — so devices are indistinguishable and revocation is structurally impossible); **(d)** enforce revocation — and note the substantive fix is to route `revokeDevice` into the existing **ROT-3a rotate-on-revoke** machinery (a revoked device already holds its DEKs, so flags can't claw back read access), with `isDeviceRevoked` required + wired as defense-in-depth; ⚠️ fix the ROT-3a receive path first per [[rotate-on-revoke-needs-receive-path-test]]; ✅ **(c)** per-device principal (shell #310) · ✅ **(e)** hold client output until `auth-ok` (#311) · ✅ **(f)** drop `rotate` on the LAN host (#311) · ✅ **(g)** canonicalize key encodings at the LAN boundary (#310) · ✅ **(h)** admission limits — auth deadline, connection cap, payload cap, one admit attempt (#311; per-source rate limit still owed, it needs the real socket). ✅ **(a)+(b)** channel-bound HPKE handshake + client-side host verification (shell #313 — the client seals a nonce to the peer's roster `deviceX25519Pub`, AAD binds both accounts, direction tags stop reflection). **Remaining: (d) revocation only** — and it is an owner decision, not a coding task: the substantive fix routes `revokeDevice` into ROT-3a rotate-on-revoke, which re-keys real user data.

> **✅ The security gate RAN 2026-07-26** — findings in [`_review/2026-07-26-lan-p2p-security-gate.md`](_review/2026-07-26-lan-p2p-security-gate.md); LAN-4 stays blocked behind `LAN-2b`. Two findings were **live in shipped code**, not LAN-gated: the admission challenge was a **signing oracle for the sovereign user key** (forged add-device roster records — fixed, shell #309) and **device revocation is enforced nowhere in production** (`isDeviceRevoked` is optional and has zero non-test producers — the revoke button is cosmetic today). Original gate text follows.
>
> **⚠️ Security gate (blocking, from the build pass itself):** LAN-1/2/6 landed as the **localhost / in-process proof only**. The real external-socket bind was **deliberately withheld** — opening a network-reachable listening socket (LAN-4's bind, LAN-9's tail) is the shell's **first inbound socket** and MUST pass a dedicated `/security-review` + `/pentester` over the whole connect → challenge → verify-roster → admit → subscribe → route path before it ships. **OQ-LAN-3** (transport TLS / PSK) is revisited by that review.

## Product polish & dogfood hardening *(standing quality track, `POLISH-*`; owner-driven)*

The owner bar is a **polished product**, and as of 2026-07-21 it is **not met**: dogfooding surfaces editor blocks that render wrong, entity properties that display / edit poorly, visual-design quality gaps, and elements positioned or laid out badly — collectively *"this does not look like a polished product yet."* This track makes that a **first-class, tracked** commitment rather than background friction-log churn: **every release train drains a `POLISH-*` batch** ([§ Release trains](#release-trains--the-forward-queue-2-heroes-each)), and each owner dogfood session that finds a functional or visual defect files a rung here. Owner directive 2026-07-21.

**How it runs.** Owner dogfoods a real vault → each defect becomes a `POLISH-*` rung tagged with its category → the rung is fixed in place (reproduce → fix → verify in the running shell, per the workflow standards) → it ships in the current train's polish batch. Routine one-off nits still land in [dogfood/friction-log.md](dogfood/friction-log.md); a defect is promoted to a `POLISH-*` rung when it's a **quality-bar** miss (not a one-off), and the friction-log **status line stays authoritative**.

**Categories** (each defect files under exactly one):

- `POLISH-ED-*` — **editor blocks**: block rendering, block-menu, embeds / transclusion, list / checklist / callout / code fidelity, caret + selection behaviour.
- `POLISH-PROP-*` — **entity properties**: property-cell rendering + inline edit, inspector layout, rollups / formulas / relations display, empty / loading states.
- `POLISH-DSN-*` — **visual-design quality**: spacing / rhythm, typography, colour + token correctness across light **and** dark, control faces, iconography.
- `POLISH-LAY-*` — **element location & layout**: alignment, panel / header baselines, overflow / clipping, responsive reflow, off-surface / teleport bugs.
- `POLISH-FN-*` — **functional**: a control that doesn't do what its label says, stale/incorrect derived state, an affordance that silently no-ops. Added 2026-07-29 (the `VID-build-apps` dry-run surfaced two defects that are neither visual nor layout — a "New chat" button that doesn't start a new chat, and a rename that leaves the file's language wrong).

- ⚪ `POLISH-1` — first owner-driven dogfood sweep (open): owner walks the fleet and files rungs per category above; the batch ships in the next train (`0.8.0`). Individual rungs get ids as filed (`POLISH-ED-1`, `POLISH-PROP-1`, …). This is a **standing, never-"done"** track until the GA polish bar is met. *Note 2026-07-28: the **0.11.0 batch was drained by an agent sweep** (owner-approved stand-in; an owner-driven sweep still supersedes this) — all-apps smoke over the Northbound vault (`tests/dogfood/.sessions/012-all-apps-smoke/`, 20/20 apps, 0 console/page errors), rungs below. One suspected defect was disproved by DOM probe: the "left-clipped" Calendar month pills (`04-app-calendar.png`) are mangled *vault data* — seeded entries literally titled "ipeline ready" / "peline ready" from old dogfood typing sessions — not a render bug (probe: `913p-polish-cal-chip-probe`).*

Root cause is a **units-vs-cells mismatch**: the renderer's icon grid stores positions in grid *units* (the seeded fleet reads `Notes@0,0 Files@11,0 Database@22,0 … Books@0,14`, i.e. one icon every 11 units across and 14 down, written by `icons-layer.tsx`'s `repackIcons`), but `placeDashboardIcon` (`main/dev/seed-demo-apps.ts`) scans for a free **cell** with a hard-coded `GRID_COLS = 12` and treats `x`/`y` as cell indices — so `1,0` looks free. Fix needs the icon footprint constants shared across the main/renderer boundary (not a one-liner), which is why it is filed rather than patched. This is the episode's payoff shot, so it is the hardest blocker of the five. **Fixed in shell #369** (2026-07-29): `shared/dashboard-icon-grid.ts` now owns the footprint constants, the overlap test and the first-free-slot scan, and every install/pin path (marketplace, sideload, vault-source, dev seeder, entity pin, Bin pin) computes its cell there. **Re-capture 2026-07-30 confirms the collision is gone** — Client Pulse landed at `220,0`, clear of every seeded tile, no overprint anywhere on camera. The fix did, however, expose `POLISH-LAY-9` (the shared scan has no *column* bound), so the payoff shot is still not filmable — see below.

- ✅ `POLISH-LAY-8` — **`brainstorm://app-icon/<id>` 404s for a sideloaded app whose manifest declares no `icon`** — four console errors per run (`…/studio.northbound.client-pulse`, `…?v=1.0.0`, and the same pair for `io.brainstorm.hello`). The initials chip renders fine, so this is invisible to the user but it is the *only* thing keeping the dry-run off a zero-console-error verdict. Same family as `POLISH-LAY-3`: request a fallback instead of a known-missing resource. **Fixed in shell #369**: the handler distinguishes "installed, declares no icon" (204 — the caller draws initials) from "resolves to nothing installed" (404), with the rules extracted to a testable `main/apps/app-icon-resolver.ts`; the request side converges on the shared `resolveAppIconSrc`, which answers `null` for a known icon-less app. **Confirmed on camera 2026-07-30 — the re-capture logs `0 console/page errors`** (was 4), so the zero-error bar is now met.
- ✅ `POLISH-FN-1` — **Agent's "New chat" does not start a new chat** when the vault already has conversations. `newChat` sets `activeId = null` (`apps/agent/src/app.tsx:1032`), and the very next effect — *"Default the selection to the most recent conversation once one exists"* (`:699`) — re-selects `conversations[0]` on any `activeId === null`, so the header title stays on the previous thread and the next turn's messages **append to it**. Captured: after three New-chat clicks the header still read "Coffee-line name ideas", and the agent's two staged code-file cards landed in that conversation. The effect wants to be mount-scoped, but it also legitimately covers the delete-the-active-conversation case, so the fix needs a deliberate "the user asked for a blank thread" signal — filed, not patched. **Fixed in shell #368**: two distinct states were collapsed onto one `null`; the selection is now a discriminated `ChatSelection` (`Unresolved` | `New` | `Conversation`), the defaulting effect fires only from `Unresolved`, and a conversation is still minted lazily on the first message (so New chat persists nothing). **Confirmed on camera 2026-07-30** — the agent act runs in its own fresh thread ("Build me a small hello app I can…" selected in the sidebar, distinct from the four seeded conversations), and both staged code-file cards land there.
- ✅ `POLISH-FN-2` — **the Code editor keeps `language: "typescript"` after a rename changes the extension.** `createNewFile` mints `untitled.ts`, the inline rename writes only `{ path }` (`entities.update(row.id, { path })`), so `client-pulse/manifest.json` and `client-pulse/index.html` both stay TypeScript: the header chip reads "TypeScript" over JSON/HTML, the buffer is tokenised as TypeScript, and the diagnostics rail shows a spurious `L1 Unclosed "{"` while JSON is being typed. Re-inferring on rename is nearly a one-liner, but it has to decide whether it may overwrite a language the user set deliberately — filed for that call. **Fixed in shell #368**: a rename re-derives the language from the new extension. **Confirmed on camera 2026-07-30** — `manifest.json` shows the header chip `JSON` with JSON tokenisation and "No problems" (the spurious `L1 Unclosed "{"` is gone), and `index.html` shows `HTML`.

**Filed by the `VID-build-apps` capture RE-RUN (2026-07-30).** The five rungs above are all confirmed fixed on camera and the run is at **0 console/page errors** — but the re-run surfaced one new blocker, which is the same payoff shot — **fixed in shell #370 and confirmed drained by the final capture 2026-07-30**.

- ✅ `POLISH-LAY-9` *(shell #370; confirmed drained on camera by the final `VID-build-apps` capture 2026-07-30)* — **a newly installed app's tile lands OFF-SCREEN, because the install placer never wraps.** `firstFreeIconCell` (`shared/dashboard-icon-grid.ts`) scans footprint-stepped slots row-major with `c` bounded only by `MAX_SLOT_SCAN` (1024), so it fills an unbounded *single row* before it ever reaches row 1. With the 20 seeded apps at `0,0 · 11,0 · 22,0 … 209,0`, Client Pulse was placed at `220,0` — `220 × 8px = 1760px` on a 1440px stage, i.e. past the right edge. `.dashboard-icons` does not scroll horizontally, so the tile is not merely off-camera: **it is unreachable**, and the same is already true of the four seeded apps beyond the fold (Books, Chat, Forms, Agent). Scene `06-installed` — *"And there it is. A real app, in her grid."* — plays over bare wallpaper, and scene `01-the-gap` shows a row of icons running off the screen instead of a tidy grid. **This is a regression exposed (not caused) by `POLISH-LAY-6`'s fix:** before #369 the seeder wrote 1×1-cell indices that tripped `isLegacyIconLayout` (every cell `≤ LEGACY_GRID_MAX = 16`), so the renderer's one-shot `repackIcons` migration silently re-packed the fleet to the measured viewport width — the wrap was an *accident* of the legacy-migration path, not a placement rule. Now that main writes real footprint cells, the migration correctly never fires and there is nothing left to wrap. **Not patched, because the column bound is a design call, not a constant:** main is explicitly the side that cannot measure the dashboard viewport (`main/dashboard/widget-host.ts`: "depends on the live viewport + scroll, which only the renderer knows"), so the options are (a) persist the viewport into the dashboard store for the placer to read, (b) pick a conservative fixed column count and accept that it is wrong on most displays — which is how the pre-#369 `GRID_COLS = 12` was already wrong, or (c) move new-tile placement to the renderer, which already measures columns for `repackIcons`. Blocks the shoot.

**Filed by the post-0.11.1 new-surface sweep (2026-07-31).** Scope was everything shipped after `v0.11.1` — the AppForge install flows (#364/#366/#371), the Code editor folder tree (#372), the Agent's `propose-code-file` cards (#365) — driven in the real production shell in BOTH appearances. Evidence: `tests/dogfood/.sessions/918-appforge-code-tree-polish/` (22 shots, light + dark), `918b-appforge-measure/` (computed-style + geometry dumps), `918c-agent-code-cards/`, `918d-agent-overflow-probe/`. **0 console/page errors across all four sessions.** Every rung below was measured, not eyeballed — the numbers are in each session's `notes.md`.

- ✅ `POLISH-LAY-10` *(shell #375)* — **the Agent window overflows horizontally the moment a `propose-code-file` card is staged.** `.agent__body` is a `248px 1fr` grid and `.agent__main` carried no `min-width: 0`, so the `1fr` track could not shrink below the card's min-content width — which a `<pre>` of unwrapped code sets to its longest line. Probe `918d`: `.agent` `scrollWidth=1245` against `clientWidth=1100`, with `overflow-x: hidden` swallowing the difference — the conversation sidebar sat at `rect -26..222` (26px of it unreachable) and `.agent__main` ran to `1219`, cutting 119px off the transcript's right edge including the card's language chip and part of the approve row. Fixed with `min-width: 0` on `.agent__main`, which hands the scrolling back to the `<pre>`'s own `overflow-x: auto`. Re-probe: `scrollWidth=1100`, sidebar `rect 0..248`. This is the flex/grid sibling of the documented `flex-shrink: 0` footgun and belongs in the same conventions family.
- ✅ `POLISH-LAY-11` *(shell #375)* — **the Code editor's REFERENCES panel header renders 19px tall against the FILES header's 44px**, in the same window, breaking the project-wide panel-header baseline. `.editor__refs-head` declares `height: 44px` but is a flex item in a column container whose empty state is `flex: 1 1 auto`, so 44px was only a ceiling and the sibling squeezed it by 25px. Fixed with `flex-shrink: 0` on `.editor__refs-head` and `.editor__diagnostics`, and defensively on `.editor__files-head` (which is one long file list away from the same fate). Measured before `h=19`, after `h=44`.
- ✅ `POLISH-DSN-7` *(shell #375)* — **the Marketplace toolbar row stacked three control heights, and its search field had no face at all.** Measured before: chips `h≈22`, `.bs-searchbar` `h=24`, `Install from…` `h=32`. The field was invisible at rest because `.marketplace__search`'s tinted surround (`background: rgba(0,0,0,0.18)` + a border) lost the specificity fight with `:root .bs-searchbar` — dead CSS since the day it was written, and a hardcoded rgba rather than a token besides. **Systemic fix rather than a marketplace patch**: a shared `.bs-searchbar--field` toolbar variant in the SDK searchbar CSS that wears the `.bs-input` face verbatim (`--control-height-md`, `--color-background-elevated`, `--color-border-default`, `--radius-sm`) — one field face, declared once, available to every consumer that needs a search bar in a control row. The chips now ride `--control-height-md` too. Measured after: chips `32` / search `32` (white fill, 1px border) / button `32`, one baseline.
- ✅ `POLISH-DSN-8` *(shell #375)* — **a disabled filled button read as the loudest control on the row.** In the install-from-vault picker the *invalid* candidate's greyed-out Install pulled more attention than the *installable* one's accent Install, worst in dark. Root cause was the F-410 fix's second answer: `filter: saturate(0.25)` preserves LUMINANCE, so desaturating a dark-theme accent face yields a light-grey slab. Fixed in the shared primitive: disabled filled variants now point both gloss stops at `--color-surface-raised` (an alpha tint in every theme, so the face tracks whatever it sits on and can never out-glow its enabled neighbour), the ink at `--color-text-tertiary`, plus a subtle inset hairline — and `opacity: 1`, because the base `.button:disabled` 55% is exactly the wash-out F-410 was about and it multiplies through both face and ink.
- ✅ `POLISH-DSN-9` *(shell #375)* — **the DOM popover had no content-fit mode**, so the Code editor's rename/create sheet — one 32px field and a footer — was padded out by `PopoverSize.Small`'s 220px floor to ~120px of dead panel. The shell renderer's React `<Popover fitContent>` has had this since it was written; the SDK's `createPopoverElement` did not. Fixed as **parity, not a per-app patch**: `fitContent?: boolean` on `CreatePopoverOptions` + `.bs-popover__panel--fit` in the SDK popover CSS (same name, same one-line rule as the shell's), adopted by the rename sheet. Unit test pins both the on and off case.
- ✅ `POLISH-FN-3` *(shell #375)* — **"New folder" asked the rename question.** Creating a folder (or a file) armed the shared naming sheet, which is right, but the sheet was titled *"Rename new-folder"* with a *Rename* button — the wrong verb on a create, and the first thing a new user sees when they make their first folder. Fixed with a `NameMode` enum (`Rename` | `Create`, per the no-string-discriminators rule) threaded from the two create-arm sites: the sheet now reads *"New folder" / Create* and *"New file" / Create*, while the rename paths are untouched. One new i18n key (`renameCreate`) translated across all six locales; test pins both questions.

- ✅ `POLISH-A11Y-1` *(shell #376)* — **the repo-wide `KBN-G-onclick-non-button` guard has been RED on `main` since #372.** The Code editor's folder row is a `<div>` carrying an `onClick`, and the guard reads literal JSX attributes only — it cannot see that `role="treeitem"` and the roving `tabIndex` arrive through the `{...itemProps}` spread from `useTreeKeyboard`. The row IS keyboard-operable (Enter / Space / ArrowLeft / ArrowRight all reach the same toggle through the tree reducer), so the sanctioned `// kbn-onclick-exempt` annotation is the correct answer rather than a literal role. Note for the next person: the token must sit on the line **directly above the opening tag** — the guard checks that one line and the tag's own line, nothing further up, so a multi-line rationale ending in prose does not register. Caught by this sweep's full-suite run, not by `verify` (which does not include the mcp-server tool tests).

**Filed, not fixed, by the same sweep — each needs a call rather than a patch:**

- 🟡 `POLISH-DSN-10` — **the Neutral button variant reads as the heaviest element on a light surface.** By design Neutral rides `--color-background-inverse` ("recedes next to the accent CTA"), but on the light themes that is a near-black slab: the Marketplace's `Install from…` is the darkest thing on a pale glass panel, and in the install-consent sheet the *Cancel* out-weights the accent *Install* it sits beside. Evidence `918/10-market-toolbar-light.png`, `918/14-market-consent-sheet-light.png`. Either Neutral's light-theme face is wrong, or these two call sites should not be Neutral — a design call, and it touches every confirm dialog in the product, so it is filed rather than guessed. **Fix in [shell #405](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/405)** (2026-08-01, conservative reading — owner review requested on the PR): Neutral keeps its role as the quiet filled secondary but its face drops from full-strength inverse to an 8→16% inverse tint over the theme surface with the theme's own ink — one CSS block, every confirm dialog benefits, symmetric in dark; revert-friendly if the owner prefers re-varianting the two call sites instead.
- 🟡 `POLISH-DSN-11` — **the Agent's proposal cards wear bespoke chrome.** `.agent-proposal__btn` (Add to vault / Discard) is a hand-rolled 24px pill next to the card's own 32px `.bs-input`, so the card mixes two control scales and two button faces — the shared `bs-btn` face is right there. Same card: the code-file field is labelled *Filename* while it holds a full path (`milestones/src/ui/panels/…/leaf.ts`), and the Agent sidebar's *"No conversations yet."* is bare text where the fleet uses the shared compact `<EmptyState>`. Evidence `918c/03-agent-card-light.png`, `918c/01-agent-empty-light.png`. **Fix in [shell #405](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/405)** (2026-08-01): the cards' buttons are the shared `bs-btn` face (approve = `data-bs-primary`, md scale beside the 32px `.bs-input`; bespoke CSS deleted), the field label reads *Path* in six locales, and the sidebar empty state is the shared compact `<EmptyState>`.
- 🟡 `POLISH-DSN-12` — **the Marketplace listing detail mixes chip and value faces.** On a sideloaded app's detail the meta row renders `App` / `Local install` / `0.1.0` as fill-only chips and `Unsigned` as the only bordered one, and the definition list below prints its values in three different faces (mono for the id, body for KIND/SOURCE, a smaller dim face for STATE). Evidence `918/22-market-detail-unsigned-dark.png`. Needs a decision on the chip family before touching it. **Fix in [shell #405](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/405)** (2026-08-01, chip-family decision taken as fill-only — owner review requested): *Unsigned* keeps warning salience via tinted fill + ink instead of being the row's only colored border; the spec list's values share one size + ink, mono reserved for the id, semantic color for install state.
- ✅ `POLISH-FN-4` — **approving a `propose-code-file` at a path that already exists silently creates a duplicate.** `propose-persist` always mints a new `CodeFile/v1`, so approving the agent's `milestones/manifest.json` on a vault that already has one leaves two entities on the same path: the Code editor tree shows two identical rows and the install-from-vault picker counts both toward the candidate's file count (observed: `milestones · 8 files` for a 6-file app). Overwrite / suffix / refuse-with-a-warning is a product decision, so it is filed. **Fixed in shell #380.** The decision taken: **the card surfaces the conflict BEFORE approval and the user picks** — a silent overwrite and a silent rename are both surprises, and the tray exists precisely so the human decides. A code-file card whose path is taken swaps its single "Add to vault" button for the two named outcomes ("Update the existing file" / "Save as `manifest-2.json`", the target path spelled out so nothing is silent), keeps the filename input live as the third way out, and shows a warning line naming the conflicting path. Underneath, `persistApprovedProposal` re-runs the same check and throws `CodeFilePathConflictError` when a conflict exists with no choice recorded, so the invariant holds fail-closed even if the UI is bypassed or the snapshot raced; `CodeFileConflictChoice` has no "create anyway" member, which makes the duplicate unrepresentable. Comparison is case-insensitive, matching the Code editor's `validateRenamePath` and the installer's `resolveBundleLayout` (macOS/Windows fold case). Three windows are closed, not one: the live vault snapshot, the files persisted earlier in this session (the snapshot has not round-tripped when a second card is approved seconds later), and the paths with an approve in flight (`claimCodeFilePath`, a synchronous ref — the only guard covering two cards approved before the first create resolves). Neighbouring cases pinned by tests: a case-only collision is a conflict, and Update keeps the existing spelling rather than re-casing the file; a soft-deleted row never blocks a create (the repo filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, so a tombstone is simply not in the snapshot); a note whose title matches a code-file path is untouched. The `-N` walk moved to `@brainstorm-os/sdk/path-names` (`firstFreeName` + `splitFileSuffix`), so the tray's "Save a copy" and the Code editor's "New file" name collisions identically. Reproduced first: a fake-vault test that stages, approves twice, and asserts one entity at the path failed on `main` by minting `ent_2`. Installer grouping re-confirmed downstream — a six-file app reports `fileCount: 6` with six distinct ids.

## App showcase videos *(standing content + polish cadence, `VID-*`; owner-driven, one app / week)*

Owner directive 2026-07-22: ship a **weekly YouTube video, one app per week**, each a full walkthrough of a first-party app's functionality. The forcing function makes this a **polish** track as much as a marketing one: a video only rolls when its subject app is **capture-ready — super-polished end to end**, so every affordance shown on screen holds up at recording resolution. The video queue is a *pull* on the [`POLISH-*` track](#product-polish--dogfood-hardening-standing-quality-track-polish--owner-driven) — each week's app gets a dedicated polish pass (its `POLISH-*` rungs drained) *before* the tape rolls, and the recording is the acceptance test: if it can't be demoed cleanly on camera, it isn't done.

**How it runs.** One `VID-<app>` rung per app, worked in [app-serial order](#app-serial-order-2026-05-23-policy-feedback_serial_shell_then_apps) (headliner apps first). Each rung is a three-gate sequence:

1. **Polish gate** — the app's open `POLISH-*` rungs (editor / properties / design / layout) are drained, then a **capture dry-run** (dogfood walkthrough of every documented affordance, against a seeded demo vault) surfaces any remaining defect; each new defect files a `POLISH-*` rung and **blocks the shoot** until fixed.
2. **Script + capture** — a shot list covering the app's full feature surface (the app doc's overview is the checklist), showing both the pointer path and the keyboard path (mirrors the user-facing-PR four-path standard), recorded against the demo vault.
3. **Publish** — cut, captioned, posted; the rung closes ✅ with the video link + the `POLISH-*` rungs it drained.

Cadence is **one per week**; the schedule follows the serial order. This is a **standing, never-"done"** track — a major app change re-opens that app's `VID-*` rung for a re-shoot, and the series re-runs the fleet as the product evolves.

- ⚪ `VID-1` — first episode (owner picks the headliner — Notes / Database / Graph are the strongest openers): runs the three gates (polish → script/capture → publish). Per-app rungs get ids as scheduled (`VID-notes`, `VID-database`, …).
- 🟡 `VID-notes` — **Notes is VID-1 (owner pick 2026-07-22).** **Polish gate PASSED** — capture dry-run [`tests/dogfood/sessions/912-notes-vid1-dryrun.spec.ts`](dogfood/../../tests/dogfood/sessions/912-notes-vid1-dryrun.spec.ts) walked the core surfaces (note list · editor typography · empty-note write-invitation · slash menu · inline toolbar · markdown block shortcuts) with **0 console/page errors** and **no capture-blocking defects** (Notes is the only app with zero open friction items). Confirmed Notes' empty-paragraph hint ("Type '/' for commands") fires on body focus — it is NOT hit by the Journal/Tasks F-405 hint/embed-parity gap. **Deeper-surface pass DONE:** properties panel, object menu (Open/Pin/Share/Add cover/Save as template/Export/Delete), icon picker, and `@`-mention people-picker (`@Marcus` → "Marcus Lee · Person") all captured clean; embeds/comments are functionally unit-tested. **One gap found + fixed → shell PR #245:** the icon-picker showed blank cells — the number keycaps `0️⃣`–`9️⃣`/`#️⃣`/`*️⃣` and `©️`/`®️` 404'd because `emojiFilename` didn't zero-pad codepoints < U+1000 to the art pack's 4-digit naming (fixed in all three copies: SDK picker, shell note-icons, graph node-icons; the picker also now hides cells for the ~11 emoji with genuinely no bundled art). **Remaining:** script + record + publish (owner).
- 🟡 `VID-build-apps` — **"Build a new app inside Brainstorm"** — the self-hosting episode: an app is written in the code editor (or drafted by the agent), installed straight from the vault, and runs sandboxed in the grid. **Storyboard rewritten against shipped reality 2026-07-29** ([`marketing/vid-build-apps.md`](marketing/vid-build-apps.md)) — the previous draft was gated on an in-app IDE program (`IDE-0`→`IDE-5`) that was **never built and is not needed**: the platform requires no build step (a valid app is `manifest.json` + `index.html`), so the honest story is stronger than the fictional one. Runs on `AppForge-1` (#364) · `AppForge-2` (#366) · `AppForge-3` (#365), all shipped; the only scripted element is the model's output in the agent act via the capture-only `BRAINSTORM_DEMO_AGENT=appforge` provider (same posture as `vid-agent-team`). **Gate 1 (polish/capture dry-run) RUN 2026-07-29 — capture pipeline ✅, polish gate ❌ (5 rungs filed, shoot blocked).** The pipeline is built and green end to end: scene table [`tools/promo/build-apps-scenes.mjs`](../tools/promo/build-apps-scenes.mjs), driver [`tests/dogfood/promo/vid-build-apps.spec.ts`](../tests/dogfood/promo/vid-build-apps.spec.ts), app source [`tests/dogfood/promo/client-pulse-source.ts`](../tests/dogfood/promo/client-pulse-source.ts), scripts `promo:capture|vo|render:build-apps`. All 10 content scenes captured, each verified frame-by-frame. **AppForge-2's owed real-shell verification is DISCHARGED**: the two files were typed in the Code editor, saved as `CodeFile/v1` rows, listed by `apps:list-vault-app-sources` as "Client Pulse · client-pulse · 2 files", consented (`Version 1.0.0 · studio.northbound.client-pulse · Capabilities requested: entities.read:brainstorm/Project/v1 · unsigned`), installed, and **launched rendering the three real seeded clients** (`Atlas — Series A deck` / `Harbor & Co — Brand refresh` / `Meridian — Booking app`, status dots off `statusKey`). The closing beat is real too: the same app calling `vaultEntities.list()` (which statically requires `entities.read:*`) is refused on camera with the broker's own words — *"refused — studio.northbound.client-pulse lacks capability for vault-entities.list"*. **One capture-blocking bug found and fixed** (shell PR, `fix/vid-build-apps-capture`): the `BRAINSTORM_DEMO_AGENT=appforge` script drafted a `hello-app/manifest.json` with **no `sdk` key**, so the agent-drafted app failed `validateManifest` and the vault picker greyed it out (`Invalid manifest: sdk must be a string ($.sdk)`) — the act's entire payoff. Fixed + pinned by a regression test that runs the real validator over the scripted manifest. **Gate 1 RE-RUN 2026-07-30 (shell `main` @ `0a3b76b6`, after #367/#368/#369): all five original blockers confirmed fixed on camera, one new blocker found — shoot still blocked.** All 10 content scenes captured with **zero degraded drivers** and, for the first time, **0 console/page errors** (`POLISH-LAY-8` drained). Confirmed on camera: `POLISH-FN-2` — the header chip reads `JSON` / `HTML` with matching tokenisation and "No problems"; `POLISH-FN-1` — the agent act runs in its own fresh thread, not appended to a seeded conversation; **#367** — the agent-drafted `hello-app/manifest.json` now carries `"sdk": "1"`, so the vault picker lists *Hello · hello-app · 2 files* with an **enabled** Install button and a real consent sheet (*"Version 0.1.0 · io.brainstorm.hello. Capabilities requested: none…"*), the act's payoff that was dead in run 1; `POLISH-LAY-7` — the grants popover renders `entities.read:brainstorm/Project/v1` in full, no ellipsis; `POLISH-LAY-6` — no tile overlap anywhere. Scenes `04`/`05`/`07`/`10` are shoot-quality: the picker, the consent sheet (*"Capabilities requested: entities.read:brainstorm/Project/v1 … unsigned"*), the app rendering the three real seeded clients with status dots, and the genuine broker refusal (*"refused — studio.northbound.client-pulse lacks capability for vault-entities.list"*). **Blocked at the time on** `POLISH-LAY-9` — the new tile was placed at `220,0` (1760px on a 1440px stage), so scene `06-installed`, the payoff reveal, played over bare wallpaper. **Gate 1 + gate 2 PASSED on the FINAL run 2026-07-30 (shell `main` @ `5f6fc673`, after #370)** `<gates: polish-capture>`: 10/10 content scenes captured, **0 degraded drivers**, **0 console/page errors**, run green in 4.0m, every clip's frames read back. `POLISH-LAY-9` is **drained on camera** — the icon-cell snapshot reads `Client Pulse@44,14` (fifth column of the second row) and the frame shows the tile on the wallpaper beside Agent, fully on stage, overlapping nothing. `07-launch` renders the three real seeded clients (`Atlas — Series A deck` / `Harbor & Co — Brand refresh` / `Meridian — Booking app`) with status dots under the header chip *vault access: entities.read:brainstorm/Project/v1*; `09` installs the **agent-drafted** app for real (*App installed — Hello 0.1.0 … unsigned*, marketplace `Apps 21 → 22`); `10-walls` now **recalls the install consent sheet** instead of the Settings grants popover — *owner decision 2026-07-30*, because the grants popover truthfully lists the ~22-capability shell baseline every app receives on top of what its manifest asked for, which reads as a contradiction under the VO *"it sees what she granted, nothing more"* (reasoning + the follow-up worth filing on the popover's own merits are in the [storyboard](marketing/vid-build-apps.md)). Capabilities requested: entities.read:brainstorm/Project/v1. … unsigned — only install apps you trust."*, and the genuine broker refusal still closes the scene. **RENDERED**: `tests/dogfood/.promo-build-apps/vid-build-apps-1080p.mp4` — 1:45, 1920×1080@60, −13.8 LUFS with the CC-BY bed ducked under the VO — plus `vid-build-apps.srt` (12 cues) and the upload kit [`marketing/vid-build-apps-youtube.md`](marketing/vid-build-apps-youtube.md). ## AI broker & vector / hybrid search *(Stage 11; lexical half shipped early as Shell 9.22)*

Goal: realise [22](platform/22-ai-foundations.md) + the vector half of [18](data/18-storage-and-search.md). BYO key, local embeddings. **Blocking OQs: OQ-128/61/62/105.**

- ✅ 11.0 — **de-risk spike (FTS5 half landed, Tantivy half deferred to 11.0b) 2026-05-28.** Engine-agnostic bench harness shipped with the FTS5 adapter wired today: `packages/shell/src/main/search/bench-corpus.ts` (deterministic synthetic corpus — seeded mulberry32 PRNG, 96-word pool + 10 rare words at ~1/200 rate, 8 BP-style entity types, 5 canonical query shapes covering common/rare/two-term-AND/three-term-AND/type-filtered) + `packages/shell/src/main/search/bench.ts` (`BenchEngine` interface — `indexAll`/`query`/`diskBytes`/`dispose`; Tantivy adapter drops in without harness edits when the NAPI binding lands) + `tools/bench-search.ts` CLI (`bun tools/bench-search.ts --size 100000 --runs 20 --warmup 5 [--json] [--path bench.db]`). Doc-18 budgets pinned in code as `FTS_QUERY_MEDIAN_BUDGET_MS = 50` / `FTS_QUERY_P99_BUDGET_MS = 100` / `FTS_INDEX_BUILD_PER_ENTITY_BUDGET_MS = 2` so the bench report's `passes` flag tracks the docs without scraping the markdown table. **Real numbers landed in `docs/_review/2026-05-28-stage-11-fts5-bench.md`** — at 100k entities FTS5 hits all build/disk budgets (~0.015 ms/entity, ~298 MiB), passes the p99 budget (91.2 ms vs <100 ms target), but **misses the common-term median by 1.7×** (86.5 ms vs <50 ms target). At ≤50k entities FTS5 is within budget on every metric (43.7 ms median, 44.5 ms p99). Linear scaling: ~0.9 ms / 1k entities for common-term queries; rare-term queries stay sub-millisecond regardless of corpus size. **Two reference JSON snapshots** saved at `tests/perf/results/search-fts5-{10k,100k}.json` for cross-run / cross-machine diff review. **OQ-128 PARTIALLY RESOLVED — lean flipped from (a) Tantivy-replaces to (b) keep-FTS5-for-v1** (filed in `11-open-questions.md` with link to the review doc); **OQ-128b NEW** — calibrate the doc-18 100k median budget against the bench reality. Near-term path documented: ship FTS5 in v1, investigate type-filter join cost + `bm25(k1, b)` tuning, schedule Tantivy comparison as 11.0b post-beta. **Tests**: 29 new across 2 files (`bench-corpus.test.ts` 15 covering PRNG determinism + corpus invariants + query-shape coverage; `bench.test.ts` 14 — stub-engine layer for harness logic + FTS5 integration for end-to-end coherence). Workspace `tsc` clean, biome clean on touched files, full shell search suite 78/78 (was 49 → +29). — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).
- ⚪ 11.0b — Tantivy comparison: wire a Tantivy `BenchEngine` adapter against the same harness, re-run the canonical 100k corpus, compare median/p99/build/disk against the FTS5 baseline. Gated on the Tantivy NAPI binding (substantial new native dep; see 13.1b pattern).
- ✅ 11.1 — **search-architecture decision recorded 2026-05-28.** Formal capture of the OQ-128 / OQ-61 calls now that the 11.0 evidence is in. **OQ-128 RESOLVED → (b) v1 ships SQLite FTS5**; Tantivy is a post-beta quality follow-up (11.0b), not a v1 dependency — FTS5 meets every doc-18 budget at ≤50k entities and stays under the p99 ceiling at 100k (only the 100k common-term *median* misses the design number, tracked by OQ-128b). Adopting Tantivy in v1 would add a ~3 MB native binary + NAPI build-pipeline dependency on the critical path to beta for headroom not yet needed; the `BenchEngine` harness keeps the swap a one-adapter change post-beta. **OQ-61 RESOLVED → `sqlite-vec`** (vector extension) — an ecosystem/maintenance call (the 11.0 spike's vector half didn't land, so no comparative vector numbers yet): `sqlite-vss` is effectively unmaintained, `sqlite-vec` is the actively-developed successor with native SQL syntax + a single-loadable-extension build story; taken now to unblock 11.2, which measures its latency/recall in-context. No code in this rung — decision capture only (OQ doc + plan + table + log + dev-vault closeout). **Next buildable spine rung: 11.2** (vector index alongside lexical, one embedding per entity) — 11.0b (Tantivy comparison) stays gated on the Tantivy NAPI binding.
- ✅ 11.2 — **vector index seam alongside lexical (one embedding per entity) — preview-drop 2026-05-28.** Lands the storage + maintenance + bench plumbing for semantic search on `sqlite-vec` (OQ-61), behind a pluggable `TextEmbedder` so 11.3's `multilingual-e5-small` drops in with zero schema/repo/wiring change — the same preview-drop shape the lexical half (9.22) and the 11.0 bench used. **Pieces:** (1) `packages/shell/src/main/search/embedder.ts` — `TextEmbedder` interface + `EMBEDDING_DIM = 384` (pinned to e5-small so the vec0 table needs no migration when the real model lands) + `StubEmbedder` (deterministic L2-normalized bag-of-tokens hash — *semantically meaningless*, exists only to exercise the plumbing). (2) `search/vector-store.ts` — `VectorStore` interface + `InMemoryVectorStore` (pure cosine over a `Map`; the tested reference + degrade fallback, rebuildable-from-sources) + blob/cosine/dim helpers. (3) `search/sqlite-vec-store.ts` — production `vec0` store (DDL in ctor like `SearchIndexer`'s sidecar, NOT a schema migration — a `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE vec0` migration would break every search.db open where the extension didn't load; `entity_vec` + `entity_vec_meta` sidecar; cosine metric; over-fetch+post-filter type filtering). (4) `storage/sqlite.ts` — optional `loadVecExtension()` on the wrapper (lazy `sqlite-vec` load on the better-sqlite3 path; returns `false`/degrades under `bun:sqlite`, which **cannot load dynamic extensions** — confirmed, so the vec0 path is real-Electron-validated, the 9.3.5.N5 deferral shape). (5) `search/vector-indexer.ts` — `VectorIndexer` (holds all reusable logic: embed-text assembly, indexable filtering, dimension fail-close, empty-query short-circuit; async so 11.3's worker model needs no caller reshape) + `createVectorIndexer` factory (returns null when sqlite-vec can't load → lexical-only). (6) `index.ts` — maintenance seam wired (construct on the same search.db handle, rebuild in lockstep with FTS) but **gated `VECTOR_INDEXING_ENABLED = false`**: the only embedder today is the stub, so populating a meaningless index in beta would burn disk/cycles — 11.3 flips the flag + swaps the embedder. No new broker verb / capability (query surface stays gated for the hybrid-retrieval rung). (7) `search/bench.ts` — `makeVectorEngine` BenchEngine (in-memory cosine baseline, portable under Bun) + `tools/bench-search.ts --engine vector`. **Tests:** +34 (embedder 8 + vector-store 14 + vector-indexer 10 + bench vector ×2); shell search suite 78 → 117; workspace `tsc` clean; biome clean on touched files; new dep `sqlite-vec@0.1.9` (shell). **Deferred:** real model (11.3); real-Electron sqlite-vec ANN bench + exact-recall type filtering via vec0 metadata columns; `search.semantic`/`search.hybrid` query verbs (hybrid-retrieval rung). **Next buildable spine rung: 11.3** (11.0b Tantivy still gated on its NAPI binding).
- ✅ 11.3 — local embedding model → **semantic search on**. **Core landed *(2026-07-03, shell PR #79)***: 11.2 shipped the whole vector stack (sqlite-vec `entity_vec`, `VectorIndexer`, hybrid BM25+cosine RRF, query path) gated behind `VECTOR_INDEXING_ENABLED=false` + a meaningless `StubEmbedder`; this supplies the real embedder + flips the gate — **no schema/query/renderer change**, hybrid search sharpens as embeddings populate. New crate **`@brainstorm/native-embed`** (napi-rs over `fastembed-rs`/ONNX Runtime), **isolated from the crypto crate** so ONNX never links into the security-critical binary; `embedderInit` downloads weights to `userData/models` on first run (off the JS thread), `embedBatch` returns flat 384-d vectors. Shell seam `FastembedEmbedder implements TextEmbedder` loaded **defensively** — null (no prebuilt `.node` / ORT fails) → lexical-only; a vector-rebuild failure is isolated (lexical rebuilds first, vector in a swallowing catch) so an offline download never breaks search. **Decisions (user, OQ-62):** runtime = **custom napi-rs/fastembed** (not transformers.js); model = **`bge-small-en-v1.5`** (~130MB, 384-d, English) — multilingual-e5-small (470MB) rejected as too heavy, and it's a later **one-line** model swap (all 384-d, no vec0 migration); packaging = **first-run download**. Verified on darwin-arm64: cos(cat,feline)=0.75 vs cos(cat,finance)=0.40 (real semantics); +12 tests, 127 search tests, tsc+lint clean. **Packaging landed *(2026-07-03, [shell PR #84](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/84))***: `ort` **statically links** ONNX Runtime (otool shows no `libonnxruntime`; the self-contained 40 MB `.node` needs no sibling dylib), so it ships exactly like the crypto `.node` — `@brainstorm/native-embed` is built per-runner in `release.yml` (the arm64 mac runner cross-builds darwin-x64; win/linux native) + shipped via the shell's `extraResources` for all 6 targets. Release-only (`ci.yml`/`verify` still skip it — opt-in — so test CI stays fast; a packaged build degrades to lexical-only where the `.node` is absent). Cross-platform build verified by a `release.yml` `workflow_dispatch` dry-run. **First-run-download progress UX landed *(2026-07-03, [shell PR #89](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/89))***: the ~130 MB weight download was silent; now Settings → Search shows a live status — Idle → Downloading (byte %) → Ready, plus Failed (retryable) + Absent (lexical-only). `embedderInit(cacheDir, onProgress?)` streams the download in chunks + emits per-file byte progress over a NonBlocking `ThreadsafeFunction` (coalesced ~1 MB; SHA256 pin + size cap unchanged, still verified before ORT); a pure `embedder-status.ts` reducer folds ticks → status, carried on `search:stats` (panel polls 1 s only while downloading; decorative `aria-hidden` bar, percent in text). Backward-compatible (older `.node` → indeterminate bar). +29 tests; native rebuilt + smoke-checked (live HF tick path exercised via fakes, same posture as #84). **Incremental vector maintenance landed *(2026-07-03, [shell PR #86](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/86))***: `VectorIndexer.reconcile` (content-hash cache + `VectorStore.snapshotIds`) — stop re-embedding all N per write. **ANN bench tail landed *(2026-07-13)*:** `openWithVecExtension` + `makeSqliteVecEngine` (better-sqlite3 + on-disk vec0) + `measureVecRecallParity` / `parseBenchOptions`; dev IPC `dev:search:bench-vector` + `dev:search:vec-recall`; `tools/bench-search.ts --engine vector-vec`; real-Electron perf spec `tests/perf/specs/search-vector-vec.spec.ts` — 10k corpus **median 4.0 ms / p99 5.3 ms** (doc-18 <50/<100 ms ✅), **16.97 MiB** on disk, exact ANN parity on unfiltered common/multi-term queries. **Doc note:** the plan's earlier "computed in the search worker" wording — embedding runs off-thread via napi AsyncTask (libuv threadpool), not the utilityProcess search worker; moving it into that worker is a later refinement, not required for the async interface. **Consent gate landed *(2026-07-21, shell #228 — shipped in v0.7.0)*:** the first-run weight download is now opt-in — Settings → Search surfaces an explicit "Enable semantic search" consent before any ~130 MB fetch (no silent network on first vault open); declined → lexical-only, re-offerable. **GA tail remaining:** semantic-search ON-by-default (second headline) once the ANN-recall/perf budget bakes across the fleet.
- ✅ 11.3.1 — **Background-activity center** *(2026-07-03, shell PR #91, stacks on #89)* — a general shell-chrome surface so long-running background work is never silent (dogfood: the 11.3 model download ran invisibly; a per-panel Settings card you must navigate to isn't the right home). New shared `activity-types.ts` (`ActivityKind`/`ActivityPhase`/`BackgroundOperation`, no imports — used across main/preload/renderer like `sync-status-types.ts`); pure `main/activity/background-activity-store.ts` registry (`set`/`clear`/`snapshot`/`onChange`, recency-ordered, dedup no-op push); `activity:*` IPC (mirrors sync-status — one accessor + one push channel to the dashboard); preload `window.brainstorm.activity.{snapshot,on}`. Renderer: `useBackgroundActivity` hook + `<ActivityChip>` (appears **only while work is in flight**, next to the sync chip — spinner/icon + freshest-op title + percent, "N tasks" when several, warning glyph on error) + `<ActivityPopover>` (a row + determinate/indeterminate bar per op via the shared `<Popover>`). **Wired producers:** the 11.3 model download (via `operationFromSemanticStatus`) and the full search reindex (surfaced only past a 500 ms guard so fast per-edit reconciles don't flicker the chip). Extensible — sync/import/export register the same way (their `ActivityKind`s are already defined). +37 tests (store 9 · mapper 3 · handlers 4 · chip/popover 6 · status reducer/seam/card carried from 11.3). tsc + lint + shell build + size clean. Complements the Settings → Search detail card (11.3 download UX) — the chip is the ambient indicator, the card the drill-down.
- ✅ 11.3.2 — **semantic-model download is consent-gated (opt-in)** *(2026-07-21, shell #228; owner call — ask before the ~130 MB fetch)*. 11.3 wired the embedder + vector index to run unconditionally on vault open, so a fresh install silently downloaded the model on first index. Now it's opt-in: new per-device `SemanticPrefsStore` (`<userData>/semantic-prefs.json`, `{consented}` default false — app-global like `UpdatePrefsStore`, since the model cache is shared across vaults); new `EmbedderPhase.NeedsConsent`. Pre-consent the shell does **nothing semantic** — no addon load, no embed, no download (download only fires on the first `embedBatch`, so gating the vector-index build fully prevents network) — and search stays lexical-only (the existing degrade path, so lexical is unchanged). `enableSemanticSearch()` (new `search:enable-semantic` IPC) persists consent, builds the vector index on the live search.db handle, and rebuilds (download starts on first embed, streams through the existing progress UX); a consented-empty vault reads Idle, an addon-absent platform flips to Absent. Settings → Search shows the rationale + an "Enable semantic search" button in the NeedsConsent phase. +17 tests. *(Open product call: "opt-in in Settings" vs "prompt on first run" — same primitives, only the default + prompt placement differ.)*

A whole-codebase pre-app-work sweep against this project's known low-level trap classes (main-thread blocking, render-loop rebuilds, unbounded caches / lifetime leaks, IPC + reactivity-layer drift). **No CRITICAL findings**; every previously-fixed bug class was verified still mitigated (wrong-key SQLCipher negative-cache, resilient-worker fail-fast + respawn, broker per-app backpressure, graph `geometryDirty` gate + dual-source visibility-pause + Pixi `{texture:false}` destroy, bounded ydoc-worker LRU + resolver retention, vault-session key zeroing).
