So once certs exist, **macOS+Windows signing = populate 4 secrets, no code**. **What is NOT wired (the real work, all gated on the cert):** (1) **macOS notarisation** — `packages/shell/package.json` `build.mac` has **`hardenedRuntime: false`**, which Apple notarization *requires* to be `true`; needs the flip + an electron-builder `notarize`/`afterSign` step + `APPLE_ID`/`APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`/`APPLE_TEAM_ID` secrets + confirming `build/entitlements.mac.plist` (not `entitlements.adhoc.plist`) is the signed-build entitlement. **Until this lands a signed-but-not-notarized `.dmg` still trips Gatekeeper** — the classic "we have the cert, why won't it open" trap. (2) **Windows EV** — an EV cert's private key is typically non-exportable on a hardware token, so `WIN_CSC_LINK` (a `.pfx`) may not apply; a cloud-HSM / Azure Trusted Signing path is a **procurement-time decision** to make before buying. (3) **Gatekeeper/SmartScreen open-clean verification** on a real machine (a green CI build is not proof the download opens). **Release-infra residue that rides alongside:** the `13.6` update-feed host URL (`BRAINSTORM_UPDATE_FEED_URL`) + the catalog CDN/bundle-store deploy (Phase 3.4c). Procurement playbook (founder action) lives in [ops/launch-plan.md §Critical path](ops/launch-plan.md). **Replaces the stale "13.2 (notarisation)" reference in 13.1** (13.2 is bundle-hash).
- ✅ 13.12 — **in-app auto-update (electron-updater), cross-platform — SHIPPED in v0.1.5 (2026-06-29)** ([shell PR #32](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/32), merged). Verified end-to-end on the signed release: `build.publish: github` bakes `app-update.yml`; `release.yml --publish always` uploads `latest*.yml` to the GitHub Release; Settings → Updates does detect → download → relaunch-to-install. Supersedes 13.6's manual-download check on packaged builds with a real self-updater: detect → download (progress) → relaunch-to-install, on macOS / Windows / Linux. **Scope: pulled forward from v2** (auto-update was a documented v1 exclusion) — a public beta can't ask testers to re-download every build. `AutoUpdateEngine` (lifecycle state machine over an *injected* `ManagedAutoUpdater` → fully unit-tested with a fake, +6 tests; mirrors 13.6's injected `UpdateService`) + `electron-auto-updater.ts` (the electron-updater binding; `autoDownload` off; channel ↔ the shared 13.6 `UpdateChannel`) + IPC (`update:get-state`/`check-auto`/`download`/`install` + a pushed `UPDATE_STATE_EVENT` stream) + the Settings → Updates panel evolved (Check → Available → Download-w/-progress → Restart-&-install / error; 13.6 feed view stays as the dev/unsupported fallback). `build.publish: github` bakes `app-update.yml` (reads `latest*.yml` off the GitHub Release; `release.yml --publish always` uploads it). Security: electron-updater's own code-signature verification (macOS Developer ID match / Windows publisher) means a compromised feed can't push a differently-signed artefact. **Verified local** (typecheck + biome + 40 unit tests + shell build); **release-time gate** = the real download→install→relaunch loop on a signed build with a higher published version (no-ops in dev) — **macOS depends on 13.11/#27 landing**. **Follow-ups:** per-OS verification on signed builds (mac after #27 · Windows gated on EV `DQ-13.1-B` · Linux AppImage) · channel `.yml` routing + optional background auto-check toggle · consolidate the 13.6 JSON-feed once the engine is proven.

## Native acceleration *(NAPI-RS, post-beta perf track)*

Goal: extract the hottest pure-CPU JS paths to a single in-tree NAPI-RS crate (`packages/native/`, npm name `@brainstorm/native`) so vault-unlock latency drops ~10× and dense-graph force simulation gets 3–5× headroom. **All iterations are 🟢 GA-only — beta ships fine on `@noble/*` + JS force-sim.** Rides on `13.1` cross-platform signed-build CI for prebuilt-binary distribution. Considered-and-skipped: CRC32 in `ydoc-store.ts` (Yjs encode is the bottleneck), FTS5 tokenizer (SQLite is already C), SHA-256 file hashing (Node `crypto` is OpenSSL-NAPI), Graph pattern matcher (demo-only path — SQL compiler is real). **OQ-NAPI-1 distribution policy gates `NAPI-1`.**

- ✅ NAPI-1a — workspace scaffold + `napi-rs` v3 toolchain landed 2026-05-24. New `packages/native/` member: Rust crate (`napi = "3"` / `napi-derive = "3"` / `napi8` ABI target, `napi-build = "2"`, release profile = LTO + strip + codegen-units 1 + opt-level 3), `build.rs` calling `napi_build::setup()`, `src/lib.rs` with one `#[napi] smoke_sum(a, b) -> i32` to prove end-to-end ABI. `package.json` declares `binaryName: "brainstorm-native"` + the five v1-platform target triples + the `napi build --platform [--release|]` scripts; `vitest.config.ts` + `test/smoke.test.ts` run the round-trip under `bun --bun vitest`. First debug build green in ~7 s on `aarch64-apple-darwin`, producing `brainstorm-native.darwin-arm64.node` (~702 KB) + auto-generated `index.js` (24 KB loader) + `index.d.ts` (camelCases `smoke_sum` → `smokeSum`). All three artifacts gitignored; the `target/` directory excluded from biome (`**/target`). Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; full workspace vitest 6228/6228 (no test count delta — smoke test is package-local, outside the root vitest include glob); biome clean on touched files. Foundation for NAPI-2..4 — no consumers yet. **README in `packages/native/README.md` documents the add-a-function loop.**
- ✅ NAPI-1b landed 2026-05-25 — same code path as 13.1b (closed in one iteration; see 13.1b row above for detail): per-target `napi build` scripts in `packages/native/package.json` + per-arch `extraResources` filter in `packages/shell/package.json`'s electron-builder block + `loader.cjs` + `packaged-resolver.cjs` that prime `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH` so the auto-generated napi-rs loader resolves the bundled binary in packaged mode without forking the codegen output. **OQ-NAPI-1 resolved** — distribution-policy answer: each installer carries only its host-arch binary (no fat binaries; CI matrix produces six host-arch bins, one per runner). 13.1c GH Actions matrix is the next rung that exercises the per-target builds across all six runners.
- ✅ NAPI-2 — Argon2id KDF landed 2026-05-24. `@noble/hashes/argon2.js` swapped for the Rust `argon2` crate (`argon2 = "0.5"`, RustCrypto) in `main/credentials/keystore-passphrase.ts`. New `#[napi(js_name = "argon2idDerive")]` export takes `Uint8Array` passphrase + salt + m_kib/t_cost/p_cost/out_len, returns the derived `Uint8Array`. **Byte-identical output to `@noble/hashes` v2.2.0 proven across the shell's TEST_KDF (m=8, t=1, p=1), the OWASP-2024 production profile (m=64 MiB, t=3, p=4), and five non-default output lengths** — existing on-disk passphrase vaults open uninterrupted. Pretest hook (`predev` / `pretest` / `verify` chain on root `package.json` + `build:native` script) ensures the `.node` exists before any consumer loads it; root vitest now scans `packages/native/test/`. Tests +7 (argon2 contract: byte-identity ×3 profiles + determinism + bit-flip diff + out_len=0 reject + invalid-params reject). Full workspace vitest **6238/6238**; workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files; `bun run verify` 223/223 integration+entities green with the new build chain.
- ✅ NAPI-3 — full crypto suite consolidation: replaces `@noble/{hashes,ciphers,curves}` wholesale across `credentials/{crypto,identity,hpke,device-ed25519,device-x25519}.ts`, `sync/envelope-seal.ts`, `pairing/sas.ts`. Each primitive swaps as its own slice with a byte-identity contract test vs the current `@noble` version (the NAPI-2 Argon2 pattern). Consolidates the audit boundary to one crate; retires 3 deps. **Each slice is independently safe to land before `10.9` close** because byte-identity is proven per primitive — no wire-format changes are masked.
  - ✅ NAPI-3a Ed25519 landed 2026-05-24 — `@noble/curves/ed25519.js` (`ed25519.sign` / `.verify` / `.getPublicKey` / `.keygen`) → Rust `ed25519-dalek = "2"` (`std + fast + zeroize` features) in `credentials/{identity,device-ed25519}.ts`, `pairing/{devices-store,pairing-frame,pairing-handshake}.ts`. New `#[napi(js_name="ed25519GetPublicKey|ed25519Sign|ed25519Verify")]` exports taking `Uint8Array` everywhere. **Byte-identical** to `@noble/curves` v2.2.0 across 4 fixed seeds × 4 fixed payloads for signatures and across all 4 seeds for public-key derivation; cross-impl verification works in both directions (Rust signs → @noble verifies, and vice versa). Tests +7 (cross-impl pubkey, cross-impl sign, cross-verify both directions, tampered-payload reject, wrong-seed reject, malformed-length reject, wrong-seed-length InvalidArg). `verifySignature` paths in the shell simplified — Rust returns `false` on malformed input (never throws), so the `try/catch` wrappers in the callers are deleted. `keygen()` calls replaced with `randomBytes(32) + ed25519GetPublicKey(seed)` (the noble keygen was just that internally). Credentials + pairing + sync suites 351/351 green; full workspace 6246/6246 stable count (the 3–5 borderline tests that flake at the 5s timeout under parallel-resource contention pre-date this iteration and pass cleanly in isolation — same documented pattern as the 4063-baseline flake set). `bun run verify` 223/223 green.
  - ✅ NAPI-3b SHA-256 + HKDF landed 2026-05-24 — Rust `sha2 = "0.10"` + `hkdf = "0.12"` (RustCrypto) added. Two new exports: `sha256(input: Uint8Array) -> Uint8Array` (FIPS 180-4) and `hkdfSha256(ikm, salt, info, outLen) -> Uint8Array` (RFC 5869), with the RFC-mandated "missing / empty / null salt = HashLen zeros" path explicitly equalised across `undefined` / `null` / `new Uint8Array(0)`. **Byte-identical** to `@noble/hashes/sha2.js` + `@noble/hashes/hkdf.js` v2.2.0 across: empty-input FIPS 180-4 anchor (`e3b0c442…`) + 8 representative inputs up to 1 MiB; 4 HKDF call-shapes (pairing/sas, at-rest-key, pairing-handshake, multi-block expand); RFC §3.1 salt-normalisation. Swapped consumers: `credentials/identity.ts` fingerprint, `pairing/sas.ts`, `pairing/pairing-channel.ts`, `pairing/pairing-handshake.ts` (HKDF half only — its `ed25519GetPublicKey` swap from 3a stays), `storage/at-rest-key.ts`. `credentials/hpke.ts` deliberately stays on @noble — its `extract` + `expand` labelled-HKDF construction is fused with `chacha20poly1305` + `x25519` into the RFC 9180 keystream, so the whole file rewrites against the `hpke-rs` crate in NAPI-3d. Native tests +7 (sha256 ×3 + hkdf ×4); 489/489 credentials+pairing+sync+storage green; `bun run verify` 225/225 green; workspace `tsc` clean; biome clean on touched files. Binary size 1.38 MB → 1.40 MB (sha2 was already in-tree via ed25519-dalek; only the hkdf+hmac wrappers added).
  - ✅ NAPI-3c X25519 landed 2026-05-24 — Rust `x25519-dalek = "2"` (`static_secrets + zeroize` features) added. Two new exports: `x25519GetPublicKey(secret: Uint8Array) -> Uint8Array` and `x25519GetSharedSecret(secret, peerPublic) -> Uint8Array`. **Critical security parity**: the binding rejects low-order peer pubkeys post-scalar-mult (throws `Status::InvalidArg` on the all-zero shared-secret signature of a small-subgroup attack), matching @noble's upfront `invalid private or public key received` throw. Without this rejection, a malicious peer could force a deterministic shared secret to a pairing-handshake HKDF — catastrophic for the SAS-mode flow. **Byte-identical** to `@noble/curves x25519` v2.2.0 across: pubkey derivation on 4 fixed secrets; DH across all 12 (i,j) pairs where i≠j; DH symmetry `shared(a,B) == shared(b,A)`; cross-impl interop (Rust signs / @noble verifies and vice versa); low-order rejection parity; malformed-length InvalidArg. Swapped consumers: `credentials/device-x25519.ts` (keygen + getPublicKey) and `pairing/pairing-handshake.ts` (keygen + getSharedSecret). `credentials/hpke.ts` left on @noble — its X25519 is fused with the labelled-HKDF construction (NAPI-3d). Native tests +6 (29 total); 350/350 across native + shell credentials + pairing + storage green; workspace `tsc` clean.
  - ✅ NAPI-3d HPKE landed 2026-05-25 — `credentials/hpke.ts` swapped from the `@noble/{curves,hashes,ciphers}` combination to two new Rust `#[napi]` exports `hpkeSealBase` + `hpkeOpenBase` against the DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305 suite. **Path picked: hand-composed HPKE** over `hpke-rs`. Reason: with `x25519-dalek`, `hkdf`, `sha2`, and now `chacha20poly1305 = "0.10"` already in-tree from NAPI-3a/3b/3c, composing HPKE base-mode directly (~100 Rust lines mirroring the legacy TS impl 1:1) costs less binary size, gives byte-level control over every label / suite-id / nonce, and the construction is validated against the RFC 9180 A.2.1 KAT directly. Public TS API unchanged (`HPKE_SUITE`, `SealBaseOptions`, `SealResult`, `sealBase`, `openBase`) — the existing 8-test `hpke.test.ts` parity proof passes verbatim. AAD + info pass through bytes-exactly (entity-bound AAD `brainstorm/entity-wrap/v1:` + entityId is unchanged on the wire); 32-byte length checks throw with `/32 bytes/` (member-wraps callers depend on this). Native tests +10 (RFC 9180 A.2.1 KAT + cross-impl byte-identity vs @noble + round-trip × 8 + cross-impl interop both directions + wrong-recipient + wrong-info + wrong-aad + tampered-ct + malformed-lengths + CSPRNG-non-determinism). **38 native total** (29 → 38, +9 plus a bonus). 26/26 `hpke.test.ts` + `member-wraps.test.ts` green on main. Binary 486 KB (down from 1.4 MB — debug→release variance; release-mode size confirmed under prior NAPI-3c at 1.4 MB, so the +400 KB hand-composed delta is in-line with planning estimates). `@noble/*` deps stay in `packages/shell/package.json` — `crypto.ts`, `envelope-seal.ts`, `keystore-passphrase.ts`, `device-x25519.ts`, `identity.ts`, `device-ed25519.ts` still consume them; NAPI-3e (XChaCha20-Poly1305) removes them. — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).
  - ✅ NAPI-3e XChaCha20-Poly1305 landed 2026-06-16 — two new Rust `#[napi]` exports `xchacha20Poly1305Seal`/`Open` (`XChaCha20Poly1305`+`XNonce` from the in-tree `chacha20poly1305 0.10`, no new dep). Byte-identity contract test vs `@noble/ciphers/chacha.js` proven BEFORE the swap (`packages/native/test/xchacha20poly1305.test.ts` — 16 random key/nonce/aad/plaintext tuples incl. empty-aad, cross-impl seal/open both directions, tamper/wrong-key/wrong-aad negatives) so existing on-disk sealed secrets keep opening. Consumers `credentials/crypto.ts`, `credentials/keystore-passphrase.ts`, `sync/envelope-seal.ts` swapped; wire format unchanged (`nonce(24)‖ct+tag`; `aad ?? empty`). **Final slice — `@noble/{hashes,ciphers,curves}` dropped from `packages/shell/package.json`** (the last `randomBytes` call sites → `node:crypto`; the two `ed25519.verify` holdouts → native `ed25519Verify`; `oauth-pkce` sha256 → native `sha256`); `grep @noble packages/shell/src` is empty. `@noble` remains a `packages/native` devDependency only, as the test parity oracle. **1057 crypto/sync/pairing/storage/apps tests green**; native rebuilt + suite re-verified on main post-merge. **OQ-NAPI-3 resolved → (a).**
- ✅ NAPI-P — **performance-bottleneck profiling sweep** *(2026-07-27, [`_review/2026-07-27-napi-profiling.md`](_review/2026-07-27-napi-profiling.md))*: all three candidates measured against the documented budgets; **no budget missed**. Graph force-sim at the 600-node soft cap is 3.0 ms/tick (180 ms per animated second — the plan's ~100–200 ms/s estimate was accurate) but runs off the main thread, so nothing a user waits on; ydoc-store persist p99 is **0.40 ms against a 50 ms budget** (125× headroom); XLSX 100k rows is 788 ms one-shot and linear (≈7.9 µs/row), with `read` dominating conversion 6:1. **NAPI-4 re-framed and returned to the owner:** it is NOT a fix for a budget miss — it is the prerequisite for raising the soft cap past ~1000 nodes, where the sim takes 33% of a core (77% at n=2000). If the cap stays at 600, close NAPI-4 as a no-op. Original rung text: **performance-bottleneck profiling sweep (gates NAPI-4 + any new native target)**. Goal: *confirm there are no strong CPU bottlenecks left* before spending more native effort — measurement before migration, the project's standing rule. Profile the real paths under a stress vault against the documented budgets ([`12-shell-architecture.md`](shell/12-shell-architecture.md) / [`18-storage-and-search.md`](data/18-storage-and-search.md)), reusing the existing harnesses (`main/integration/stress.test.ts` 100k-entity / 50MB-Y.Doc, `tests/perf/specs/idle-footprint.spec.ts`, the `LARGE_DOC_PROFILES` editor bench from `9.3.5.N5`). Candidates to score (from the territory map, ranked by expected ROI): **(1) graph force-sim** `apps/graph/src/render/force-layout.ts` — only superlinear path (O(n²)/tick at 600+ nodes); already off-main-thread so it gates NAPI-4 *only if* warm-tick exceeds budget on a dense graph; **(2) ydoc-store load/append/compact** `main/storage/ydoc-store.ts` — hand-rolled binary parse + sequential update apply; the real win if any is avoiding the JS↔native buffer copy, not CRC; 13.4 already showed persist p99 ≪ budget, so only pathological tail-counts matter; **(3) XLSX large-sheet parse** `apps/preview/src/renderers/office-renderer.ts` (SheetJS) at 100k+ rows. **Already confirmed NOT worth it** (re-stated from the §-header skip list): CRC32, FTS5 tokenizer, SHA-256, RAW-TIFF parse `apps/preview/src/logic/raw-preview.ts` (<5ms, bounds-safe), line-diff LCS `apps/code-editor/src/logic/line-diff.ts`, CSV/Notion import (I/O-bound). **Deliverable**: a `docs/_review/<date>-napi-profiling.md` with raw numbers per candidate → for each, *budget met (close NAPI-4 / no-op)* or *budget missed (proceed, with the measured gap)*. No code change unless a budget is missed.
- ❌ NAPI-4 — Graph force simulation engine: port `apps/graph/src/render/force-layout.ts` (Verlet + O(n²) repulsion + spring + center-pull) to Rust. **Closed as a no-op — owner decision 2026-07-28**, exactly as NAPI-P's verdict framed it: no budget is missed (3.0 ms/tick at the 600-node soft cap, off the main thread — nothing a user waits on), so the port's only value would be raising the cap past ~1000 nodes; the owner keeps the 600 cap. Re-opens only if the cap decision changes (the measured numbers to justify it are in [`_review/2026-07-27-napi-profiling.md`](_review/2026-07-27-napi-profiling.md): 33% of a core at n=1000, 77% at n=2000).

## Commercial backend & company ops *(Stage 14, v2)*

Goal: realise [43](platform/43-monetisation-strategy.md)/[44](platform/44-pricing.md)/[45](platform/45-payments-architecture.md). v1 ships **no** commercial surface. Stripe-only posture supersedes the dual-processor design (45 flagged for revision; 14.4+14.5 collapse).

### Collaboration layer — multi-user sharing *(v2 scope, pulled forward 2026-06-04)*

Pulled ahead of the rest of Stage 14 to unblock the collaboration/hiring dogfood arc (a hired teammate = a second *person* sharing entities). Builds the multi-**user** authorization layer on the already-complete Stage 10 sync substrate (blind relay + per-entity DEK + HPKE member-wraps + pairing — all done `10.0`–`10.9`). The v1 transport is reused unchanged; this adds the membership + share/revoke layer that [16-identity-orgs-encryption.md](security/16-identity-orgs-encryption.md) frames as the org/spaces work. **Design positioned by the resolved OQ-29** (`root.meta.access` = append-only, signed membership log inside the entity Y.Doc; revoke = `revokedAt`, audit retained).

- ✅ **Collab-C1** — access-record primitive: the `root.meta.access` signed, append-only membership log inside the entity Y.Doc — `grantAccess` / `revokeAccess` / `resolveMembers` / `activeMembers` / `roleOf`, Ed25519-signed grants + revokes, entity-bound (no cross-doc replay), tamper + forged-revoke rejected on resolve, CRDT-merge of concurrent grants into an owner-bootstrapped log. `packages/shell/src/main/collab/access-record.ts` + 8 unit tests. (2026-06-04)
- ✅ **Collab-C2** — share/invite flow: the `ShareInvite` primitive (a collaborator's self-signed `{userEd25519Pub, x25519Pub}` bundle — the Ed25519 signature **binds the wrapping key to the identity**, closing the user→X25519 gap that the owner's own add-device log can't bridge for a *different* person) + `shareEntityWithInvite` owner orchestration (verify invite → C1 `grantAccess` → HPKE-wrap the DEK for the invite's X25519 key → `appendWrap`, returning the wrap to emit via the existing `emitWrapBootstrap`). Pure over the doc (caller opens+zeroes the DEK, owns the emit); idempotent re-share. Recipient reuses `unwrapDekForRecipient` + C1 `isActiveMember`/`roleOf`. `packages/shell/src/main/collab/share-invite.ts` + 10 unit tests (invite tamper-rejection, owner authorize+deliver, idempotency, entity-binding, and the full wrap-over-loopback-relay path with a blind-relay ciphertext assertion). (2026-06-04)
- ✅ **Collab-C3** — two-different-users E2E: two real `VaultSession`s with distinct sovereign identities + separate vaults. Collaborator mints a `ShareInvite` from their session keys (signed via `session.signPayload`, secret never exposed — new `createShareInviteSigned` closure form); owner runs `shareEntityWithInvite` → emits the wrap-bootstrap over the loopback relay → collaborator installs the DEK into its own `EntityDekStore`; owner emits the encrypted doc state, the collaborator decrypts and confirms it is an active Editor (the grant rides *inside* the now-decryptable doc); both then edit concurrently and the two docs converge. Blind-relay asserts: no frame body ever holds the plaintext DEK or any plaintext body text. `packages/shell/src/main/collab/two-user-share.test.ts` (mirrors the `new-device-join` harness but for a different *person*, not a second device). (2026-06-04)
- ✅ **Collab-C4** — two-vault collaboration harness. **Landed (in-process tier):** `collab-harness.ts` — a reusable `CollabLink`/`CollabVault` scaffold that boots two real `VaultSession`s with distinct identities over a `LoopbackRelayPort` (local relay) and packages the C1/C2 moves (invite → share → wrap-bootstrap install → encrypted doc-state sync → live bidirectional sync → revoke) behind a story-shaped API. C3's `two-user-share.test.ts` refactored onto it (single impl, no duplicated plumbing) + `collab-scenario.test.ts` with the Mira↔Marcus arc: share a brief → Marcus reads + is an active Editor → both co-edit to convergence → Mira revokes → Marcus inactive but the grant→revoke audit retained → Viewer-role fidelity → blind-relay ciphertext. Audited by reading the wired code and running the 11 two-shell `tests/dogfood/collab/` specs against a real build, not by grepping for filenames.
    - **What was already true (plan was stale, code was shipped):** rotate-on-revoke merged in #128 and is driven from `SharingEngine.revoke`, with the ROT-3a-ii `pending_rotations` drain wired to relay-connect + session boot; collection sharing (`containment-registry.ts` + `auto-share-reactor.ts` + `shareCollection`) is on `main` and the reactor IS subscribed to the real entities-service change emitter in `main/index.ts`; presence is live-wired per session (`installPresenceRouter`), not dormant. The `collab-c5-collection-sharing` branch the plan pointed at no longer exists - it merged.
    - **🔴 The find: F-288 deadlocked the production first-share path.** `authorizeWriter` resolved the sender against the receiver's LOCAL access record - but a first-time member has no local doc, so the record is empty, so the owner is denied - and the frame being denied is the one that CARRIES the record. Every later frame is then denied on the same empty doc: a permanent deadlock, not a conservative refusal. Reproduced on real shells (dogfood `009`, main-process log: `[live-sync] receive failed for ent_chan_general: envelope-pipeline: sender … is not an authorized writer`). It was invisible because every green collab spec receives through the ungated `CollabDevBridge` receiver, and every unit test stubs the predicate `() => true|false`. **Fix:** the predicate now receives the decrypted plaintext, and `authorizesAsShareBootstrap` (`main/collab/access-record.ts`) admits a sender ONLY when the local doc holds no access entries at all AND the incoming state makes that sender a signature-verified active Editor+, merged into a throwaway doc. Authority stays with the Ed25519 grant signatures, so this is not weaker than checking a persisted copy of the same entries; a doc that already resolved a record is authoritative, so no one can re-bootstrap around a revoke. The closure also short-circuits on this identity's OWN sovereign key (a paired device and the cold-restore backfill both re-deliver our own data, and a never-shared entity has no record to check at all). New `main/collab/share-bootstrap-authz.test.ts` runs the real closure over a second real `VaultSession` and fails without the fix.
    - **🔴 The second find: an unauthorized wrap could re-key an entity.** `receiveWrapBootstrap` had no writer check, and `installEntityDek` accepts any strictly-newer DEK ordinal (ROT-3a-i). The inbox channel is `inbox:<pubkey>` and every member's X25519 wrapping key is published in the signed access record, so any member - a Viewer included - could seal a DEK of their choosing at a bumped ordinal and rotate an entity out from under its owner (the victim then fails to decrypt real traffic and emits under a key the attacker holds). **Fix:** `main/collab/wrap-install-authz.ts` - the authenticated wrap sender must be an ACTIVE Owner of the entity whenever this device already holds a DEK for it; a first install and our own identity stay open, since a first install can only create an entity we did not have and a cold device has no record to read. Fail-closed on an unreadable record or an undecodable key; +8 tests incl. a revoked Owner.
    - **Dogfood specs, real two-shell runs (built `main`, then re-run on the fix; no regressions - `003`/`006`/`007`/`008`/`011` green before and after):** `001` ✅ (the F-466 regression stays fixed) · `003` ✅ · `006` ✅ · `007` ✅ · `008` ✅ · `011` ✅ · `009` ✘ still, but for a different and much later reason - before the F-288 fix NOTHING converged; after it the channel + one of the two messages do, and `ent_msg_followup` deterministically receives its wrap and never a state frame (**F-471**: the initial-state gap on the cross-user inbox path - the owner emits a child's full state right after that child's wrap, while the receiver only subscribes that child's channel once the wrap resolves, so a forward-only relay drops what lands in between). Design 71 §flow-1 nominates the durable node's snapshot+tail backfill to close it, but the production node **ignores the Collab-C5 `route` inbox override** (already filed on the `10.11` bullet), so pointing `009` at the node is strictly worse - measured: no wrap reaches the receiver at all and even the channel stops converging. Own rung: fan by `route ?? entityId` in `../brainstorm-sync`, or give the receiver a state request after subscribe. `009` deliberately stays red until a team's whole channel really arrives · `002` + `005` were asserting `awaitConverged(…, everyone)` AFTER a revoke - a stale pre-rotate-on-revoke expectation, since forward secrecy means the revoked member MUST diverge; both rewritten to converge the survivors only and to positively assert that a post-revoke edit reaches the survivor and never the revoked member (so F-286 is now proven on real shells, from the survivor's side, rather than only in-process) · `004` had been dead since the package extraction (`packages/shell/src/shared/selective-sync-types` moved to `packages/protocol`) - import repointed.
    - **🟡 Still open - `010` presence-live fails, root-caused, not fixed.** Both shells emit awareness (the relay audit shows frames in both directions, so the transport IS on) but each fails `xchacha20poly1305: open failed` - they hold different DEKs. Cause: the dogfood's `installShareReceiver` creates the receiver's row with `dek_id IS NULL` before the share lands, the boot `retroWrapNullDeks` pass then MINTS a local DEK for it (marcus logs `wrapped 9 entities` where every other shell logs 8), and `installEntityDek`'s monotonic rule then rejects the owner's v1 wrap as not-strictly-newer. The trigger is dev-bridge-shaped (production's `installWrap` creates the row and the DEK together, so a null-DEK row awaiting a wrap should not exist), but the underlying hazard is real and the fix touches DEK version semantics on a security-critical path - **filed as its own rung rather than half-built here.** Presence in the product is otherwise wired and covered by `presence-scenario.test.ts` + the PRES-4 gate.
    - **🔴 Collab-C6 (b) and (c) are NOT built** (the lead bullet said so; the C5 bullet implied otherwise). A remote member renders as `ed25519:<16 hex>`: `share-dialog.tsx` `memberName` falls back to `m.fingerprint`, `roster-service.ts` resolves names via `readProfile(repo, pubkey)`, and the only writer of a `Profile/v1` row is `writeSelfProfile`, which hardcodes the session's own pubkey - so `readProfile` returns null for every remote member, always (asserted by `roster-service.test.ts`: *"includes a silent granted member (no name until their profile propagates)"*). `ShareInvite` carries a signed `label`, but the only shipping mint site passes `""` (`share-dialog.tsx:191`) and the only shipping save site passes `displayName: ""`, so an auto-saved teammate renders as a **blank quick-add chip**. `ContactsStore` has no rename and no UI; "petname" appears twice in the repo, both in doc comments. `ResolvedProfile.verified` is computed and then dropped at the service boundary, so no trust chip can exist. Presence names are self-asserted and unverified - a member can publish any `name` and any `id`. **Recommendation:** C6-b is the 0.12.0 blocker for "share for real" (names, not keys) and is a rung of its own - a signed profile snapshot on the `ShareInvite` + a cache the roster reads for non-self pubkeys; C6-c/d ride behind it.
    - **Also found, not fixed:** `SharingEngine.recascadeCollection` has **no production caller** (only tests), though its own doc comment claims "the trigger … is wired in the sync layer" - so the deferred re-cascade for a member who joins after children exist never runs. And `grantAccess` still has no Owner-only policy, so any Editor can mint a valid grant for a stranger and every peer honors it (the access record's own header already flags this as a deliberate follow-up).
    - **✅ `Collab-C5-invite-anchor` - LANDED 2026-07-31 ([shell #378](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/378) + **[#379](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/379), the gate findings**) `<gates: security-review, pentest>`; it was the blocking rung for the 0.12.0 release.** The `/security-review` on the fix above ([_review/2026-07-31-collab-c5-authz-security-review.md](_review/2026-07-31-collab-c5-authz-security-review.md), ledger verdict `fail`) found that `authorizesAsShareBootstrap` accepts a **self-signed** grant, because `resolveMembers` verifies each grant under its own `addedBy` and `grantAccess` still has no Owner-only policy. The empty-local-record guard is no constraint on an attacker who picks the entity id: anyone who already co-members ONE entity with you can read your sovereign pubkey and device X25519 out of that entity's access record, seal a wrap for an id you have never seen, take the pre-existing first-install allowance, and then bootstrap-authorize a forged record - injecting a populated, arbitrarily-typed entity into your vault with persistent write. That reaches automation execution, since the entities service projects a remotely-applied doc into `repo.update(id, properties)` and the automations wiring schedules every `Workflow`/`Trigger` row with no provenance filter. Signatures cannot root this: the distinguishing fact is out of band, namely that the real receiver MINTED a `ShareInvite` for the owner while the attacker scraped the same key. **Fix: make the invite a single-use secret the owner must echo (a Collab-C2 change), and anchor both the bootstrap branch and the first-install wrap allowance on it.** Landing #375 is still right - the alternative is a product where cross-user sharing does not work at all - but **0.12.0 must not ship until this rung lands**, because the exposure is to people you have already shared with. Also worth folding in: `isDeviceRevoked` is built but never passed by `installLiveSyncEngine`, so the OQ-203 cheap-path revoke drop is inert in production.
      - **The anchor, as built.** The invitee's `ShareInvite` (v2, `main/collab/share-invite.ts`) carries a 16-byte **nonce**, and the anchor secret is **derived, not drawn**: `SHA-256(domain‖Ed25519_sign(sovereign_sk, domain‖nonce‖expiresAt))`. The owner echoes `HMAC-SHA256(secret, domain|inviteId|expiresAt|entityId|memberPub|ownerPub)` into the member's grant as `"<inviteId>.<expiresAt>:<mac>"`, **covered by the grant signature** (`grantAccess` gained tagged, omitted-when-absent `|a=` / `|v=` segments, so every pre-existing grant still verifies byte-for-byte). The receiver re-derives the secret under its OWN key and compares in constant time. The MAC binds `(entity, member, granter)`, so the anchor a co-member can read out of a shared entity's record is worth nothing anywhere else - which is exactly the attack. **Deriving rather than randomising is what makes it survive a vault wipe**: a cold-restored device has no `share_invites` table left but still holds its keystore, so it re-derives and the owner's backfill is admitted; it also lets a **paired** device redeem an invite its sibling minted. Verification therefore depends on no local state at all - the new `share_invites` table (entities.db v10 + `ShareInvitesRepository`) is a **replay ledger**, not the trust root. The expiry rides inside the derivation, so a holder can neither strip it nor extend it by redeeming where the row is missing.
      - **Single use, retries, expiry, revocation.** Redemption **claims** the invite for the first **granter** that redeems it; a second party holding the same token is `deny-invite-spent`, and the claiming granter may redeem again (a re-sent opening frame still applies) for anything they later share. Pinning to the granter rather than to one entity is deliberate and is argued in the review doc: the invite is minted by the **receiver** and saved by the **sharer** (`ContactsStore`), and `sharing.share({contact})` re-presents that one stored invite for every later share, so an entity pin would silently refuse the SECOND thing a saved teammate ever shares - the same class of break as the deadlock this rung exists to close. A hard burn-on-first-use was rejected for the same reason: authorization runs *before* the update is applied. Expiry (7 days) gates the FIRST claim. `ShareInvitesRepository.revoke` withdraws an outstanding code. A **collection cascade** carries the container id (`via`) instead of an anchor and is judged against local state only - we are an active member of that container, the granter is an active Editor+ of it, the entity's type is the containment registry's declared `childType`, **and the incoming doc really names that container under the rule's parent property**. That last check is load-bearing: the type comes from the sender's own wrap, so without it the "a channel co-member can introduce a Message and nothing else" claim would be a self-declaration (see the gate findings below).
      - **Proof.** `share-bootstrap-attack.test.ts` runs the original attack over two real `VaultSession`s and asserts BOTH halves - that `authorizesAsShareBootstrap` **admits** the forgery (the hole, pinned in-repo so it cannot silently return) and that `authorizeShareBootstrap` refuses it `deny-no-anchor`. **14 of its 19 cases fail with the anchor requirement removed**, measured by reverting the check and re-running. Cases: the injection, an anchor lifted out of the entity they legitimately share, a fabricated anchor, garbage anchors, pipe-ambiguity, a second party holding the same token, share-by-contact's legitimate second entity, expired, revoked, restart-persistence, a record that does not name us, an Editor-only granter, cascade allowed only at the right child type AND the right parent property, a three-entity container injection, a revoked container member, and a graft onto a pre-existing private entity. Plus `invite-anchor.test.ts` (derivation, what the MAC binds, the non-canonical-handle refusal, every refusal reason, the no-row cold-restore shape) and `share-invites-repo.test.ts` (incl. reopen-from-disk). The existing two-`VaultSession` `share-bootstrap-authz.test.ts` was rewired onto the **real** production closure, so the LEGITIMATE first share is proven to survive the gate rather than only the signature half.
      - **🔴 The gates found six things, and all six are fixed in [#379](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/379)** - #378 was merged before they landed, so `main` briefly carried the two CRITICALs ([_review/2026-07-31-collab-c5-invite-anchor-security-review.md](_review/2026-07-31-collab-c5-invite-anchor-security-review.md)). Two were CRITICAL and both were reproduced with runnable PoCs by `/pentester`: (1) **a non-canonical `inviteId`** - base64url is lenient, so 16 strings decode to the same 16-byte nonce while the ledger keys on the *string*; a claimed invite could be re-spelled onto a fresh unclaimed row, past a `revoke` and past expiry (*15 extra entities admitted after an explicit revoke*), fixed by demanding a canonical re-encoding round-trip; (2) **container descent admitted arbitrary entities** - the child *type* came from the attacker's own wrap and the child's parent property was never compared to the container, so any Editor+ co-member of a Channel/Project/Whiteboard could inject unbounded arbitrary content with **no invite at all** (*5/5 unrelated entities admitted*), fixed by the parent-property check. Then (3) **the restore-window anchor authorized an entity ID rather than a SENDER**, off the untrusted relay's catalog answer, letting a Viewer's stored self-signed record be applied as Owner at restore - fixed by **removing** that anchor, since the derived secret already covers cold restore (the `RestoreEngine` change was reverted with it); (4) **`sharing.createInvite` was gated on the read-tier `sharing.read`** while now minting a bearer credential carrying the anchor secret, the inbox channel and the X25519 key - re-gated on the scarce `sharing.share`; (5) the signed-grant **separability guard covered 2 of 6** concatenated fields - extended; (6) **a bootstrap could graft onto a pre-existing private entity** (a doc with content but no access record), turning injection into takeover of something you authored - fixed with a content-roots check that deliberately ignores the meta map, because membership bookkeeping get-or-creates it before the gate runs.
      - **Dogfood is PARTIAL and declared as such.** `001` ✅ `002` ✅ `003` ✅ `004` ✅ `005` ✅ `006` ✅ `007` ✅ `008` ✅ `011` ✅ ran green on two real shells against a build of this branch, with exactly ONE gate refusal across the whole set (`deny-local-record` on `ent_issue4_brief` - the pre-existing F-288 enforcement refusing a revoked member's write on a doc that already carries a record). `009` / `010` stay red for F-471 / F-472, unchanged. **`004` is the find of the run**: the first cut broke cold restore (`deny-invite-unknown` - the wiped vault had no invite row), precisely the "a bootstrap that is too strict silently breaks legitimate sharing" failure mode, and that is what drove the derived-secret design; no unit test would have found it. **But those runs predate the six gate fixes above** - real-shell verification was suspended mid-rung because the test shells were stealing the owner's screen, so the fixes are covered by unit + two-`VaultSession` integration tests only. **A two-shell re-run is owed** once the harness lands an off-screen launch mode.
      - **Two residuals accepted, neither blocking.** (a) **`Collab-C5-wrap-anchor`** - an unanchored FIRST `WrapBootstrap` install is still accepted (`authorizesWrapInstall` only gates an ordinal bump), so a co-member can still cause an **empty** row of a chosen type to be materialized; `installWrap` seeds `properties: {}` and the properties projection is exactly what the anchored gate now refuses, so the row is inert and never syncs (`isShared` reads an empty access record). Gating the wrap needs the anchor on the wrap payload and its failure mode is the ROT-3a **lock-out** class (a wrongly-refused first install is permanent data loss), so it is a rung of its own rather than a rider on a release gate. (b) The granter-rather-than-entity claim, argued above. Also noted: `ShareInvitesRepository.purgeExpired` has no production caller and should not get one without re-reading the review.
    - **🟡 `Collab-C6-b` - a shared member should render as a name, not a key.** The 0.12.0 "share for real" headline needs this: a signed `Profile/v1` snapshot riding the `ShareInvite` / access record, plus a cache `roster-service.ts` consults for non-self pubkeys (today `readProfile` can only ever resolve your own). Small dependent fix in the same rung: `share-dialog.tsx` mints invites with `label: ""` and saves contacts with `displayName: ""`, so an auto-saved teammate is a **blank quick-add chip**. Then `Collab-C6-c` (petname + a trust chip off the already-computed `ResolvedProfile.verified`, currently dropped at the service boundary).
- 🟡 **Collab-C6** — human-facing user identity **(slice (a) ✅ shipped; (b) + (c) + (d) NOT BUILT, audited 2026-07-31; see the audit sub-bullet under Collab-C5)** (resolves [OQ-ID-1](reference/11-open-questions.md#oq-id-1--human-facing-user-identity-for-collaboration); design in [16-identity-orgs-encryption.md §Self-asserted display profile](security/16-identity-orgs-encryption.md#self-asserted-display-profile-the-human-facing-identity)). The crypto spine (C1…C4-live) is keyed on pubkeys; C5's share dialog / member list / presence cursors can't render a 32-byte key, so they need a name + face. Slices: (a) **self-asserted profile as a synced `Profile/v1` entity** — a per-identity singleton carrying `{displayName, avatarRef?, pubkey}` signed by the sovereign Ed25519 key, edited in Settings → Identity (avatar via the OQ-240 media-at-rest seal). Storing it as a vault entity (entities.db) means it **syncs across the user's own paired devices** like any other entity — it must NOT be a renderer-local `localStorage` pref; this slice *replaces* the `localStorage` presence-name hack the B11.9 cursors/comments currently read (`apps/notes` `presence.ts`, shared `peer-presence.ts` `localPresenceName`), reading the synced profile instead. (b) **cross-identity distribution** — a signed snapshot of the profile rides the `ShareInvite` (Collab-C2 already binds X25519→Ed25519) and is cached in the access record / Yjs awareness, so members render names with no directory service. (c) **petname / local override** — each user can locally rename a contact; UI distinguishes self-asserted name vs. your petname vs. not-yet-verified pubkey; fingerprint compare (reuse device-pairing SAS) upgrades trust. (d) **Contacts as registry** — `Person/v1` gains `pubkey` + petname; "people I've shared with" live there. Additive to the encryption model: no relay plaintext, no new wire capability (signed app-data, not a privileged record). **Blocks C5** (member list needs it); **does not block** the already-done crypto spine. Consumer-account verified profile (v2) supersedes the self-asserted one without changing this shape.
  - **Landed 2026-06-21 (slice a + the read/render layer):** the signed **`Profile/v1`** data layer (`packages/shell/src/main/collab/profile-store.ts` — deterministic per-pubkey singleton id, sign-in-process under the sovereign key, signature binds name+avatar to the pubkey; the secret never crosses IPC) + a new capability-gated **`roster` broker service** (`packages/shell/src/main/roster/` — `members(entityId)` joins the entity's signed access record to resolved profiles, always-includes-self; `self()`/`setSelf()`; `roster.read` is a default grant, `roster.write` scarce). The chat/comment mention plugin was extracted to a shared `@brainstorm/editor` `MentionComposerPlugin`; **comments** gained roster-backed @-mentions (`CommentDef.mentions: string[]` = pubkeys). A **mention notifier** (`roster/mention-notifier.ts`) posts a "you were mentioned" notification on a created Message/Comment that names the local pubkey, self-suppressed (fires for agent/other authors now; **cross-user delivery is sync-gated on C5** — a peer's mention only lands once channels/comments sync cross-vault). **Settings → Identity** section added (privileged `profile:get`/`profile:set` IPC + preload `profile` bridge + `IdentitySection`) — edits the display name + shows the sovereign fingerprint. The **`sharing` service** gained `saveContact` / `listContacts` (read-tier) and `share`/`shareCollection` now accept a `contact` pubkey (resolves the stored invite) as an alternative to a pasted token; SDK `SharedContact` type + proxy. The **`<ShareDialog>`** shows known non-member teammates as one-click **quick-add chips** (share-by-contact, cascade-aware) and **auto-saves a pasted invite** so a teammate becomes a chip next time — replacing repeated code-paste with click-a-name for a known team. +11 tests (8 store, 1 service save→list→share-by-name with the message cascading, 1 dialog chip, +fakes). typecheck (packages + apps) + chat/notes app builds + biome + css-token check clean. **Still open for share-by-name:** seeding the Northbound cast's mutual contacts so the chips are pre-populated for the demo (rides M1 task #6 — the team-day scenario seed); petname/local-rename UI (c).

#### App lifecycle: catalog-driven install/update (replaces demo seeding) — designed in [`apps/59-app-lifecycle-and-catalog.md`](apps/59-app-lifecycle-and-catalog.md)

The 0→1 app lifecycle: the bundle cache becomes an offline-first snapshot of catalog entries; the **catalog** is the source of truth; **first-party apps are unified catalog entries that update separately from the shell binary** (two update planes). Staged migration M1–M5 retires the demo seeder *last*, behind a proven catalog path. M1/M2 (provenance + bootstrap refit) are landable earlier as beta-hardening since they only refit the existing `seedPackagedApps`. Reuses the existing `AppInstaller` chokepoint — no second install/update mechanism. Gated on OQ-LC-1..6.

New `main/apps/install-provenance.ts` (`InstallOrigin` enum — named to avoid the existing `InstallSource` *input* type collision — + `InstallProvenance` + `DEFAULT_INSTALL_PROVENANCE` + `parseInstallOrigin`/`parseChannel`, reusing the 13.6 `UpdateChannel` enum; `OFFICIAL_CATALOG_ID`). `AppRecord` + `AppsRepository` (upsert/updateBundle/rowToRecord) carry the fields; `AppInstaller.install` takes optional `provenance` (defaults to `DEFAULT_INSTALL_PROVENANCE`), `update` preserves the prior row's provenance unless the caller overrides. +4 repo tests (v9 columns present · provenance round-trip · pre-v9 backfill · existing signature tests intact); 5 fixture sites spread `...DEFAULT_INSTALL_PROVENANCE`. typecheck:packages + biome clean; repos/installer/platform/launcher/intents suites green (197). *(Pre-existing unrelated automations-pipeline failure noted.)*

### Durable sync node — zero-knowledge sync plane (out-of-product-repo)

The hosted sync infrastructure — a **third** deploy boundary, distinct from both the Electron client and the commercial control plane. It is **relay-blind**: it stores and forwards **ciphertext only**, never holds a DEK or identity key, and authorizes routing/fetch off the entity's signed access record. This is why it cannot live in `brainstorm-cloud` (whose invariant is "no vault content, no CRDT, no relay traffic, even encrypted") **nor** bloat the product repo. The cross-plane contract is the **Stage-10 wire protocol** (`wire.ts` routing header + the sealed envelope) — the sync analog of `api-client`. A forward-only relay alone is **not** sync: it keeps nothing, so lose the local copy and there is no restore. The durable node is what makes "upload changes to the infrastructure → restore from zero" real, the same model as Anytype's sync nodes; design is [20 §Sync](data/20-database-growth-and-sync.md) + [16](security/16-identity-orgs-encryption.md).

**Repo:** `brainstorm-sync` (sibling working tree `../brainstorm-sync`) — its own Bun + biome + vitest workspace, its own `CLAUDE.md` asserting the relay-blind / ciphertext-only / no-product-import invariants. It shares **no** code with the app (the relay core is deliberately copy-able — `wire.ts` is already duplicated for exactly this decoupling); the product keeps `packages/relay-server` as the in-process relay the soak + collab dogfood harnesses spawn. The deployed node is the production form.

- ✅ SYNC-0 — **repo scaffold + boundary `CLAUDE.md`** (2026-06-20, `../brainstorm-sync` `c713bf1`): sibling repo stood up (Bun workspace, biome, vitest, tsconfig, `bun.lock`). `CLAUDE.md` pins the invariants — relay-blind (no `@noble/*` / crypto on the route path, CI-fenced like the in-repo relay), ciphertext-only audit, holds no key, imports no product/shell code, speaks only the wire-protocol contract.
- ✅ SYNC-1 — **forward-only relay node (online live layer)** (2026-06-20, `c713bf1`): protocol core (`server` / `router` / `wire` / `audit`) ported from `packages/relay-server`; env-driven `Bun.serve` (`main.ts`), `/healthz` + graceful SIGTERM drain, `Dockerfile` + `.env.example`, `relay.test.ts` + `config.test.ts`. The deployable form of the in-process relay — the live layer `10.12` connects to. **No durability yet.** Admission is **open** behind the dev gate (OQ-SYNC-2 resolved); the entitlement token lands with `SYNC-4`.
- ✅ SYNC-2 — **storage-backed durable node (zero-knowledge)** — *core landed 2026-06-22 (`../brainstorm-sync` `14459c3`).* New `src/sync/`: a pluggable **`SnapshotStore`** (in-memory + durable `FileSnapshotStore`) implementing the **OQ-SYNC-3 snapshot+tail** layout — `Update` frames append to a per-entity tail; a client-uploaded **`Snapshot` frame is client-driven compaction** (bumps the version, resets the tail); the per-entity version is the catalog (`entityId → latest version`). The server persists routed doc-state frames `store`-optionally and, on **subscribe, replays `snapshot ++ tail`** to that connection (**offline backfill** — the client CRDT merges idempotently, so the blind node never needs the client's state vector). The filesystem backend uses base64url-safe entity names (traversal-safe for untrusted wire ids) + atomic snapshot writes + per-entity write serialization. No-store node ⇒ forward-only (SYNC-1) unchanged. Powers `10.14`. **Deferred by design:** the **object-storage backend (R2/S3) is `SYNC-3`** (the `SnapshotStore` interface is the seam); **crypto-based "authorized fetch" is intentionally NOT a node check** — the node is relay-blind (no Ed25519 verify on the route path), so confidentiality is the DEK's job (it serves ciphertext only) and verified admission + `(account, …)` scoping ride **`SYNC-4`**. +12 tests (store contract · OQ-SYNC-3 policy · filesystem durability across a restart · traversal-safety · server backfill/compaction/transient-skip/forward-only); 22 pass, `tsc` + biome clean. **OQ-SYNC-3 ✅.**
- ✅ SYNC-3 — **pluggable storage provider (local / managed / self-hosted)** — *landed 2026-06-23 (`../brainstorm-sync` `66913ec`).* One wire protocol, swappable backend behind the `SnapshotStore`/`AccountCatalog` seam: new `object-store.ts` adds an `ObjectBucket`-backed `ObjectSnapshotStore` + `ObjectAccountCatalog` (the SAME opaque snapshot+tail shape as the local file backend — durability/backfill/cold-restore work identically), and `bun-s3-bucket.ts` is the zero-dep S3/R2/MinIO adapter (Bun's built-in S3 client; not-found→null, paginated list). `main.ts` selects **forward-only** (nothing set) · **local** (`STORAGE_DIR`) · **s3** (`S3_BUCKET`+creds — our managed bucket or a self-hoster's bring-your-own R2/S3/MinIO) from env. The bucket credential is transport auth, not a vault key — relay-blind preserved. **`.bsbundle` export remains the local-only backup.** +11 tests. **OQ-SYNC-1 ✅.**
- ✅ SYNC-4 — **entitlement-gated admission + metering + account catalog** — *SYNC-4b landed 2026-06-23 (`../brainstorm-sync` `66913ec` + product `cbcf7158`).* **SYNC-4a ✅** account catalog (records `sender→entityId`, answers the `catalog` control query). **SYNC-4b ✅** the gated handshake: `entitlement.ts` verifies the `brainstorm-cloud` Ed25519 **entitlement token** (WebCrypto, **offline**, the contract mirrored not imported), and `admission.ts` runs a **two-proof** handshake because the planes don't share ids — (1) the token (`sub` = billing account → admission + plan + quota), **plus** (2) a server **nonce signed by the device identity key** (`account` = base64url pubkey = wire `sender` → proves the wire account). The node challenges on connect, gates frames/subscribe/catalog until authenticated, **scopes the catalog to the proven account** (closes the open-admission metadata leak), checks emission against it (no impersonation), and meters connect/ingress/egress (`metering.ts` → `METERING_LOG_PATH`) for `billing-edge` ingestion. Both verifies are the one reviewed `relay-blind-exempt` (auth, never content); `server.ts` consults only an **injected** `Admission` (type-only import) so the route path stays crypto-free. **Client half** (product `cbcf7158`): `WebSocketRelayPort` gained an injected `onChallenge` (stays relay-blind — ships opaque strings); `challenge-responder.ts` is the credential-aware glue (account + identity-signer + cached token); `BillingService.currentToken()` + the orchestrator `makeRelayPort` wiring read the live session lazily. Open node (no `ENTITLEMENT_KEYS`) ⇒ open admission, wire path unchanged; the client path is dormant until a managed node + a `14.3` token exist. +30 node tests (entitlement/admission/gated-server socket-free/gated real-WS) + 7 product tests. **Resolves the SYNC-4b seam; `brainstorm-cloud` token issuance is `14.3`.** — **dep met: `brainstorm-cloud` api-client token format (`packages/api-client` §EntitlementClaims); OQ-SYNC-2 ✅.**
- ✅ SYNC-5 — **ops** — *landed 2026-06-23 (`../brainstorm-sync` `66913ec`).* `limits.ts` — a pure, injected-clock `Limits` facade over token-bucket `KeyedRateLimiter`s: per-IP connection rate, per-connection message + byte rate, per-account frame rate, and hard caps on frame size / control-message size / subscriptions-per-connection; on by default (`LIMITS_DISABLED=1` to disable), with idle-limiter eviction to bound memory + rejection counters for ops. Audit sink/rotation = the existing `AUDIT_LOG_PATH` NDJSON + external logrotate; deploy manifests = `Dockerfile` + `.env.example`. +8 tests + the SYNC-5 limit assertions in the gated-server suite.

## Encrypted attachment sync — asset byte-plane (Part B)

Goal: realise [data/70-encrypted-attachment-sync.md](data/70-encrypted-attachment-sync.md). The Y.Doc plane (`10.x` + `SYNC-0`–`SYNC-5`) moves **only Y.Docs**; attachment *bytes* have no path off the device. The asset subsystem shipped **Part A** ✅ (per-asset random DEKs, content-addressed `<vault>/data/assets/<id>.enc`, `brainstorm://asset/` serve — see the asset-subsystem bullet under [Bookmarks](#bookmarks-918)); **Part B is the sync transport** for those blobs. Each rung is **post-beta** (it gates no beta-exit item — `9.18.9` captured-image offline assets is the lone product consumer waiting on it). **Blocking OQs: OQ-236 ✅ (resolved Part A, recorded for this review); OQ-237 (cross-app/shared asset access); OQ-238 ✅ (resolved Asset-B4 — no separate `assets.bind` cap, binding folds into entity-write); OQ-239 (orphan-asset reap TTL); asset-DEK re-homing migration ✅ (resolved in Asset-B1 — see [data/70 §Open questions](data/70-encrypted-attachment-sync.md)); cross-device/offline-peer GC ✅ (resolved Asset-B6 — client-reported full ref-sets; grace-mark + last-seen guard + owned-index; see sync PR #2).**

- ✅ Asset-B1 — **asset-DEK re-homing** *(2026-06-26)*: the per-asset DEK now re-homes from the vault-master-key wrap (`asset_deks`) into the referencing entity's Y.Doc, sealed under the **entity DEK** so a paired device that fetches the ciphertext blob can open it. New `credentials/asset-dek-wrap.ts` seals/opens the DEK under the entity DEK with a domain-separated AAD bound to **(entityId, assetId)** — distinct from both the master-key asset-DEK prefix and the entity-DEK prefix, NUL-separated so the id pair can't collide. The wrap lands on the entity doc's `brainstorm.meta → assetDeks` Y.Map (keyed by assetId) via a new crypto-free `ydoc` worker method `installAssetDekWrap` (idempotent, mirrors `installWrap`). An open-time pass (`entities/rehome-asset-deks.ts`, modeled on the 10.x retro-wrap drain) drains every `asset_refs` pair with `rehomed_at IS NULL` (schema **v7** marker → steady-state boot is one empty query): opens the master-key DEK + entity DEK, re-seals, installs, stamps. Per-pair isolation; **defers** (un-stamped, retries next boot) when either DEK is absent; **local-only** stamps non-syncable shell singletons (unsafe ids); every DEK handle zeroed in `finally`. The `asset_deks` master-key row is **left in place as a derived cache** (not deleted). Wired in `onVaultOpened` after the retro-wrap pass; session exposes `assetDekStore()`. +18 tests (codec round-trip + AAD-binding/cross-id; worker set/idempotent/bad-shape; migration re-home/idempotent/defer/local-only; schema v7). Typecheck + targeted suites (assets/entities/credentials/storage/ydoc/vault/integration) green. — **gate: 10.1 entity-DEK ✅ + asset Part A ✅.**
- ✅ Asset-B2 — **`WireKind.Asset` chunked transport** *(2026-06-27)*: the client-side chunked blob transport (`main/assets/asset-{chunks,cas,transport,wire}.ts`). A blob splits into 4 MiB chunks (`ASSET_CHUNK_BYTES`), each independently sealed under the per-asset DEK (the one Asset-B1 re-homed into the entity Y.Doc) with AAD bound to **(assetId, index)** and content-addressed by the **sha256 of its ciphertext** (never plaintext — OQ-236). The seal nonce is a **synthetic IV** (a DEK-keyed HMAC over `domain‖assetId‖u32(index)‖plaintext`, new `sealBytesWithNonce` in `credentials/crypto.ts`): the same chunk re-seals to the same address → stable content-addressing, so `has`-skip + resume work without leaking plaintext equality (the per-asset-random DEK still hides cross-asset/cross-user equality). The ordered manifest `{ v, assetId, chunkBytes, totalRawLen, chunks:[{hash,encLen,rawLen}] }` is the authoritative record (assets are immutable — each upload mints a fresh id, so a blob is chunked once); `parseAssetChunkManifest` validates an untrusted synced manifest fail-closed (64-hex addresses, `totalRawLen == Σ rawLen` over-allocation guard). `AssetCas` (`has`/`put`/`get` by ciphertext-hash) is the node contract; `uploadAsset` seals one chunk at a time (bounded memory), skips chunks already on the node, and returns the manifest; `downloadAsset` fetches+verifies (address + length + AEAD)+opens+reassembles, treating the node as untrusted. The blob-plane wire — a request/response channel DISTINCT from the relay's entity-routed pub/sub — is `AssetWireKind` (`Has`/`Put`/`Get`, `u32`-len JSON header + opaque trailing chunk); `WireAssetCas` adapts `AssetCas` onto a round-trip transport and `serveAssetRequest` is the node-side responder (one protocol, both ends). +49 tests (round-trips across all chunk boundaries + a generative loop; tamper / wrong-DEK / AAD-binding / missing-chunk / lying-node; deterministic-address stability; manifest validation; wire codec + end-to-end upload→wire→download). Typecheck + assets/credentials suites green. **The WS transport binding + writing the manifest onto the entity Y.Doc land with the node in Asset-B3** (you can't upload without a node). — **gate: Asset-B1 ✅; 9.10a chunked upload ✅.**
- ✅ Asset-B3 — **durable-node asset CAS** *(2026-06-27)*: the blob plane on the durable node (`../sync`), the byte-plane analogue of `SnapshotStore` keyed by **ciphertext-hash** instead of entityId. `AssetCas` contract (`has`/`put`/`get`) with a `MemoryAssetCas`, a durable **`FileAssetCas`** (sharded `<aa>/<hash>.bin`, atomic temp+rename, per-hash write serialization, immutable PUT) mirroring `FileSnapshotStore`, and an **`ObjectAssetCas`** (`<prefix>assets/<hash>.bin`) over the same `ObjectBucket` the Y.Doc plane uses — `main.ts` `buildStorage` selects File↔Object from the existing backend choice. The wire is the node's lockstep copy of the Asset-B2 protocol (`asset-wire.ts`: `Has`/`Put`/`Get`, `u32`-len JSON header + opaque trailing chunk) served by `handleAssetRequest`; `server.ts` adds a **third channel byte `0x02`** for the blob plane (request/response, NOT entity-routed fan-out), gated by the same SYNC-4 admission as frames, a PUT metered ingress / a served GET egress (the `14.7` hook). **Relay-blind preserved** — the node stores opaque ciphertext keyed by an opaque hash, computes no hash, holds no key, can't decrypt (integrity is the client's download-side verify; addresses are per-vault-DEK-unique so cross-vault poisoning is impossible); the one address check is `[0-9a-f]{64}` input-sanitization (path-traversal defense, not crypto). The CAS is content-addressed, **not per-chunk ACL'd** (access control = hashes only knowable via the encrypted manifest); per-account ref-tracking for GC is `Asset-B6`. +20 tests (CAS contract over memory+file incl. durability/traversal/concurrency; wire decode+validate; server PUT/GET/HAS round-trip + ingress/egress metering + drop paths); full node suite **104 green**, typecheck + biome clean. — **gate: Asset-B2 ✅; SYNC-2/3/4 ✅ (`../sync`).**
- ✅ Asset-B4 — **lazy fetch + eager thumbnail tier**: materialise bytes on access (not eagerly on restore); small eager tier for thumbnails/previews; integrate the `10.13` selective-sync tiers; `assets.bind` cap (OQ-238) — **gate: Asset-B3 ✅; 10.13 ✅.** **Foundation landed *(2026-06-27)***: the two pieces B2/B3 deferred — (1) the chunk manifest's home on the entity Y.Doc (`workers/ydoc` `installAssetManifest`/`readAssetManifest`, `brainstorm.meta → assetManifests` keyed by assetId, plain metadata that inherits the Y.Doc's transport encryption, idempotent), and (2) the WS binding for the blob plane (`websocket-relay-port` `requestAsset(frame)→Promise<frame>` on a new channel byte `0x02`, request/response distinct from the entity fan-out, **serialized** one-in-flight FIFO correlation, timeout + close-reject; relay-blind preserved, the `WireAssetCas` transport B2 left abstract). +8 tests. **Lifecycle core landed *(2026-06-27)***: the testable orchestration over that plumbing — `asset-sync.ts` `uploadBoundAsset` (chunk+seal+PUT then install the manifest, only after every chunk lands) + `materializeAsset` (read+validate the manifest → fetch+verify+open+reassemble); `relayAssetCas(surface)` binding `WireAssetCas` to the live relay (+ `ActiveRelayOrchestrator.requestAsset` forward); `recover-asset-dek.ts` per-asset DEK recovery (local master-key cache → else the B1 re-homed wrap on the entity Y.Doc, opened with the entity DEK, handles closed in `finally`); `workers/ydoc` `readAssetDekWrap`. **Security (review→fixed)**: `parseAssetChunkManifest` now caps a peer's `totalRawLen`/`chunkBytes` at `MAX_ASSET_RAW_BYTES` (2 GiB) + enforces `rawLen ≤ chunkBytes` + an exact chunk-count check — the untrusted reassembly buffer is allocated up front, so a tiny-chunk multi-GB lie could OOM the victim; rejected before allocation now. +13 tests; 476 assets/sync/ydoc/credentials green (shell PR #8, stacked on #5→#6). **Implicit bind writer landed *(2026-07-01, shell PR #73)***: the missing production writer for `asset_refs` — the table asset-DEK re-homing (Asset-B1), GC reachability, and sync all read, which had **zero call sites** so re-homing was running against an empty table. `derive-asset-refs.ts` (pure) recursively scans an entity's properties for `brainstorm://asset/<id>` URLs (anchored charset, deduped) and maps kind→`AssetRefRole`; `entities-service` `reconcileAssetRefs` runs after a **committed** create/update/delete (never per-keystroke `applyDoc`) and reconciles refs to the row's full post-write properties — create (desired−existing) / `deleteRef` (existing−desired), **filtered to locally-stored assets** so a dangling/remote id never binds, fully contained (a reconcile throw can't fail the committed write), with an explicit prune on soft-delete (the entity FK cascade never fires). Gated on a `getAssetKind` dep = the Asset-B4 feature flag. **This resolves OQ-238 — no separate `assets.bind` cap; binding folds into the entity-write cap the app already holds** (see [OQ-238](reference/11-open-questions.md)), overriding the doc's tentative separate-cap leaning (an explicit bind verb is forgeable-by-omission; implicit derivation can't be skipped and self-heals). +tests (extraction + `deleteRef` + 6 service reconcile cases); lint + shell typecheck clean. **Byte-plane transport wired *(2026-07-03, shell PR #75, stacked on #73)***: the up/download lifecycle onto the live relay. (1) **Manifest `mime`** — `AssetChunkManifest` gains `mime` (threaded through seal/upload; `materializeAsset` returns it); `normalizeManifestMime` validates the untrusted peer field to a strict RFC token (anchored regex → no `Content-Type` injection; bounded), absent → inert `application/octet-stream`, a bad mime fails the whole manifest closed. (2) **Serve-on-miss** (`materialize-on-serve.ts`) — on a `brainstorm://asset/` 404 where the row+ref+DEK are local but the blob **file** is absent (restored DB / evicted blob), resolve the owning entity via `asset_refs`, recover the DEK, read+materialize the manifest, and re-seal into the blob file under the **existing** DEK (`AssetStore.restoreBlob`, content-hash guarded); `serveSafeMime` downgrades script-capable types (svg/html/xml)→octet-stream + `nosniff`. Fully fail-closed. (3) **Upload-on-bind** (`upload-on-bind.ts`) — a connect-time drain over every `asset_refs` pair (`listAllPairs`) pushes chunks + installs the manifest for anything not already on the node (a present manifest is the done-marker); per-pair isolation, DEK zeroed, single in-flight, triggered on relay state once `hasAssetPlane()`. **A schema constraint scoped this:** `asset_refs.asset_id` FK-references `assets`, so a ref can't exist without a local `assets` row — serve-on-miss targets the **metadata-present/blob-absent** case (restore + selective-sync eviction, the "materialise on access" goal); true **cold-first-fetch** needs manifest-driven metadata reconstruction (a stub `assets` row) → a later rung. **Reviews**: adversarial pentest + defensive review found **no exploitable path**; hardened the nice-to-fix items (per-asset materialize dedupe caps the untrusted-`totalRawLen` reassembly-alloc amplification; nosniff). **Deferred (documented)**: owner-scoped access (widens OQ-237 to the fetch path — no key escalation, `recoverDek` only yields DEKs the device holds); selective-sync gating of the upload drain (blind ciphertext only — no plaintext/equality/association leak). +112 tests; lint + shell typecheck clean. **Remaining gate**: a live 2-device relay-loop dogfood (unit-unverifiable). **Scoped 2026-07-27** — the collab dogfood harness has 10 specs (`tests/dogfood/collab/001…010`) covering share, three-way, durable node, wipe+restore, isolation, contention, offline-reconnect, cascade, presence — and **zero asset coverage**, so the blob plane is the one transport never exercised across two real shells. Closing it needs three pieces, in order: (1) asset verbs on the shell's dogfood collab IPC bridge (bind an asset to an entity, materialise by id, read back bytes) — the bridge today exposes only entity/text/share verbs; (2) matching methods on `tests/dogfood/lib/collab-team.ts`; (3) a `011-asset-relay-loop.spec.ts` against `launchDurableNode` proving A-binds → uploads → **B materialises on access** with byte equality, which is precisely the lazy-fetch claim. Budget it as its own session: it is a full Electron build + durable node per run, so the edit→verify loop is minutes, not seconds. The **eager thumbnail tier** needs a native image-resize dependency → split to **Asset-B4b**; **cold-first-fetch metadata reconstruction** → **Asset-B4c**. **Immediate per-bind upload landed *(2026-07-03, shell PR #93, CI green)***: `onAssetBound` post-commit hook (fires ONLY for refs the reconcile created, contained per-invocation) → `uploadBoundAssetNow` single-pair push with per-pair in-flight dedupe against the connect-time drain; shared `assetUploadDeps` builder extracted. +3 service tests. **Relay-loop dogfood landed *(2026-07-28, shell PR #341 + harness same-branch)*** — the remaining gate is CLOSED, live across two real shells through the REAL durable node. (1) Asset verbs on the dogfood collab bridge (`dev:collab:bind-asset`/`asset-status`/`materialize-asset`/`read-asset-local`, thin over new `CollabDevBridge` verbs) whose injected deps are the PRODUCTION paths, not re-implementations: real `AssetStore.writeAsset` mint, a real `entities.update` (as `io.brainstorm.dev.collab` behind an idempotent runtime ledger grant) so the implicit-bind reconciler + post-commit `onAssetBound` push fire, the boot-time DEK re-home pass invoked mid-session, the Asset-B4c reconstruction pass, and serve-on-miss materialise — plus a ydoc-worker cache evict before peer-side reads (the dogfood receiver appends via the main-process doc store, which the worker cache can't see). +6 bridge unit tests (`collab-dev-bridge-assets.test.ts`). (2) Matching `tests/dogfood/lib/collab-team.ts` methods (base64 across the evaluate boundary; `awaitAssetUploaded` polls the manifest upload-done marker). (3) `tests/dogfood/collab/011-asset-relay-loop.spec.ts` against `launchDurableNode`, GREEN: A binds 96 KiB → chunks upload ON BIND (node `STORAGE_DIR` file count grows before the share; console pins `asset uploaded on bind`) → share → converge → B holds NO local bytes (`readAssetLocal` null, no `assets` row) → B materialises ON ACCESS (`asset metadata reconstruct: created 1`) with `source: relay-fetch` and **byte equality** against A's original → the fetch restored the blob locally, so a second access serves `source: local-blob`. That is precisely the lazy-fetch claim. The three gates from data/70 §GC: (1) grace-mark before delete (`ASSET_GC_GRACE_MS`, 30d default; any re-reference or re-PUT un-marks), (2) last-seen guard (`ASSET_GC_RETENTION_MS`, 90d; an account with no within-retention report is skipped entirely), (3) delete only after both, ledger-commit-first (a crash leaks an orphan chunk, never a live entry over deleted bytes). **Owned-index** (recorded on gated PUT, backfilled by reports) + a GLOBAL protected set close the hostile co-claim deletion attack and protect dormant accounts; unattributed pre-B6 chunks are never swept; device entries capped 64/account. `RefLedger` seam with memory/file/object backends riding the SYNC-3 provider choice; `MeterKind.Reclaim` metering; explicit `sweep()` + opt-in `ASSET_GC_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`. ## Mobile companion *(design-only track — development NOT started; design [platform/76-mobile-companion.md](platform/76-mobile-companion.md))*

Goal: the vault in your pocket — capture / triage / reference / reminders on iOS + Android, **as device N+1 on the unchanged Stage-10 + `brainstorm-sync` plane** (no server-side change; no app platform on mobile; explicitly *not* parity, per [01 §Non-goals](foundations/01-vision.md)). The load-bearing architecture call: extract the portable TS vault core (Yjs + `@noble` crypto + wire + sync engine + entity codecs) as **`@brainstorm/vault-core`** behind three platform-adapter seams (SqliteDriver / KeystoreBackend / SocketTransport) — the desktop shell becomes consumer #1, the React-Native companion consumer #2; a forked crypto/sync core is rejected. **This ladder is a separate contributor track with its own owner and its own serial spine (`MOB-0 → MOB-3`)** — it lives outside the Phase-2 serial app policy (own repo boundary, like `../brainstorm-sync`); its only product-repo coupling is the `MOB-1` core extraction (integrator-reviewed shell PR). **Blocking OQs: OQ-MOB-1 (framework — resolve via the `MOB-0` spike, nothing starts first), OQ-MOB-2 (editor strategy), OQ-MOB-5 (repo home / extraction mechanics); OQ-MOB-3/4/6/7 are leaf-local.** No rung below is scheduled; the ladder exists so the track starts decided, not so it starts now.

- ⚪ MOB-0 — **portability spike (the `10.0` analogue)**: bare RN/Expo (Hermes) scaffold pairs with a real desktop shell over the dev relay (QR scan → SAS → sealed identity transfer), subscribes, and merges a real vault's entity Y.Docs; measure `@noble` crypto + Yjs load on Hermes. Exit: ciphertext-only sync proven on-device **and** OQ-MOB-1 confirmed or reopened with numbers — **gate: OQ-MOB-1 position.**
- ⚪ MOB-1 — **`@brainstorm/vault-core` extraction** (product monorepo): identity + DEK/wrap crypto + wire + sync engine + codecs + query store packaged Electron-free behind SqliteDriver/KeystoreBackend/SocketTransport adapters; desktop shell migrates onto the extracted package (no behavior change, full suite green) — **gate: MOB-0; OQ-MOB-5.**
- ⚪ MOB-2 — **companion scaffold + pairing**: `brainstorm-mobile` repo (own CI running the MOB-0 pairing test against a shell build as the skew gate); Keychain/Android-Keystore `KeystoreBackend` (hardware-backed, non-cloud-synced keys); camera pairing flow; device visible + revocable in the desktop roster — **gate: MOB-1.**
- ⚪ MOB-3 — **sync + local store**: `op-sqlite`/`expo-sqlite` driver; metadata-eager / body-lazy selective sync per OQ-MOB-3; lazy asset fetch over the [70](data/70-encrypted-attachment-sync.md) byte-plane; local FTS rebuild — **gate: MOB-2.**
- ⚪ MOB-4 — **read surfaces**: tab scaffold (Home / Search / Capture / Inbox / Vault); the one stacked-layout object screen (cover → icon+title → properties → read-only body → backlinks) rendering every type; Tasks/Journal/Calendar as curated collection views over it; `@brainstorm/tokens` theming — **gate: MOB-3; OQ-MOB-2 (b)-first leaning.**
- ⚪ MOB-5 — **capture**: OS share sheet → `Bookmark/v1` ([58](apps/58-readable-content-extraction.md) object); quick note / task / photo / voice → sealed assets; the **write-without-unlock HPKE capture outbox** (extension holds a vault-scoped public key only; drains into entities on next unlocked launch) — **gate: MOB-3; OQ-MOB-7.**
- ⚪ MOB-6 — **reminders as local notifications**: portable scheduler core (incl. `onMissed: FireOnce` watermark) registers local notifications from synced `Reminder/v1` entities; no push plane (OQ-MOB-4 stays deferred) — **gate: MOB-3.**
- ⚪ MOB-7 — **editing**: property edit + task check-off + append composer first; full block editing via WebView-hosted `@brainstorm/editor` on the same Y.Doc — **gate: MOB-4; OQ-MOB-2.**
- ⚪ MOB-8 — **hardening + store beta**: biometric-gated keystore unlock (gate, never custody — [51](security/51-account-recovery-and-web-auth.md)); app-lock parity (background lock, switcher-snapshot blur, screenshot policy); wire-version skew → read-only degrade; crypto-export self-classification; TestFlight / Play internal track — **gate: MOB-4–MOB-7; OQ-MOB-6.**

# Shell

The privileged surface: Electron main process + the trusted dashboard renderer. Cross-app isolation is the security boundary; the shell owns the ledger, broker, window manager, registry, and every privileged overlay (Settings, Marketplace, Bin, lock screen, help/feedback).

## Window manager, menus & shortcuts *(Stage 6)*

Goal: realise [33](shell/33-windows-and-menus.md) + [24](shell/24-keyboard-shortcuts.md). **OQ-5 → native default chrome, opt-in custom (v2).**

  - ✅ 6.10a — **attach-at-create + layout-invariant match** (landed 2026-05-21). `before-input-event` attach moves to a global `app.on('web-contents-created', …)` listener filtered to `webContents.getType() === "window"` so every Brainstorm BrowserWindow (dashboard + every app + later spawns) is covered by construction — drops the `launchSetup.onSessionRebuilt` indirection that silently missed app windows on certain boot orderings (the `⌘ Shift L`-from-app-window regression). `chordMatchesInput` switches to `code`-first matching for ASCII letters / digits (`KeyL`, `Digit3`) with `key`-based fallback for semantic keys (`Space`, `Enter`, `Escape`, `Arrow*`, `Tab`, punctuation) and when `input.code` is absent — fixes the same chord on AZERTY / Cyrillic / Dvorak without per-layout rebind. +7 chord-match tests (layout-invariant L on AZERTY/Cyrillic, US regression guard, remapped-code negative, digit chords, semantic-key fallback, code-absent fallback); 16/16 shortcut-setup green. New install-time validation: (a) `validateShortcuts` (in `apps/manifest.ts`) now rejects duplicate ids + duplicate normalized chords + non-boolean `shadowsShell` + non-string `scope`; (b) new pure `validateShortcutShellCollisions(manifest, shellChords)` rejects an install/update whose manifest chord collides with a shell-layer chord unless the manifest entry sets `shadowsShell: true` (per docs/24 §App opt-in shadowing). Five touch points. (1) `renderer/shortcuts/chord-capture.ts` — pure `captureChord(event) → { chord, isModifierOnly }`.
