- ✅ **7.14 — app notification badges (iOS-style unread counts on app icons)** — **core shipped 2026-07-22 (shell `dc2d150b`·`b01bfdbf`·`8f33b89d`, feat/7.14-app-badges).** An app paints a badge (numeric count or dot) on its **own** dashboard icon so ambient state is visible without opening it. Delivered: a capability-gated **`services.ui.badge`** (`set(spec)`/`clear`, sibling of the 7.7 `ui.notify` host) with its **own `ui.badge` capability** (OQ resolved — least-privilege, not riding `notifications.post`); a pure `BadgeHost` keyed by the **broker-verified caller** (an app can only badge its own icon; `count<=0` clears; `reset()` on any vault switch/close — per-vault app state); the shell-owned **dashboard icon-corner chip** (count capped `99+` / dot, aria-labelled + attributed, `ui:badges-changed` push mirroring `apps:running-changed`); and **Mailbox as the reference consumer** (mirrors its unified unread count, effect keyed on the derived count). **+35 tests** (BadgeHost 13 · ui-service 15 · icon-chip render 4 + keyboard mock · mailbox regression) · typecheck/biome/css-token/reactivity/i18n clean. **Follow-ups shipped 2026-07-28 (shell PR [#348](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/348), feat/7.14-badge-followups — pending owner merge):** (1) **OS dock/taskbar single owner** — pure `OsBadgeAggregator` (`main/ui/os-badge.ts`) composes notification-unread + the vault-wide countable app-badge total into ONE diffed `app.setBadgeCount` (applier wired once in `main/index.ts`; late-wiring retained; vault switch drops the app half; dots contribute 0 — an uncountable cue never fabricates a dock number). (2) **Consumers** mirroring the Mailbox pattern (cap `ui.badge` + effect keyed on an existing derived count + regression tests each): **Chat** badges others' messages above a per-channel read watermark (`logic/unread.ts`; open channel = continuously read, first observation baselines so history never badges, watermarks persist via `storage.kv`); **Agent** badges pending attention items (staged proposal cards + the open escalation prompt — acting on them drains to 0); **Automations** badges unacknowledged failed/timed-out runs (`logic/failure-badge.ts`; opening the Runs tab acks + prunes, persisted via `storage.kv`). (3) **Running-windows-strip chip** — the grid chip extracted to shared `renderer/dashboard/icon-badge.tsx` (`IconBadge` + `useAppBadges` + `badgeAriaLabel`, reusing the `shell.dashboard.badge.*` ICU keys), consumed by both surfaces; strip-condensed sizing is two CSS deltas on the shared class. **+31 tests** (os-badge 9 · strip-chip 4 · chat unread 12 + 2 app · agent 2 app · automations failure-badge 4 + 2 app) · `bun run verify` 35 files / 408 tests · typecheck (packages+apps+per-app tsc) + lint ratchets clean. Standing *Decide* points: clearing is **app-owned** (no auto-clear on focus); cross-restart persistence rides the consumer re-asserting on mount (push-only, no registry persistence); Agent's in-memory buffer means its badge self-corrects to 0 on next open; Automations deliberately badges historical unacknowledged failures (actionable, unlike chat history).

## Layouts & design system *(Stage 8 + shared fundamentals + covers/pickers)*

Goal: realise [27](shell/27-layouts.md) for `stacked`/`grid` + [13 §Themes](shell/13-frontend-stack.md) (Phosphor + typography). Contracts are frozen in `@brainstorm/sdk-types`; render-application halves are renderer-locked. **OQ-71 resolved (Phosphor); OQ-67/72 non-blocking; OQ-85..90 see [27](shell/27-layouts.md).**

- ✅ 8.1 / 8.2 — `Layout/v1` contract freeze + layout resolver (`@brainstorm/sdk/layout-resolver`, scope-precedence chain).
- ✅ 8.5 — `validateAppLayouts` wired into install-time manifest validation: the shell's ad-hoc shallow layout check is replaced by the frozen `@brainstorm/sdk-types` contract (single source of truth, DRY), fed the app-owned entity-type ids so doc 27 §App-shipped-defaults is enforced at install — non-empty + app-owned `type`, valid `LayoutContext`, no duplicate `(type,context)`, well-formed `config` body. No first-party app ships `layouts:` so zero install regression; +4 contract tests (ForeignType / malformed-config / valid-owned / context).
- ✅ 8.6 — `IconPack/v1` render-application complete: `<Icon>` + `createIconElement` (Phosphor base) now resolve through the frozen sdk-types contract — `setActiveIconPack`/`resolveIconOverride` (epoch-invalidated resolver-cache) + `useIcon` (useSyncExternalStore) make an installed pack override individual canonical glyphs over the built-in base (same base/override layering as 8.7 Typography). Default = no pack → byte-identical to before across all 11 apps (zero regression); +16 tests. Pack-install UX is marketplace/theme-editor surface (9.x), not this contract.
- ✅ 8.7 — `Typography/v1`: contract ✅ (sdk-types) + **render-application ✅** — `typographyCssVars` resolves the frozen contract into the `--text-family-{ui,body,code,display}` vars the renderer already consumes (+ `--typography-scale`), applied by ThemeProvider as the **base layer** under the per-theme `text.family` tokens (Sepia serif etc. preserved → zero visual regression; never-empty per `resolveFontStack`; 5 tests). The v1 deliverable (contract + render-application against system stack) is complete — theme-editor wiring (a user `TypographyDef` source) is its own iteration at **9.9** and is not part of 8.7's scope.
- ✅ 8.3 — **the `Layout/v1` render pipeline** *(shell branch `feat/8.3-layout-render-pipeline`, 2026-07-25)*. 8.2's `resolveLayout` already picked which layout wins; nothing rendered it. **`@brainstorm-os/sdk/layout-view` → `<LayoutView>`** closes that: property values through the shared cell registry (a cell's `display` override beats the property's default view), groups with their own nested mode, text / divider inline, and two host seams — `renderBlock` (the BlockEmbed bridge is app-side, doc 15) and `renderChrome` (8.4's registry). Modes are CSS: `stacked` a flex column, `grid` CSS-Grid from each cell's `{col,row,colSpan,rowSpan}` (collapsing to stacked under 640px, per doc 27 §grid), `freeform` an absolutely positioned canvas that sizes itself to its content. `condition` runs through the shared `evaluatePredicate` — the Database filter language, never a second mini-language. **Two load-bearing decisions.** (1) **DOM order IS reading order** — doc 27 makes `readingOrder` the a11y contract precisely because grid/freeform position via CSS, which says nothing about traversal; so the plan orders the DOM by `effectiveReadingOrder` and lets CSS move cells visually, and screen readers + `Tab` follow the contract by construction with no parallel aria-order to keep in sync. Ordering is applied per sibling group, so nested groups keep their containment and their nested modes. (2) **One property cell = one subscription** — `LayoutValueSource` is a two-method contract (`get` + per-key `subscribe`) the host implements over its own store (Yjs in an app, a plain object in a preview); each cell reads its key through `useSyncExternalStore`, so a write to `email` repaints the email cell and nothing else. **This is what 8.10.2's per-cell subscriptions were gated on.** A cell whose seam has no host renderer, or whose property has no schema, renders a *visible* placeholder — a silently dropped cell reads as a layout bug with no clue where it went. +43 tests; the css-token ratchet caught three phantom tokens in the new stylesheet before they shipped. **Gate: none.**
- ✅ 8.4 — **chrome cells + OQ-90 resolved** *(shell branch `feat/8.3-layout-render-pipeline`, 2026-07-25)*. **`@brainstorm-os/sdk/layout-chrome`** draws the six kinds 8.1 froze — `actionBar` / `breadcrumb` / `meta` / `windowControls` / `entityHeader` / `tabs` — so doc 27's decision ("the shell renders no fixed chrome outside of the layout system") is finally true in code. Host wiring is one call: `chromeSeam(host)` as `<LayoutView seams.renderChrome>`. **OQ-90 resolved as (a): the set is shell-curated and CLOSED.** A chrome cell is shell-rendered by definition (active theme, shared menu runtime, shell a11y semantics); a kind an app registered would have none of that, and would make a layout's portability depend on which apps happen to be installed. The escape hatch already exists and is honest about what it is — a `block` cell the app renders itself. Enforced structurally: `renderChromeCell` is exhaustive over `ChromeKind`, so a seventh kind is a compile error until it has a renderer. Marked `*[RESOLVED in implementation-plan Stage 8.4]*` in [11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md). **Split of responsibility:** the SDK owns the kinds and how they render; the **host owns the data** (its actions, its breadcrumb trail, its tabs) — chrome cannot know an app's navigation, and an app should not redraw the shell's chrome. `More` opens the shared object menu *via the host*, so the SDK never owns menu policy. `ChromeCell.options` is deliberately `Record<string, unknown>` in the frozen contract, so each kind gets a typed reader that falls back rather than faults — a hand-edited `alignment: "sideways"` degrades instead of breaking the render. +31 tests, driven through `<LayoutView>`'s seam (how a host actually wires it) rather than the components in isolation. **Gate: none.**
- ✅ 8.8 — `@react-fancy-menus/core` swap-in **landed (2026-06-01)**, brought forward once the dep published (`@react-fancy-menus/core@0.1.0`). New `@brainstorm/sdk/menus` subpath wraps the dep (OQ-32: SDK pins the exact version): `BrainstormMenuProvider` owns one `MenuStore`, wires the shortcut-suppression seam (`store.isOpen()` → `isAnyShortcutSuppressed`, the contract `shortcut/suppression.ts` was built for) and pushes open menus onto the renderer-wide `getEscapeStack()` for LIFO Escape nesting with `<Popover>`; `menus.css` bridges `--fm-*` onto Brainstorm tokens (reactive on theme switch, glass backdrop) + a scoped utility shim so the dep's Tailwind-based panels render in a non-Tailwind app; an imperative `openContextMenu` + `mountMenuHost()` bridge serves non-React call sites. **Migrated**: cheatsheet + launcher (ComposedBody search + sectioned list, fed via `updateData`), dashboard icon context menu (`openContextMenu`), and the shared `openAnchoredMenu` — which routes every app's object menu, the graph export menu, and the database/tasks column-adder through the bridge, with a no-host DOM fallback. All 11 apps call `mountMenuHost()` (menu CSS arrives centrally via `app-theme.css`). **Verified in the production shell** (tests/perf): cheatsheet, launcher, icon context menu, and the graph export menu in a sandboxed app window — open / filter / Escape. Resolves **OQ-33**. **Deliberately not migrated** (dialogs/modals, not menus — kept on `<Popover>`/native): the open-with intent prompt, the icon picker; the OS-native tray (main-process, would need a new renderer tray window — stays post-v1 per OQ-TRAY-1).

## Keyboard accessibility *(KBN ladder — [61-keyboard-accessibility.md](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md))*

Goal: the whole product is reachable, operable, and orientable from the keyboard alone — Tab order, arrow-key composite navigation, focus traps, focus restoration, visible-focus, Escape stack, region (`F6`) jumps, and the screen-reader scaffolding that pairs with all of it. The non-chord half of keyboard handling — chords stay in [24-keyboard-shortcuts.md](shell/24-keyboard-shortcuts.md) / the `6.10` ladder. **Decomposed into one shared substrate (`KBN-1..4`), one rung per shell surface (`KBN-S-*`), and one rung per first-party app (`KBN-A-*`)** — same pattern as `B9` find/replace and `B8` nav-history.

**Gates (both 🟢 post-v1; the v1 ladder ships in-tree primitives against the same call-site contract per [[feedback_avoid_blocking_on_deps]]):** `8.8` `@react-fancy-menus/core` (menu keyboard nav — swap-in for context / launcher result / cheatsheet / object-menu / slash-menu bodies) and `8.9` `react-aria` non-menu primitives (dialog / listbox / combobox / popover keyboard — swap-in for the SDK hooks below). **OQ-KBN-1..6.**

Per-app priority follows the [[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]] order — shell rungs land first, app rungs interleave with each app's serial slot.

- ✅ **KBN-1 — `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` substrate.** *(2026-05-27 — all three rungs landed.)* New subpath: `useCompositeKeyboard` (roving-tabindex, vertical/horizontal/grid orientation, Home/End/Page/Enter/Space/type-ahead — the doc-61 composite-listbox contract), `useTreeKeyboard` (collapse/expand + level-aware arrows), `useFocusTrap` (modal trap + initial-focus + restore-on-close + onEscape), `useRegionNavigation` (F6 / Shift+F6 across major panes — registers `shell/region.next` / `shell/region.previous` in the chord registry per [24] §Region jumps), `useFocusVisible` (JS twin of `:focus-visible` for surfaces that need to react in JS), `announce(message)` writing into a shell-mounted polite/assertive `aria-live` region. Six exports cover ~95% of the composite-keyboard surface in this codebase. Includes typed `Orientation` enum + `RegionId` enum + `KbnAnnouncePoliteness` enum per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]]. **Ungated; no new IPC/capability/network.** Three rungs:
  - ✅ **KBN-1a — controller + tests.** *(2026-05-27)* Pure logic for `useCompositeKeyboard` + `useTreeKeyboard` + `useFocusTrap` + `useRegionNavigation`, no DOM observation. New subpath `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` with seven source files (`orientation` / `region-id` / `announce-politeness` enums, `composite-keyboard` / `tree-keyboard` / `focus-trap` / `region-navigation` controllers, `index`) and four test files; +69 tests (composite 31 incl. wrap/no-wrap × orientation × disabled-skip + grid-row + page + typeahead property tests · tree 14 incl. flat-walk, collapse/expand, parent navigation · focus-trap 12 incl. LIFO property over random push/unsubscribe interleavings · region-navigation 12 incl. 4× cycle returns home + wrap). SDK 860/860 green; workspace `tsc` clean; biome clean on touched files.
  - ✅ **KBN-1b — DOM bindings.** *(2026-05-27)* Five React hooks (`useCompositeKeyboard` / `useTreeKeyboard` / `useFocusTrap` / `useRegionNavigation` / `useFocusVisible`) on top of the KBN-1a reducers + a `<LiveRegion>` shell-mount in `dashboard.tsx` driving `announce(message, { politeness })`. Module-scope focus-trap stack (one per renderer) so KBN-2's Escape handler can pop topmost-first; trap is StrictMode-safe (LIFO test covers a sequential outer→inner open and unwind). `useFocusVisible` is the JS twin of `:focus-visible` (document-level modality tracker, keyboard vs pointer). Shared `createTypeaheadBuffer` helper with ≤500ms reset + same-char cycling. ### AppForge — apps built inside Brainstorm become real apps *(`AppForge-*`; sideload install path, OQ position in [foundations/49-self-hosting.md](foundations/49-self-hosting.md))*

Goal: close the loop from "app authored inside (or next to) Brainstorm" to "installed, launchable app" — user-chosen bundles flow through the same `AppInstaller` trust chokepoint as catalog installs, quarantined as unsigned/local rather than blocked (v1 advisory signature policy). This is the install half the flagship "build an app inside Brainstorm" video needs.

- ✅ AppForge-1 — **install from a local folder or `.brainstorm` file** (shell #364). New `apps:install-from-folder` / `apps:install-from-file` IPC (privileged: dashboard-sender-gated fail-closed, typed `SideloadInstallResult`, `InstallOrigin.LocalFile` provenance, dashboard icon pinned like catalog installs) + Marketplace toolbar "Install from…" menu + unsigned-advisory surfaced in listings/detail. Hostile-input hardening: manifest size-bound + fail-closed validator, archive size-bound before read, decompression-expansion bound (`unpackBundle maxOutputBytes`, gzip-bomb defense), tar zip-slip guard exercised from the install call site. Packaged-path fixes ride along: marketplace first-party resolution via `process.resourcesPath/apps` when `app.isPackaged` (was an asar-relative walk that doesn't exist), and `reinstallFirstPartyApp` never spawns `vite build` in a packaged shell (`prebuiltOnly` installs the extraResources bundle with `bootstrap-cache` provenance).
- ✅ AppForge-2 — **install-from-vault** *(2026-07-29, shell #366)*: the app you wrote in the code editor installs straight from the vault — no folder, no zip, no OS filesystem round-trip. **Seam decision: the affordance lives in the dashboard, not the code-editor app** — Marketplace → *Install from…* → *From vault code files…* opens a shell-rendered picker over the vault's `CodeFile/v1` rows. An app-side entry point (intent verb or cap-gated forwarder) would add a new app-reachable surface whose only purpose is reaching a privileged action, and it would not remove the need for shell-owned consent (an app can be driven, so an app-side confirm is worthless); the dashboard placement gives the identical flow with **zero new app surface**, and a code-editor entry point can dispatch to the same handler later without changing the trust story. Two handlers, both dashboard-sender-gated: `apps:list-vault-app-sources` (groups CodeFiles into candidates by their shallowest `manifest.json`, validates each manifest **server-side**) and `apps:install-from-vault` (**entity ids only on the wire** — type, path and content all resolved server-side per the resolve-type-server-side rule → `mkdtemp` materialise → the same `AppInstaller.install` with `InstallOrigin.LocalFile` → icon pin → typed result; staging removed in `finally`). Path handling is an **allowlist, not a scrub** (`sanitizeVaultRelPath`): rejects absolute/drive-letter/backslash (Windows-separator ambiguity refused rather than normalised), `.`/`..`/empty segments, control chars, >512 chars or >16 segments; around it, exactly one shallowest manifest (two roots → `no-manifest`), every file under that root, case-insensitive duplicate + file-vs-directory conflict rejection, per-write `resolve()` containment re-check, ≤256 files, ≤4 MiB/file, ≤32 MiB total. Confirm sheet reuses the shared consent chrome (name · id · version · requested capabilities · unsigned advisory). +10 tests (23 total in `sideload-handlers.test.ts`, real stores/repos/ledger/installer with only Electron mocked; the happy path asserts installed bytes **and** that the source entities are untouched); `bun run verify` + typecheck + lint green. **Residue:** ~~proven at the IPC/installer layer — the real-shell pass (write in Code editor → install → launch) is owed~~ **real-shell pass DONE 2026-07-29** via the `VID-build-apps` capture dry-run (write two files in the Code editor → picker lists the candidate → consent sheet → install → launch → the app renders real seeded entities; see the `VID-build-apps` rung); bundles are text-only (a `CodeFile` body is a string, so binary assets still need the folder/`.brainstorm` path); reinstall over an existing id still returns `already-installed` (no update-from-vault path yet, inherited from AppForge-1).
- ✅ AppForge-3 — **the agent's eighth staged-artifact kind: `propose-code-file`** *(2026-07-29, shell #365)*. The agent can now DRAFT a `brainstorm/CodeFile/v1` (path + language + content) as an approvable tray card, under the identical propose→approve contract as the other seven verbs — approve is exactly **one** `entities.create`, discard writes nothing, and the model can never save on its own. Args are hardened at staging (`logic/propose-code-file.ts`): `path` through the SDK `sanitizeInlineText` (control/zero-width/bidi strip + 200-char clamp, same treatment as the code-editor's rename) with empty refused; `content` **refused, not truncated**, above `CODE_FILE_CONTENT_MAX` (256 KiB); `language` validated against the `CodeLanguage` enum else inferred from extension/shebang, degrading to PlainText. Double-gated: offered only with `entities.write:brainstorm/CodeFile/v1` **and** `intents.dispatch:propose-code-file` through `intersectAgentTools` (both added to the agent manifest, consented at install). **The create shape is the code-editor's own**: v1 keeps source text in the `content` property and `code-pane.ts` seeds the Y.Doc `Y.Text("content")` buffer from it on first open — so an approved file opens cleanly in Code (verified in the real shell, not just tests). Tray preview reuses the shipped Shiki tokenizer via `@brainstorm-os/sdk/code-highlight`, **dynamic-imported** so shiki stays out of the agent's initial chunk, rendering as inert React text nodes (injection-tested); the `LanguageKey→shiki-id` map was extracted to `@brainstorm-os/sdk/language-detect` at copy two and code-editor now delegates to it. Capture-only demo sequence behind `BRAINSTORM_DEMO_AGENT=appforge` (proposes `hello-app/manifest.json` + `hello-app/index.html`) so the `VID-build-apps` agent act is drivable — *fixed 2026-07-29 (shell `fix/vid-build-apps-capture`): the scripted manifest omitted `sdk`, so the approved files failed `validateManifest` and `apps:install-from-vault` refused them (`Invalid manifest: sdk must be a string ($.sdk)`) — caught by the real-shell capture dry-run, not by the staging tests, because staging only checks path+content shape. A regression test now runs the real validator over the scripted manifest.* +15 dedicated tests (injection renders as text, oversized refused, tool absent without cap/grant, approve = exactly one create, discard = none, traversal-shaped path stays inert vault text) inside 942 green across agent/code-editor/sdk/shell-ai; typecheck + all lint ratchets clean. Residue: no shared `IconName` code glyph (card uses `KindText`) — SDK glyph is a possible follow-up.

## Network broker & readable extraction *(doc 38 + 58 — gates Bookmarks 9.18.5/.6, Feedback-1/2, Mailbox-1, Browser-1, Automations)*

Realises [security/38-network-and-proxy.md](security/38-network-and-proxy.md) (the shell-mediated egress broker) and [apps/58-readable-content-extraction.md](apps/58-readable-content-extraction.md) (clean page-content capture). Default is zero outbound; every request is declared, capability-gated, per-vault-toggled and egress-audited. Consolidates the previously-nameless "gated on network broker" dependency referenced by Feedback-1/2, Mailbox-1, Browser-1, Automations.

- ✅ Net-1a — network-broker core slice (foundation half) ✅ landed 2026-05-24 across four steps: step 0 SSRF guard primitive (`9d05560`) + step 2 core `executeNetworkFetch` + audit log (`7993d28`) + step 3 broker service handler + SDK proxy + production bindings (`cab33f6`) + step 4 `network.preview` HEAD probe with OG/Twitter/JSON-LD extractor (`8a66465`). **Net-1b (`.private` cap surface) ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: `network.fetch.private` capability widens the SSRF guard to accept private / loopback / link-local addresses for callers who hold it; public-only callers stay byte-identical (zero regression). Five touch points. (1) `packages/shell/src/main/network/ssrf-guard.ts` — `checkUrl` + `checkResolvedIp` accept a new `SsrfCheckOptions = { allowPrivate?: boolean }` arg. When set, the `LocalHostname` pre-DNS rejection (`localhost`, `*.local` mDNS, `*.localhost`) AND the `PrivateIp` post-DNS / IP-literal rejection (RFC1918 + loopback + link-local + IPv6 ULA) flip to accepts. The hard floor — `NonHttpScheme` (file:/javascript:/data:), `MalformedUrl`, `BlockedPort` (SSH/SMTP/DNS/DB ports), `IdnDecodeFailed`, `MalformedIp` — remains unconditional; `.private` only relaxes private-network reach, never the URL floor. (2) `packages/shell/src/main/network/network-service.ts` — `NetworkFetchRequest` gains `allowPrivate?: boolean`; `executeNetworkFetch` threads it through to both SSRF checks. (3) `packages/shell/src/main/network/network-service-handler.ts` — exports `NETWORK_FETCH_PRIVATE_CAP = "network.fetch.private"` + private `hasPrivateCap(envelope)` helper. Both `handleFetch` + `handlePreview` read `envelope.caps`; when the widener is present they pass `allowPrivate: true` to the executor. Header doc lifted to explain the dual-cap model: `network.fetch` is the umbrella permit, `.private` is the scope-widener never standalone. (4) `packages/sdk-types/src/index.ts` `NetworkFetchInput` gains the public `allowPrivate?: boolean` opt-in. (5) `packages/sdk/src/runtime.ts` `networkProxy.fetch` conditionally includes `network.fetch.private` in the envelope's declared caps when the caller passed `allowPrivate: true`. The broker enforces both caps are user-granted; an app whose manifest doesn't declare `.private` gets a `Denied` from the broker before the handler runs. **Tests +27**: `ssrf-guard.test.ts` +18 (allowPrivate accepts `localhost` / `*.local` / RFC1918 literals / IPv6 `::1` / fc00::1 / cloud-metadata `169.254.169.254` / 10.0.0.0 / 192.168.x; floor still rejects javascript:/file:/blocked-ports/malformed-URLs/malformed-IPs; public IPs still pass without the option; private IPs still rejected without the option). `network-service-handler.test.ts` +9 (cap-gated handler tests: with `.private` cap → fetch to a private IP succeeds + literal RFC1918 URL succeeds + `.local` preview succeeds + public IP still works; without `.private` → private IP refused as Denied + literal RFC1918 URL refused; `.private` does NOT relax non-HTTP schemes + blocked ports; audit log records the private host honestly — `.private` doesn't hide audit). 158/158 across `network/` (was 131 — +27 net); full shell 2535/2535 green; workspace `tsc:packages` + `tsc:apps` clean; biome clean on touched files. **Net-1c (per-(canonicalUrl, locale) preview cache) ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: wraps `network.preview` in a process-singleton 24h TTL cache with 1024-entry LRU. Cache hits skip the egress entirely — no SSRF, no DNS, no audit-log entry; misses fall through to the executor + store the result. Three touch points. (1) `packages/shell/src/main/network/preview-cache.ts` — pure `LinkPreviewCache` class with `get` / `set` / `clear` / `prune` / `size`; `cacheKey(canonicalUrl, locale)` exported; `DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 24h`, `MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE = "en"`. Injected clock for deterministic TTL tests (no `vi.useFakeTimers`). LRU promote on `get` AND `set` (re-cache resets TTL clock); lazy prune on expired `get`; proactive `prune()` available. (2) `packages/shell/src/main/network/network-service-handler.ts` — `NetworkServiceOptions.previewCache?: LinkPreviewCache` optional injection; `validatePreviewArgs` accepts `locale?: string`; `handlePreview` consults the cache before any egress and stores the result against both `args.url` AND the post-extractor `preview.canonicalUrl` (hit symmetry — pasting either form is a hit). When no cache is wired, behaviour is byte-identical to the pre-Net-1c world. (3) `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` — `new LinkPreviewCache()` singleton wired into `makeNetworkServiceHandler`; production caches across vault switches within one process; `clear()` will be called from Settings → Privacy when Net-1f lands. SDK surface widened: `NetworkService.preview({url, locale?})` per the new contract. **Tests +25**: `preview-cache.test.ts` 17 (key composition; get/set/clear; locale-keyed; re-set replaces; TTL lazy prune; just-inside TTL; custom TTL; proactive prune; re-cache re-anchors TTL clock; LRU eviction at cap; LRU touch on get; re-cache doesn't trip cap; default `MAX_ENTRIES` cap is real). `network-service-handler.test.ts` +8 (cache hit skips fetch + audit; cache miss falls through + stores; distinct locales mint distinct entries; TTL expiry forces fresh fetch; no cache → pre-Net-1c byte-identical; hits don't write audit log; `clear()` resets; invalid locale args → Invalid before any fetch). 183/183 across `network/` (was 158 — +25 net); full shell 2560/2560 green; workspace `tsc:packages` + `tsc:apps` clean; biome clean on touched files. **Net-1c periodic prune scheduler ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: the cache's `prune()` method existed but wasn't called anywhere — expired entries lingered in memory until the LRU cap evicted them. New `packages/shell/src/main/network/preview-cache-scheduler.ts` exports `schedulePreviewCachePrune({cache, intervalMs?, intervals?})` returning `{stop, totalPruned}`. Default cadence is 30 minutes — well shorter than the 24h TTL (entries don't pile up for a full day) and long enough that the O(n)-over-MAX_ENTRIES walk is microseconds of CPU. Production wiring in `main/index.ts` schedules the pruner alongside the cache singleton and tears it down on `before-quit`. The scheduler accepts an injectable `IntervalFactory` so unit tests use a manual ticker (no fake timers). **Tests +6**: scheduler default interval, custom intervalMs, tick calls cache.prune + accumulates totalPruned, stop cancels the interval, stop is idempotent (no double-clear), totalPruned only counts actual evictions. 206/206 across `network/` (was 200 — +6 net); workspace `tsc:packages` clean; biome clean.

**Net-1c privacy hardening (preview cache cleared on vault switch) ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: `previewCache` declaration moved to the top of the `app.whenReady` IIFE so the `onVaultOpened` callback (defined further down) can call `previewCache.clear()` without a TDZ boundary when the boot vault is already open at start. Closes a privacy gap where vault A's cached `network.preview` snapshots could surface in vault B's session — the cache is process-singleton in-memory, so wiping on every vault switch is the simplest privacy-safe behaviour and stays well under the 24h TTL boundary. Idempotent (a no-op when the cache is already empty). 2535/2535 across the full shell unchanged; workspace `tsc:packages` clean.

**Net-1 audit log rotation ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: `makeFileAuditSink` now rotates the network-audit JSONL file when it crosses a size threshold so the production audit file doesn't grow unbounded. Three pieces. (1) `DEFAULT_AUDIT_ROTATE_BYTES = 10 MiB` constant (Net-1 audit panel is for recent investigation, not long-term forensics — one generation of history is enough). (2) New `FileAuditSinkOptions = { rotateBytes? }` and a new exported `rotatedPathFor(path)` helper that turns `foo.jsonl` → `foo.1.jsonl` (falls back to `<path>.1` when no recognisable extension). (3) `makeFileAuditSink` tracks the current file size locally (one `stat` on first write to pick up a previous-session file; subsequent writes add the line's byte length so we don't `stat` on every append). When the next line would push past the cap, the sink unlinks any stale `.1.jsonl` (Windows can't replace via `rename`), renames the current file to `.1.jsonl`, and starts a fresh empty file. Rotation failure is non-fatal — logged + we keep appending past the cap for this session (a disk-full / permission issue surfaces in the console without breaking egress audit). **Tests +17**: `audit-log.test.ts` covers `rotatedPathFor` × 3 (canonical extension shift; no-extension fallback; long-extension fallback); `hostOf` / `pathOf` × 5 (query / fragment hygiene + default ports + non-default ports + malformed-URL defensiveness); basic append × 3 (single line, multiple lines, picks up existing on-disk size); rotation × 6 (rotates over cap; second rotation overwrites the first archive; doesn't rotate under cap; default 10 MiB constant; two rotations in a row; happy-path smoke). 200/200 across `network/` (was 183 — +17 net); workspace `tsc:packages` clean; biome clean on touched files.

**Net-1d (proxy config keystone) ✅ landed 2026-05-25**: third Net-1 slice — `ProxyConfig` discriminated union (Direct / System / Manual / Pac per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]]) is the one source of truth shared by every shell egress path (network broker, update, AI broker, sync transport, embed sandbox) per doc-38 §Decision "one proxy configuration". Three pieces. (1) `packages/shell/src/main/network/proxy-config.ts` — pure keystone with `ProxyMode` enum + `ProxyEndpoint{host, port, authKey?}` + `validateProxyConfig(unknown)` (every field strictly typechecked, returns `{ok:false, error: ProxyConfigError, detail}` on every rejection — `MissingMode` / `InvalidMode` / `MalformedEndpoint` / `InvalidPort` / `EmptyHost` / `MalformedNoProxyPattern` / `MalformedPacUrl` / `MissingPacUrl`) + `matchesNoProxy(host, patterns)` (exact / leading-dot suffix / leading-star glob / IPv4 CIDR /0–/32 / `*` full bypass; IPv6 falls back to exact-string match) + `resolveEffectiveProxy(config, url)` (emits `Direct` / `Http` / `Https` / `Socks5` or `Deferred` when System / PAC require Electron's session resolver) + `ProxyResolutionError` + `ProxyResolutionErrorKind` (`Unreachable` / `PacEvaluationFailed` / `AuthFailed` / `TlsHandshakeFailed`) mirroring `NetworkFetchError`'s broker-mapping shape. `authKey` is an opaque per-vault credential-store lookup key (`proxy.<host>:<port>` per doc-29) — never an inline password (Net-1e wires the credential-store side). (2) `packages/shell/src/main/network/network-service-handler.ts` — `NetworkServiceOptions` grows `getProxyConfig?: () => ProxyConfig` + `applyProxyConfig?: ApplyProxyConfig`. When both are present `makeNetworkServiceHandler` calls `applyProxyConfig(config)` before the first request and on every config change; idempotence is keyed on `JSON.stringify(config)` so a stable session config triggers `setProxy` exactly once. Apply runs before fetch + preview, so a stale Chromium proxy can't service an SSRF-refused request either. `productionApplyProxyConfig` calls `session.defaultSession.setProxy` with the Chromium-flavoured `{mode: 'fixed_servers', proxyRules: "http=h:p;https=h:p;socks=h:p", proxyBypassRules}` shape for Manual / `{mode:'system'}` / `{mode:'direct'}` / `{mode:'pac_script', pacScript}`. The mapping is exposed as `electronProxyConfigFor(config)` for testability — the session-side call is the only Electron-touching line. `authKey` intentionally never serialised into `proxyRules` (assert in tests). (3) `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` — network broker registration passes `getProxyConfig: () => DEFAULT_PROXY_CONFIG` (System mode) + `applyProxyConfig: productionApplyProxyConfig`. PAC scope per spec: plumbing only — Electron's built-in `session.resolveProxy` consults the PAC URL natively; a custom evaluator stays deferred. **Tests +63**: `proxy-config.test.ts` 49 (every validator error variant + `matchesNoProxy` table + `resolveEffectiveProxy` per-mode + `ProxyResolutionError`); `network-service-handler.test.ts` +13 (proxy apply on first request, idempotent re-call, re-applies on change, applies on preview path, no-op when half-wired, runs before SSRF; `electronProxyConfigFor` per mode + authKey-never-leaked). 269/269 across `network/` (was 206 — +63 net).

Adversarial tests expanded in `sanitize-html.test.ts` / `extract-html.test.ts`: mutation XSS via SVG nesting; `<style>@import` + `expression()` legacy CSS; `javascript:` / `data:text/html;base64,…` in href/src/srcset; `on*` smuggling via attribute namespaces (`xlink:href`, `xml:base`); polyglot HTML/JS payloads (doctype-less SVG browsers parse as HTML); malformed UTF-8 in attr values (`%c0%80` null-byte smuggling); HTML-entity-encoded `javascript&colon;` URLs (entity-decoded only after the floor); base64 payloads in `<img src=…>`; `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=javascript:…">`; quoting-style confusion in attributes (`href=javascript:alert(1)//"` with no closing quote). Each adversarial input has both a "passes" expectation (sanitised output is safe) **and** a "doesn't strip too much" expectation (legitimate links survive). Net-2e closes the Net-2 row.
- ✅ Net-3 — **live-DOM feeder** *(shell `feat/net-3-live-dom`, 2026-07-24; gate Browser-1 ✅)*: the partitioned `WebContentsView`'s **rendered** DOM goes to the **same Net-2 extraction worker** the static `network.readable` feeder uses, so an in-browser read and a fetched URL agree on one shape (OQ-RX-5 — one captured-page object everywhere). Why the live DOM and not a re-fetch: the page on screen is often not the page a second GET returns (login-gated, script-rendered, personalised), so re-fetching would silently capture something else — and reading what's already rendered costs no extra egress. `ManagedWebView.captureHtml()` is the Electron half (page's own isolated world; a destroyed/internal/script-blocked page yields null rather than throwing into the capture path); `web-live-dom.ts` is the pure half — the 8M-char DOM clamp before the parser and the ~1 MB text cap from **OQ-RX-2**, with truncation **flagged on the result** rather than silently elided. A suspended tab reports "nothing" instead of being re-mounted behind the user's back to answer a read. First consumer is Browser-8's `ExtractText` (now production-bound); `capture` → `Bookmark/v1` (Browser-5's half) binds the same way.

Earlier scoped post-v1 then removed-to-separate-effort (2026-05-30); now fully superseded by Net-3 and no longer a tracked rung. **OQ-RX-7** retired with it.

(32 KiB cap) / appId? / routePath? / recentLogExcerpt (64 KiB tail) / clientVersion / clientPlatform / capturedAt / submittedAt? / requestId / installationId / durationSinceBootMs). `redactCrashPayload(payload, {vaultPath})` applies the **same substitution rules as Feedback-1's `redactPayload`** — vault → `<vault>`, home → `<home>/`, credentials → `<credential>`, emails → `<email>`. (2) `crash-queue.ts` — `<userData>/crash-reports/<requestId>.json` one-file-per-crash queue; atomic write via tmp + fsync + rename; malformed JSON or invalid-shape files are logged + skipped; idempotent `remove`; `prune(maxAgeMs=30 days, maxCount=100)` two-axis cap keeping newest. (3) `crash-reporter-service.ts` — composes queue + network-broker fetcher + redactor; never broker-exposed. `capture(input)` resolves vault path lazily. **Privacy invariant**: when `crashReportingEnabled === false`, hooks fire but only increment a local counter (kind + capturedAt); full payload + stack + log excerpt enqueue only when the opt-in is on. `submitPending` drains the queue via `executeNetworkFetch` with the privileged `__crash__` sentinel `appId`; 2xx → remove, 4xx → drop + log, 5xx / transport → leave for the next pass. (5) Settings store extension — `FeedbackSettingsStore` grows `crashReportingEnabled: boolean` (default false) + `lastCrashSubmitAttemptMs: number | null`. ## Onboarding & starter content *(group G — first-launch UX)*

Realises [28 §First-launch flow](foundations/28-vault-and-onboarding.md)'s promise that a fresh vault is a *working, populated* vault — not an empty grid with a "now go install some apps" empty state. Two rungs: a tiny baked-in starter set every new vault gets, and an opt-in gallery of curated full-vault templates for common use-cases. Both ride the existing entities-service + first-party app installer pipeline — no new privileged path, no new capability.

- ✅ Welcome-1 — preseeded "Get started" content on first-launch (Path A): a small cross-linked starter set that demonstrates every bundled app the way Notes/Tasks/Database/Graph/Whiteboard expect to be used — a welcome Note explaining the dashboard + launcher + shortcuts, two-three sample Tasks, a Files folder, a Journal "day 1" entry, a Calendar event, a Whiteboard sketch, a Bookmark, all stitched together with `@`-mention links so Graph paints a non-empty default. Lands through the entities service during Path A's "Initialize the vault directory" step (sibling to the bundled-app install — the shell vouches for its own seed, no per-entity capability prompt). Idempotent (per-vault `welcome:seedVersion` stamp, never re-runs on re-open), per-vault opt-out checkbox on the create-vault step, removable any time via Bin without trace (soft-deleted entities purge cleanly). ## Import, export & migration *(doc [45](platform/45-import-export.md) — switch-in / takeout; **IE-1 → IE-6 in beta**, IE-7 → IE-9 ride post-beta deps)*

Realises [platform/45-import-export.md](platform/45-import-export.md): the two scopes (per-entity format I/O + vault-level `.bsbundle` takeout/restore) and the **"Migrating from…"** first-launch path that lets a Notion / Obsidian / Markdown / HTML user switch *seamlessly* — their workspace lands as native vault entities with types, properties, relations, links and assets preserved, not a flat dump of files. This is the counterpart to [Onboarding & starter content](#onboarding--starter-content): Welcome seeds *new* users; this section migrates *existing* ones. **Gap closed (2026-06-12, user request):** the design (doc 45 + OQ-245/246/247/186/187 + the 2026-06-02 OQ-242/243/244 extensibility pass) was fully drafted but never sequenced in the release plan; nothing built. *(Doc 45's three inline import/export questions were renumbered OQ-245/246/247 in the same turn — their original "OQ-183/184/185" tags collided with already-resolved canonical questions; see the ledger.)* Three lanes, one engine:

1. **Generic in-app importers/exporters** — per-app `import`/`export` intents per [17 §Format I/O](platform/17-interoperability.md) (Notes Markdown, Database CSV/JSON; HTML→Lexical already shipped as the reused Net-2a `html-to-blocks` path). Already partly built, folded onto the shared engine at IE-4.
2. **Canonical `.bsbundle` vault round-trip** — whole-vault + cherry-pick takeout / restore (doc 45 §Bundle format, §Round-trip guarantee). The data-portability floor (cut-lever §5 — *"data integrity / migration reversibility, never cut"*); the hard-floor rung — even under a date-crunch this one ships.
3. **Heavy first-party migration importers** — one per source product (Notion, Obsidian, page-DB, wiki) on the shared **Source → Parse → Map → Project → Dedupe → Write** pipeline (doc 45 §The import flow + §Parse/Map split). Separately installable per doc 45's bundle-size decision; offered by the first-launch "Migrating from…" picker (OQ-247).

Reuses, not reinvents: the privileged **create + plant** write path (`makeSeedEntityDeps` — the same one Welcome-1 / template-import use), **Net-2a `htmlToSerializedBlocks`** for body conversion (✅ shipped), the property-cell **`effective-def` ValueType inference** + the `entity_types` registry for the Map stage, the **connector OAuth + scoped-egress broker** (✅ shipped) for the one-shot API Source, and the utility-worker pattern (mirrors the extraction worker) for off-main-thread parse. Merge-not-replace by construction (imports only create rows; a parent Collection makes the whole import Bin-removable, mirroring template-import). **In beta (2026-09-01, user decision 2026-06-12): the file-based migration ladder IE-1 → IE-6** — `.bsbundle` takeout, the shared engine + mapping model, the wizard + "Migrating from…" picker, the folded generic importers, and the **Obsidian + Notion-export-zip** switch-in importers. The extension rungs ride their own post-beta dependencies and stay out-of-beta: **IE-7** (Notion-API source) on the Connector framework, **IE-8** (automated export) on Automations, **IE-9** (adapter market) on the Marketplace. None of IE-1 → IE-6 sits on the sync/crypto critical path, so they run as **G3 parallel fan-out** behind the spine; IE-6 (Notion) is the switch-in keystone.

- ✅ IE-1 — **`.bsbundle` vault export / import spine** (takeout + restore): the canonical round-trip format (doc 45 §Bundle format, §Round-trip guarantee) — whole-vault **and** cherry-pick a type/subtree (**OQ-245 ✅**), streamed with progress + cancel (§Streaming), provenance-stamped (§Identity and provenance), merge-not-replace conflict resolution (§Conflict resolution). Write side reuses the seed create+plant path. The beta data-portability floor (backup + device-move). **Landed 2026-06-17 (#149)**: `packages/shell/src/main/bundle/` — deterministic traversal-safe tar codec inside a self-describing `BSB1` container (zstd/gzip seam) + export/import engines; the CI round-trip guarantee (export → import-as-new-vault → re-export is byte-equivalent) is green. Residue = schema/app-inventory restore (couples to app-install). — **gate: 9.3.5 single-object-space (uniform cross-type create) ✅; OQ-245 ✅; OQ-246 ✅ (no v1 signature).**
  - **Data round-trip spine landed 2026-06-16** (`packages/shell/src/main/bundle/`): a self-contained codec + export/import engine + the CI round-trip guarantee. **Codec** — `bundle-format.ts` (shared vocabulary: `BundleManifest`/record types + `BundleCompression`/`BundleExportScopeKind`/`BundleConflictStrategy` enums + reserved `BundlePath`s), `bundle-tar.ts` (deterministic USTAR with GNU long-name support — entity paths can exceed the 100-byte ustar cap — and path-traversal-safe extraction), `bundle-archive.ts` (self-describing outer container `BSB1`+ver+algo so a reader picks the decompressor before reading the inner manifest; **compression seam** — zstd when the runtime's `node:zlib` exposes it, gzip fallback, so no native dep on the beta path), `canonical-json.ts` (sorted-key JSON/JSONL so identical content serializes byte-identically). **Engine** — `vault-export.ts` (`exportVaultBundle`: whole-vault | `types` | link-reachable `subtree` scope → entities + Yjs bodies + intra-set typed links + content-addressed deduped blobs + synthesized provenance; reuses `EntitiesRepository.query`/`linksFromMany` + `ydocStore.load`/`encodeStateAsUpdate` + `AssetStore`), `vault-import.ts` (`importVaultBundle`: restores into a fresh vault via `EntitiesRepository.create` with **preserved id / createdBy / distinct created+updated stamps** [new optional `CreateEntityInput.updatedAt`] + `ydocStore.writeSnapshot` + re-sealed blobs with **preserved assetId** [new optional `WriteAssetInput.assetId`]; rejects bad magic / unsupported major / missing `importedBy`). **CI guarantee** — `integration/vault-bundle-roundtrip.test.ts` proves export → import-as-new-vault → re-export is **byte-equivalent** (modulo volatile manifest `createdAt`/`vaultId`) over a seed exercising entities, distinct timestamps, Yjs bodies, a typed link, and a bound asset referenced by a property. **+13 tests** (codec 10 + integration 3); typecheck + biome clean. **Deferred to the next IE rungs (not in this spine):** entity-type schema + app-inventory restore (an `entity_type` FKs the introducing app → couples to the install / pending-install flow, doc 45 §apps-referenced-not-embedded; the format reserves `schemas/`+`apps.json`), shell-level state (settings/ledger/themes/wallpapers), streaming progress/cancel + pause/resume, persistent cross-source provenance, and the Settings → Backup & Migration surface (**IE-3**).
- ✅ IE-2 — **shared import engine: Source → Parse → Map → Project → Dedupe → Write** (doc 45 §The import flow + §Parse/Map split): the pluggable pipeline every migration importer builds on. **Source** stage is pluggable (file picker | folder | zip | one-shot API at IE-7); **Parse** emits a normalized record/draft IR decoupled from any source; **Map** does column→property + ValueType inference + dedupe-key (reuses property-cell `effective-def` inference + the shared `entity_types` registry — map a source "database"/collection to an existing vault type or mint a new one); **Project/Dedupe/Write** commits via the privileged create+plant path in a utility worker (batched, streamed; idempotent on a provenance/external-id key so re-import updates rather than duplicates). The keystone — the mapping model that makes a switch *correct*. **Functionally complete + merged 2026-06-17 (#149)**: engine + `services.import.{preview,plan,run}` broker + SDK proxy + safe column mapping + streaming progress/cancel all landed; the one remaining rung (off-main-thread utility-worker batching) is GATED on an entities single-writer re-architecture (out of scope), not on import work. — **gate: IE-1 write path ✅ + 9.3.5 ✅.**
  - **Engine spine landed 2026-06-16** (`packages/shell/src/main/import/`): the mostly-pure pipeline + its vault binding + the dry-run/run contract. `import-types.ts` (the stage IR — `ParsedTable`/`ImportRecord`/`MappingPlan`/`EntityDraft`/`ImportPlan`/`ImportRunReport` + the abstract `ImportWriteDeps` seam + `IMPORT_EXTERNAL_ID_PROP` flat dedupe marker, mirroring the connector framework's `connectorExternalId` but for one-shot import). **Parse** `import-parse.ts` — JSON + JSONL reference adapters (native, zero-dep; the generic CSV/Markdown/HTML adapters fold onto this same IR at **IE-4** per doc 45 §Parse/Map split, so the engine doesn't reach into the Database app's CSV parser), with heuristic external-id extraction (`id`/`uuid`/… → the row's stable key). **Map** `import-map.ts` — `inferValueType` (conservative: bare numbers stay Number, only ISO-ish date strings promote to Date — a wrong silent guess is worse than a re-mappable Text) + `inferMapping` (default column→property bindings the IE-3 wizard overrides). **Project** `import-project.ts` — `coerceToValueType` external→typed coercion (numeric/boolean strings, `"2026-01-02"` → `{at,granularity}` DateValue) — distinct from the SDK's hydration-only `coerceValue`; absent columns skipped, not nulled. **Dedupe/Write** `import-engine.ts` — `planImport` (the required non-destructive dry-run) + `runImport` (idempotent upsert, atomic-per-entity continue-on-error) sharing one dedupe decision so plan can't drift from run; `vault-import-engine.ts` binds `ImportWriteDeps` to `EntitiesRepository` (create via the privileged path stamping the external-id marker; upsert resolved by `listIdsWithProperty` so a second import of the same source updates rather than duplicates). **+15 tests** (pure pipeline 14 — parse/infer/coerce/project/plan/run/idempotency/failure-continue — + a vault integration proving JSON import → real `entities.db` rows → idempotent re-import shallow-merge-updates with no duplicates); `typecheck:packages` + biome clean.
  - **App-facing broker service landed 2026-06-17** (`import/import-service.ts`, registered in `index.ts`): the capability-gated `import` service so a sandboxed app runs the engine (`plan`/`run`) instead of hand-rolling an importer — the seam **IE-4's per-app consolidation needs**. Type-scoped exactly like `entities` (the handler is the sole cap authority; reuses the app's **`entities.write:<targetType>`** grant, so NO new capability surface). Two hardening invariants, independently security-reviewed in-design: **inference-only** (no app-supplied mapping → the written entity type is always the cap-checked `targetType`, closing the `projectRecord` `mapping.targetType`-override hole) and **app-scoped dedupe** (`<app>::<source>` namespace → one app can't update another's imported rows); provenance stamped `createdBy:<app>`; fails closed (`Unavailable`) on no vault/ledger, `Denied` on a missing write grant. **Chores hardening** — the dedupe lookup resolves the flat external-id marker to a row **of the cap-checked target type only** (`findByExternalKey` filters by type), closing a fail-open where a cross-type marker match could overwrite an entity of a type the app may not write (the entities service re-checks fetched-row type on update; the import path now matches it); regression-tested. Registered with the same post-write stale-broadcast + reindex + snapshot-republish wrap as `entities`. **+7 tests** (plan→run, idempotent re-import, cross-app non-collision, Denied wrong-type, wildcard grant, bad-input/unknown-method, fail-closed-no-ledger). Map-onto-existing-type (`propertiesStore` `knownProps`) is wired into the service. **SDK proxy landed same day** — `ImportService` + `ImportRequest`/`ImportPlanResult`/`ImportRunResult` in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` + the `brainstorm.services.import.{preview,plan,run}` runtime proxy (caps:[]; the handler is the authority), so the service is now callable by apps. **`preview` + safe column mapping landed 2026-06-17** — `preview` returns columns + a row sample (no write) to drive an app mapping UI; `plan`/`run` accept an optional column `mapping` (column→property→include) overlaid onto the engine's inferred base (`resolveMapping`, mirroring the IE-3 dashboard handler) so the targetType stays the cap-checked value (a mapping can't redirect the write). This makes the service a **complete importer backend** for the long-tail apps IE-4 targets (+6 tests: preview-no-write, mapping rename/exclude keeps cap-checked type, proxy round-trips). **Streaming progress + cancel landed 2026-06-17** (doc 45 §Streaming): `runImport` is now async, streams `onProgress(done,total)`, and honours an `AbortSignal` — it yields to the event loop every 50 drafts so a mid-run abort is observed and the remaining drafts become `skipped`/`cancelled`. Threaded through `importRecordsIntoVault` + the dashboard `run` handler (emits `import-export:progress` events + an `import-export:cancel` channel); Settings → Backup & Migration shows a live progress line + Stop button. +engine progress/cancel + handler progress-stream tests. **Migration-importer streaming landed 2026-06-17** — `importNotionExport` + `importObsidianVault` now take the same `onProgress` + `AbortSignal`, yield every 50 pages/notes, and on a mid-run abort skip attachments + links and report `cancelled`; the `run-notion`/`run-obsidian` handlers emit `import-export:progress` + honour the shared `import-export:cancel` channel (+progress/cancel tests for both). So all three import paths (source-file, Notion, Obsidian) stream + cancel. **Utility-worker batching is GATED, not a clean transport move (assessed 2026-06-17):** `entities.db` is opened **only in the main process** (the vault session's single cached connection; the storage/ydoc/mailbox utility workers never touch it). Moving the import write loop into a separate `utilityProcess` would make it a **second concurrent writer to `entities.db`** — a WAL lock-contention + data-integrity hazard against the live entities-service/dashboard writes. Doing it safely requires re-architecting **all** entities writes (service + seeder + bundle-restore + import) to route through one owner process — a large cross-cutting storage change with its own security/stability audits, out of scope for an import rung. Meanwhile the engine is already async + yields every 50 drafts, so a large import stays responsive (the event loop flushes between batches). **So IE-2 is functionally complete; the worker move is parked on the entities single-writer-ownership decision, not on import work.**
- ✅ IE-3 — **import wizard surface + "Migrating from…" onboarding entry**: the privileged dashboard surface (Settings → Backup & Migration + the first-launch "Migrating from…" picker, doc 45 §Discoverability) — source pick → filtered `dialog.showOpenDialog` → engine **dry-run plan** (created / merged / skipped / unmapped) → **mapping screen** (live sample-object preview, fancy-menus `SelectMenu` pickers, property-cell previews, override auto-mapping) → run with progress → completion report linking the parent Collection. Mirrors the `network-egress-panel` privileged-surface pattern. **Landed 2026-06-17 (#149)**: Settings → Backup & Migration ships export + JSON/JSONL/CSV/MD/HTML dry-run import + interactive column remap + streaming/cancel. **First-launch "Migrating from…" entry landed 2026-06-17**: a Welcome-menu CTA (popover naming Obsidian / Notion-export / generic-file sources) routes into vault creation, then a one-shot auto-opens Settings → Backup & Migration on the new vault. **IE-3 complete.** — **gate: IE-2; OQ-247 (migration importers in-shell vs install-on-demand); OQ-187 (migration-app store category).**

## Open resolution *(group I — the glue)*

Designed ([platform/57-open-resolution.md](platform/57-open-resolution.md), [[project_open_resolution]]); OQ-OR-1…5 registered + resolved 2026-05-19. Gate lifted — buildable.

- ✅ OpenRes-1a — open-resolution **pure keystones** (2026-05-19): `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `brainstorm/open-resolution/v1` — `OpenTargetKind` (internal|entity|scheme|file) + `normalizeOpenInput` + the fixed dangerous-scheme hard-block floor (`javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`about:`-class + out-of-vault `file:`) + the pure terminating ladder `decideOpen` (rungs internal-resolver→stored-default→in-vault-openers→universal-editor→os-handoff→explained-refusal), total-by-construction (property test over the whole fact space). Per-vault OS-handoff **consent memory** on the dashboard Y.Doc (`osHandoffConsent` map, `granted`/`denied` per `scheme:`/`ext:` signature, sibling to `defaultHandlers`). `launchInto` extracted so the entity + opener paths deliver context identically. ~64 tests. **Deferred to OpenRes-1c (UI tail):** the interactive first-use consent *prompt* (until then first-use is a fail-closed explained refusal — total + safe, the doc-57 invariant), Settings → Defaults(scheme/ext) + Privacy→Network egress panel, inline shared "Open with…" menu, "Why did this open here?" explainer UI, sticky app-vs-OS first-use fork.

Three actions: **Allow** (sticky → persists Granted), **Never for this kind** (sticky → persists Denied), **Cancel** (non-sticky — re-prompts next time). `Enter` confirms Allow via `useShortcut("shell/popover.confirm")` so the binding remains user-rebindable and cheatsheet-listed; `Escape` routes to Cancel via the Popover's built-in shortcut so closing the modal never silently makes a denial sticky. Mounted in `dashboard.tsx` next to `<CapabilityPromptHost />` (both render-paths — the no-current-vault path + the main dashboard). **`IntentsBus.dispatchExternalOpen`** rewired: when `decideOpen` returns `needsConsent`, the bus calls `promptOsHandoffConsent(signature, uri)`; on `allow` it persists `OsHandoffConsent.Granted` via `recordOsHandoffConsent` and falls through to the existing `openExternal` chokepoint; on `deny` it persists `Denied` and returns an explained refusal; on `cancel` it returns an explained refusal **without** persisting (the next attempt re-prompts — pinned by a regression test). New preload bridge `osHandoffPrompt: { on, respond }` (the dashboard renderer's only entry into the host) + `OsHandoffPromptRequest` / `OsHandoffPromptDecisionWire` types. # Apps

Sandboxed first-party apps. Each ships separately from the shell (`bun run --filter @brainstorm-app/<name> build` + reload). Each app's scaffold rung (`9.x.1`) freezes the manifest + entity types + caps + `types/` surface before the renderer exists. App ids/iterations unchanged.

## App serial order (2026-05-23 policy, [[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]])

**No app slot opens until Phase 1 (all Shell + Infra) clears.** Once it does, apps are claimed **one at a time**; each app's remaining ladder — including its G2 BP-block adoption tail — finishes inside that slot before the next app starts.

The **Agent composer migrated off its `<textarea>` onto the same CompactEditor+mention surface** (user turns persist `richBody`, render rich; control-faces baseline tightened; `CompactEditorHandle.setText` carries intent-seeded drafts). Chat avatars: image avatars now fill the circular host (were a rounded square inside the ring). Real-shell verified (`377-inline-mentions` — inline chip in both composers, sent message renders the mention inline, zero attachment boxes). **Slack-level markup landed 2026-07-03** (user-reported, F-385/F-386, shell branch `chat-rich-composer`): `<CompactEditor>` grew the message-sized blocks — bulleted / numbered / to-do lists, quote and code block (`ListNode`/`ListItemNode`/`QuoteNode`/`CodeNode` + `ListPlugin`/`CheckListPlugin`), a curated Markdown shortcut vocabulary (`- ` `1. ` `[] ` `> ` fenced code, inline marks, links — deliberately NO headings: a message is not a document), typed-URL autolink, and Slack Enter semantics (Enter sends; Shift+Enter is a newline, or the NEXT list item when the caret is in a list). The shared selection toolbar gained opt-in bullet/numbered/to-do toggles (`InlineToolbarPlugin lists` prop, on for every CompactEditor); baseline theme + `compact-editor.css` carry the checklist face, and the Lexical-free `renderEditorState` renders `check` lists with their checked state so sent messages match the draft. Comments + Agent composers inherit all of it (one shared surface). Also fixed F-385 — the selection toolbar rendered as a clipped vertical stack in chat: the `.fm-menu` runtime base (`column` + `overflow:hidden`) beat `.notes__inline-toolbar` at equal specificity when the bundle emitted it later; now the order-proof compound `.fm-menu.notes__inline-toolbar` (same pattern its own dropdowns used). Real-shell verified (`tests/visual/specs/chat-rich-composer.spec.ts` — horizontal toolbar geometry asserted from computed style, toolbar list toggle, Shift+Enter next-item, `[ ] `→to-do and `1. `→numbered round-trips through send). **Remaining**: real-shell verify of 313 + the **cross-shell synced** channel (a teammate's posts converging in another vault) which needs **in-product channel sharing (Collab-C5)** — today's collab dev bridge shares one entity at a time, not a growing message set. The general arbitrary-multi-user Chats GA stays v2 (gated on org/consumer-accounts); this contained internal slice is not. Goal + status in [dogfood/README.md → "July 2026 goal"](dogfood/README.md).

Order is the integrator's call at each handoff. Constraint: no second app claim while one is in flight ([[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]]).

**Release-scope note**: being in this sequence does not change v1/beta scope. Apps 1–10 (Notes through Preview) are the beta-blocking core; apps 11+ (Theme-editor, Books, Contacts, Form-designer, Mailbox, Browser, Automations, Agent, Connector) remain out-of-v1-beta scope per [Release plan & roadmap](#release-plan--roadmap) — they ship across the post-beta GA window, in this order. Community-board and Chats are v2.

Pure (cycle wins over depth; default `MAX_TRANSCLUSION_DEPTH`=10), so the depth/cycle math is proven without mounting the nested editor — mirrors how B6.4a(a) landed its keystones before the renderer. **Tests +7** (`transclusion-ops.test.ts` 26/26: not-in-chain renders · self-loop · multi-hop loop · at-budget elides · one-below renders · cycle-over-depth precedence · custom budget); collapse to the existing "↪ open in source" chrome on `CycleElided`/`DepthElided`. **Render-half landed 2026-06-02 (nested mount)**: chose the live nested-editor mount over the `EditorPreview` path — a transcluded body keeps full fidelity (mentions / embeds / images / tables / *nested* transclusions all paint through the same node set), which a Yjs-XmlText→`SerializedEditorState` reconstruction for the Lexical-free preview would have re-implemented fragile-ly. `TransclusionNode.decorate()` (via the exported `TransclusionView`) reads a new `TransclusionRenderContext` ({`ancestorChain`, injected `renderBody`}), runs `decideTransclusionRender(ancestorChain, entityId)`, and on `Render` mounts `renderTransclusionBody` → a read-only `<BrainstormEditor editable={false}>` bound to `useYDoc(entityId)` (`transclusion-body.tsx`) with `NOTES_ADDITIONAL_NODES`; on `CycleElided`/`DepthElided` it shows a muted "open source" hint under the header card. **Two non-obvious constraints solved**: (1) the chain provider sits *above* `<BrainstormEditor>` — Lexical paints decorators through `RichTextPlugin`/`useDecorators`→`createPortal`, so only a provider that is an *ancestor* of `<LexicalComposer>` (like `EditorI18nProvider`) reaches them; a composer-*child* provider is invisible to decorators. (2) `renderBody` is *injected through context* rather than imported, because the body renderer pulls in `NOTES_ADDITIONAL_NODES` (→ `TransclusionNode`) and a direct import would cycle. Each nested body re-provides the context with its own id appended, so the cycle/depth guard converges at render time. **Tests**: `transclusion-render.test.tsx` (+5 jsdom: render mounts the injected body · host-first chain passed minus target · cycle elides without calling the renderer · depth-budget elides · degraded header-only mount when no renderer wired) + real-shell `tests/perf/specs/notes-transclusion-body.spec.ts` (note T transcludes note H → H's body marker paints inside the read-only `.notes__transclusion-body-content`; `data-decision="render"`; `contenteditable="false"`). Added `insertTransclusion` + `currentNoteId` dev hooks (keystroke-free, per the Yjs-keystroke-corruption rule). Workspace `tsc` clean; biome clean; apps/notes suite green (the one pre-existing `property-block-decorator` failure is unrelated). — detail in [log](implementation-log.md). B6.4b complete.

Cross-cutting items (find-replace, shortcut registry, export-file, icon-picker) extract to `@brainstorm/sdk` per [[feedback_extract_to_sdk_at_copy_two]].

Builds on `@lexical/table`. **Sort-by-column landed 2026-06-01**: `sortTableBySelectedColumn(editor, ascending)` in `packages/editor/src/plugins/table-ops.ts` reorders the body rows of the table the caret sits in by the selected cell's column — numeric columns sort numerically, otherwise locale string compare; a leading header row (first cell `hasHeader()`) stays pinned; rows travel as units (re-`append` moves the whole `TableRowNode`). Both hover + drag-start run off **capture-phase document listeners** (sibling marquee/block-selection plugins stop `mousedown` propagation before React's delegated root, so an `onMouseDown` handler never fires; the cosmetic handle is `pointer-events: none` so the mousedown reaches the cell). **Key fix**: the cell→TableNode resolution uses `editor.read()` (not `getEditorState().read()`) so `$getNearestNodeFromDOMNode` has an active editor — the bare editor-state read throws Lexical #196. **Test**: real-shell Playwright spec (`notes-table-resize.spec.ts`: insert table → dismiss the covering toolbar → drag the boundary +80px → the persisted `colWidths[0]` grew, read via a new `firstTableColWidths` dev hook). packages + apps/notes typecheck + biome clean; Notes bundles. **Column reorder landed 2026-06-01**: `moveTableColumn(editor, toRight)` swaps the selected cell's column with its neighbour in every row (and the `colWidths` entry), surfaced as "Move column left / right" toolbar buttons. **Tests +2** (`table-ops.test.ts`: move-right swaps every row's two columns · first-column move-left is an edge no-op) + a real-shell spec (`notes-table-move-column.spec.ts`: seed a cell → Move column right → it lands one column over). packages + apps/notes typecheck + biome clean; Notes bundles. **Inline checkbox cell landed 2026-06-04**: new inline `CheckboxFieldNode` (`apps/notes/src/editor/nodes/checkbox-field-node.tsx`) — a `DecoratorNode` reusing the shared **property-ui cell registry** (`getCell(Boolean, Checkbox)` → `CheckboxCell`, rendered with a synthesised Boolean `PropertyDef`), so a Notes table cell (or any paragraph) can hold a checkable status box that looks/behaves like a property cell everywhere else. Checked state IS shared content (a collaborator sees it as left), so `__checked` lives on the node + syncs through @lexical/yjs (the opposite of the per-device toggle-collapse); `getTextContent()` → GFM `[x]`/`[ ]`. ## Code-editor *(9.7)* — 🟡

`brainstorm-editor` + Shiki. `CodeFile/v1` is vault-resident; no source-tree access.

Persistent `CodePane` controller across file selections so mid-typing render doesn't tear down the textarea / caret / IME (the Notes survival pattern). +47 tests across `logic/highlight` + `logic/code-y-buffer` + `ui/highlight-overlay` + `ui/citation-hover`. — detail in [log](implementation-log.md).

offered as a `code-pane` object-menu toggle (`wrapEnable`/`wrapDisable`), persisted per-app via `localStorage` (`code-editor:wrap`), exposed as `toggleWrap()`/`isWrapped()`; +2 tests, 192/192. **Bracket-match + indent-guide LOGIC landed (2026-06-09)**: pure `logic/brackets.ts` (`matchBracket(text, caret)` — caret-adjacent pair, nesting-aware) + `logic/indent-guides.ts` (`indentGuideDepths` — per-line depth, tab expansion, blank-line bridging); - ✅ 9.12.20 — **Live-rolling relative-date filters**: "Last 7 days" re-evaluates continuously instead of snapshotting to absolute bounds on apply. **Resolver keystone landed 2026-06-02**: pure `apps/database/src/logic/relative-date.ts` — `RelativeDateRange` (Today/Yesterday/Tomorrow · Last7/30Days · Next7/30Days · ThisWeek/Month/Year) + `resolveRelativeRange(range, now)` → a half-open `[start, end)` ms window computed from an **injected `now`** using local calendar time (Monday-start weeks; month/year/DST via the Date API, not ms arithmetic) + `isInRelativeRange(value, range, now)` membership (ISO/ms coercion; non-date → out of range) + `toTimestamp`. Injecting `now` is the whole point — the same token resolves to a *different* window as the clock advances, so a filter built on it rolls live instead of freezing to apply-time bounds. **Tests +14** (`relative-date.test.ts`: every range's window against a fixed Wed-mid-month-mid-year reference incl. the month-crossing Last30Days, Monday week start, half-open end-exclusivity, live-rolling (same range + later now → later window), and `isInRelativeRange`/`toTimestamp` coercion). apps/database `tsc` clean; biome clean. **Predicate-language integration landed 2026-06-04**: a new `$relativeDate` operator on the canonical `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `PropertyPredicate` (RHS = a relative-date range *token* string, kept a plain string so the sdk-types leaf module stays free of the app's `RelativeDateRange` enum). The in-app `evaluatePredicate` gained an injected `now` (Unix ms, default `Date.now()`, threaded through `$and`/`$or`/`$not` recursion) and resolves `$relativeDate` against it via `isInRelativeRange` — so the same persisted token re-rolls every recompile instead of freezing to apply-time bounds. An unknown / future-version token matches **nothing** (never everything), and a non-date cell is never in range. The SQL `byFilter` compiler doesn't understand the operator and falls through to match-nothing, so it is a **client-side view-overlay filter** (the dominant relative-date use). - ✅ 9.17.20 — **Canvas renderer perf** (decision + migration). Whiteboard paints nodes/edges as DOM today (`render/node-dom.ts` + `paint()`'s `replaceChildren`) — fine at small boards, but per-node DOM + full-layer repaint on every drag/zoom is the SVG/DOM perf trap ([[feedback_svg_is_a_perf_trap]]) and won't hold at scale. **Spike first to pick the approach, then migrate, with before/after frame-time numbers (doc-13 budget posture):**
  - **(a) Pixi canvas** — max ceiling at scale; reuse Graph's scaffolding (`apps/graph/src/render/pixi-renderer.ts` `mountPixi` + the Page-Visibility rAF-pause IPC + `{texture:false}` destroy discipline) and extract the shared parts to the SDK at copy two. Cost: text editing + a11y must move to a DOM overlay (Pixi can't host `contentEditable`); sticky/text rich content + CSS theming re-implement on the canvas.
  - **(b) Optimized HTML ("HTML in canvas")** — keep DOM nodes (native `contentEditable`, a11y, CSS/theme tokens, the existing inline-edit + selection chrome) but fix the perf: transform-based pan/zoom on a single GPU-composited layer (no per-frame `replaceChildren`), viewport culling / virtualization of off-screen nodes, and per-node incremental repaint instead of full-layer rebuild. Lower ceiling than Pixi but preserves the rich-HTML node model and avoids a DOM-overlay split.
  - Likely a **hybrid**: HTML for the interactive/near layer + edited node, canvas for bulk static nodes + edges. The model + `logic/*` (align/snap/connector/containment) stay untouched either way; only the render layer changes.
  **Gate**: land after the cheaper 9.17.9–.19 functional gaps; sequence as the Whiteboard slot's perf-hardening rung (mirrors Graph `9.13.15`). Resolve the approach as an OQ before code. — **🟡 approach resolved + first rung landed 2026-06-15**: **OQ-WB-5 ✅ = optimized-HTML first** (Pixi's max ceiling unjustified vs. the load-bearing rich-DOM node model — `contentEditable` text, CSS theme tokens, a11y, inline-edit/selection chrome — that a Pixi rewrite would re-implement behind a DOM-overlay split; the camera-paint split 9.17.21 already removed per-frame layer rebuilds, so the remaining bottleneck is per-node DOM **count**). First migration rung: the pure **viewport-culling selector** `logic/viewport-cull.ts` (`visibleNodeIds` AABB-overlap over padded world viewport + `worldViewport` camera→world-rect) — only nodes whose world box intersects the padded viewport get mounted, so per-node cost scales with what's *visible*. **+6 tests**; renderer-agnostic (survives a later static-layer canvas hybrid). Also fixed a **pre-existing** whiteboard test (`node-dom.test.ts` — `var(--border-width)` missing its `1px` fallback in 3 node-chrome border decls), green now (28/28). **Residue**: wire culling into the engine paint (mount/unmount on camera change) + per-node incremental repaint + before/after frame-time numbers (real-Electron); escalate to the canvas hybrid only if measured. — **✅ DONE 2026-06-18** (decision doc `docs/_review/2026-06-18-whiteboard-9.17.20-renderer-decision.md`): the three optimized-HTML increments landed in `engine.ts`, all inside the existing DOM model (no Pixi-for-nodes, no new dependency, every behaviour preserved — `contentEditable`, theme tokens, a11y, embeds, selection, pan/zoom frame-stability). **(1) Drag without rebuild** — node-drag + connector-authoring `pointermove` stopped calling the full `paint()`; a new `paintDragFrame()` writes moved nodes' geometry onto their existing elements (`applyNodeBox`) + repaints GPU edges/bounds, full `paint()` only on `pointerup`/settle. **(2) Viewport culling wired** — `paintNodes` mounts only `visibleNodeIds(...)` (the landed selector) force-including the edited node; `paintCamera` re-culls the mount/unmount delta past a half-screen drift (small pans stay node-DOM-free); a zero-size wrap disables culling (never hides a node). **(3) Keyed diff reconcile** — `paintNodes` reconciles by `data-node-id` + a content signature, keeping element identity (live editor / embed iframe / focus) for unchanged nodes, rebuilding only changed, removing gone. **Before/after** (deterministic jsdom op-cost, median per drag-frame, 0 node subtrees rebuilt vs O(N) before): 100 nodes 38.9 ms → 9.4 ms (4.1×), 500 nodes 413.6 ms → 95.7 ms (4.3×), 1000 nodes 2835.6 ms → 89.0 ms (31.9×) — the before path scales superlinearly with N, the after path is flat in node count + culled to ~visible in real Electron. Regression guard `apps/whiteboard/src/engine-drag-perf.test.tsx` (drag/settle element identity, keyed-reconcile identity, cull mount/unmount on pan). 468 whiteboard tests green, `bun run typecheck` (packages+apps) + biome + css-token + reactivity guards clean. **Residue**: a real-Electron Playwright frame-time bench (Increment 4) for live frame numbers; escalate to the canvas hybrid only if it misses budget.
