## Form-designer *(Stage 8.10)* — 🟡

WYSIWYG layout editor for `stacked`/`grid`; first first-party app bundled with the design-system completion.

> **v1 shipped 2026-06-13** (commit `8f70d400`, dogfood-verified session 222) — a **property-form builder + fill flow**, deliberately narrower than the full WYSIWYG-layout-editor the rungs below envision: a form is a `brainstorm/Layout/v1` entity (stacked, type-scoped to its target); the Builder names it, picks a target type, and adds/orders/removes property fields from the live vault catalog; Fill renders those fields as the shared editable property cells and creates a new entity of the target type. Scope kept tight: stacked mode, **property fields only** (block/chrome/group cells deferred), reorder via buttons (not drag), built directly on `Layout/v1` (not the 8.3 per-cell render pipeline), no PDF export. The 8.3/8.4-pipeline rungs (`8.10.2` grid/drag, `8.10.3` chrome cells, `8.10.4` visibility rules) stay open against the post-v1 pipeline.

- ✅ 8.10.1 — scaffold: manifest + caps + `types/`. **Done in the v1 build** — graduated from the coming-soon stub to a real React app (`apps/form-designer/src/app.tsx` + pure `logic/form-model.ts` with 10 tests; shared cell-bridge / SelectMenu / `.bs-btn` / `.app-header` ⋯-last / PropertiesProvider / AppErrorBoundary). Took the narrower property-form path (builds `Layout/v1` directly) rather than consuming the 8.3 render pipeline.
- ✅ 8.10.2 — **editing canvas: the fill surface renders through the 8.3 pipeline + grid mode** *(shell #292, 2026-07-25)*. Drag-to-reorder shipped earlier; the remaining half was gated on 8.3, which has now landed. **The swap:** the fill pane ran its own field loop (look up the def → `getCell` → render), which is precisely why a grid form was "cosmetic without the pipeline" — it could not get grid placement or per-cell subscriptions without re-implementing both. A form **is** a `Layout/v1`, so `<LayoutView>` now draws it, and each field cell subscribes to its own key (a keystroke repaints that field, not the form). **Grid mode:** `LayoutDef` places cells individually and has no notion of "the form's columns", so the designer keeps the authoring-level **track count** on the form and derives each cell's `{col,row}` from it on save (row-major, 1-based per CSS Grid lines). The mode is *derived* from the track count on both write and read, so a form can never persist — or reload as — a grid with nothing to place against. <2 tracks ⇒ stacked (a single-track grid is ceremony); capped at 4 (beyond that a field is narrower than its own label). Builder control is a `<SelectMenu>`, per the no-native-`<select>` rule. **Two SDK seams the swap needed, both generic rather than form-shaped:** `renderCell(cell, body)` — a host still owns what *surrounds* a cell (label / required marker / validation message) even though the layout owns which cells exist and where; without it every such host forks the pipeline just to get a label. And `renderMissingCell(cell, def)` — a property cell the registry can't draw; the pipeline's placeholder is visible but **not editable**, which for a form means a field the user cannot complete, so the designer supplies its text input and a vault with no properties service stays fillable. That second one was a **real regression the existing 8.10.4 visibility tests caught** (their shell mock ships no properties service). +13 tests; 2672 SDK + form-designer tests green; typecheck + all 7 ratchets + `build:apps` clean; i18n in all 6 locales. **Gate: none (8.3 ✅).**
- ✅ 8.10.3 — **group nesting + the chrome-cell palette** *(shell #293, 2026-07-25)*. **Closes 0.10.0's Hero 1.** The builder knew one item kind (a property field); doc 27 has six, and with 8.3 rendering them and 8.4 drawing chrome the designer now authors three — a field, a **section** (`group` cell, with its own optional mode) and a **page element** (`chrome` cell, the whole curated OQ-90 (a) set). All three land from the same "add" gesture rather than a second control to find. **Authoring model** is a small item tree (`logic/form-items.ts`) with two deliberate limits, both about the *builder surface* rather than the contract: **one level of nesting** (a deeper layout still loads, renders and round-trips — `cellsToItems` *flattens* a nested group into its parent rather than dropping the user's fields), and **the leaf stays `FormField`** so fill / validation / create keep working unchanged on `itemFields(items)` — a group is presentation, not a data boundary. **Identity:** groups and chrome cells carry a creation-time `id` that is also their persisted cell id; fields key on `property`, these have no natural key, and without one a reorder made React reuse the wrong card (a section's label input followed the *position*, not the section). **Two bugs the tests caught before they shipped:** `readingOrder` was `cells.map(id)` — top level only — so the first form containing a section would have persisted a layout the frozen contract rejects (fixed to `collectCellIds`, which recurses); and reusing one id across two chrome cells trips the duplicate-cell-id check, which is the validator doing its job. Fill draws placed chrome through 8.4's `chromeSeam`, so a page element renders the shell's real chrome, not a placeholder. +18 tests; 2690 SDK + form-designer tests green; typecheck + all 7 ratchets + `build:apps` clean; i18n in all 6 locales. **Residue:** cross-group *drag* (nesting is a button gesture today — one unambiguous target). **Gate: none (8.4 ✅).**
- ✅ 8.10.4 — conditional visibility rules per field **(2026-07-22, shell `7733b813`)**: the `visibility-rules.ts` logic (shared `@brainstorm-os/sdk/predicate-eval` — the same evaluator the Database filter language runs, no second mini-language) existed with 13 tests but was fully unwired. Now (1) a per-field **Builder `ConditionEditor`** — "only show when \<field\> \<op\> \<value\>", a single clause (`is`/`is not`/`is set`/`is empty`) compiled to the canonical `PropertyPredicate` via new pure `logic/condition-model.ts`; a composite/unsupported predicate degrades to a read-only "advanced condition" state (never silently rewritten); value control is type-aware (boolean → checked/unchecked select); (2) **Fill mode** renders only `visibleFields(values)`, validates via `requiredEmptyFields`, and creates via `visibleFillProperties` — a hidden field never blocks Create nor lands in the created entity. **+16 tests** (condition-model round-trip 14 + 2 app-level Fill integration = 69 form-designer green), i18n en/es parity, css-token/reactivity/biome/tsc clean, bundle builds.
- ✅ 8.10.5 — save-as-`Layout/v1` entity + apply-to-type + install-time `validateAppLayouts` (8.5) round-trip *(shell #273, 2026-07-24)*. A saved form now persists its type `scope` (self-describing, resolver-consumable default `Layout`, not an app-private blob; scope derived from `targetType` on read, back-compat with pre-scope v1 forms). New pure helpers `toAppLayoutEntry`/`formLayoutIssues`/`isFormApplicableToType` project a form to the manifest-entry shape and validate it through the SAME frozen `validateAppLayouts` contract the shell runs at install; the Builder "Apply to type" action gates on that contract before persisting so a designer can't publish a default the installer would reject. Round-trips proven against the REAL `resolveLayout` (form resolves as its type's default layout) + `validateAppLayouts`. No new IPC/capability surface (apply writes through the existing cap-gated `entities` service; cross-type *user* layouts are allowed by doc 27, only manifest defaults are owned-type-restricted). +9 net tests (78 form-designer green); typecheck/lint:apps/build clean. **Visible render of the applied default stays gated on the 8.3 pipeline** (8.10.2/.3 unchanged).

A real-db `scheduler-store.test.ts` proves restart survival end-to-end (register through the live migration → fresh service `hydrate()` on the same db → recurring trigger still fires + re-arms, persisted). +9 tests. **Remaining (→ folds into 11b.3)**: real-timer drain loop + `workers.ts`/broker registration deliver `WorkflowRunRequest`s to the `WorkflowRunner` (which 11b.3 introduces — the scheduler has no consumer until then); `EntityEvent`/`Manual` wiring is 11b.6.
- ✅ 11b.3 — `WorkflowRunner` core landed 2026-06-06. The shell-main interpreter that executes a workflow's steps once the scheduler hands over a fire (doc 39 §Scheduler — shell-side, runs whether or not the app window is open). This slice is the **core**: the step-interpreter *loop*, the `WorkflowRun/v1` *provenance*, and the *failure / retry* policy; the concrete per-kind interpreters are **injected** (an `InterpreterRegistry` = `StepKind → StepInterpreter`) and land in 11b.4. Mirrors the scheduler's discipline — clock, sleep, and every side effect behind injected ports, so the whole fire→interpret→provenance→fail/retry path is timer-free and exhaustively unit-tested. **Loop**: walks steps in order, threads a live `outputs` map (a later step reads an earlier step's output; the leading `Trigger` pseudo-step is seeded with the fire payload), builds a flat **depth-tagged** `stepLog` (each entry = input/output/duration/attempts/status — `depth` lets the Runs view 11b.13 render nesting). **Container steps**: `RunContext.runChildren(steps)` drives a Branch/ForEach body through the same machinery (provenance + retry inherited) — so 11b.4's container interpreters recurse without re-implementing the loop. **Failure** (doc 39 §Failure modes): a step that throws, returns a non-retriable failure, or exhausts retries → run `failed`, downstream steps `skipped`, `run.error` carries the message; a declared-but-gated kind with no interpreter fails cleanly as `unsupported-step-kind:<kind>`. **Retry**: a bounded `RetryPolicy { maxAttempts, backoffMs }` re-attempts only `retriable` failures, sleeping the computed backoff via the injected sleeper. **Cancellation**: an `AbortSignal` cancels mid-run → remaining steps `skipped`, status `cancelled` (or `timed-out` when the host aborts with the `timeout` reason). `toWorkflowRunDef` maps a finished run into the `brainstorm/WorkflowRun/v1` entity shape for the host to persist. +20 tests (loop/provenance, failure→skip, retry+backoff, abort/timeout, container recursion+depth, run-def mapping); typecheck (packages) + biome green. **Wiring to a live timer + scheduler→runner delivery + entities-service persistence of the run is the 11b.4/.6 host glue** (the runner is pure of IO by design).
- ✅ 11b.4 — core-set `StepKind` interpreters landed 2026-06-06. The concrete behaviour the 11b.3 runner loop drives, built against **injected ports** (intents bus / entities service / notifications / sleep) — never a direct broker import — so each is unit-testable with fakes and the live wiring lives in one adapter. `createCoreInterpreters(ports)` returns the `InterpreterRegistry`; Trigger stays a runner no-op. **Interpreters**: `Intent` (dispatch verb+entityType+args), `Entity` (create/update/get/delete/query via the entities port), `Notify` (post title/body/target), `Wait` (sleep `durationMs`, pass input through; `untilCondition` parked), `Branch` (evaluate condition → run consequent/alternate via `runChildren`), `ForEach` (resolve collection → run body per item, seeding each iteration with the item, collecting per-item outputs), `SubWorkflow` (load the referenced workflow's steps + run them). **Linear data-flow** (the enabling runner change): the runner now threads `ctx.input` = the prior step's output (trigger payload for the first step) + a `runChildren(steps, seedInput?)` seam, so a step's operand is the upstream output — the faithful engine-spine binding (doc 39 §The step model "reference outputs of prior steps"); the rich per-field `RelativePosition` binding is the builder's concern (**OQ-166 / 11b.11**), refinable without changing this runtime contract. **Branch/ForEach evaluation** ship a deliberately tiny default (`defaultConditionEvaluator` / `defaultCollectionResolver` — literals, `input`, and prior-step-id refs; conservative `false`/`[]` for unknown expressions) behind injectable ports, so the full sandboxed-expression form drops in with the `Code` step (**OQ-167 / 11b.9**) untouched. **Host glue** (`broker-interpreter-ports.ts`): `createBrokerInterpreterPorts` backs the ports with the real broker service handlers, stamping every envelope with the **automations app identity + the workflow's frozen capability set** so the host services' own ledger checks enforce the three-tier model (doc 39 §Capabilities) exactly as for any app call — the one seam between the pure interpreters and the service mesh, testable with a fake `getServiceHandler`. +30 tests (8 interpreters incl. operand coercion / fail-on-missing-id / nested failure propagation, the two default evaluators, the broker adapter's envelope shaping + identity/caps stamping + service-unavailable). automations suite **75/75**; typecheck (packages) + biome green. **Remaining host wiring → 11b.6**: construct these ports per fire + the live timer drain loop + scheduler→runner delivery + persist the `WorkflowRun/v1` via the entities service (the in-process pipeline integration test lands there).
- ✅ 11b.5 — `Reminder/v1` runner landed 2026-06-06. The "degenerate workflow executor" for reminders (doc 39 §Reminder — sugar around a single notify, its own high-volume entity type, not a Workflow+Trigger trio): a fire just posts the notification, no step interpretation. Pure cores, timer-free, same discipline as the rest of the spine. **(1) RRULE→Recurrence adapter** (`rrule-to-recurrence.ts`): `Reminder.recurrence` is RFC-5545 RRULE text, but the scheduler speaks the structured `Recurrence` — `parseRrule` maps the common subset (`FREQ` + `INTERVAL` + `BYDAY`/`BYMONTHDAY`/`BYMONTH` → Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Yearly, incl. ordinal-weekday `3TU`/`-1FR`) so recurring reminders reuse the 9.15.5 `nextOccurrence` engine wholesale, exactly like Tasks/Calendar; anything richer round-trips as `Custom { rrule }` (no in-tree expander yet → never auto-fires until it lands, documented). **(2) Schedule + transitions** (`reminder-schedule.ts`): `reminderToTriggerConfig` (snoozedUntil overrides dueAt as the one-shot; recurrence drives subsequent fires; a `Done` non-recurring reminder → `null` = never fires; a `Done` *recurring* reminder still schedules its next occurrence), `reminderNextFire`, `reminderNotification` (subject + click-to-open target), and immutable `snoozeReminder` (re-opens a completed one) / `completeReminder` (clears a pending snooze). The reminder's whole schedule is **derivable from its own persisted fields** — no extra schedule state. **(3) `ReminderRunner`** (`reminder-runner.ts`): injected store + notify ports; `configFor` (what the host registers with the `SchedulerService`), `fire` (load → defensive active-check → post notification), `snooze`/`complete` (apply transition + persist). Reuses the step-interpreter `NotifyPort` (DRY). **Host wiring → 11b.6**: register `configFor` with the scheduler on create/update/snooze/done, route a due fire to `fire(id)`. +35 tests (RRULE subset incl. Custom fallbacks; schedule/transitions; runner fire/snooze/complete/guard); automations suite **103/103**; typecheck (packages) + biome green.
- ✅ 11b.6 — `AutomationsHost` orchestrator + the in-process integration test landed 2026-06-06; the engine now **fires end-to-end** (the live session-open registration + the entities change-emitter remain — see below). The per-vault orchestrator (`automations/automations-host.ts`) is the keystone that ties 11b.2–.5 together: it owns the `SchedulerService`, drains it on an injectable real timer, and **routes each due fire to the right runner** — a workflow fire → `WorkflowRunner` (load steps+caps → run under the workflow's **own** frozen caps via `makeInterpreterPorts(caps)`, the three-tier model per fire → persist a `WorkflowRun/v1`), a reminder fire → `ReminderRunner.fire`. Covers all four engine triggers: `Time` (scheduler tick), `Manual` (`runNow`), `EntityEvent` (subscribes to an injected entity-change source → matches type+verb → runs with the changed entity as payload), and reminders. Every fire is fault-isolated (one failure is logged via `onError`, the rest of the tick proceeds). All IO injected, so the whole fire→run→persist orchestration is unit-tested (+9) **and** proven against the **real** entities + ydoc services by a CLAUDE.md §4 in-process integration test (`integration/automations-pipeline.test.ts`, +3): a workflow fire really creates a `Note/v1` in `entities.db` and persists a `WorkflowRun/v1` with the right status; a gated-kind step persists a `failed` run; a spent one-shot fires exactly once. Automations suite **115/115** + integration green; typecheck (packages) + biome clean. **Remaining (deploy into the running shell — needs a real Electron restart to verify, so split out)**: (a) `VaultSession`-open registration that loads `Workflow`/`Trigger`/`Reminder` entities → `ScheduleRegistration` → `host.hydrate()` + `host.start()`, backing the ports with `getWorkersHandle().broker` + the entities service, and `host.stop()` on dispose; (b) the entities-service post-commit **change emitter** that feeds `EntityChangeSource` (a small edit to a security-critical core file — wants its own security pass); (c) a `Manual`/`runNow` surface for the Runs view (11b.13). These are wiring, not logic — the engine itself is built and verified. **Code-review fixes (2026-06-06, iteration-chores)**: (1) the duplicated reminder RRULE parser was **deleted** — `rruleToRecurrence`/`recurrenceToRRule`/`stripRRulePrefix` extracted from `apps/calendar/src/logic/rrule.ts` to **`@brainstorm/sdk-types` `recurrence-rrule.ts`** (the one shared parser for Calendar + Automations + future consumers; calendar re-exports it), which also fixed a `FREQ=YEARLY;INTERVAL=2` bug (a biennial rule now degrades to `Custom` instead of silently firing annually); (2) `runChildren(steps, seed?: { input })` now signals seeding by the *wrapper's presence*, so a `ForEach` item of exactly `undefined` seeds `undefined` rather than falling back to the container input; (3) `AutomationsHost.hydrate` clears `reminderIds` so a re-derived schedule can't mis-route a workflow fire through a stale reminder id. +3 regression tests. **Documented limitations (deliberate, not bugs)**: (i) **fire-on-missed-once is not implemented** — `computeNextFire` uses strict `> now`, so a one-shot reminder/Time-trigger that comes due while the shell isn't draining registers dormant and is skipped rather than firing once on next launch (doc 39 §Failure modes' default); deferred with the `onMissed` policy (an un-frozen contract field, same class as `onError`). (ii) **notification `target` (click-to-open) is dropped** — the `ui.notify` host has no `target` field, so a reminder/Notify-step `target` can't route a click to the entity yet; needs the notification surface extended first. **Security review (iteration-chores) — fixed**: the three-tier capability model is now **enforced at run time**, fail-closed: `AutomationsHost.runWorkflow` refuses to run (persists a `capability-denied` `WorkflowRun/v1`, no steps execute) when a workflow's steps' aggregate caps exceed its frozen declared `capabilities[]`, or its declared set exceeds the injected app-grant ceiling — closing the HIGH finding that a workflow saved with a benign capability sheet could otherwise act with the full automations-app grant (the frozen caps were carried on the envelope but inert, since the entities service checks the *app* ledger and `getServiceHandler` bypasses the broker cap gate). +3 tests. **Security gates on the live deployment (must land before the host is wired into a running shell)**: (1) **SubWorkflow re-scoping** — `loadWorkflowSteps` returns only the callee's steps, so a sub-workflow runs under the *caller's* ports; the callee's own `capabilities[]` must be loaded and the sub-workflow re-validated/intersected at the call boundary (today a caller's static aggregate doesn't include sub-workflow steps). **Gate (1) LANDED 2026-06-14**: `WorkflowStepsLoader` now returns `{steps, capabilities}` (the callee's own frozen caps), `InterpreterPorts` carries the running caps the ports were built under, and the `SubWorkflow` interpreter re-scopes at the boundary with the SAME two-tier `missingCapabilities` check the host uses (`AutomationsHost.capabilityViolations`) — callee steps ⊆ callee declared caps, AND callee declared caps ⊆ the caps in effect — failing closed `sub-workflow-capability-denied:<caps>` (child never runs) on either tier. The broker glue (`createBrokerInterpreterPorts`) reads `props.capabilities` defensively and exposes `ports.capabilities = opts.caps`. +6 tests (callee-exceeds-own-decl, callee-decl-exceeds-running, happy run, broker loader returns caps / defaults to [] / exposes running caps); automations suite **151 green** + §4 pipeline test green; packages typecheck + biome clean. **Both 11b.6 security gates now landed** — the remaining 11b.6 residue is only the live session-open registration (real-Electron deploy). (2) **Runtime entity-type scope** — `Entity` update/delete/get resolve the id from the (untrusted) trigger payload and the entities service authorizes by the *fetched* entity's type, so a step declared on `Task/v1` can touch an entity of any type the app can write; the interpreter must verify the fetched entity's type is within the step's declared `entityType` scope before mutating. **Gate (2) LANDED 2026-06-14**: the `Entity` interpreter now fetches the target first and refuses (non-retriable `entity-<op>-out-of-scope`) when `fetched.type !== step.entityType` — update/delete also fail closed on a missing target (`entity-<op>-not-found`, the mutating ops can't confirm scope without the row); `get` keeps returning `null` for a missing entity (no scope question, no leak) but refuses to return a present out-of-scope one. So a step declared on one type can no longer reach across to another even though the entities service authorizes by fetched type. +5 tests (update/delete/get out-of-scope refusal — mutators never called; get-missing→null; update-missing→fail); automations suite **144 green** + the §4 in-process pipeline test still green. **Chores-pass follow-up 2026-06-14 (security review of the gate)**: the **Query op** was the remaining scope hole — the interpreter passes the untrusted prior-step output as the query filter, and the broker glue spread it *after* `type` (`{type, ...filter}`), so a payload `{type:"Secret/v1"}` overrode the step's declared `entityType` and (under an `entities.read:*` grant) read cross-type rows. Fixed by forcing the declared type last (`{...filter, type}`) in `createBrokerInterpreterPorts` (+1 test). **Nested re-scoping RESOLVED 2026-06-14** (the previously-deferred gap): `RunContext` now carries a per-subtree capability ceiling and `runChildren(steps, seed?, { capabilities })` lets a container narrow it; the `SubWorkflow` interpreter validates against `ctx.capabilities ?? ports.capabilities` (top-level falls back to the ports' running caps) and runs the callee's body with the ceiling narrowed to the callee's OWN declared caps. So a nested A→B→C now re-scopes C against B's caps, not A's — a narrow intermediate's consent surface is honored, not just the hard service-enforced ceiling. Branch/ForEach inherit the current ceiling unchanged. +2 tests (nested-denied-against-intermediate, nested-allowed-within-intermediate). **Both 11b.6 security gates fully landed (single + nested).** **Live deploy landed 2026-06-16 (PR #148)**: `VaultSession`-open registration (`automations/automations-registration.ts` + `wiring.ts` — hydrate/start on open, re-arm on `onActiveVaultSessionChanged`) backed by the broker + entities service, the security-reviewed entities-service post-commit **change emitter** (`entities/entity-change-emitter.ts` — identifiers-only `{verb,entityId,type}` payload, fires only after the per-type write gate + successful commit, never on `applyDoc`, throwing listeners caught), and the `runNow` surface. **Independent adversarial security review: no exploitable finding** (SSRF blocked, fail-closed caps with no TOCTOU, amplification loop closed via the `WorkflowRun/v1` EntityEvent refusal). The only remaining 11b.6 residue is real-Electron verification of the live registration.
- ✅ 11b.7 — `AICall` + `AIAgent` steps + the **shared tool-calling agent loop** (2026-06-18; gate Stage 11 ✅). **The reusable loop** lives in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `agent-loop.ts` (the dependency-free contract leaf both Automations *and* the Agent app import — "one agent loop, two front-ends", per §Agent app): `runAgentLoop(ports, config)` is pure orchestration over two injected seams (`generate` → the broker `ai` service; `dispatchTool` → an intent), so the whole generate → parse → dispatch → feed-back → repeat path is timer/IO-free and exhaustively unit-tested. **Tool-call wire format (OQ position taken — the v1 `ai.generate` surface is a plain `{messages}`→`{content}` transcript with no uniform native tool-calling across Ollama + cloud providers)**: a single auditable JSON convention in the assistant text — `{"tool","args"}` to call, `{"final","citations"}` to finish; a non-protocol reply is treated as the final answer (always terminates). Additive — a native channel can replace the parser without touching the control flow or security model. **Security keystone (fail-closed, capability-sensitive)**: the tools offered to the model are the INTERSECTION `declared-tools ∩ { t : agentToolCapabilities(t) ⊆ frozenCaps }` (`intersectAgentTools`); a tool the frozen set doesn't fully cover is never offered, and — defence in depth — a tool *call* for an off-list / uncovered name is REFUSED at dispatch (re-checked, never trusted from the model); no new wildcard cap; `maxIterations` is hard-clamped (ceiling 12) against runaway/cost. **Interpreters** (`automations/step-interpreters.ts`, port-gated exactly like HTTP/Export — registered only when the host wires `ports.ai`, else a clean `unsupported-step-kind`): `AICall` (single-shot `generate` — instructions as `system`, prior step output as the `user` turn), `AIAgent` (drives `runAgentLoop` with `frozenCapabilities = ctx.capabilities ?? ports.capabilities` so a nested SubWorkflow's narrowed ceiling is honored; tool dispatch goes through the SAME capability-checked intents port the Intent step uses → the ledger re-enforces `intents.dispatch:<verb>` server-side; the dispatch carries the tool's *declared* `entityType`, never a model-supplied one; the loop transcript is the step output for run provenance). **Host glue** (`broker-interpreter-ports.ts`): `ports.ai` maps to `ai.generate` carrying the workflow's frozen caps on the envelope (broker enforces `ai.use` + `ai.provider:<id>` fail-closed; a missing/unconfigured provider surfaces as `Unavailable` → a recorded step failure, never silent success). **Builder**: AICall/AIAgent added to `BUILDER_STEP_KINDS` + param UI (instructions textarea, provider, AIAgent tools list + maxIterations) via `<SelectMenu>`/`t()`; their tools' `intents.dispatch:<verb>` caps surface in the save-time capability sheet (the consent surface bounding the agent fail-closed at run time). +50 tests (agent-loop intersection incl. a property pass · fail-closed refusal · bounded iterations · parse/wire-format; AICall/AIAgent interpreters incl. gated-kind, declared-entityType dispatch, never-dispatch-uncovered, generate-failure; the `ai` broker port mapping; builder palette/validation/sheet). packages + apps typecheck · biome · css-tokens · reactivity green. **Reused by Agent-3** (intents-as-tools chat) — the loop is consumed, not re-implemented. **Residue**: real-Electron verify of an AI workflow firing end-to-end (rides the live deploy); token-streaming is its own rung.

The Automations app gained a `<Popover>` workflow builder authoring a `Workflow/v1` + bound `Trigger/v1` the existing runner executes unchanged (no runtime-contract change): **step palette** over the engine-spine `StepKind`s (Intent/Entity/Notify/Wait/Branch/ForEach/Code/SubWorkflow), **linear composition** (add/remove/reorder/duplicate; duplicate mints a fresh uuid), **per-step config + output-binding field**, a **capability sheet computed at save** (`aggregateWorkflowCapabilities` × `missingCapabilities` vs the app ceiling — a missing cap blocks save, mirroring the host's fail-closed `capabilityViolations`), and a **save-time validation pass** surfacing `<unbound>` inputs. Closed the live-takeover correctness gap: `wiring.ts` now watches the designation entity for changes and **stops scheduling on this device the moment a takeover names another device** (no double-fire) — still no liveness/failover (v2); a host that merely dies leaves its stale designation for the user to re-claim. +1 test (live takeover stops the old host). Lists derive from `useVaultEntities` via pure snapshot projections; every menu (incl. the former recurrence native `<select>`) routes through fancy-menus; `.app-header` contract + `#root` viewport-fill preserved. Same features, no behavior change. +87 tests; tsc + build + biome + reactivity + css-token guards clean.
- ✅ 11b.18 — **"classify + file": Entity steps write computed fields (F-458) + the trigger feeds the Entity step directly (F-459)**. The 914 business-automation audit found the engine could *think but not file* — an AI step's answer had nowhere to land, and every entity-triggered workflow needed a `Code: input.entityId` glue step. **Engine ✅ (shell #301 + #302, 2026-07-26):** `operandId` accepts the trigger payload's `{ entityId }` (explicit `id` still wins), and `EntityStep.properties` — field → expression in the existing audited Code grammar, evaluated against prior-step outputs + `input`; declared fields are authoritative (no operand merge — with an entity trigger the operand is event metadata); a bad expression fails the step naming the field. The `business-triage-flow.test.ts` proof is the report's exact workflow: Email trigger → Get → AI classify → Create Task{priority: AI answer} with the glue step DELETED. **Builder UI ✅ (shell #305, merged 2026-07-26):** "Fields to write" rows on Entity Create/Update — key + value expression with the shared prior-step binding picker (`BindingControl` extracted from `BindingField`); save-time validation blocks dangles (bare reference chains only — literals/computed values are legal); `builder.entity.*` in all 6 locales. **Shipped in `v0.10.1` (2026-07-26).** `<gates: security-review>` Residue: **session 915 (2026-07-27) ran the real-shell followup** and answered its first half — Northbound has **zero workflows**, and Automations additionally reports *"Schedules need one of your devices to run on"*, so nothing would fire even if one existed. It also found a plausible reason nobody ever set one up: the template gallery — the empty state a user with no workflows lands on — rendered raw key ids on exactly the two **business** templates (email triage, follow-up nudge), in every locale, for two releases (F-463, fixed shell #329). Rebuilding Mira's triage flow end-to-end is still owed, and is now unblocked. **The owed `/security-review` of the expression-evaluation surface RAN 2026-07-27** ([report](_review/2026-07-27-entity-step-expressions.md)): three findings fixed in shell #325 — a workflow could rewrite its own `capabilities` sheet (escalation to the full automations app ceiling), a 21-character expression amplified an 8 KB field to a persisted 64 MB value, and nested sub-cap operations froze the main process for ~4.5 s. Three design questions left open and named (broker-dispatch bypass, unenforced read-only lock, no schema validation). The original flag was: `EntityStep.properties` values are evaluated through the Code grammar, which widens where that evaluator runs, and a reviewer flagged it as needing its own pass that never happened. Surfaced by the [gate ledger](_review/evaluations.jsonl) exercise (see [70-graph-engineering.md](foundations/70-graph-engineering.md)) — declaring the gate was what made the missing evidence visible.

## Mailbox *(group I)* — 🟡

User-requested 2026-05-17 ("make users leave the app less"). Realises [apps/53-mailbox.md](apps/53-mailbox.md): the inbox as entities; protocol engine is a shell-side `MailTransport` worker, the app is designer + viewer, sending is an idempotent intent. Reference connector for [56](apps/56-connector-framework.md). **OQ-MB-1..6 (added via dev-MCP `oq.*` before code).**

- ✅ Mailbox-1 (2026-06-08) — scaffold: `MailAccount/v1` / `MailFolder/v1` / `Email/v1` contracts in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` (`mail.ts`: enums `MailProtocol`/`AuthKind`/`SyncWindow`/`FolderRole`/`MailFlag`, defs, structural validators incl. the custody invariant — a secret-shaped field on `MailAccount` is a validation error, mirroring `connector.ts`); shared address helpers (`parseMailAddress`/`parseAddressList`/`normalizeAddress`/`formatMailAddress`) + `deriveThreadKey` (OQ-MB-3 encoded as code) + `syncWindowDays`/`SYNC_WINDOW_ALL_MAX_MESSAGES` (OQ-MB-4). Manifest registers all three entity types + caps. 21 contract tests.
- ✅ Mailbox-2 (2026-06-08) — shell-side `MailTransport` worker **spine** proven in-process. New `mailbox` `utilityProcess` worker (`workers/mailbox/`, registered in `electron.vite.config.ts` + `workers.ts`; `_shell`-gated driver RPC — credentials/sockets never reach a renderer). `MailDriver` interface (`main/mailbox/mail-driver.ts`) behind which IMAP/SMTP/JMAP live; `FakeMailDriver` (in-memory) proves the path. `MailSyncEngine` (`mail-sync-engine.ts`, the `SyncRunner` analogue — every IO injected): list→upsert `MailFolder`, fetch bounded by `syncWindow`, **idempotent upsert** of `Email/v1` on `Message-ID` (server authoritative for flags only), **idempotent send** on client-stamped `submissionId`. `mail-sanitize.ts` (HTML → `bodyHtmlSafe`, layer 1) + `mail-projection.ts` (one audited parse/sanitize/thread path every driver shares). **OQ-MB-1 resolved** (own worker) / **OQ-MB-2 resolved** (socket owned inside the driver/worker, special-cased behind `network.connect:<host>`, no generic `network.socket` channel). 28 tests. **Residue (needs live accounts to verify, like the connector live-OAuth round-trip):** the real IMAP/SMTP/JMAP wire drivers (default factory reports `Unavailable` — *gmail-api landed 2026-06-11 via Mailbox-5; IMAP/SMTP/JMAP sockets still open*) + VaultSession-open registration (load accounts → read Tier-2 creds → `connect` → schedule syncs; manual `mail.syncNow` landed with Mailbox-5).
- ✅ Mailbox-3 (2026-06-08) — viewer: the coming-soon stub is now a real React app (`useVaultEntities`, no hand-rolled `onChange`). Three-pane folder rail (unified-inbox + flagged smart views + per-account folders) / message list (search, unread/flag/attachment affordances) / reading pane. Sanitized HTML body renders in a **sandboxed iframe** with its own `default-src 'none'` CSP and **remote content blocked by default + one-click "Show remote content"** (tracking-pixel defeat — `remote-content.ts`, layer 2). Flag / mark-read are the only writes (immutable received mail). Demo mail when no vault. 16 app tests.
- ✅ Mailbox-4 (2026-06-18) — compose / reply / forward as send **intents** (not a Mailbox API); idempotent on message-id. The `IntentVerb` union gained the send-family verbs (`compose`/`send`/`reply`/`forward`) with the `SendIntentVerb` enum in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` (per the no-raw-string-discriminators convention). The `IntentsBus` routes the composer verbs to the mail app (launch context for a fresh window, `app:intent` push for a running one) and handles `send` **shell-side** via the injected `sendMail` channel (the MailTransport submits + dedupes on the client-stamped `submissionId` → `Message-ID`; the broker ledger-checks `intents.dispatch:send` before the bus runs). The Mailbox composer (`apps/mailbox/src/ui/composer.tsx` + pure `logic/compose.ts`: `replySeed`/`forwardSeed`/`emptySeed`/`seedFromIntentPayload`/`sendPayloadFromSeed`, stable `submissionId` so a dispatch retry can never double-send) is a `<Popover>` form over the shared `.bs-btn` + fancy-menus From picker; reply/forward prefill from the active message, and inbound `compose`/`reply`/`forward` intents from other apps open it. Discoverable via the header Compose button + per-message Reply/Forward in the reading pane. **Compose body + subject adopt `@brainstorm/sdk/spellcheck` (`spellcheckForSurface(TextSurfaceKind.Prose)`); recipient fields opt out (`TextSurfaceKind.Code`)** — closes the B11.16b Mailbox-compose follow-up. +3 composer component tests (spellcheck surfaces, validated-send dispatch, no-recipient guard) on top of the existing 17 `compose.ts` logic tests; mailbox suite 36 green; app typecheck + biome + css-token + reactivity gates clean. *(Residue: real-shell verify of an end-to-end send rides the Mailbox-5 live-OAuth round-trip — needs Electron restart + a Google desktop OAuth client.)*
- ✅ Mailbox-5 — JMAP transport + OAuth2 (Gmail / Microsoft 365) via the connector OAuth broker — **gate: Connector-2 ✅ (cleared)**; rides the Mailbox-2 driver seam. **Gmail slice landed 2026-06-11** (Mailbox becomes the live reference connector per Connector-7, replacing the removed github-issues app): (1) `GmailDriver` (`workers/mailbox/gmail-driver.ts`, dependency-free Gmail REST `MailDriver` — labels→folders w/ role map, `messages.list`+`format=full` projection to `RawMessage`, MIME submit w/ self-stamped Message-ID idempotency; 16 tests) wired as the worker's default factory for `MailProtocol.GmailApi`; (2) the OAuth broker gained installed-app `clientSecret` support (Google Desktop clients require it at exchange/refresh even with PKCE — sealed into the Tier-2 `StoredToken`, never on an entity); (3) new app-facing **`mail` broker service** (`main/mailbox/mailbox-service.ts` + `worker-mail-transport.ts`, registered in `index.ts` sharing the connector wiring's broker/egress/entities closures): `connectGmail` (ensures the Gmail `Connector/v1`, runs loopback OAuth w/ `access_type=offline&prompt=consent`, resolves the address via `users/me/profile`, creates a `MailAccount/v1` linked by `connectorAccountRef`) / `syncNow` (fresh token → worker `connect` → `MailSyncEngine` over entity ports incl. the Mailbox-7 person index → driver always closed) / `disconnect`; server-side `mail.manage` cap (manifest + SDK `mail` proxy); (4) Mailbox app connect dialog (client id/secret → consent), header Sync-now, sync status bar, no-account CTA. 7 service tests + 2 broker tests; `bun run verify` green. **JMAP transport landed 2026-07-21** (shell #241, first rung of the 0.8.0 "Reach out" train): `JmapDriver` (`workers/mailbox/jmap-driver.ts`, RFC 8620 core + RFC 8621 mail — the second stateless-HTTPS driver alongside Gmail, **zero engine changes** on the `MailDriver` seam). Session-URL autodiscovery from the account host (RFC 8620 §2.2 `.well-known/jmap`); `Mailbox/get` folders with role map + full hierarchical paths; chained `Email/query`+`Email/get` via a `#ids` back-reference in one request, projecting to `RawMessage` (structured addresses rebuilt to header strings for the shared projection, `bodyValues`, `$seen`-absence = unread, `blobId` attachment partRefs, thread/inReplyTo/references); `downloadUrl`-template attachment fetch (template kept raw so `new URL()` can't encode the RFC 6570 braces) with the received-bytes size cap; `Email/set`+`EmailSubmission/set` submit with `onSuccessUpdateEmail` (Sent filing + `$draft` clear), CR/LF header-injection guard, and `submissionId`→`Message-ID` idempotency. **Microsoft 365 (`ms-graph`) transport landed the same day** (shell #241): `MsGraphDriver` (`workers/mailbox/ms-graph-driver.ts`) — the third stateless-HTTPS driver, over `graph.microsoft.com`. `/me/mailFolders` paged by `@odata.nextLink` with `wellKnownName` role map + hierarchical paths; `$select`+`$expand(attachments meta)`+`$orderby desc` fetch (forward `$filter receivedDateTime ge`, backfill drops it, the opaque `@odata.nextLink` is the resume cursor); `/messages/{id}/attachments/{aid}/$value` byte fetch; raw-MIME `/me/sendMail`. **DRY:** the RFC 822 MIME builder is extracted to `mail-mime.ts`, shared by Gmail + Graph. **With this, all four `MailProtocol`s (imap · jmap · gmail-api · ms-graph) build a real driver — the worker factory's residue throw is gone** (unknown protocol → `Invalid`). 27 driver tests (13 JMAP + 14 MS Graph) + updated worker-factory tests; **150 mailbox tests green, typecheck + lint clean** (Gmail's 20 unchanged after the MIME extraction). **Marked ✅ 2026-07-24 (actualisation):** all four `MailProtocol`s build a real driver and the worker factory's residue throw is gone — the 0.8.0 hero's code is complete (shell #241). What remains is not code: **Residue:** live-account verification against real JMAP (Fastmail) + M365 servers (the real-shell round-trip, like IMAP's — needs Electron restart + live credentials); `Mailbox-9` official Google/Microsoft OAuth client registration (org task); MS Graph returns one body (html *or* text) per message — multipart both-bodies deferred.
- ✅ Mailbox-6 (2026-07-20) — ~~threading UI~~ (shipped with Mailbox-1/10 — thread rows + expansion exist) → **attachments as File entities**: data path **shell #224**, reading-pane chips **shell #225**. Chips render from `attachmentParts` with nothing downloaded; a click fetches the bytes, mints the `File/v1`, and dispatches the shared `open` verb so Files/Preview pick the viewer (Mailbox ships no viewer). Chip state is per-chip not per-pane — only the fetching chip disables, an in-flight second click is ignored, a failure marks that chip alone, and retry is another click (the service is idempotent per part). `formatBytes` extracted Files→`@brainstorm/sdk/format-bytes` on the second-consumer rule. **Lazy, not eager-at-sync** (OQ resolved in review): sync stays metadata-only, bytes move only on a user gesture. `Email/v1` gained `attachmentParts` (filename · mime · size · driver-minted `partRef`); `attachments` now means real `File/v1` refs only — the `pending:<name>` pseudo-ref placeholder is gone. New optional `MailDriver.fetchAttachment` seam (Gmail `messageId:attachmentId`; IMAP `uidValidity:uid:index`, where a `uidValidity` change **fails closed** because a recreated mailbox reuses uids for different messages), bounded against bytes *actually received* rather than the server's declared size. New capability-gated `mail.fetchAttachment` writes an encrypted asset (`writeAsset`+`markBound`) into a `File/v1` carrying `assetMime` (F-421), idempotent per part with an in-flight latch. **Security:** the caller passes only `{emailRef, partRef}` — a `partRef` the email doesn't itself declare is refused before the driver is reached, and account/folder resolve from the stored row, so `entities.write:Email/v1` can't be escalated into reading arbitrary parts of any message. +16 tests; suite 2590 green. — **gate: 9.10 ✅ (cleared 2026-05; the gate note was stale)**. Scheduled: 0.7.0.
- ✅ Mailbox-7 (2026-06-08) — address→`Person/v1` resolution: `person-resolver.ts` (`buildPersonIndex` + `resolveParticipants`, **OQ-MB-6 resolved: link-to-existing, never auto-create**) wired into the engine projection via an optional `loadPersonIndex` port; matched participants get a `personRef` so Graph/Database edges fall out. Unified inbox surfaces as the rail's unified-inbox smart view (a query, not a new type). 6 resolver tests. *(Residue: the live VaultSession wiring of `loadPersonIndex` ships with Mailbox-2's session registration.)*
- ✅ Mailbox-8 (2026-07-21, shell #227) — `Email/v1` `entity-event` trigger source for Automations + AI-triage step — **gate: 11b + Stage 11 (both cleared)**. Both mechanisms already existed generically — mail-created Email entities emit change events (they write through the same entities handler that feeds the automations change bus), the `EntityEvent` framework is type-generic, and the `AICall`/`AIAgent` interpreters run whenever the host wires the AI broker port (production always does) — so this rung **proves + exposes** rather than builds. Proof: a host integration test drives `Email/v1` create → `EntityEvent` trigger → `AICall` triage step (system=instructions, user=email ref) → Succeeded run. Authorability: the builder's EntityEvent trigger type became a combobox (`<datalist>`, free-text preserved) suggesting a curated set of common triggerable types unioned with the vault's actual types (`triggerTypeSuggestions`), so email-triage is authorable without knowing `brainstorm/Email/v1`. Content-triage composes existing steps (Entity `get` → `AICall` → Entity `update` label); a canned template is a follow-up. +7 tests.
- ⚪ Mailbox-9 — **official Google OAuth client registration** (pre-release, org/process task — START EARLY, weeks-to-months of external lead time): today's connect dialog asks each user for their own GCP client id/secret (dogfood-grade). Ship path: (1) Brainstorm-owned Google Cloud project + OAuth consent screen + Desktop-app client; (2) ship its client id (+ non-confidential installed-app secret) as the prefilled default on the Gmail `Connector/v1` — the dialog collapses to one "Sign in with Google" button, custom client behind an "advanced" toggle; (3) Google **restricted-scope verification + annual CASA security assessment** for `gmail.readonly`/`gmail.send` (testing-mode client caps at 100 test users w/ 7-day refresh tokens — fine for team dogfood, not shippable); (4) same exercise for the Microsoft identity platform when the M365 transport lands. **Gate for *shipping* Mailbox-Gmail to users; not a code gate** — the per-user-client path keeps working meanwhile.
- ✅ Mailbox-10 (2026-07-18, shell PR #202) — **account management in the rail** (dogfood F-431/F-432): every account always renders in the folder rail ("Not synced yet" when folderless) with a per-account ⋯ menu — *Sync this account* / *Remove account* — the first UI exposure of `mail.disconnect`; `accountsFromEntities` hides `enabled:false` retired rows. ## Web Browser *(group I)* — 🟡

Realises [apps/54-web-browser.md](apps/54-web-browser.md): web research inside the vault; content runs in shell-managed, partitioned, Node-less `WebContentsView`s (the 38 embed sandbox generalized); the app renderer is chrome only. Clipping captures one `Bookmark/v1` (OQ-RX-5: `WebPage/v1` retired). (The external-browser web-clipper is a separate development, removed from the release 2026-05-30; the in-app browser clip is the in-product capture path.) **OQ-WV-1..6.**

- ✅ Browser-1 — scaffold + `BrowsingSession/v1` contract + caps + `types/` *(✅ 2026-06-09)*: pure contract iteration, no engine yet. **Types** (`apps/browser/src/types/`): `browsing-session.ts` freezes `brainstorm/BrowsingSession/v1` (the ephemeral, vault-local, never-synced tab/history model) as two shapes — the live `BrowsingSession`/`BrowserTab` (carries runtime `TabLoadState`/`TabSecurityState`/`blockedTrackerCount` painted from host events) and the persisted `BrowsingSessionRecord`/`TabSnapshot` (runtime metadata dropped; restore re-navigates) — plus `MAX_RECENTLY_CLOSED`/`NEW_TAB_URL` and the `TabLoadState`/`TabSecurityState` enums (no raw discriminators). `web-view.ts` is the **chrome-only / shell-engine split keystone**: the full `WebView` host-service wire contract — `WebViewMethod` (open/navigate/back/forward/reload/stop/close/activate/set-bounds/find/capture) with per-method request shapes, `WebViewEventKind` + the metadata-only `WebViewEvent` union (title/favicon/url/load-state/security-state/tracker-blocked/find-result/permission/captured/closed — the page DOM + bytes never cross this boundary), and the `WEB_BROWSE_CAP`/`WEB_CAPTURE_CAP` constants. Browser-2 implements the host against these types and lifts the module to a shared wire-types home. **Logic** (`logic/session.ts`): a pure, clock-free, id-injected `BrowsingSession` reducer (`createSession`/`openTab`/`closeTab`/`reopenClosedTab`/`activateTab`/`navigateTab`/`goBack`/`goForward`/`canGoBack`/`canGoForward`/`setPinned`/`applyTabMeta`/`toRecord`/`fromRecord`) — back/forward history with forward-branch truncation, neighbour-picking active marker on close, the bounded reopen-closed ring, and the live↔persisted round-trip; no-op transitions return the same reference (identity-stable). **Manifest**: declares the `web.browse` (High) + `web.capture` (Medium) capabilities and the `entities.read/write` grants for `BrowsingSession/v1` + the shared `Bookmark/v1` (clip target), and registers the `BrowsingSession/v1` entity type with its inline JSON schema. Per least-privilege + the chrome-only split, the app renderer does **not** hold `network.connect:*` — the shell-side `WebView` host performs all page egress under the shared proxy + egress audit; `web.browse` IS the egress consent, and granting the app the broadest raw-fetch cap it never exercises would undercut the very split this iteration establishes (security-review call). The app renderer stays the `coming-soon` placeholder until Browser-3 lands the chrome. **+22 reducer tests** (session.test.ts) green; first-party manifest validation + installer + seed suites green (188/188 across `apps/` + `dev/`); `typecheck:apps` (all 20 apps) + biome clean; browser app builds. No OQ flips (OQ-WV-1..5 + OQ-168 are Browser-2 engine decisions).
- ✅ Browser-2 — `WebView` host service *(✅ 2026-06-09)*: the shell-managed, partitioned, Node-less `WebContentsView` engine the chrome drives (the page DOM/bytes never reach a Brainstorm renderer). **OQ-WV-1 resolved** = one `WebContentsView` per tab with its own ephemeral, non-`persist:` partition destroyed on close (private-by-default, no cross-tab cookie linkage). **OQ-WV-2 resolved** = soft cap of 6 live views/window, LRU-suspend the oldest non-pinned tab (destroy view, retain URL, reload on re-activation); pinned tabs exempt. Wire contract lifted to the shared `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `web-view.ts` (shell + app speak one vocabulary; the app re-exports it, frozen values intact). **Pure core** `web/web-view-service.ts` (`WebViewService` + `makeWebViewServiceHandler`): tab registry, method routing (open/navigate/back/forward/reload/stop/close/activate/set-bounds/find/capture), metadata-event fan-out, suspension — every Electron touch-point injected, exhaustively fake-tested (+14). **Security keystone** `web/web-policy.ts` (pure, +10 tests): HTTPS-upgrade (loopback-exempt, top-level only), bundled tracker/ad blocklist (OQ-WV-4 static v1 list), fail-closed navigation-scheme allowlist (`file:`/`javascript:`/custom refused), security badges. **Electron glue** `web/web-view-factory.ts` (verified live, like `print-to-pdf`): builds the locked-down view (`sandbox`/`contextIsolation` on, `nodeIntegration` off, **no preload**), deny-default permission handlers (surfaced as a `PermissionRequested` event), blocklist `onBeforeRequest`, window-open denied, wires native events → metadata events, offsets bounds by the window body origin (new `WindowContainer.bodyBounds()`). Registered as the `webView` broker service (`web.browse`-gated, fail-closed) + SDK `webViewProxy` (cap-stamped) + preload `APP_WEBVIEW_EVENT_CHANNEL` fan-out. **+24 web tests**; packages typecheck/biome clean. Reader-extraction `capture` → `Bookmark/v1` is wired as an injected port but not yet implemented (Browser-5).
- ✅ Browser-3 — tabbed chrome *(✅ 2026-06-09)*: graduated `apps/browser` from the coming-soon stub to a React chrome-only app (`app.tsx` + `main.tsx`) driving `services.webView` and painting from its metadata events — tab strip (open/close/switch/new), omnibox (URL-or-search normalize), back/forward/reload/stop, per-tab security badge + tracker shield, all strings via `t()`. Tab state is the pre-existing pure `logic/session.ts` reducer (in-memory; `BrowsingSession/v1` persist + restore is a follow-up). The web region is a placeholder div whose rect the chrome reports via `setBounds` so the shell floats the `WebContentsView` under the chrome. Builds clean; `typecheck:apps` + biome green. **Find-in-page + `BrowsingSession/v1` restore landed 2026-06-11**: a chrome find bar over `WebViewMethod.FindInPage`/`StopFind` (Cmd+F via the SDK shortcut binder, Enter/Shift+Enter cycle, Escape close, match counts from `FindResult` events); `BrowsingSession/v1` persistence as a debounced single-entity upsert of the session record + restore-on-launch (fresh-minted tab ids, lazy view mount on first activation, deep-link seed kept foreground), pure codec in `logic/persistence.ts`. **Reopen-recently-closed landed 2026-06-10** (a fancy-menus anchored menu of closed tabs + Cmd+Shift+T to reopen the most recent, driving a new `reopenClosedTabAt` reducer fn over the bounded reopen-closed ring + re-mounting the restored `WebContentsView`; +pure menu-projection tests). **Link-routing landed alongside**: the manifest registers `http`/`https` **primary scheme openers**, so a web link opens in the in-app Browser by default through the existing open-resolution ladder (`decideOpen` Scheme branch honours `hasInVaultOpener`); the **Settings → Default apps → Schemes** section auto-populates `http:`/`https:` rows with an "Open with system default" choice (zero new UI), giving the user the system-browser escape hatch. +1 open-resolution regression anchor. *(Remaining: a per-page "open in system browser" affordance inside the chrome — needs a small cap-gated force-OS-handoff intents option, deferred.)*
- ✅ Browser-4 — tracker/ad blocklist + HTTPS-upgrade **landed with Browser-2's locked session** (`web-policy.ts`) *(v1 scope COMPLETE; web-policy 21 unit tests re-verified green at close-out 2026-06-14)*. **Third-party-cookie block landed 2026-06-11**: pure registrable-domain third-party decision + Cookie/Set-Cookie strip helpers in `web-policy`, applied via `onBeforeSendHeaders`/`onHeadersReceived` on the locked per-tab session (main-frame exempt; the partition isolation already gives per-tab cookie jars). **Post-v1 follow-on (not Browser-4 residue)**: the **OQ-WV-4 signed updatable blocklist feed** — the static v1 list ships and covers v1.
- ✅ Browser-5 — clip-to-vault **affordance landed** *(2026-06-09, F-161)*: per-tab "Save to vault" button in the chrome toolbar (star; disabled on non-http(s)/no page; Saving→Saved flash + `role="status"` announce + Failed retry) maps the metadata the chrome already holds (url + page title from host events) onto a `brainstorm/Bookmark/v1` property bag (`logic/clip.ts`, matches the Bookmarks codec exactly; remote favicon deliberately NOT persisted — `faviconUrl` is contractually a local asset URL the Bookmarks scrape backfills) and creates it via `entities.create` under the manifest's existing `entities.write:brainstorm/Bookmark/v1` (zero new IPC/capability surface; `web.capture` stays reserved for the shell-side reader extraction). Page-supplied title hardened via the new shared `@brainstorm/sdk/sanitize-text` (`sanitizeInlineText` — extracted from editor peer-presence at copy two; control/zero-width/bidi strip + whitespace collapse + clamp); URL re-serialized through `URL` with scheme allowlist + length bound. +13 clip tests, +7 sanitize tests. **Full version landed 2026-07-28** (shell `feat/browser-5-capture-reader`), completing the rung: (1) the injected `capture` port is **wired** — `WebViewMethod.Capture` pulls the tab's RENDERED DOM (the Net-3 live-DOM feeder, 8M-char clamp), runs the **same Net-2 extraction worker**, pulls article images into the encrypted asset store through the exact `network.readable` guard chain (`enrichBlocksWithAssets` — SSRF/privacy/size/MIME, now exported), and writes the `Bookmark/v1` through the shared entities create path (per-type cap applies) via the new pure seal `web/web-capture.ts` (URL re-serialized + scheme allowlist + length bound; title/description/siteName/author `sanitizeInlineText`-hardened; publish date parsed-or-dropped; block tree capped) — scrape-parity metadata, one codec, three feeders converge. (2) **Reader mode** in the chrome: per-tab toggle (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R, Escape closes) rendering the extracted article — title / sanitized `byline` (new on `WebViewExtractedText`) / paragraphs — as plain React text nodes (no HTML injection, no `srcdoc` — F-439; app CSP unchanged), with the native `WebContentsView` parked at zero bounds while the sheet is up (it composites above the chrome; same reasoning as the summary panel). Navigation / tab close invalidates the article. (3) Save-to-vault now **prefers the shell seal** (the live logged-in/script-rendered DOM, offline images) with the chrome-side re-fetch kept as fallback. **SECURITY**: `Capture` / `ExtractText` now fail closed server-side unless the broker VERIFIED `web.capture` on the call (previously only the SDK proxy stamped it). +41 tests (seal hostile-input, service live-DOM/clamp/cap-denial, app reader states + park/restore + capture-preference, pure reader logic); reader strings in all six catalogs.
- ✅ Browser-6 — downloads → Files host service — **gate: 9.10** *(shell #272, 2026-07-24)*. Page downloads captured in the web-view host (session `will-download`) → buffered under a size cap → sealed into the encrypted asset store → `brainstorm/File/v1` entity via the shared `entities.create` path (per-type cap `entities.write:brainstorm/File/v1` granted to Browser; DEK + asset-ref bind + live change event all apply). Untrusted bytes hardened in pure `web-download.ts`: basename-only filename sanitize (no path traversal, control/zero-width/bidi strip, extension-preserving clamp), served-mime allow-list (no active content off the asset protocol), size ceiling (256 MiB), http(s) source-URL validation. New `DownloadStarted`/`Completed`/`Failed` WebView events + `DownloadFailReason` enum + a chrome downloads notice (top-chrome flow). +24 tests. **Open:** private-tab downloads currently also persist to the vault (an explicit user action) — revisit if they should be excluded.
- ✅ Browser-7 — per-site permission grants + per-host egress audit *(✅ 2026-06-11)*: deny-default camera/mic/geolocation with per-origin grants — `SitePermissionKind` in sdk-types, a `SetSitePermission` wire method, pending-ask `PermissionRequested` events carrying the origin, a per-vault grant store persisted at `<vault>/shell/web-site-permissions.json` (fail-closed across vault switch), a chrome ask banner (Allow persists + reloads; Block persists the refusal), and Settings → Privacy browser groups (grants list with revoke + a per-host egress aggregate from the locked session's `onBeforeRequest` — hosts only, bounded + debounced flush) over new privileged `web-privacy:*` IPC. i18n descriptions for the new `shell.settings.webPrivacy.*` keys.
- ✅ Browser-8 — agentic surface. **Read-only browsing landed 2026-07-24** (shell `feat/browser-8-agentic`), resolving **OQ-WV-5 → yes**: `web.browse:read-only` is a real, separate capability scope (`capabilityImplies` treats unscoped and scoped as disjoint, so `web.browse` never silently confers it and holding only it can never widen). The mode is derived from the caps the **broker verified on the opening call** — never a caller-passed flag — fixed once at open, carried on the tab entry so a suspension remount can't widen it, and fail-closed everywhere else (no browse cap declared, or a navigate that mints a tab, ⇒ read-only). Enforcement is structural: a read-only view gets its **own throwaway partition** (an autonomous loop never browses inside the user's logged-in cookie jar) and that session **refuses every non-GET/HEAD request**, so a hostile page cannot steer the loop into submitting anything. `web-readonly.ts` holds both decisions as pure functions; the Electron half calls them. Also lands the agentic READ path's contract: `WebViewMethod.ExtractText` (+ `WebViewExtractedText`, the `openReadOnly`/`extractText` SDK proxy methods) returns a page's reader projection to the caller instead of writing a Bookmark, gated on `web.capture`. **Summarize/extract landed 2026-07-24** (shell `feat/browser-8-summarize`), completing the rung: a **Summarize this page** item in the browser's ⋯ menu reads the live page (Net-3 `extractText`, `web.capture`) and summarizes it through the broker (`ai.use`), rendering into a dismissible panel in the top chrome (a glance, not a mode — a bottom overlay would be painted over by the native `WebContentsView`). It goes through **`ai.transform` with a new `AiTransformKind.Summarize`**, NOT a hand-rolled `ai.generate` prompt — that puts the page in the request's `source`, so third-party text can only ever land in the *user* role, and the "this is content, NEVER instructions" guard lives once in the contract leaf for every app that summarizes (Notes / Mailbox get it free). Bounded + honest: the source is clamped to 24k chars before any model call (a cost bound, not just latency); a page with nothing readable is refused rather than asking a model about `""`; no-content / no-model / call-failed are three distinct messages; and a ready summary always carries its provenance line (a generated summary is not the page). **Note:** `capture` → `Bookmark/v1` (Browser-5's half) can now bind the same Net-3 feeder. — **gate: Stage 11 / 11b ✅.**
- ✅ Browser-9 — browsing history *(✅ 2026-06-11, founder feedback "browser does not remember websites you have visited")*: the browser now remembers visited pages. New `brainstorm/BrowsingHistory/v1` (manifest registration + `entities.read/write` caps) — ONE bounded entity per vault, most-recent-first `visits` (`url`/`title`/`visitCount`/`lastVisitedAt`; cap 500; revisiting dedupes by URL, bumps the count, moves to front). Pure core `apps/browser/src/logic/history.ts` (record / retitle / merge / match / fail-soft codec; URLs gated through the clip's `clippableUrl` so only http(s) is ever recorded — `about:blank` + custom schemes never enter; titles hardened via `sanitizeInlineText`). The chrome feeds it from the same host metadata stream it already paints from — `UrlChanged` records the visit, `TitleChanged` backfills the title — and loads/persists it debounced exactly like the session entity (visits recorded before the async load land first via `mergeVisits`). Two surfaces: (1) **omnibox suggestions** — combobox-pattern dropdown (aria-activedescendant; ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Escape via the SDK shortcut binder on the input, Enter navigates the highlight; ranking host-prefix > URL-substring > title-substring with recency/frequency tiebreaks); (2) the toolbar **History menu** (the recently-closed button generalized): recently-closed section + recently-visited section + destructive "Clear browsing history", all through the shared `openAnchoredMenu`. Recording is default-ON per the founder feedback (doc-54's opt-in-retention default superseded for visits); residue: Settings → Privacy retention toggle + clear surface, and folding `retainHistory` semantics into it. 24 pure + 5 wiring tests (93 total in the app).
- ✅ Browser-10 — encrypted persistent cookies + private tabs *(✅ 2026-06-13, founder feedback "not very usable without cookie storage; cookies should be encrypted")*: **OQ-WV-6 resolved** = persistent-by-default + private tabs, cookies-only v1, encrypted under the vault key. Normal tabs now SHARE one in-memory partition (`PERSISTENT_WEB_PARTITION = "bs-web-persist"`) so a login sticks across tabs and restarts (the old per-tab `bs-web-<tabId>` partition meant two tabs of one site weren't even logged in together); **private tabs** keep the throwaway per-tab partition (no persistence, never written to the jar, never persisted to the session record — `private` lives only on the runtime `BrowserTab`, deliberately absent from `TabSnapshot` so it's type-impossible to snapshot; `closeTab` skips the reopen ring; `toRecord` filters them + re-points a private active id). **Encryption is the keystone**: we do NOT switch to a Chromium `persist:` partition (its cookie store is only OS-keyed — Keychain/DPAPI/`v10`-on-Linux — and it writes DOM storage in plaintext, below the vault's at-rest bar). The session stays in-memory (Chromium writes nothing to disk) and the shell owns persistence: a new 6th DataStore `cookies.db` (`AtRestDb.Cookies` → its own HKDF subkey, same SQLCipher path as `entities.db`), a typed `CookieJarRepository` (no inline SQL; RFC-6265 `(name,domain,path)` identity; `deleteExpired`/`clear`), a pure Electron-free `cookie-serde` (live cookie ↔ record ↔ `cookies.set` spec, reconstructing the `url` Electron wants; session cookies refused), and `WebCookieJar` (hydrate-on-open + mirror live `cookies.on("changed")` write-through; clears the live session on dispose so a vault switch can't leak). Wired in `index.ts` via `onActiveVaultSessionChanged` (open→hydrate, close/switch→dispose, serialized). **Factory refactor (security-critical)**: the locked-down session policy (deny-default permissions, tracker/ad blocklist + egress, third-party-cookie strip) now installs **once per session** (a webRequest/permission slot is singular per session — the shared persistent session would otherwise let the last tab's handler win for every sibling, silently breaking the third-party strip) and attributes per request via a new `resolveTabContext(webContentsId)` from the service (tab id + the tab's authoritative first-party URL). **Chrome**: a "New private tab" + "Clear browsing data" overflow menu (shared `openAnchoredMenu`, right-aligned), `webView.open(tabId, url, isPrivate)` + `webView.clearBrowsingData()` on the wire contract. The jar lives entirely in the main process — **no new app-facing IPC/capability**; the Browser renderer still never sees a cookie. **+18 storage/serde + 7 jar + 4 service + 4 reducer tests** (340+ across web/storage/app); packages + apps typecheck + the new suites green. **Residue**: real-shell verify (login persists across restart; private tab isolated; clear-data wipes) — needs a full shell restart; `localStorage`/IndexedDB persistence is a deferred follow-up (needs per-origin scripting). The covers/wallpapers/icons plaintext-blob gap surfaced alongside (OQ-240) is tracked separately.

## Agent app *(group I, Stage 11c)* — 🟡

Realises [apps/55-agent-app.md](apps/55-agent-app.md): the conversation surface of [22](platform/22-ai-foundations.md). **One agent loop, two front-ends** — Automations runs it on a trigger, the Agent app on a turn; no second engine. **Reverses doc-22 "chat post-v1"** (reconciliation flagged in 55). **OQ-AG-1..5.**

**Started early (priority insert, 2026-06-07) via a LOCAL-MODEL path**, the same way Automations (11b) jumped the serial order: an Ollama provider behind the designed `ModelProvider` seam ungates a dogfoodable AI stack **without** waiting on the bundled-model decision (OQ-57/OQ-62) or a cloud key (consistent with **OQ-60 = v1 is BYO**). This pulled forward a **partial Stage 11.5** (the `ai` broker host service) — see the Stage 11 section. Two documented positions taken here:
- **Messaging-compatible foundation** (per the build directive): `Message/v1`'s sender is a discriminated `MessageSender` union (`user`/`assistant`/`tool` + forward-compat `participant{personRef}` for the v2 Chats app) rather than doc-55's bare `role`. The AI surface is a strict subset of the messaging surface, so Chats reuses these contracts + the transcript UI rather than forking. **New OQ-AG-6** (Agent↔Chats foundation sharing).
- **Messages are first-class `Message/v1` entities** (reactive via `useVaultEntities`, natural for both Agent + Chats), a deliberate divergence from doc-55's "one Yjs transcript doc, one node per message" sketch; the Yjs-body upgrade is additive and does not change the contract.

- ✅ Agent-1 — scaffold + contracts: `Conversation/v1` + `Message/v1` frozen in `@brainstorm/sdk-types` (`conversation.ts` — enums/sender-union/validators + the shared `ai.generate` request/result/stream-event types + `aiCapabilitiesForRequest`, mirroring `automations.ts`); app graduated from the coming-soon stub to a React build (manifest registers both types with inline schemas + narrow caps — `ai.use`, Conversation/Message r/w, **no `entities.read:*`** since the broker assembles retrieval); doc-22 reversal reconciled in the preamble.
- ✅ Agent-2 — **first slice: plain chat over the broker + local model.** Send → user `Message/v1` → `services.ai.generate(transcript)` → broker `ai` service → Ollama provider → reply persisted as an assistant `Message/v1` with `aiProvenance`. **Non-streaming** (the broker is request/reply; token-streaming over a push channel is the next rung) and **no tools yet**. Dogfood session `174` drives it end-to-end against a live Ollama (skips when unreachable). Remaining for full Agent-2: the **shared 11b agent-loop** (tool-calling) — **gate: 11b.7 + Stage 11 broker proper**; token-streaming rung.
- ✅ Agent-3 — intents-as-tools, three-tier fail-closed intersection (agent-tools ⊆ conversation-grants ⊆ app-caps), audited on the standard capability sheet. **Landed 2026-06-18**: the Agent app consumes the shared `runAgentLoop` (`@brainstorm/sdk-types` `agent-loop.ts`, from 11b.7) — no second engine. `apps/agent/src/logic/agent-tools.ts` adds the third tier: `effectiveAgentCapabilities(appCaps, conversationGrants) = intersect` (fail-closed — a conversation can only narrow), passed as `frozenCapabilities`; `defaultConversationGrants` defaults to full app-caps (the per-conversation grant UI is Agent-5, structured as a separate input). One curated read-only tool `open` (no declared `entityType` — shell resolves the id's type; requires only the manifest's existing `intents.dispatch:open`, no new cap/wildcard); `toolCallToIntent` strips any model-supplied `entityType` and re-keys to the declared tool; dispatch goes through the cap-checked `services.intents.dispatch` (ledger re-checks server-side). `app.tsx` branches the turn to the loop when tools are offered, else Agent-2 plain chat; tool steps persist + render "Used …" chips. +24 tests (482 agent/sdk-types pass); typecheck + own-file lint clean. Residue: real-Electron verify that `services.intents` is injected + a live `open` dispatch navigates.
- ✅ Agent-4 — broker-assembled hybrid retrieval; cited answers as clickable vault-object links. **Landed 2026-06-18** (gate Stage 11 hybrid / 9.22 cleared): `apps/agent/src/logic/retrieval.ts` — on each user turn `retrieveContext` calls the capability-gated `services.search.hybrid({text, limit:6})` (RRF), reduces to bounded top-K context items (`<mark>` stripped, snippet clamped) injected into the model's instruction region so it grounds + cites real ids; fail-soft (no service / empty / throw → ungrounded chat, never crash). Retrieval rides ONLY the gated `search` service (`search.read` + `search.hybrid` added to the manifest) — no `entities.read:*` for retrieval. The loop's `{"final","citations":[…]}` ids render as clickable links (labelled by the turn's search-hit titles) that open via the SAME cap-checked `open` intent Agent-3 wired (`openEntity`); citations persist on the `Message/v1`. +21 tests (501 agent/sdk-types pass); typecheck + own-lint + css-token clean. Residue: real-shell verify `services.search` injection + a live citation-link navigation. *(Hardening follow-up: the app's own conversation/message list still uses the whole-vault `useVaultEntities` snapshot — `entities.read:*`; migrating it to type-scoped `entities.query` (the Books pattern) would drop the wildcard — a platform-wide pattern, not Agent-specific.)*
  - **✅ Agent-4 grounding fix — real-shell verified 2026-06-30 (Qwen dogfood, session 372; F-311).** Dogfooding the Agent against Mira's vault on a local model (qwen2.5:7b) proved `services.search` injection works but retrieval returned **0 hits every turn**, so the agent fabricated company data ("ACME Tech Solutions" / "Global Innovations Inc.") presented as vault-grounded. Two root causes fixed on `feat/agent-vault-grounding`: (1) **NL query** — `buildMatchExpression` (`search/search-indexer.ts`) ANDed every token (stopwords included), so a full-sentence turn matched nothing and lexical-only hybrid degraded to empty; now the precise AND stays primary and, on an empty match, retries as a bm25-ranked **OR over content words** (stopwords dropped) — keyword/launcher behaviour unchanged. (2) **Self-pollution** — the just-asked question, persisted + indexed as a `Message/v1`, outranked every real note; added **`excludeTypes`** through the search stack (`SearchQuery` → `IndexerQuery` → service `requireQuery`) and the Agent now excludes its own Conversation/Message/Memory from retrieval. (3) **Anti-fabrication guard** — shared `AGENT_GROUNDING_GUIDANCE` appended to both agent system prompts (answer only from provided context; say "not in your vault" rather than invent). +tests: search-indexer NL-fallback + excludeTypes, `grounding-prompt.test.ts`; typecheck (packages+apps) + biome clean. Re-dogfood (372) confirms the retrieval block now carries real vault objects.
- ✅ Agent-5 — per-conversation tool grants + model + budget; inline mid-conversation escalation prompt — **OQ-AG-1 / OQ-AG-2**. **Landed 2026-06-18**: a per-conversation settings dialog (shared `<Popover>` + `<SelectMenu>`, opened from a header gear) scopes THIS conversation. **Grants** — `Conversation/v1.toolGrants` (`string[]`) persists the user-chosen capability subset; `app.tsx` now feeds the conversation's stored grants into Agent-3's `effectiveAgentCapabilities(appCaps, conversationGrants)` (defaulting to full app-caps when unset, so behaviour is unchanged until the user narrows) — the three-tier intersection stays the single chokepoint. Toggles scope exactly the `intents.dispatch:*` surface (infra caps `ai.*`/`search.*`/`entities.*` always survive so chat never breaks); `composeGrants` re-filters to caps the app holds (defence in depth — grants only ever NARROW). **Model** — `Conversation/v1.provider`/`model`; the picker offers only the providers the app's `ai.provider:<id>` caps allow (manifest gained anthropic/openai/glm/gemini alongside ollama), AUTO = shell default; threaded onto `ai.generate`/the loop (broker re-checks the provider cap server-side). **Budget** — `Conversation/v1.tokenBudget`/`tokensSpent` (token-based; local model is free); `budgetCheck` (fail-closed, strict-greater) refuses a turn whose estimated cumulative prompt tokens — via `estimateTokens` (the same `ai.cost` estimator) — would exceed the budget, with a clear inline error rather than overspending; `accrueSpend` bumps the running total after each turn. **Inline escalation** — when the loop REFUSES a tool for `CapabilityDenied` (a `tool-refused` step now persisted on `Message/v1.toolCalls`), an inline prompt offers to grant that one cap for THIS conversation; accept routes through `grantCapability` (adds the cap ONLY when ⊆ app-caps — a no-op otherwise; explicit user action, never auto-grant), dismiss is sticky for the session. New `logic/conversation-settings.ts` (all pure: grant narrowing/escalation merge/provider derivation/budget accounting) + `conversation-settings-popover.tsx` + `escalation-prompt.tsx`. +29 tests (530 agent/sdk-types pass); packages+apps typecheck · own-file biome · css-tokens · reactivity green; app builds. **Residue**: real-Electron verify (open settings, narrow a tool, pin a cloud model, hit a budget, accept an escalation); Agent-6/7 deferred. *(OQ-AG-1/-2 to be marked RESOLVED in 11-open-questions.md.)*
- ✅ Agent-6 — save-as-automation → `Workflow/v1` (generalize args, user-reviewed diff). **Landed 2026-06-18** (gate 11b cleared): `apps/agent/src/logic/save-as-automation.ts` generalizes a conversation's executed loop steps into a Workflow/v1 draft = Manual trigger + a single `AIAgentStep` (a 1:1 replay of the same `runAgentLoop` the conversation drove — not a lossy per-tool transcription), saved disabled for review. `generalizeInstruction` rewrites entity-id-looking tokens to a `{{input}}` parameter bound to the trigger (reusable, not a one-run replay). Review-then-commit via a shared `<Popover>` diff; persists Trigger/v1 + Workflow/v1 over the cap-checked entities service (`entities.write:brainstorm/{Trigger,Workflow}/v1` added — no wildcard). **Cap-subset invariant**: step tools = dispatched tools ∩ frozen-covered; `aggregateWorkflowCapabilities` + `validateCapabilityTiers` assert `workflow-caps ⊆ frozenCaps ⊆ appCaps`, fail-closed (`GeneralizeRefusal` on any out-of-range cap / empty set), identical to Agent-5's grant model.
