### Agent writes your vault *(Agent-11 — 0.9.0 hero, [platform/75-agent-notes-seam.md](platform/75-agent-notes-seam.md) OQ-ANS-4)* — 🟡

The agent generates real vault data in chat — the model-callable *write* half deferred by Agent-10. **Owner decisions (2026-07-23):** (1) **preview + confirm each write** — so create tools are **propose, not persist**: the model stages a bounded draft, the human approves, and only then does the app's own `entities.create` run (no model output — including a prompt injection — can put bytes in the vault; `entities.write:*` stays a human-gesture cap); (2) **single-user first** (multi-human shared agent chat rides the Collab/sharing train `0.12.0`, reusing this); (3) **coverage = all three tiers** (simple entities → DB rows → new databases). The shared `runAgentLoop` needs no change — the propose/persist split lives in the tool catalogue + the host `dispatchTool`. Per-type propose verbs (`propose-note`…) are gated by the existing Agent-5 grant UI (`intents.dispatch:propose-<type>`). New capability surface → security-review + pentest (prompt-injection) gate; resolves OQ-ANS-4; no self-merge.

- ✅ Agent-11a — **propose-artifact catalogue + fail-closed staging** *(shell `feat/agent-11a-propose-tools`, 2026-07-23)*. Pure, fully-tested foundation (loop unchanged; nothing wired yet — the manifest caps + host dispatch + cards land together in 11b so no tool is ever offered before it can be handled). `apps/agent/src/logic/propose-artifacts.ts`: `ProposeKind` + `PROPOSE_DESCRIPTORS` for Note/Journal/Task/Event/Bookmark/Contact with canonical owner-app-visible entity types (Note = `io.brainstorm.notes/Note/v1`, resolved against each app's live query); `proposeTools` (no `entityType` → cap is just `intents.dispatch:propose-<verb>`); `proposeToolCapabilities`/`proposeEntityWriteCapabilities`; `buildProposal` (allowlist + drop-non-string + clamp + require-primary, fail-closed); `buildProposalAck` (honest "not saved until approved") + `PROPOSE_TOOL_GUIDANCE`; `proposalReducer` pending buffer (add/edit/discard/remove/clear). +20 tests incl. the security invariants (no propose tool carries read/write; grants gate every tool via the fail-closed intersection); typecheck + biome clean.
- ✅ Agent-11b — **preview-confirm UX** (the hero surface) *(shell `feat/agent-11a-propose-tools` `936117a6`, 2026-07-23)*. The agent now GENERATES vault data in chat. `turn.ts` intercepts a `propose-*` verb BEFORE any dispatch — it stages a bounded draft via an `onPropose` sink and returns the pending-approval ack; **it never calls `intents.dispatch`, so no model output (prompt injection included) reaches the vault** (pinned by `turn.test.ts`). `curatedAgentTools` now offers the propose tools alongside read-only `open`; the system prompt carries `PROPOSE_TOOL_GUIDANCE`. `proposal-tray.tsx` renders approve/edit/discard cards above the composer (bs-input faces, shared Icon, accent approve, full a11y); `app.tsx` owns the conversation-scoped buffer and — **only on the approve gesture** — runs `entities.create`, the one place `entities.write:<type>` is exercised for a proposal. `propose-persist.ts` is the schema-aware mapper (Task `title→name`/`dueDate→dueAt` ms; Event `notes→description` + synthesized `start`/`allDay`; Bookmark `tags[]`/`savedAt`; Contact `notes→bio`; Note plain body the editor rebuilds; required timestamps synthesized, unparseable dates → null). **Journal dropped** from the catalogue (stable per-day id + Y.Doc body ≠ plain create; 11a's descriptor wrongly aliased it to the Note type — a journal proposal would land invisibly in Notes; deferred to a later rung). Manifest declares the propose dispatch caps + the 5 `entities.write:<type>` caps + its de/fr/it/pt packs (undeclared-but-tracked — the app's slice of a pre-existing i18n-gate breakage on `main`). +22 tests (mapper all 5 kinds + date/required edges; turn security invariant; tray interaction contract). 242 agent tests green; typecheck + biome + css-tokens + control-faces clean; app bundles. **Resolves OQ-ANS-4.** Residue: real-shell dogfood; security-review + pentest before the 0.9.0 cut.
- ✅ Agent-11c — **provenance + back-links** *(shell #271, 2026-07-24)*. Each entity the agent creates on approval carries a **server-authoritative provenance stamp** — `agentProvenance = { agent, conversationId, createdAt }` in the entity's properties (new `@brainstorm-os/sdk-types/agent-provenance`, mirroring `aiProvenance`-on-Message; no DB migration). **Non-forgeable**: the entities service strips any caller-supplied reserved key from every create/update, then re-stamps `agent` from the broker-verified `envelope.app` — an app can only ever attribute a create to itself, and the model never reaches the path (only the human approve gesture persists, and it supplies just the conversation id from app state). `entities.create` gains an optional `provenance` arg; `update` treats provenance as create-time + immutable. Chat renders **created-object chips** derived reactively from the live vault snapshot via the provenance back-link, each opening through the cap-checked `open` intent (`intents.dispatch:open`, ledger + type resolved server-side). No new capability surface. i18n en/es/de/fr/it/pt. +17 tests. Residue: real-shell dogfood (approve → chip → navigate); security-review + pentest. Threads into 11d/11e (DB rows / new databases).
- ✅ Agent-11d — **database rows** *(shell `feat/agent-11d-db-rows`, 2026-07-24)*. Coverage tier 2: the agent proposes a ROW in one of the user's databases, and the row's shape is the USER's, not a build-time allowlist. `logic/propose-row.ts` derives a `DatabaseSchema` per Collection from the live snapshot (default view's visible non-computed columns + the title column; each column's `ValueType` inferred from that database's existing rows) and builds the model's context block from it, so the model targets a database by name and fills real columns. `buildRowProposal` resolves the named database (exact id → case-insensitive name; **ambiguous or unknown = refused**, never a guess into the wrong database), then keeps ONLY that database's own columns (matched by key or humanized label), dropping non-strings and clamping each value — a null-prototype bag, so no invented/prototype key can reach a write. On approval `persistApprovedProposal` coerces each cell to its column's type (`coerceScalarValue`: number / boolean / Unix-ms date; unparseable → property omitted, never a wrong value) and creates the row — a typed database's own type, or the generic `Object/v1` + ONE additive `members.include` pin for a manual collection (`memberPinPatch`, capped at `MEMBERS_HARD_CAP`, never rewriting membership it didn't add). Fail-closed twice over: the tool isn't offered at all when the vault has no databases, and `writableDatabaseSchemas` drops any database whose row type (or membership) the manifest can't write, so the model is never shown a target whose approval would be denied. Same security posture as 11a/11b — `turn.ts` intercepts the verb before any dispatch, so a row only ever becomes bytes on the human approve gesture. The tray renders the draft as the row it will become (label column / editable value column, target database named). Shared pieces promoted rather than copied: `decideRowCreate` + `GENERIC_OBJECT_TYPE` and the new `coerceScalarValue` to `@brainstorm-os/sdk-types` (Database's CSV import now consumes both), and `humanizeKey` to `@brainstorm-os/sdk` (Database + Files + Agent on one implementation). Tests-first: schema derivation / resolution / allowlist + clamp / capability filter, per-column coercion + member pin + the create path, the turn-seam never-dispatch invariant, the row card, the manifest caps.
- ✅ Agent-11e — **new database** *(shell `feat/agent-11e-new-database`, 2026-07-24)*. Coverage tier 3, and the **only propose kind whose approval creates more than one entity**: a `List/v1`, its default Grid `ListView/v1`, and one generic `Object/v1` per seed row. `logic/propose-database.ts` stages the two-part proposal — the inferred **schema** (`columns: [{name, type}]` *or* a bare `string[]`; the model's type words — `integer`/`currency`/`checkbox`/`datetime`/… — map onto real `ValueType`s, unknown → Text) and the **seed rows** (cells keyed `r<i>.<column>` in the artifact's `fields`, so the 11b edit reducer + card inputs work unchanged). Column names are **slugged into derived keys** (`Deal size` → `dealSize`) — the model never chooses a property path — a cell for an undeclared column is dropped, structured values are dropped, strings clamped, and both columns (12) and rows (10) are capped so one tool call can't stage an unbounded table. The name is control-stripped, clamped and **uniquified against every existing collection** (`uniqueName`, promoted to `@brainstorm-os/sdk`), so approving can't shadow a collection the user already has. `propose-database-persist.ts` writes in the order **rows → view → Collection**: the Collection is created LAST and lands complete (`views` / `defaultViewId` / `members` already filled), so there's no membership fix-up write and no window where the user sees an empty database; every entity is provenance-stamped with the source conversation (11c), and the shapes go through the SDK codecs (`listToEntityProperties` / `listViewToEntityProperties`) so the Database app reads back exactly what it writes. `proposalToEntityProperties` throws for this kind on purpose — a mis-route is loud instead of writing half a database. The tray card shows the schema line, an editable name, and the seed rows as the grid they'll become. Tests-first: schema/type-word/row-cell/caps/uniquify staging, the multi-entity write order + provenance + partial-row tolerance, the turn-seam never-dispatch invariant, the card, the manifest caps.

### Agent observability *(Agent-12 — [platform/77-agent-observability.md](platform/77-agent-observability.md), OQ-AO-1..5)* — ⚪

Make the agent's actions legible: a **per-run trace substrate** (shell-written, metadata-only, both front-ends of the one loop) and the surfaces that read it — per-turn timeline, automation run detail, vault-level activity query, live chip. The missing *audited* leg of the [67](foundations/67-ai-native-company.md) governed-agent story, and the pre-work [69](platform/69-agent-teams-and-orchestration.md) "what this agent did is a query" assumes. **Denials are the headline**: fail-closed's failure mode is silence (the packaged-shell cap-scope bug — stripped `:scope` suffixes silently killed the agent's tool offering — is the proof case); every refused call gets a row naming the missing capability. Local-only per [12 §Observability](shell/12-shell-architecture.md); no prompt/completion/arg-value bytes ever (the 11.8 / MCP-1 posture, property-tested). New read surface → security-review + pentest gate; no self-merge. **All five OQs resolved 2026-08-01** (the track's gate): **OQ-AO-1** retention is **tiered** — events ~30 days, runs ~12 months, *both* additionally count-capped (an age window alone does not bound a runaway automation loop), pruned on the `AiUsageRepo.prune` shape, with `agentProvenance` permanent regardless because it lives on the entity; **OQ-AO-2** reads are **shell-surfaces-only** — no `agent.trace:read` capability exists, since it would hand any installed app a map of which entities the user touches and when, to serve a consumer that does not exist; **OQ-AO-3** metadata-only is **absolute** (no debug capture on any path); **OQ-AO-4** denials are **active-but-coalesced in chat** via the existing Agent-5 escalation prompt (offer the grant, don't just report the refusal) and a **passive badge** for automations, whose user is not present at the moment of refusal; **OQ-AO-5** there are **no `model-call` rows** — `ai_usage` gains a nullable `run_id` and the timeline derives model steps from the join, so token/cost numbers have exactly one home.

- ⚪ Agent-12a — **trace substrate**: `agent_runs` + `agent_events` repos in `account.db` beside `ai_usage` (repo pattern, enums for `surface`/`kind`/`outcome`, count+age-capped prune per OQ-AO-1); write hooks at the existing chokepoints — broker service dispatch (cap-check outcome incl. `tool-denied` with the missing cap), the shared `runAgentLoop` host seam, the propose/approve gesture; both surfaces (chat turn + `WorkflowRun/v1`) emit the one shape. Fail-soft writes (full disk never breaks a turn); non-forgeable (identity from the verified envelope); **metadata-only pinned by a property test over the record codec**. Ships the OQ-AO-1 prune contract in the same rung (an unbounded table is the failure that decision exists to prevent) and the OQ-AO-5 `ai_usage.run_id` migration. — **gate: OQ-AO-1 ✅ resolved 2026-08-01.**
- ⚪ Agent-12b — **per-turn timeline (Agent app)**: expandable "what I did" disclosure per assistant message — ordered events (retrieval / tool calls / proposals with approve-state / MCP calls), denials named ("missing `intents.dispatch:open`") and wired into the existing Agent-5 escalation prompt; run-level denial badge. Renders the conversation's own runs — no new read capability. Keyboard + SR paths per workflow standards. — **gate: Agent-12a.**
- ⚪ Agent-12c — **automation run detail (Automations app)**: `WorkflowRun/v1` drill-in rendering the run's trace (step → tool → outcome → duration); failed runs show the denying capability instead of a bare error. — **gate: Agent-12a.**
- ⚪ Agent-12d — **vault-level activity (Settings → AI)**: runs filtered by surface / app / date / outcome with **"denials only"** first-class; click-through to entity / conversation; per-entity "agent history" via the `agentProvenance` back-link + `target_entity_id`. Privileged shell renderer — no app-facing capability; bounded paginated projections over IPC, never raw rows. — **gate: Agent-12a; OQ-AO-2 ✅ resolved (shell-surfaces-only — the app-facing variant is not built).**
- ⚪ Agent-12e — **live activity**: in-flight runs register with `BackgroundActivityStore` (named, cleared on completion) so a long agent turn / automation run is visible on the dashboard chip like indexing or sync. — **gate: Agent-12a.**

### MCP integrations *(Stage 11c, [platform/64-mcp-integrations.md](platform/64-mcp-integrations.md))* — ⚪

Brainstorm as an MCP **client**: the user connects external MCP servers and their tools join the agent harness's Tools layer ([62 §Layer B](platform/62-agent-harness.md)) — the *tool* analogue of the [Stage 11](#ai-broker--vector--hybrid-search-stage-11-lexical-half-shipped-early-as-shell-922) provider registry. **No new trust primitive** (capabilities + Tier-2 credentials + egress + audit + confirm-writes are all existing machinery). Distinct from the dev MCP server (Brainstorm-as-server for Claude Code, out of the product). **Gated on OQ-MCP-1/-2/-3; OQ-MCP-4/-5/-6 non-blocking.**

- ✅ MCP-1 — **MCP broker core service** (HTTP-first). **Landed 2026-06-18. OQ-MCP-1 resolved**: per-vault server *record* (`<vault>/shell/mcp-servers.json`, syncs) + per-device *enablement* + rug-pull baseline (`mcp-enablement.local.json`, non-synced) — a disabled/unreachable server shows status, never breaks config; new servers default disabled. **OQ-MCP-3 resolved**: server-level grant `mcp.server:<id>` (tool-level post-v1). `main/mcp/` — config store + JSON-RPC transport (Streamable-HTTP + SSE) over the egress broker's `executeNetworkFetch` (per-origin gated, SSRF-guarded, auth header stripped on cross-origin redirect), `tools/list` discovery, tools project as `McpAgentTool`s into the shared `runAgentLoop` via `intersectMcpTools` (offered only when the frozen set grants the server — **re-checked against the live ledger** in the broker, never trusts envelope caps), Tier-2 credential custody (`credentials/mcp-server-auth.ts`, sealed, read main-only in `connectMcpServer`, never crosses IPC/audit), per-call audit (arg-shape only). Fail-closed (`Denied`/`Unavailable`/`NeedsConfirm`, never a silent call). +94 tests; typecheck + lint clean.
- ✅ MCP-2 *(landed 2026-06-24; OQ-MCP-2 RESOLVED — plain child + `mcp.spawn-local`)* — **stdio transport** (local-process servers). A local server spawns via `child_process.spawn` with **`shell:false`** (argv verbatim — no shell-injection surface), runs the `initialize` handshake, then the one method, and is **killed when the RPC completes** (spawn-per-RPC — no lingering process, no cross-call state leak; size-capped + timeout-bounded, killed on timeout, pure over an injected `StdioSpawn` seam). Gated on the scarce, **default-off `mcp.spawn-local`** capability re-checked vs the live ledger in the broker (in addition to the per-server `mcp.server:<id>` grant — both required); stdio tools are hidden from `listTools` and `callTool` is `Denied` without it. v1 carries `command` + `args` only (no config-supplied env — a secret-leak surface; parent env inherited for PATH). Config store + `connect` + service wired; Settings → AI → MCP add-form gained a stdio transport option (command + one-arg-per-line argv + a "this runs a program on your computer" consent note). +23 tests; typecheck + biome + css-token clean. **Hardening pass (chores, `97d4e702`):** SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation (no lingering zombie), process-wide concurrent-spawn cap (8, fail-closed — no fork-bomb), in-flight-awaiter drain + post-settle data guard. **Residue:** real-shell verify a live local server (e.g. `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`) spawns + lists + calls; the hardened-sandbox convergence rides the unbuilt code-runner (OQ-AH-4). **Deferred perf (MCP-2.1):** `handleCallTool` spawns twice per call (discovery `listTools` for friction/rug-pull, then `callTool`) — a per-connection stdio *session* (spawn+handshake once, reuse, dispose; `McpConnection.dispose?()`) would halve spawns/handshakes per stdio tool call (matters most for `npx` cold-starts). Deferred from MCP-2 to keep the leak-proof spawn-per-RPC model; pairs with the code-runner track.
- ✅ MCP-3 *(landed 2026-06-18)* — **Settings → AI → MCP servers panel** + tools inspector (verbatim untrusted descriptions shown marked-untrusted, read-only/destructive annotations), mirroring the provider-key surface; add/remove/enable + per-device status; transport picker offers only HTTP families (stdio is MCP-2).
- ✅ MCP-4 *(landed 2026-06-18; OQ-MCP-4 resolved)* — **confirm-writes / read-only-hint friction model** + post-approval description-change re-prompt (rug-pull defense). `decideToolFriction` auto-runs ONLY a `readOnlyHint && !destructiveHint` tool; everything else confirms; the hint **never** overrides (a destructive+read-only tool still confirms) and is never a security boundary — the cap gate + audit apply regardless. `detectRugPull` re-prompts on a changed/new tool fingerprint (name+description+hints) even if read-only (benign→malicious swap); a confirmed call re-baselines. *(Remaining: MCP-derived artifact provenance tagging — thin follow-up.)*

- ✅ Agent-9 — **draft-as-email** (2026-07-21, shell #229): a per-reply "Draft as email" button on assistant turns dispatches the existing `SendIntentVerb.Compose` intent with the reply text as the seed body (`buildComposeEmailEnvelope`); the shell re-checks `intents.dispatch:compose`, the IntentsBus routes to Mailbox, the composer opens pre-filled. User-gesture only — the Agent never sends. The agent manifest gains `intents.dispatch:compose` (the verb + broker gate exist since Mailbox-4; the seed-upgrade path grants it). Button gated on the intents service (hidden in demo mode). +5 tests. *(Follow-up: plain-text seed today; rich HTML via Mailbox-11 `setHtml` needs a markdown→HTML serializer the SDK lacks.)*

## Agent teams & orchestration *(0.12.0 flagship — [platform/69](platform/69-agent-teams-and-orchestration.md))* — 🟡

**Status (2026-08-01): `Agent-Teams-1/2/3/4` ✅ — the hero interaction is complete end to end (slices 1–2 + the closure that shut its own review's two open items, shell #409). `Agent-Teams-5` (single-hop delegation) is the remainder.**

The vision the `vid-agent-team` reel is named for: **a team of people AND agents on one shared vault** — agents are first-class *members* you permission like a hire (scoped grants, propose-not-persist), they draft into a shared object space every human sees, and a human always commits (**dual provenance**: which agent proposed, which human approved). Design in [69](platform/69-agent-teams-and-orchestration.md); reuses the Agent-11 propose→approve pipeline + Agent-11c provenance + the Collab-C6 `Profile/v1` roster + LAN P2P sync. **The single-device demo is v1-buildable now** (doc 69 §Identity: local key-gen + roster + per-agent grants + audit are v1; only *cross-device* agent identity defers to the Collab-C5 identity track). Filed 2026-07-24 (the design's "file the rungs" follow-up, and the owner directive to build the team feature after the 0.9.0 single-user reel showed no team). New principal kind + per-agent capability surface → **every rung gates on security-review + pentest** (the prompt-injection boundary now crosses delegation). Resolves OQ-AINC-1; adds OQ-AT-1..5.

- ✅ Agent-Teams-1 — **agents as principals**: `Agent/v1` entity type (a member kind beside `Profile/v1`) + own **Ed25519 keypair** generated locally at create (reuse `credentials/identity.ts` `generateIdentity`; private-key custody stays in `main/credentials/`, never crosses IPC — the crypto-routing rule) + **roster registration** (the roster widens from human-only to resolve both `Profile/v1` and `Agent/v1` members) + **ledger principal generalized app→member** (an agent fingerprint is just another principal value in `CapabilityGrant`; no schema change, per doc 69 §Identity). Foundation for the rest. **gate: none** (builds on shipped identity/roster/ledger). **1a ✅** *(shell #276, 2026-07-24)* — the `Agent/v1` member type + roster member kind. **1b ✅** *(shell #277)* — agent key custody: each agent's own Ed25519 keypair, sealed. **Remainder ✅** *(shell #397, 2026-07-31)* — the fingerprint is now a real ledger principal (`@brainstorm-os/capabilities/principals` pins the app/agent value spaces disjoint) with a **fail-closed agent-grantable vocabulary** (`agent-grants.ts`: scoped `entities.read`, `intents.dispatch:propose-*`, `ai.use`/`search.*`/`roster.read` — a write, network, MCP or non-propose dispatch is structurally refused, preserving the Agent-11b propose→approve invariant); `main/agents/agent-directory.ts` (create mints the sealed key; delete revokes the whole ceiling + destroys the key first; identity immutable on update; every mutation an `agent.*` audit row keyed on the fingerprint); the roster service resolves `Agent/v1` members (`kind=Agent`, directory name; `members(id, {includeAgents})` appends vault agents as Viewers); `agents:*` dashboard IPC + preload bridge. `<gates: security-review, pentest>` — ⚠️ **the fixes are NOT on shell `main` yet.** Shell #397 was merged at 14:46Z; its two security-fix commits were pushed at ~15:10Z and ~15:50Z, so the squash took only the four feature commits. [shell #398](https://github.com/brainstorm-os/shell/pull/398) carries them cherry-picked onto current `main` — **until it merges, `main` has this feature with every finding below still open, and no release or dogfood build should cut.** **Both gates came back FAIL first and are recorded that way.** The review found `Agent/v1` records were app-forgeable and the roster resolved the agent map ahead of verified humans; the pentest then *defeated those fixes* with a nine-finding chain (an unreserved `shell` app id → the `import` service bypassing the new fence → non-canonical base64 binding two "agents" to one ceiling → actuation forged with the local user's public pubkey). All fixed on the branch and pinned by **36 retained probes** (`agent-teams-pentest.test.ts`, each attack inverted to assert refusal with a positive control). Two items stay open **by design** and are documented rather than claimed closed: a message body can still impersonate a speaker inside its own turn (inherent to untrusted text in a prompt — bounded today by `tools: []`, and **must be revisited before the propose-card slice**), and the `shell` principal's ceiling is still broad (the mitigation is that the id is now unclaimable).
- ✅ Agent-Teams-2 — **Team surface + scoped grants** *(shell #397, 2026-07-31)*: Settings → Team ships doc 69 §Management's three jobs — directory (create/configure/delete `Agent/v1` members, monogram avatar, persona editing), **per-agent grant/revoke** as a curated checklist (reads per-type or all · propose verbs · run/grounding set) whose options are **pinned by test to be a strict subset of the main-process agent-grantable vocabulary** (the UI can never offer what policy refuses; the privileged click IS the consent gesture), and an **Activity list** over the vault audit log filtered to the agent fingerprint ("what this agent did" is a query, not a build). Grants are ordinary `CapabilityLedger` rows keyed on the agent principal; fail-closed; an audit row per gesture, appends serialized. `<gates: security-review, pentest>`. **Residue: screenshot/dogfood pass.**
- ✅ Agent-Teams-3 — **@-mention an agent in a Chat channel** (the hero interaction): mentioning an agent runs the shared `runAgentLoop` under the *agent's* frozen ceiling → the propose→approve cards render inline in the channel for every member to see → a human approves → `entities.create` runs (human-gesture cap, unchanged). **Dual provenance**: the created object carries which agent proposed (Agent-Teams-1 principal) + which human approved (extends Agent-11c). Human-in-the-loop default (OQ-AT-2). **gate: Agent-Teams-1/-2; reuses Agent-11 propose + Agent-11c provenance + Chat @-mention (people→member scope).** **Slice 1 ✅** *(shell #397, 2026-07-31)* `<gates: security-review, pentest>` — the conversational half: `main/agents/mention-runner.ts` hooks the entities create-wrap; a HUMAN participant's mention (agents are Assistant senders → agent→agent actuation structurally impossible, the OQ-AT-2 default) runs the ONE shared loop in main with `envelope.app` = the agent fingerprint + `envelope.caps` = its live ledger grants, so the ai service's fail-closed re-check enforces the agent's own ceiling; the reply posts into the channel (sender Assistant + agent pubkey/name, `agentProvenance` stamped, main's own repo write — an agent never holds `entities.write`); no `ai.use` → an honest "not permitted yet" reply with zero model calls; Chat's `@` typeahead offers agent members ("AI agent" caption, six locales). **Slice 2 ✅** *(shell #400 → #402, 2026-07-31)* `<gates: security-review>` — the propose→approve half. First, the **injection residue the pentest had accepted had to close**, because it was safe only while the loop was offered no tools: every turn now carries a system-written `[#n from Name]` header with the untrusted body escaped so it can never contain that marker, plus an explicit untrusted-content contract (P12 flips NOTE→REFUSED, joined by P12b). Then: the propose catalogue was **promoted out of `apps/agent` into `sdk-types`** (pure move — same descriptors, clamps, verbs, caps) so main, the Agent app and Chat share ONE implementation; a mentioned agent is offered the curated propose tools it holds, and a propose call is **intercepted and staged, never dispatched**; each draft becomes its own card message every channel member sees; Chat renders approve/discard with its own fail-closed parser (a malformed card renders as an ordinary message). **Approval is a privileged MAIN-side write, not an app write** — dual provenance has to be attested rather than asserted: `proposedBy` comes from the card's host-written `created_by` (an app id can never contain `:`, so it can never name an agent), `approvedBy` from the session's own identity. The new `agent-proposals` service is gated on the scarce `agents.approve` (Chat declares it), re-checked server-side; the write is bounded by the build-time descriptor allowlist, a terminal decision, and a still-trusted proposing agent. **Scoped out deliberately:** row / database / code-file proposals (they need live vault schema this path does not assemble, so the tool is never offered rather than staging drafts approval could not honour), and per-agent retrieval grounding beyond the agent's own `entities.read` grant. **Closure ✅** *(shell #409, 2026-08-01)* `<gates: security-review, pentest>` — slice 2 passed its review with **two items documented rather than fixed**, and a rung is not done while its own review's open list is live. Both are now closed, failing-test-first. **(a) the DEK gap:** approve wrote `dekId: null`, so a channel-approved object carried no key and no member wrap and stayed un-shareable until the next vault open's retro-wrap. Rather than duplicate a security-critical ordering, the mint→persist→wrap→zero sequence was **extracted to one shared seam** (`main/entities/create-with-dek.ts`) that `entities.create` and the approve path now both route through; it carries an explicit `DekWrapFailurePolicy` — `RollbackRow` for `entities.create` (nobody has seen the row) vs. `KeepRow` for approve (the user has already been told the object exists, and the row still carries a real DEK so the wire path never sees an ambiguous null-DEK row — the posture `retro-wrap-deks.ts` already takes). The approve path's Pending re-check rides the seam's `guard` hook, so it stays atomic with the create; a 5-way race probe pins that there is no TOCTOU window. **(b) the card phishing surface:** Chat attached an approve button to *any* message carrying the property, including one synced in from another vault where it could only ever fail. `toMessage` now takes a context bag and attaches a proposal **only** when the row's host-written `ownerAppId` is a fingerprint from a **shell-authored** `Agent/v1` row — **fail-closed by default** (omit the set, no card), and a bag rather than a positional arg precisely because `.map(toMessage)` would otherwise hand the callback an array index as the trust set. **(c) was verified, not assumed:** the scoped-out row/database/code-file proposals are structurally unofferable (those verbs are Agent-app-local and absent from `PROPOSE_DESCRIPTORS`), confirmed by a probe that grants the agent *every* grantable propose dispatch and scripts the model to call each by name — so it is recorded as confirmed-structural and pinned, not claimed as a fix. +423 lines of retained pentest probes; full suite 17,005 green. **Residue: no real-shell or packaged-build exercise of the approve path.**
- ✅ Agent-Teams-4 — **seeded starter agents** *(shell #397, 2026-07-31)*: three neutral-role starters (Researcher / Builder / Reviewer) in the marketplace-forward `AgentTemplate` format (persona + traits + a `requestedCapabilities` REQUEST manifest; the keypair + grants are structurally non-portable), seeded on **vault create** so the team directory is alive on first look. OQ-AT-3 position: always-on, fully editable/deletable, `LocalOnly`+`ConfirmOnWrite`, and **zero grants at seed** — a starter is a visible, powerless member until the human scopes it (grants never ship as data); seeding is a no-op when any agent exists (never resurrects a deleted starter) and fail-soft. Every template request is pinned grantable. `<gates: security-review, pentest>` *(The Northbound demo-world extension — `seedMarketingEntities` multi-member + reel wiring — rides the Teams-3 propose-cards slice.)*
- ⚪ Agent-Teams-5 — **single-hop delegation** (`delegate` tool; child caps = child ∩ delegator, never escalating) + **assignment-driven runs** (`assignee` agent on a `Trigger`; the loop runs under the agent's re-checked ceiling). Post-demo orchestration depth. **gate: Agent-Teams-2.**

*Deferred (later, per doc 69 §Phasing):* cross-device agent identity (rides Collab-C5), multi-hop delegation trees (OQ-AT-4), autonomous agent↔agent chat (OQ-AT-2), marketplace agent/team templates (OQ-AT-5).

## Connector framework *(group I)* — 🟡

Realises [apps/56-connector-framework.md](apps/56-connector-framework.md): one signed bridge-app contract + one shell OAuth/credential/sync broker turns any external system into a sandboxed, capability-scoped connector. **Custody invariant**: a connector never holds the client secret/token; the shell injects auth and enforces the frozen egress set. Mailbox is the reference impl. **OQ-CN-1..6** — CN-1/CN-2/CN-4 RESOLVED in this slice; CN-3 RESOLVED with Connector-5 (2026-06-11, LWW + per-mapping override); CN-5/CN-6 remain. **Spine Connector-1..4 functionally complete + proven in-process (2026-06-06); the lean GitHub-issues connector is the end-to-end reference (Mailbox deferred to its own slice).**

- ✅ Connector-1 — scaffold: `Connector/v1` / `ConnectorAccount/v1` / `SyncMapping/v1` / `SyncRun/v1` contracts + enums + validators in `@brainstorm/sdk-types`; the **custody/egress keystone** (`isEgressAllowed` / `validateConnectorRequest` fail-closed, `connectorRequiredCapabilities`, `*` rejected, `EmbeddedSecret` structural check). +21 tests.
- ✅ Connector-2 — shell OAuth broker: Auth-Code + PKCE (RFC 7636 S256), **loopback `127.0.0.1` redirect** (OQ-CN-2 resolved) + custom-scheme fallback interface, token exchange via Net-1 egress scoped to frozen origins, tokens sealed in Tier-2 `CredentialStore` keyed by `ConnectorAccount` id (never cross IPC), shell-side refresh → on failure disable+notify (OQ-CN-4 resolved). `connectors` broker service (`authorize`/`revoke`, server-side `connectors.oauth` cap). +tests.
- ✅ Connector-3 — `connectors.request`: resolves account→frozen origins, refuses out-of-scope URLs (Denied + logged), injects `Authorization` (stripped from the response), rides Net-1 `executeNetworkFetch` (SSRF + audit); server-side `connectors.request` + derived `network.connect:<origin>` caps. +tests.
- ✅ Connector-4 — pull + selective + incremental sync engine: declarative `PullSpec`, `applyFieldMap`, **idempotent upsert on a flat `connectorExternalId`** + `connector.source` provenance, `SyncRun/v1`, default `external-wins` (push/two-way gated to Connector-5). Registers a `Time` trigger with the **existing** `SchedulerService`; `AutomationsHost` gains a sync route. In-process pipeline test (`connectors-pipeline.test.ts`, CLAUDE.md §4): fire → `connectors.sync` → real `Task/v1` rows → `SyncRun/v1`, **no-dup on re-run** + external-wins. 200/2000 mapping volume cap. +41 unit +3 integration tests. **Sync-run history surfaced in the reference connector 2026-06-10**: the `github-issues` app now renders its `SyncRun/v1` records (status · pulled count · relative start time · error) read reactively via `useVaultEntities` over a pure unit-tested derivation — the in-app view of what the engine writes on every pull.
- ✅ Reference connector — **GitHub-issues → Task/v1** (`apps/github-issues/`): a lean signed first-party connector declaring frozen egress (`api.github.com`) + OAuth + a `github:issue → Task/v1` `SyncMapping`; rides the substrate with **no connector-specific shell code**. Registered in `FIRST_PARTY_APPS`. SDK `connectors` proxy added. **React conversion landed 2026-06-10** (the reference conversion for the all-apps-React decision): rebuilt on the `new-app` React scaffold — `main.tsx` (createRoot) + `app.tsx` renders the `.app-header` from the shared contract (`app-header--chrome`, `app-header__title`; the hand-copied `.gh__title` face deleted), broker logic untouched in `connector.ts`, all strings through `createT` + `plural` (`i18n.ts`). Build/tsc/biome/css-token/reactivity gates green. **App removed 2026-06-11** (`apps/github-issues/` deleted, deregistered from `FIRST_PARTY_APPS`): the substrate it proved is fully covered by the in-process suite (`connectors-pipeline.test.ts` + the connectors unit tests keep `github:issue` as a pure string fixture — no app dependency); Mailbox takes over as the live reference connector per Connector-7, exercised with real user credentials.
- ✅ Connector-5 — push / two-way per-mapping + conflict policy *(✅ 2026-06-11; richer merge stays v2)* — **OQ-CN-3 RESOLVED**: conflicts resolve **last-writer-wins with a per-mapping prefer-local / prefer-remote override** — the existing `conflictPolicy` field IS the override (`vault-wins` = prefer local, `external-wins` = prefer remote, `two-way-merge` = LWW by timestamp: remote `pull.cursorField` vs the entity's `updatedAt`, unknown remote timestamp resolves remote); the queued-conflicts-view lean (option a) needs a conflicts surface no connector app has yet and layers on top later without changing the mapping contract. Engine (`sync-runner.ts`): `PushSpec` (`{path}` template with `{externalId}`, method=PATCH, fieldMap) rides the mapping entity like `PullSpec` — the shell executes it generically, no connector code runs shell-side; change detection is **content-based, not clock-based** (`connector.source` gains `pushedState` + `pulledState` stable-serialized sync-point states — echo-free by construction and immune to clock skew); two-way = pull leg with both-sides-changed detection then push leg (pure pull keeps exact Connector-4 semantics); the first push-enabled run **baselines** (records sync-point states without writing to the provider) so flipping a pull mapping to two-way never floods the remote; push only writes back provider-mirrored entities (vault-born creates are v2); `isMappingSyncable` validates the push path against the frozen egress origins too; push rides `connectors.request` (auth + egress + caps). **Also fixed a latent wire-shape bug this surfaced**: the entities service `update` reads `{id, patch}` but the connector wiring + mailbox-service sent `{id, properties}` — every connector-attributed update (authState flips, cursor advance, external-wins overwrite, mail engine updates) was a silent no-op in production; all callers now send `patch` and the mailbox test fake mirrors the real arg shape. 13 new runner cases + a two-way leg in the CLAUDE.md §4 in-process pipeline test (write-back exactly once, local value unclobbered, no duplicate mirrors).
- ✅ Connector-SEC1 — **token-endpoint egress hardening** *(✅ 2026-06-11; defense-in-depth, found in the Mailbox-5 pentest; latent, not live)*: `OAuthBroker.refresh`/`exchangeCode` egressed to `provider.tokenUrl` gated only by `assertInScope` against `provider.egressOrigins` — but when the provider config is built from a `Connector/v1` *entity* (`wiring.ts providerFromConnectorProps`), `tokenUrl` **and** `egressOrigins` both come from that entity, so an app holding `entities.write:Connector/v1` could widen the origins, repoint the token endpoint, and exfiltrate the refresh token + installed-app client secret on the next refresh. **Fix (variant 2 of the proposed routes)**: every token-endpoint egress (exchangeCode / refresh, plus an early gate in authorize) now also requires the token URL's https origin to be **registered via `OAuthBroker.registerTokenEndpoint` from a static source** — shell code for built-in providers (`index.ts` registers the Gmail token endpoint), a signed manifest at install for future marketplace connectors — never from entity properties. Fail-closed: nothing is registered by default; non-https endpoints cannot be registered. Regression tests: an unregistered token URL is refused before any secret leaves the credential store (egress never called, account not flipped, no notify); a registration for one origin does not admit another; origin-not-path matching; https-only registration.
- ✅ Connector-6 — webhook-in connectors (network ingress) — **gate: Net-1 ✅ + 11b.8 ✅** `<gates: security-review, pentest>`. **Code landed 2026-07-28 (shell PR #352); both recorded gates ran 2026-07-28 and FAILED FIRST, fixed in shell PR #354 ([report](_review/2026-07-28-connector-6-webhook-in.md), runs in the [ledger](_review/evaluations.jsonl))**: a connector's `SyncMapping` registers a shell-minted inbound endpoint on the **existing 11b.8 loopback listener** (one HTTP server — routes/hits generalized with a `WebhookTargetKind` enum: `workflow` | `connector-sync`); an authenticated `POST /wh/<routeId>/<secret>` is a **doorbell** dispatching `connectors.sync(mappingRef)` (doc 56 §Sync model, literally) — the payload is size-bounded then **discarded**, so hostile bytes never enter the projection; dispatch is per-mapping coalesced (one in-flight sync + one trailing run — sync rate capped by sync duration, not inbound rate). **Custody is hash-only at rest**: `registry.db` v12 `connector_webhooks` (typed `ConnectorWebhooksRepository`) stores the SHA-256 of the secret; plaintext exists exactly once in the `webhookRegister` response URL (reveal-once); ingress planes (loopback + relay re-verify) hash-then-`timingSafeEqual`; status never returns it. **Fail-closed gates**: server-side `connectors.webhook` cap on the new `webhookRegister`/`webhookStatus`/`webhookRevoke` methods; registration requires the RESOLVED connector app's runtime `network.ingress` grant (11b.8 Settings-prompt model, per connector app); `envelope.app` pinned to the mapping's server-resolved owner; routes register only while the grant holds. **Lifecycle**: endpoints survive restart via the registry repo, die with the mapping (revoke) and with the account (disconnect cascade); mint/revoke re-derive the route table live (a first mint mid-session lazily binds the listener — fixed a latent 11b.8 host gap where a post-`start()` listener never subscribed). SDK proxy + sdk-types types added. +45 tests (repo custody/rotation/persistence, listener digest-auth + oracle-free 404s + fail-closed no-verifier, host doorbell/coalescing/re-arm, real-loopback deployment wiring incl. per-app grant fail-closed + live revoke, service cap/owner/reveal-once). **Scoped OUT (documented boundary, not shipped unsafely): public reachability — loopback `127.0.0.1` only, relay plane stays dormant until a transport is paired (owner-ops, unchanged from 11b.8); provider-specific HMAC signature schemes (X-Hub-Signature etc.) — the shell-minted per-endpoint secret is the v1 auth contract; endpoints are device-local (registry.db never syncs), matching the designated-automation-host model.** **Gate outcome (2026-07-28):** the defensive `/security-review` and the adversarial `/pentester` pass both **failed first** and are fixed in **shell #354**. **C1 (Medium)** — a revoked `network.ingress` left already-minted endpoints answering `202` *and still running* `connectors.sync` (provider egress + entity writes) indefinitely, because the route table re-derives only on an automation-entity write and `ledger:revoke` triggered neither; closed twice over (a per-fire live ledger re-check before every webhook-driven sync, fail-closed on throw and scoped to the webhook path so Connector-4's scheduled fires are untouched, **plus** `ledger:revoke` re-deriving the table so the URL actually 404s — which also closes the same latent gap for 11b.8's workflow routes). **C2** `Invalid`-vs-`Denied` gave any `connectors.webhook` holder a cross-app mapping-existence oracle → one uniform `Denied`. **C3** `resolveMapping` is purely structural, so an endpoint could be minted against a non-`SyncMapping` entity → `SYNC_MAPPING_TYPE_URL` asserted server-side. **C4** `mint`'s `DELETE`+`INSERT` was unwrapped → transaction. **C5** the pushed head did not typecheck (2× `TS2349` in its own tests) → CI would have rejected it. **18 of 19 attacks correctly failed** and are kept as regression tests (owner-pinning bypass by a sibling holding every capability, forged `envelope.app`, digest-as-secret replay, `timingSafeEqual` length confusion, 9 traversal/encoding shapes, byte-identical 404 differentiation, the 405 method oracle, oversized doorbell bodies, `WebhookTargetKind` confusion both ways incl. a malicious `Trigger/v1` claiming a connector's `routeId`, coalescer starvation + cross-mapping fairness, `__proto__` argument shapes); the C1 fix is red-checked. Six residual items are named and accepted rather than dropped: the entity-authored owner pin (inherited from Connector-2/3 — defense-in-depth, not a boundary), a sub-microsecond timing delta between a map miss and one SHA-256, no rate floor on the coalescer (Connector-7's scheduling work), no read timeout on `readCappedBody` (pre-existing 11b.8, authenticated + loopback-only), no cascade when the `SyncMapping`/`Connector` entity itself is deleted, and the untested `ledger:revoke` ipc glue.
- ✅ Connector-7 — Mailbox as the reference connector (proves the contract end-to-end on the socket-exception path) — **gate: Mailbox-2 ✅** *(back to being the mainline reference: the GitHub-issues connector app was removed 2026-06-11; Mailbox proves the OAuth broker + custody + sync substrate with real credentials)*. **Proven in-process 2026-07-28 (shell #351)** — this was a verification rung: the code had all shipped with Mailbox-2..-6/Mailbox-5, but no single test exercised the contract as one chain. New `mailbox-pipeline.test.ts` (9 tests) wires the **production shape** end-to-end: real `Broker` + `RendererIdentityRegistry`, a real `CapabilityLedger` (ledger.db) granted **exactly the installer's set from `apps/mailbox/manifest.json`**, the production connector wiring (`buildConnectorsServiceDeps` → `OAuthBroker` over a real Tier-2 `CredentialStore`, ciphertext on disk), the real `mail` service, and the real MailTransport worker envelope handler behind `createWorkerMailTransport` (only the process edges canned: provider HTTP, OAuth redirect, `FakeMailDriver`). Clauses pinned: manifest declares no network/socket cap; connect → OAuth broker → **Tier-2 custody** (token/refresh/client-secret never on an entity, never in a reply toward the app); server-side `mail.manage` re-check fail-closed at broker + service; **socket exception** (doc 53/OQ-MB-2 — a renderer can neither spoof `_shell` nor drive the broker-registered `mailbox` worker RPC; the worker does the I/O with the shell-injected token and drops driver+secret after every run); real Email/MailFolder rows idempotent on `messageId`/`submissionId`; entity writes ride the ledger (revoking `entities.write:Email/v1` fails the sync closed); disconnect revokes cleanly. **Real defect the manifest-exact harness exposed + fixed (1 line)**: `mail.fetchAttachment` (Mailbox-6) creates a `File/v1` under the mailbox identity but the manifest never declared `entities.write:brainstorm/File/v1` — every attachment fetch in a real vault failed capability-denied (the unit suite's `callEntities` fake checks no caps, so 150 mailbox tests never saw it). **Honest residue (unchanged, tracked under Mailbox-5/-9):** live-credential real-shell round-trips vs. real Gmail/JMAP/M365; the Mailbox worker-socket transport stays the sanctioned OQ-CN-5 exception (egress frozen in static driver code, not via `connectors.request`; generic-substrate generality remains proven by `connectors-pipeline.test.ts`).
- ⚪ Connector-8 — starter set (Calendar / Contacts / Slack / GitHub / Jira / Linear → canonical types) + Marketplace "connector" content-kind — **OQ-CN-6 (review tier); gate: 14.17**.

**Spine remaining (real-shell, split out):** the production session-open registration (load `Connector`/`SyncMapping` → `ScheduleRegistration.syncMappings` → `AutomationsHost.hydrate`) + the live loopback-OAuth round-trip — needs a real Electron restart to verify (the engine is fully unit-tested + proven in-process). The `connectors` broker service is registered in `index.ts`.

## Action surface *(group I — agentic extensibility)* — ⚪

Realises [platform/63-action-surface.md](platform/63-action-surface.md): **install an app → relevant new actions appear in other apps' menus** (the desktop-OS Share-sheet / Services / Quick-Actions model). The mechanism already exists — intents registry (`findHandlers`), curated verb namespace, `intents.suggest`, the shell menu component ([17](platform/17-interoperability.md)); the missing wire is making menus suggestion-aware. Ships as **two SDK framework elements** (a *contributor* declaration + a *host* primitive) first- and third-party apps share. Security by construction (a contribution **renders in the host, executes in the contributor's sandbox**, fail-closed — the "no plugins for plugins" invariant holds). **The mechanism by which AI stays optional**: the Agent app is one contributor among many; uninstall it and its `process` actions ("Summarize"/"Generate image") vanish. **OQ-AS-1..5; gate: OpenRes-1a/1b/1c ✅ (the `open` half done) — these add the non-`open` verbs.**

- ✅ AS-1 — **Landed 2026-06-18.** **the missing wire**: an `intents.suggest` registry pass inside `buildObjectMenuItems` ([37](shell/37-cross-app-navigation.md)), so every existing object menu becomes contribution-aware with no per-app change (incremental rollout, the universal-icon/cover pattern). Relevance-gated by discriminators (`entityType`/`mime`/`format`); dispatch rides the existing fail-closed intents bus.
- ✅ AS-2 *(landed 2026-06-18; OQ-AS-1/-2 adopted)* — **host framework element**: the SDK `useContributedActions({target, verbs})` hook + `<ActionMenu>` primitive (the single code path turning a registry contribution into a rendered, dispatchable item), adopted by the cover menu / editor-selection menu / block menu / slash picker — **OQ-AS-1** (verb-to-surface eligibility). **Update 2026-07-29:** the *primitive* landed and is correct; the *adoption* half did not — `useContributedActions` / `<ActionMenu>` have **zero callers** in the repo, and the only live suggestion path is the `suggestActions` pass inside `openObjectMenu` (AS-1). The editor's inline toolbar, block-gutter menu and slash menu are still hardcoded lists. Residue picked up by **Tool-7**; the id stays ✅ for the primitive it shipped.
- ✅ AS-3 *(landed 2026-06-18; OQ-AS-5 resolved: `process`+`kind`, no `generate` verb)* — **contributor framework element**: manifest intent **presentation metadata** (`label`/`icon`/`group`/`priority`, t-translatable) + curated-verb manifest validation; first live contributor = the Agent app's `process` actions — **depends: Agent-3; OQ-AS-5** (whether a `generate` verb is ever needed; `process`+`kind` for v1).
- ✅ AS-4 *(landed 2026-06-18; OQ-AS-3/-4 resolved: sideloaded→More quarantine, ~3/group inline cap)* — **anti-menu-rot + trust**: grouping buckets (`Open with…`/`Share to…`/`Actions`), inline cap + "More actions…", trust-tier gating (sideloaded contributions quarantined under "More…" until promoted), per-app "disable contributions" in Settings — **OQ-AS-3 / OQ-AS-4**.

- ❌ AS-5 / AS-6 / AS-7 / AS-8 / AS-9 / AS-10 / AS-11 — **superseded 2026-07-29, same day they were filed (#156), by the App tools track below** (`Tool-1..Tool-9`, [78](platform/78-app-tools.md)). They specified cross-app actions on a *fragment* (paragraph/selection/block/cell) via `intents.request`/`intents.fulfill` plus a host-held Yjs anchor. The owner reframed it: apps should expose **typed callable methods** other apps discover and call *"like an MCP"*, not a new kind of menu target. That subsumes every rung here and is strictly better — a tool takes values and returns values, so it is never told *where* the data came from and **cannot aim a write**, which deletes the anchor machinery `AS-5` existed to build. **None were started.** Their content maps to: AS-5→`Tool-2`/`Tool-3`, AS-6→`Tool-1`/`Tool-4`, AS-7/AS-10→`Tool-8`, AS-8/AS-11→`Tool-7`, AS-9→the `Tool` track's first live provider. OQ-AS-6..10 superseded by OQ-TOOL-1..6.

### App tools *(Tool-1..Tool-9 — [platform/78-app-tools.md](platform/78-app-tools.md), OQ-TOOL-1..6)* — ⚪

`AS-1..4` shipped contributed actions on *objects* that **launch** the contributing app. This track makes an installed app a **typed tool provider — exactly as a connected MCP server already is** ([64](platform/64-mcp-integrations.md)): an app declares named, individually-addressable tools with typed inputs/outputs in its manifest, the shell registers and validates them, and **one registry feeds three consumers** — other apps' menus ([63](platform/63-action-surface.md)), the agent's tool layer ([62](platform/62-agent-harness.md)), and automation steps ([39](apps/39-automations-and-workflows.md)). Hero story unchanged: with the Agent installed, selecting a paragraph in a Journal entry offers "Rewrite"; the mechanism is now `app.io.brainstorm.agent.rewrite(text, tone) → text` rather than a new menu-target concept. **This corrects a shipped limitation rather than adding a surface**: today the loop addresses a tool by its intent **verb alone, so two tools collide** (why the Agent ships ONE curated `open` tool), and `AgentTool` carries **no input schema** — the model gets a verb name and a prose label. Verbs stay the *routing* layer (curated, one-way, "somebody handle this"); tools are the *calling* layer (app-namespaced, typed, request/response). Safety is inherited: a tool takes values and returns values so it **cannot aim a write**, `proposes-write` results are proposals a human approves ([75](platform/75-agent-notes-seam.md)/OQ-ANS-4 generalized to every app), and provider-authored tool text is **untrusted input** reusing MCP's hardening. New IPC direction + new capability strings → **security-review + pentest gate on Tool-1 and Tool-4; no self-merge.** **Gated on OQ-TOOL-1 (schema language) and OQ-TOOL-2 (subsume vs coexist); OQ-TOOL-3..6 leaf-local.**

- ⚪ Tool-1 — **the reverse channel** (`AppCallHost`): correlation-id request/response from shell INTO an app renderer — **which does not exist today**; all ~20 shell→app channels are fire-and-forget `webContents.send`, the app-side `LifecycleEmitter` discards handler return values, and `menu:invoke` (the one channel designed as a trusted shell→app dispatch) is dead — the app preload never subscribes. Copy the shipped precedents rather than invent: `OpenWithPromptHost` (correlation map, timeout, `MAX_PENDING`, dedup, drain-on-detach, fail-closed default) and `WorkerBridge` (30 s timeout → reject, `dispose()` → resolve `Unavailable`), plus the block-frame transport's six inbound gates. **The one genuinely new invariant: validate the reply's `event.sender` through `RendererIdentityRegistry` against the app the request was sent to** — the existing prompt hosts skip this check, safe only because their channels are dashboard-only, and app preloads are shared across every app. Shell owns the deadline (a provider can hang forever: the preload deliberately returns never-settling promises after `pagehide`). App side: `brainstorm.tools.handle(name, fn)`, a real handler registry — `on()` cannot return a value. Settle pending on renderer death / park-eviction (crash handling is observe-only today). — **`<gates: security-review, pentest>`.**
- ⚪ Tool-2 — **declaration + registry**: manifest `registrations.tools` (`name`/`title`/`description`/`input`/`output`/`effect`/`appliesTo`/`surfaces` + `AS-3` presentation metadata) with hand-written validation in the house style (JSONPath-ish error paths); `app_tools` table + repo in `registry.db` following the `openers`/`blocks`/`entity_types`/`widgets`/`intents` pattern; `tools.list({appliesTo, surface})` broker method filtered by applicability + capability + the `AS-4` per-app disable. Ids are `app.<appId>.<toolName>`, mirroring `mcp.<serverId>.<toolName>`.
- ⚪ Tool-3 — **typed arguments**: tool inputs described as `PropertyDef`s (**not raw JSON Schema** — the repo has no JSON-Schema validator, and the two inline-schema readers only *distill*; `PropertyDef` is the one system with a real validator the broker already re-runs), so **args are validated at the broker before reaching the provider** — a property MCP's opaque `inputSchema` lacks. A JSON-Schema projection is generated for the model's tool definition. — **gate: OQ-TOOL-1.**
- ⚪ Tool-4 — **invocation + capabilities**: `tools.call({tool, args})`; new grants on the existing `(appId, capability, scope)` ledger shape with no new machinery (`scope` is a free string) — `tools.provide` (provider), `tools.call:<appId>` and `tools.call:<appId>/<toolName>` (caller, mirroring `mcp.tool:<id>/<tool>`); `effect` (`pure`/`reads-vault`/`proposes-write`/`external`) drives friction through the shipped `decideToolFriction` — **declared effect lowers friction, the capability check is the boundary** (a provider can lie, exactly as MCP's `readOnlyHint` can). — **`<gates: security-review, pentest>`.**
- ⚪ Tool-5 — **untrusted-descriptor hardening**: a provider's tool `name`/`description` reaches the model's prompt, so it is the same vector doc 64 calls "the under-appreciated one" — a sideloaded app would be authoring part of the agent's prompt. Reuse wholesale: `sanitizeToolDescriptor`, the length caps, quarantined rendering (never `<system>` text), `toolDescriptorFingerprint`/`detectRugPull` re-prompt, and **no tool id may collide with a curated intent verb or an `mcp.*` id**. — **gate: OQ-TOOL-4.**
- ⚪ Tool-6 — **agent projection**: `projectAppTools` → `AgentTool`-shaped rows carrying the namespaced id (lifting the verb-collision limit) + the input schema, unioned into the harness Tools layer beside `projectMcpTools`, still bounded by `intersectAgentTools`' three-tier `tools ⊆ conversation grants ⊆ app caps`. Note MCP tools **do not reach the loop today** (no app calls `listTools`/`callTool`), so the union is being built for the first time here. — **gate: Tool-4; OQ-TOOL-2.**
- ⚪ Tool-7 — **menu presentation** (closes the `AS-2` residue): tools declaring a UI surface render as contributed actions in the editor inline toolbar / block-gutter menu / slash menu / object ⋯ menu, all through `useContributedActions` — **which has zero callers today**; only `openObjectMenu` does a suggest pass. `AS-4`'s anti-rot policy (group / dedupe / rank / inline cap / trust quarantine / per-app disable) applies unchanged and is NOT rebuilt; the inline toolbar takes a harder cap since it resolves on every text selection. — **gate: Tool-2, Tool-4.**
- ⚪ Tool-8 — **results + lifecycle**: `proposes-write` results render through a shared proposal/diff tray and apply as ONE undo step in the caller's own transaction; locked-object refusal before the call; a **named refusal chip** for every failure mode (provider uninstalled mid-call, deadline, validation, over-cap) — a hung spinner is the bug; one metadata-only trace row per call. Headless/cold-provider invocation (a `LaunchReason` variant over the existing invisible `createWidgetSurface` pattern, which already mounts a real app renderer with identity registered) is the post-v1 half. — **gate: Tool-4; OQ-TOOL-3, OQ-TOOL-6.**
- ⚪ Tool-9 — **automations**: `AgentTool` gains the namespaced id + the real input schema so a workflow step can call an app tool; **no new `StepKind`** — that enum is deliberately closed ("an open extension surface would make workflow audits intractable"), so app tools ride the existing `AgentTool`/`IntentStep` path. Files `outputSchema`'s promised-but-unimplemented `output-schema-violation` validation honestly rather than assuming it. — **gate: Tool-6.**

## Object selection & cross-app drag-and-drop *(group I — direct-manipulation interop)* — 🟡

Realises [platform/65-object-selection-and-cross-app-dnd.md](platform/65-object-selection-and-cross-app-dnd.md): **select objects in one app, drag them into another** — the direct-manipulation front-end to the intents bus. **Central constraint (corrects [17 §Drag-and-drop](platform/17-interoperability.md)):** a drag crossing the per-app renderer boundary ([OQ-4](reference/11-open-questions.md)) **cannot** use native HTML5 DnD — a `DataTransfer` does not cross renderer processes (`webContents.startDrag` carries files only) — so cross-app drag is a **shell-mediated drag session** (shell stamps `sourceApp` + owns the cursor-following ghost overlay + hit-tests the target window via `WindowIndex` + negotiates the drop over the broker — types+location on hover, **reference-only** payload on drop — re-checking caps fail-closed). The **target decides the meaning** (link/transclude/add-membership/set-property/move/copy/compose, least-destructive default, declared not guessed). Design-only so far; no code. **OQ-DND-1..6; gate: shares the selection service + declared-capability registry with the Action surface (AS-1..4 ✅).**

- ✅ DND-1 — **selection host service**: build the `selection.publish` / `selection.current` broker service [17 §Selection](platform/17-interoperability.md) specified but never shipped, + a `useSelection()` SDK hook over the existing `@brainstorm/sdk/selection` math whose state is the canonical `ObjectDragItem[]`; shell keeps only the focused app's selection (one slot). Independently lights up selection-driven intents (summarize/export selection). **Precondition for the rest — the drag payload is the published selection in motion.**
  - **✅ DND-1a — `selection` broker service landed (2026-06-21).** The host service shipped end-to-end: `SelectionStore` (one in-memory slot, vault-independent; `publish`/`current`/`clearForFocus`/`clearApp`) + `makeSelectionServiceHandler` (`packages/shell/src/main/selection/selection-service.ts`), registered in `main/index.ts` with the live ledger + a `getFocusedApp` that reads the window index. **Privacy by construction:** one slot, `sourceApp` stamped from the broker-verified `envelope.app`, and **validated against LIVE focus on every `current()` read** (the slot self-clears when the focused app isn't its owner — race-free, no fragile focus-event wiring) so app B can never read app A's selection unless A is focused. Caps: `selection.publish` (default-minimum — publishing your own selection is benign + reference-only, enables ratcheted `useSelection` adoption) + scarce shell-only `selection.read` (re-checked server-side, mirroring `billing.read`). Wire types: `ObjectDragItem`/`ObjectDragPayload` + `hardenObjectDragItems` (dedupe-by-id, drop-malformed, clamp to `MAX_DRAG_ITEMS`, Trojan-Source strip) in `@brainstorm/sdk/entity-drag`; `SelectionService`/`SelectionSnapshot` in `@brainstorm/sdk-types`; `services.selection.publish/current` SDK proxy. **+30 tests** (store semantics, focus self-clear, cap gating Denied/Unavailable, hardening). packages+apps typecheck clean, biome clean. **Remaining (DND-1b):** the `useSelection()` React hook + per-app adoption replacing bespoke `Set`/anchor containers (ratchet, rolls with DND-4).
- ✅ DND-2 — **drag-session machinery**: a `dnd` broker service + the shell drag-session state machine (begin/track/over/drop/cancel) + the shell-owned drag-ghost overlay + `WindowIndex` point-hit-testing. **Gate: DND-1; OQ-DND-1** (ghost mechanism) **✅ resolved → option (a)**, **OQ-DND-2** (hover-vs-drop leak) **✅ resolved → payload drop-only**, **OQ-DND-3 ✅** (ambient hover, gated drop).
  - **✅ DND-2a — drag-session core + `dnd` service landed (2026-06-21).** The testable spine: pure `DragSessionStore` (one active session, replace-on-begin, target/effect tracking, `payloadOf`; `packages/shell/src/main/dnd/drag-session.ts`) + pure `hitTestWindow` (top-most non-minimized window under a screen point → within-window offset; `dnd/hit-test.ts`) + `makeDndServiceHandler` (`dnd/dnd-service.ts`: begin/move/drop/cancel/setEffect over injected `GhostOverlay` + `WindowNotifier` + window snapshot + ledger). **Privacy invariant in the wire shape (OQ-DND-2):** `app:drag-over` carries `{sessionId, payloadKind, itemTypes, pointInWindow}` — structurally cannot hold items/`sourceApp`; the full `ObjectDragPayload` reaches a target ONLY on `app:drop`. **Security:** `dnd.drag` (begin/move/drop/cancel) + `dnd.drop` (setEffect/receive) re-checked server-side fail-closed; the target's `dnd.drop` is re-checked again before delivery (a target lacking it silently never receives); the real op cap (`entities.write:<type>`) is the target's own perform-time gate. `sourceApp` stamped from the broker-verified `envelope.app`. Wire types (`DragPayloadKind`/`DropEffect`/`DragOverNotice`/`DropDelivery`/`DropResult`/`DndService`) + `ObjectDragPayload` promoted to `@brainstorm/sdk-types` (single home; `entity-drag` re-exports); `services.dnd.*` proxy; `dnd.drag`/`dnd.drop` default-minimum caps. Registered in `main/index.ts` with the real per-window notifier (via launcher `allWindows`) + window-index snapshot. **+45 tests** (hit-test edges, session lifecycle, over/leave on target change, drop delivery + target-cap refusal, cap gating). packages+apps typecheck clean, biome clean.
  - **✅ DND-2b (ghost overlay) — the real cursor-following drag ghost landed (2026-06-22).** `dnd/ghost-overlay.ts`: `createElectronGhostWindow` (OQ-DND-1 → option (a)) builds a transparent, frameless, click-through (`setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)`), focus-less (`focusable:false` → source keeps pointer-capture + the Esc-cancel key), always-on-top-over-fullscreen (`setAlwaysOnTop(true,"screen-saver")` + `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(…, {visibleOnFullScreen:true})`) `BrowserWindow`. **Reference-only by construction** — it renders the `DragGhostSpec` (label + optional glyph + N-badge + drop-effect cursor affordance) via main-initiated `executeJavaScript` against a self-contained inline page (no preload / IPC surface), never the payload. Reduce-motion honoured in CSS (fade-in gated on `no-preference`; the follow itself is inertia-free `setPosition`). The overlay logic (`createGhostOverlay`: lazy-create-on-first-`show`, cursor-offset positioning, last-spec re-render on `setEffect`, destroyed-window recovery) is pure over an injected `GhostWindow` seam → **+11 tests** without Electron; wired into `main/index.ts` replacing the no-op stub. biome clean. **Remaining (DND-2b tail):** the source renderer's pointer-capture forwarding (`pointermove`→`dnd.move`, `pointerup`→`dnd.drop`, Esc→`dnd.cancel`) — pairs with the DND-3 `useDropTarget`/`useDragSource` SDK primitives. Real-shell verify (needs a source driving `dnd.begin`+forwarding): cross-monitor follow + reduce-motion + click-through.
- ✅ DND-3 — **wire + drop-target primitive**: standardise the payload on the shipped `application/vnd.brainstorm.entity+json` widened to `{ v, sourceApp, items[] }` (supersedes doc-17's `x-brainstorm-entity`/`-blockprotocol`); ship the `useDropTarget({accepts, onDrop, dropEffectFor})` SDK hook spanning both transports (native intra-renderer + `app:drag-over`/`app:drop` cross-app); migrate Notes' `entity-drop-plugin` onto it as the reference target. **Gate: DND-2.**
  - **✅ DND-3a — wire reconciliation + `useDropTarget` + Notes reference target landed (2026-06-22).** **Wire** (`@brainstorm/sdk/entity-drag`): `serializeObjectDragPayload`/`parseObjectDragPayload`/`setObjectDragData`/`readObjectDragData` carry the widened `{ v, sourceApp, items[] }` under the SAME `application/vnd.brainstorm.entity+json` MIME; the reader normalises BOTH the widened shape AND the legacy single-`{entityId}` shape (back-compat with every shipped native drag source) → a one-item list. `sourceApp` from the native transport is self-asserted and explicitly NOT trusted for authorization (only the shell session stamps a trustworthy one). **Hook** (`@brainstorm/sdk/object-dnd`, new subpath): `useDropTarget` gives an app ONE drop handler over BOTH transports — native intra-renderer (`dropProps` spread on the drop-zone; reads the entity MIME) and the shell-mediated cross-app session (a process-wide `CrossAppDropRegistry` subscribing to the preload-forwarded `brainstorm:cross-app-{drag-over,drag-leave,drop}` DOM events, replying the hover effect via `dnd.setEffect`, routing the drop to the LIFO accepting target). **Privacy preserved (OQ-DND-2):** the registry never reads items at hover — `drag-over` carries kinds+point only; the payload arrives on `drop`. **Transport:** added `payloadKind` to `DropDelivery` (shell `deliverDrop`) so the drop info is complete; the `APP_DRAG_*` push-channel names + `CROSS_APP_*` DOM-event names moved to `@brainstorm/sdk-types` (single home shared by the shell `dnd` service emitter + the lean preload forwarder + the SDK registry — no React pulled into the preload). **Notes** `entity-drop-plugin` now registers as a cross-app reference target (`nativeDisabled` — the native path stays Lexical-command-based; cross-app drop → `MentionNode` per item, least-destructive default). **+34 tests** (widened/legacy wire round-trips + hardening; registry bind/LIFO/effect-report/drop-route/leave; `useDropTarget` native accept/ignore/dragover-effect/nativeDisabled + cross-app delivery). biome clean.
  - **✅ DND-3b / DND-2b source tail — `useDragSource` landed (2026-06-22).** The renderer that STARTS a cross-app drag (`@brainstorm/sdk/object-dnd`). Native `dragstart` can't drive a cross-renderer drag, so the source drives the shell session with POINTER events: a press-drag past a small threshold → `dnd.begin` (shell stamps `sourceApp` + paints ghost + hit-tests), each move → `dnd.move` **coalesced to one per animation frame** (the raw stream is 60–120 Hz), `pointerup` → `dnd.drop`, Escape / `pointercancel` / source-unmount → `dnd.cancel`. Threshold-gated so a plain click never starts a drag. The gesture logic is an imperative `DragMachine` (`drag-machine.ts`) separated from the thin React `useDragSource` wrapper so it's unit-testable without a renderer — including the begin-still-in-flight edge cases (an up/Escape that lands mid-`begin` resolves once the session id arrives) and `window`-listener cleanup. `setPointerCapture` on the handle + reliance on OS button-down drag-capture for cross-window delivery. **+10 tests** (threshold gating, ghost/screen-point at begin, rAF move-coalescing, drop/cancel, begin-in-flight up, empty-selection abort, listener cleanup, non-primary-button ignore). biome clean. **Remaining:** sub-window rect-scoping of cross-app drop targets (v1 is window-level, LIFO); **real-shell verify** the full source→ghost→target loop (cross-monitor follow + reduce-motion + click-through + the OS cross-window pointer-delivery assumption — fallback if it fails: a shell-side `screen.getCursorScreenPoint()` poll); then per-app adoption (DND-4 drop targets + drag handles on list rows).
- ✅ DND-4 — **roll drag sources + drop targets across apps**: collection / Database-view membership-add, Calendar date-set, Files folder move (Alt=copy), kanban column set-group-by, relation cells — each declaring accepted kinds + semantic. **Gate: DND-3; OQ-DND-4** (heterogeneous selection), **OQ-DND-5** (auto-scroll/spring-load scope).
  - **✅ DND-4b — app rollout landed (2026-06-23, `a9e05fdf`).** Drag sources + drop targets across the native-source apps: Database rows-as-source (hover grip, selection-aware) + board-column set-property/membership-add + grid-view source, Calendar day-cell date-set (`resolve-drop-date-key`), Files source-grip + folder/tree membership-add (`folder-tree`). Notes editor stays the reference drop target (DND-3a). Pairs `useDragSource` grips with `suppressNativeDragRef` (pointer vs native-draggable conflict) and the **rect hit-testing** fix so multiple positioned drop zones in one window route by cursor (was window-level LIFO → N targets collapsed). **+~120 tests** fleet-wide. biome clean. **Remaining gate:** real-shell pointer-drag + startDrag-latency dogfood.
  - **✅ DND-4a — drop-semantics foundation + first reference drop target (2026-06-22).** The shared decision layer (`@brainstorm/sdk/object-dnd` `drop-semantics.ts`): `DropSemantic` enum (the design's meaning matrix — reference/transclude/add-membership/set-property/move/copy/compose, an enum not raw strings), `effectForSemantic` (→ the `DropEffect` cursor affordance) + `leastDestructive` (the safe default when a target accepts several — never copy-by-default). Wired into the **Chat** composer (`chat__composer-wrap` `dropProps` + drop highlight). The pure pieces (`objectItemToAttachment` isolated in a sdk-types-only module; semantics) are unit-tested locally; **+10 tests**. biome clean. **Remaining (the regression-risk / real-shell-gated half):** the native-source apps (Notes list → `useDragSource` on rows, conflicting with the existing native `draggable`), Files move, Calendar date-set (type-specific date property), Database/kanban membership — all deferred to the real-shell verification pass per the DND-2b/3b gate.

Inbound OS file-drop already works (editor media stack). **Gate: DND-2.**
- ✅ DND-6 (shell #185) — **keyboard / a11y twins**: "Move to… / Add to… / Link to…" target-picker commands (object menu + action surface [63](platform/63-action-surface.md)) performing the same drop semantic; cut/copy/paste as the move/copy isomorph on the structured clipboard; `aria-dropeffect` + live-region operation announcements; reduce-motion ghost. **Gate: DND-1 (selection), DND-4 (semantics).**

## Object read-only lock (fleet, cross-app)

User feature (2026-06-28): *"lock should be present in all apps where possible, and synced."* A per-object **read-only lock** — block edits, allow view/navigate — carried by a normal synced entity property (`locked`), so it converges across devices like any other edit. Distinct from the Stage-13.8 PIN/app-lock (which locks the whole vault); this locks a single object's content. **Retro-filed 2026-06-28** — the feature shipped end-to-end through the dogfood loop (sessions 354–360) ahead of a tracked rung; recorded here so the plan reflects what's built.

- ✅ Lock-1 — **foundation** *(shell `5471c90` + `c43621d`)*: shared `@brainstorm/sdk/lock-button` `<LockButton>` (one header toggle for the fleet — `.header-icon-btn`, `aria-pressed` accent-styled locked state; Notes migrated off its bespoke button) + a reactive `EditableSync` plugin in the shared `@brainstorm/editor` (`editor.setEditable` on prop change). **Keystone fix:** `<BrainstormEditor>` previously only seeded `editable` in `initialConfig`, so a post-mount lock did nothing for any consumer (Notes only worked via its own `EditablePlugin`); `EditableSync` unblocks read-only for **every** BrainstormEditor host. Verified real-shell (dogfood 354): `contenteditable` flips true → false (locked) → true (unlocked), 0 console errors.
- ✅ Lock-2 — **fleet rollout, one app per commit, dogfood-verified each**: ✅ Notes + ✅ Journal (354, `c43621d`), ✅ Code-editor (355, `fe5dc2b` — `textarea.readOnly`), ✅ Whiteboard (356, `3d08f1f` — board-level engine `readonly`), ✅ Tasks (357, `140b60f` — body editor via EditableSync), ✅ Calendar (358, `de96e68` — EventDetail `<fieldset disabled>` + Save/Delete suppressed), ✅ Database (359, `dfad0fc` — per-record lock gates the shared `editProperty` commit → cells read-only across every view; inspector rename frozen), ✅ Bookmarks (360, `e728e95` — detail body via EditableSync). **All 8 lockable apps ship a synced read-only lock.**
- ✅ Lock-3 — **retro-fill the workflow bar** *(partly paid by shell PR #18 `lock-rollout-fixes`/`5ffda45`, 2026-06-28)*. The lock fleet shipped dogfood-verified, but `bun run verify` runs only the integration/entities subset — so the **full `bun run test` went red on shell/main** (the CI failure surfaced 2026-06-28). #18 greened it + completed enforcement: added the missing `@brainstorm/sdk/lock-button` vitest alias (every test transitively importing whiteboard/code-editor `app.tsx` was failing), a `code-projection` locked-field expectation, a keyboard-raw-keys baseline prune, and the real per-app gates (a locked task hands back no field persisters; a locked note freezes the property bag; database lock labels localised via `t()`). **Still owed:** dedicated unit tests for the shared `<LockButton>` + `EditableSync` primitives, and the keyboard/screen-reader path evidence (lock toggle reachable + announced; locked state announced to SR). **Process fix worth making:** `verify` not running the full suite is *how this slipped* — close that CI gap. **Gate: none (cleanup; not beta-blocking).** **Closed 2026-07-28 (shell #346):** LockButton 8 dedicated tests (controlled toggle, native-button keyboard semantics, aria) + EditableSync 5 through a real `<BrainstormEditor>`+Y.Doc (live lock/unlock without remount, blur-on-lock — and `EditableSync` DRY'd onto `EditablePlugin`, so Journal/Tasks gain Notes' blur behaviour); keyboard/SR evidence recorded in the PR. Failing-first lock-gap fixes: calendar locked events were drag-reschedulable / bulk-movable / cross-app-droppable / menu-deletable (fixed via locked→readonly projection + commit gates), tasks locked cards draggable across board columns (fixed). Bonus SDK-wide a11y fix: React `<Icon>`'s default Phosphor branch lacked `aria-hidden`/`focusable=false` — every React-app icon leaked an unnamed graphic into the a11y tree. The verify-vs-full-suite CI gap needs NO change — CI's ubuntu leg already runs the full `bun run test` (added post-incident); widening `verify` would only duplicate it. Full suite 15,953 green.
- ✅ Lock-4 — **enforcement gaps closed** *(shell PR #47 `fix/lock-enforcement-gaps`/`83ac38d`, 2026-06-30)*. An iteration-chores retrospective (2-day code review) found Lock-2's per-app rollout gated each app's *primary* surface but left *secondary* write paths live — a record could show "locked" yet still be edited. Fixed: **database** routed cover/icon/inspector-properties + board/calendar/timeline drag through a new exported `isRecordLocked()` (the Lock-2 claim "cells read-only across every view" was only true for grid + title); **bookmarks** gated the cover button + OR'd `locked` into every properties-panel row; **code-editor** extracted `isCodeFileEditable()` (content file AND not locked) gating rename/delete in the object menu + defense-in-depth guards. **Tests:** `isCodeFileEditable` matrix, bookmark-panel read-only-when-locked, new `inspector-properties` read-only-when-`onEdit`-absent — closing part of Lock-3's owed unit coverage. typecheck (packages+apps) + lint clean. Logged as **F-303**. **Gate: none.**
