## Shared control-face primitive (design-system enforcement)

User feedback (2026-06-30): *"we have a design system, so [an input not matching the button beside it] should not happen."* Right — the failure (Calendar New-event date field taller than the time `.bs-select` next to it) wasn't a weak polish pass; it was that the design system shipped a control-height **scale** (`--control-height-*`) and button/select faces (`.bs-btn`/`.bs-select`) but **no input face** and **no enforcement**, so apps hand-rolled `<input>` boxes with padding-based heights that drift. The fix makes the system *prevent* the drift, not just describe it. Logged as **F-304**.

- ✅ DS-input-1 — **`.bs-input` primitive + ratchet + Calendar migration** *(shell branch `feat/sdk-control-face-primitive`, 2026-06-30)*. **Primitive:** `.bs-input` in `@brainstorm/sdk/app-theme.css` — the text-field counterpart to `.bs-btn`/`.bs-select`, on the same `--control-height-*` scale (`--sm`/`--lg`/`--multiline`, placeholder/hover/focus/disabled), for text inputs, `<textarea>`, and field-trigger buttons (e.g. a date picker). A control's height comes from the scale, never hand-rolled padding; apps supply only layout deltas. **Enforcement:** `tools/check-control-faces.mjs` (in `bun run lint`/`lint:apps`) — a grep-grade shrinking-baseline ratchet (same shape as `check-app-reactivity.mjs`) that fails when a non-baselined app file gains a native `<input>`/`<textarea>`/`<select>` without a face class; **29 pre-existing offender files baselined** for later migration. **Migration (proof):** Calendar's date trigger + title/location/description/search/attendee/caldav inputs all moved onto `.bs-input` (date field now lines up pixel-exact with the time select — the reported bug); title row swatch bumped to `--lg` to match the title input. Documented in [apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md](apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md) → "Control faces". typecheck (apps) + calendar build + 18 calendar tests + css-token/control-face/biome checks clean. **Remaining (DS-input-2):** migrate the 29 baselined apps' inputs onto `.bs-input` (baseline shrinks to zero → absolute ban). **Gate: none.**
- ✅ DS-grip-1 — **`.bs-drag-grip` primitive + Database/Files migration** *(shell branch `feat/sdk-control-face-primitive`, 2026-06-30)*. Reported (dogfood): the reorder/drag-handle grip "sticks to the content" in every list/table — the hover-revealed grip was absolutely positioned over the first cell with **no reserved gutter**, so its 16px box overlapped the leading content (status glyph / title). Root cause was the same class as DS-input: the grip element + its spacing CSS were **re-implemented per surface** (`.dbv-grid__drag-grip`, `.content-row__drag-grip` — identical copy-pasted 18-line blocks), so there was no single place that owned "the grip clears the content." **Primitive:** `.bs-drag-grip` in `@brainstorm/sdk/app-theme.css` — owns the box, the `text-faint` six-dot glyph, the grab cursor, the hidden→revealed transition and the absolute pin; the host supplies only the gutter offset (`--bs-drag-grip-inset`) + its one row-hover reveal selector. **Migration (proof):** Database grid + Files content rows both moved onto the face and now reserve a real leading gutter so the grip parks **clear** of the first cell (the stage/list scroll containers clip overflow-x, so the gutter is reserved *inside* the row, not floated into negative space — a negative offset just hid the grip's left half). Measured **4px gap** between grip and content on both surfaces, no clipping; head/body/foot rows share `.dbv-grid__row` so the grid columns stay internally aligned. Documented in [apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md](apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md) → "Control faces". Verified by dogfood session **372** (grip rect vs content-start measured + captured on both apps). typecheck (apps) + database/files build + css-token/control-face/biome checks clean. **Remaining (DS-grip-2):** the in-flow grips (dictionary-editor — duplicated in `packages/editor/src/editor-theme.css` — and form-designer field cards) don't crowd (they reserve a track) but should migrate onto the shared face to kill the remaining copies. **Gate: none.**
- ✅ DS-cell-combobox-1 — **select-like text cells edit as a type-or-pick combobox** *(shell working tree, 2026-07-01; dogfood F-314)*. Reported (dogfood): editing a status/select cell in the Database grid dropped into a bare free-text input — no way to pick from the values already in use. Root cause: the option picker (`TagCell`) only fires when the column's effective `PropertyDef` carries a `vocabulary` (catalog-backed); **inferred** columns (`effective-def.ts` never attaches one) fall through to the plain `FormattedPillCell`. **Shipped:** optional `suggestions?: readonly string[]` on the shared **`CellProps`** (additive — existing cells unchanged); `columnValueSuggestions` (database `logic/`) gathers a column's distinct existing values and **self-gates to enumerable columns** (short values · ≤24 distinct · they repeat) so prose / identifier columns stay plain text; the grid memoizes per-column suggestions and threads them through `EditableCell` → the cell; the formatted text cell, when given suggestions, opens a combobox via the shared **`openSearchPicker`** (`@brainstorm/sdk/menus`) — filter the existing values or commit a new one through a synthetic "use «typed»" row (free text preserved), falling back to the inline input when no menu host is mounted. New shared primitive `openValueCombobox` / `comboboxRows` in `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui`. +tests (`comboboxRows` filter/synthetic-row, `columnValueSuggestions` heuristic); typecheck (packages+apps) + biome + reactivity ratchet clean; 752 database + 203 SDK property-ui tests green. Ships alongside the F-313 Database grid/popover polish pass (hover scheme, padding, ellipsis, shared checkbox, action rows). **Gate: none.**
- ✅ DS-input-2 — **fleet migration of hand-rolled inputs onto `.bs-input`; baseline 29→2** *(shell branch `feat/ds-input-2`, 2026-07-02; dogfood F-315)*. First migrations (2026-07-01) took the baseline 29→27 (Agent budget field + memory-popover rename). The 2026-07-02 sweep migrated the **remaining 21 baselined files across 14 apps** — automations, browser (omnibox + find-bar), chat, contacts (hero name `--lg`, add-company, search), database in-cell rename, files search, form-designer + invoices (15 fields), graph (where-editor + subject), journal reminder-time, mailbox (To/Cc/Subject/From + all IMAP credential fields + search), notes select-field option input, preview sidebar search, theme-editor (name/CSS/typography/token value inputs) — each onto `.bs-input`/`--sm`/`--lg`/`--multiline` (or the already-shared `<SelectMenu>` for enumerated choices), deleting the per-app box CSS and keeping only genuine layout deltas. **Composite pattern made first-class:** searchbars that wrap an icon + input in a `.bs-input` label now use a shared `.bs-input__control` inner-slot + `.bs-input:focus-within` ring (Files / Contacts / Mailbox), recognized by the ratchet as a face token — no per-app opt-out. **`control-faces-baseline.json` now holds exactly 2 files** — the Agent composer and Mailbox message-body `<textarea>`s, the two deliberately-distinct primary compose surfaces (documented exceptions, not debt). Full `bun run verify` + `bun run lint` (control-faces ratchet + css-tokens + reactivity + i18n) green; every touched app's suite passed. Documented in [apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md](apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md) → "Control faces". **Gate: none.** *(The last 2 baselined surfaces are intentional; the ratchet is effectively at its floor — a new native control anywhere else fails CI.)*

- ✅ DS-panel-toggle-1 — **right-panel toggles declare their availability; ratchet + fleet sweep** *(shell branch `fix/panel-toggle-availability`, 2026-07-25)*. Reported repeatedly (dogfood): a right-hand panel toggle that "goes dead" — the inspector only renders with a selection, but the header button stays enabled, so clicking it changes nothing. **Audit (23 call sites, 14 apps, read not grepped):** the fleet was in better shape than the complaint implied — 6 apps already passed `disabled`, and 3 (Files / Preview / Journal) are correctly *always live* (own empty state, or a CSS collapse) where disabling would remove a working panel. Four real gaps: **Bookmarks** conditionally *rendered* the toggle (vanishing header control → the panel is undiscoverable and the header jitters) → migrated to `disabled` + `hint`; **Database** hand-rolled both header toggles in `index.html` and painted them with the SDK's private `panelToggleIcon`, so their `aria-label`s were hardcoded English that never tracked open/closed → rebuilt on `createPanelToggleButton` (ids kept — they're the dogfood-spec selector contract) and the inspector now disables itself on a view with no rows to seed; **Books / Notes / Tasks** disabled without a `hint`, and a disabled control fires no pointer events so the tooltip chip can never explain itself → hints added (Books in all 6 locales). **SDK:** `createPanelToggleButton` gained the `hint` option + `setHint` its React twin already had — the two are exact twins again. **Enforcement:** `tools/check-panel-toggles.mjs` (in `bun run lint`/`lint:apps`) — every `PanelSide.Right` toggle passes `disabled` or is baselined as always-live in `panel-toggle-baseline.json` (3 entries, each with its reason), and zero-baseline ban on `panelToggleIcon` in apps. Left toggles exempt (a nav sidebar has content regardless of selection). The ratchet immediately paid for itself: it found the Bookmarks call site that `grep` had silently missed on a large `.tsx`. +11 ratchet tests +3 SDK hint tests; full `lint` (7 gates) + workspace/apps typecheck + build:apps + 2341 app/SDK tests + 407 integration/entities tests green. Documented in [apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md §Panel-toggle availability](apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md) + a CLAUDE.md convention bullet. **Gate: none.**

## Properties-panel management (fleet, cross-app)

Audit (2026-07-25, this session; **substantially revised after verification — the first pass was wrong on 3 of 5 rungs**). Original claim: "eight apps hand-build property rows on the low-level primitive instead of the complete shared panel, migrate them." Verification killed most of it. What survives is small and specific.

Two shared surfaces exist, one layered on the other: the primitive **`@brainstorm-os/sdk/properties-panel` → `<PropertiesPanel>`** (chrome + rows the host builds), and **`@brainstorm-os/sdk/property-ui` → `<EntityPropertiesPanel>`** (a stored `ValuesMap` → editable rows + add-menu + remove + a `canMutate` gate, wrapping the primitive). Journal and Preview use the complete one.

**The decisive question is not "which panel does it import" but "does the app own a stored `ValuesMap`."** Most don't — they hold *typed fields* and project them into a bag for display only:

| App | Shape | Migratable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Notes | `note.values` — a real stored bag, rows derived from its keys | **yes** (gated, see Props-4) |
| Tasks | **hybrid** — typed task fields *plus* a real `task.values` bag; already exposes `onValuesChange(next: ValuesMap)` | **partly** (blocked, see Props-3) |
| Bookmarks | `bookmarkToValues(bookmark, tagsDict)` → fixed `BOOKMARK_PROPERTY_DEFS`; writes via `applyBookmarkPropertyValue` → typed partial, dictionary-resolved at event time | no |
| Contacts | `personToValues(person)`; writes via `applyPersonPropertyValue` → typed patch | no |
| Books | `bookToValues(book)` — typed author/format/pages | no |
| Files | `customPropertyRows()` — size/type/path | no |
| Database | columns via `EditableCell` | no |
| Graph | selection summary | no |

`onWriteValues(next: ValuesMap)` is a **whole-bag write**. An app with no bag has nothing to write it to: the shared panel would hand back a bag the host must reverse-map per key back into typed fields — strictly worse than the per-key `onChange` it already has, and for Bookmarks it would also lose the live-dictionary resolution that tag edits depend on. Those six apps sit on the primitive **because that is the correct layer for them**, not through drift.

Lock enforcement is **sound everywhere it applies**, just spelled three ways: row-level `readOnly` (Bookmarks, Books, Contacts, Notes, Tasks) · shared `canMutate` (Journal, Preview) · *absence of* `onEdit` (Database — `app.ts:1608`, per Lock-4). Graph and Files have no lock concept.

**Net remaining work: one app (Notes), gated on a design decision — plus an optional SDK slot if Tasks is wanted.** Recorded below with the rejected rungs kept so the false leads are not re-filed.

- ❌ Props-1 — **"Database: raise the lock to row level" — rejected, premise false.** `app.ts:1608` passes `onEdit: recordLocked ? undefined : …`, and `InspectorProperties` documents *"Absent ⇒ the record is read-only (locked): every cell paints read-only"*. **Lock-4 already closed this** (2026-06-30, shell PR #47), with an `inspector-properties read-only-when-onEdit-absent` test pinning it. The audit grepped each panel for the literal `readOnly` and read 0 hits as "not threaded"; Database spells the lock as the *absence of* `onEdit`. **No work owed.**
- ❌ Props-2 — **"Bookmarks + Contacts onto `<EntityPropertiesPanel>`" — rejected, they have no stored bag.** Both derive their values (`bookmarkToValues` / `personToValues`) and write typed partials per key (`applyBookmarkPropertyValue` / `applyPersonPropertyValue`); Bookmarks additionally resolves the tags dictionary at *event* time, which a whole-bag write cannot express. Filed off a `ValuesMap` grep that matched their `readValue()` **usage** on a derived bag rather than an owned one. **No work owed.**
- ✅ Props-3 — **Tasks on `<EntityPropertiesPanel>` via the host-row slot** *(2026-07-28, shell PR #356)*. **Slot decision (a): `extraRows?: readonly PropertiesPanelRow[]`** — the plan's own smallest-composable candidate, taken as-is: host rows merge into the SAME `.bs-props__list` grid, rendered BEFORE the name-sorted bag rows, in host order; each row keeps its own cell value / `onChange` persister / `readOnly`, so per-field lock enforcement stays host-side (a locked task hands over no handlers → every bridged row freezes, `canMutate:false` freezes the bag half). Companion `pickerExcludeKeys` (→ `AddPropertyPicker.excludeKeys`) keeps `assigneeId` out of the picker — the bridged Assignee row already edits that F-152 def, and binding it into `values` would mint a divergent second "Assignee". Tasks' `boundCustomDefs` / `unboundCustomDefs` + the flat `openAnchoredMenu` add-list deleted; the inspector now gets the rich shared picker (search + create-new). `emptyLabel` became optional (extraRows hosts are never empty). **Gate: none (decision recorded here + in the PR).**
- ✅ Props-4 — **Notes on `<EntityPropertiesPanel>` — picker decision: the panel owns it** *(2026-07-28, shell PR #356)*. **Picker decision (b):** the "two pickers" premise had half-dissolved — Notes' rich picker was extracted to the SDK `<AddPropertyPicker>` earlier, so its `addPropertyStore.BindToNote` route was pure mount-point indirection over the *same component*. Resolution: the shared panel mounts the picker itself; `AddPropertyTargetKind.BindToNote` deleted (store + plugin keep only the three genuine Lexical-mutation targets: `/property` slash, insert-after, append-to-list). `EntityPropertiesPanel` gains `pickerLabels` / `relationTargetTypes` passthrough; Notes' localized label set moved to `apps/notes/src/properties/picker-labels.ts`, shared by BOTH mount points so the flows can't drift. Notes' adapter now wraps `EntityPropertiesPanel` with ONE whole-bag `onWriteValues` (lock-gated in `app.tsx`; the old `onSetValue`/`onClear`/`onBind` triple deleted). **Gate: none (decision recorded here + in the PR).**
- ✅ Props-5 — **the six non-migrators recorded as deliberate** *(2026-07-25)*. [apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md](apps/09-shared-sdk-catalog.md) → *"What is deliberately not shared"* now carries the **stored-bag-vs-projection test** ("does the app own a stored `ValuesMap`" — not "which panel does it import"), why a whole-bag `onWriteValues` is strictly worse than a per-key `onChange` for a projection, a table naming each of Bookmarks / Contacts / Books / Files / Graph / Database with its projection helper and its write-back shape, and the three spellings of lock enforcement (row `readOnly` · `canMutate` · *absence of* `onEdit`) so the `readOnly`-grep false lead cannot be re-filed. Each helper re-verified at HEAD before it was written down. **Gate: none.**

**Method note for the next audit:** three of five original rungs were filed off greps for one spelling of a concept — `readOnly` (missed Database's `onEdit: undefined`), `onAdd=` (missed the conditional-spread `onAdd:`), and `ValuesMap` (matched `readValue` usage on derived bags). Grep locates candidates; it does not establish absence. Read the call site.

## How to use this plan

1. **Pick a section** (Infrastructure first where there's a dependency; Shell/App work parallelises once its substrate exists).
2. **Resolve its gating OQs** in [11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md); take a position; update the entry.
3. **One PR per iteration**, tagged with a domain. PR description: iteration id, design doc(s) realized, OQ resolved, tests (per-package floor), perf numbers if budget-touching, capability surface diff, UX evidence if user-facing.
4. **Update all three files in the same turn an iteration lands** (this doc + [implementation-log.md](implementation-log.md) + [implementation-plan-table.md](implementation-plan-table.md)) — flip the task icon, append the log narrative, bump the table row. See [[feedback_keep_plan_table_in_sync]] / [[feedback_update_plan_as_we_go]].
5. **At a section boundary**, run the three audits (stability + performance + security) under `docs/_review/<date>-<section>-audit.md`; sweep resolved OQs.
6. **Any structural plan edit** (decomposition, restructure, re-domaining — not a routine icon flip) must re-validate the dev-MCP projector in the same turn: run `bun run test -- mcp-server` (the `parsePlan` / resources / self-host-audit suites) and fix drift before moving on. The 2026-05-18 restructure silently red-lined 14 of these suites until SH-29 — the source-of-truth doc broke its own parser and nobody noticed. Until 0.12 lands (markdown edit-only-through-the-tool), this manual check **is** the gate; while dev-MCP is offline, every hand-edit carries the "re-validate via dev-MCP when available" debt and the changelog of shipped iterations lives in [implementation-log.md](implementation-log.md), **not** in the table's header line.

## What this plan is not

Not a schedule. Not a design doc (a design doc wins on *what something is*; this plan updates to match). Not exhaustive (bugs/polish/refactors live in the tracker). Not v2 (a v2 plan is a separate doc when v1 ships; the v2 commercial work is captured here only as the Infrastructure → Commercial-backend section because its client wiring lands inside v1's foundations).
